title: t2887: headless canary: validate opencode binary, detect claude CLI misconfig, long backoff on config errors
body:
alex-solovyev runner has 468 launch_recovery:no_worker_process failures in 48h because OPENCODE_BIN_DEFAULT resolves to anthropic/claude CLI (returns '2.1.119 (Claude Code)' from --version) instead of anomalyco/opencode (returns '1.14.x'). The canary then runs 'claude run -m model' which fails with 'unknown option -m' since claude CLI does not accept -m. Add pre-canary validation that detects this misconfig, searches alternative paths for a real opencode binary, falls back if found, and uses 1h backoff (vs current 90s) on structural config errors to stop the dispatch-claim spam.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---
[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.11.6 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.14.25 with claude-opus-4-7 spent 4h 13m and 295,705 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

title: t2888: restore setup_opencode_cli install logic; add to non-interactive path
body:
Companion fix to t2887. The setup_opencode_cli function in .agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh:49-53 is a no-op stub (TODO: Extract from setup.sh lines 4771-4823) since PR #20189. The original install body was deleted from setup.sh during t316.3 module extraction (PR #1253) but never ported. Result: 'aidevops update' calls setup.sh --non-interactive, which never installs the opencode-ai binary. Worse, _setup_run_non_interactive (setup.sh:951-1036) does not invoke setup_opencode_cli at all — only cleanup_stale_bun_opencode + validate_opencode_config + update_opencode_config (config-only paths). This means runners with a missing or wrong-package opencode binary (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/opencode resolving to @anthropic-ai/claude-code via collision on the 'opencode' bin name) are never healed by the framework — they spam canary failures until t2887's fail-fast cache kicks in.

## Why
Alex-solovyev's runner (t2887 root cause) had OPENCODE_BIN_DEFAULT='/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode' returning '2.1.119 (Claude Code)' — Anthropic's claude CLI, not anomalyco/opencode. t2887 stops the spam (1h backoff) but does not heal the binary. The framework should detect-and-install: install opencode-ai when missing, force-reinstall when the resolved binary is the wrong package.

## How
EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh:48-53 — replace stub setup_opencode_cli body with real install logic. Reuse _validate_opencode_binary + _find_alternative_opencode_binary from headless-runtime-lib.sh (deployed since t2887). Detect wrong-package via the validator, force 'npm install -g opencode-ai@latest' (or bun equivalent), re-validate post-install. Write resolved path to ~/.aidevops/.opencode-resolved-path for diagnostics.

EDIT: setup.sh:951-1036 (_setup_run_non_interactive) — add 'setup_opencode_cli' call between cleanup_stale_bun_opencode (line 968) and validate_opencode_config (line 972). Also keep the existing line 1121 call from _setup_run_interactive.

NEW: tests/test-setup-opencode-cli.sh — smoke test: stub bin returning 'Claude Code', verify validator detects + install path triggered (use a fake npm shim).

### Files Scope
- .agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh
- setup.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-opencode-cli.sh (NEW)

## Acceptance
1. setup_opencode_cli body is non-empty and validates+installs opencode-ai when missing or wrong-package
2. _setup_run_non_interactive calls setup_opencode_cli — visible in setup.sh:951-1036
3. Smoke test passes: fake claude-code shim → triggers install path
4. After running 'setup.sh --non-interactive' on alex-solovyev's runner: opencode --version returns ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ (semver, not '(Claude Code)')

Verification:
shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh setup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-opencode-cli.sh
grep -n 'setup_opencode_cli' setup.sh   # expect 2 hits: 968 area + 1121

title: bug: auto-decomposer-scanner re-fires on already-decomposed parents and ignores prior decision provenance
body:
## Problem

`auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` re-fires on a parent-task even when it has filed children, when the parent body still contains an `## Open questions` section that mentions an alternative the maintainer has already settled in prior closed issues.

## Real-world failure

<webapp> parent #2547 — "Self-host Tambo for AI chat interactive UI" (`parent-task`):

- Filed 2026-04-18 by maintainer with `## Open questions` section that mentioned "Vercel AI SDK as alternative — evaluate if worth it"
- That question was already settled by t011/#172 (eval DONE 2026-02-23) and t059b/#433 (Tambo self-host+rebrand DONE 2026-03-04) — but the parent body kept the legacy question text
- 2026-04-25: auto-decomposer scanner read the parent and filed three children:
  - #3044 — "Evaluate Tambo vs Vercel AI SDK" (treating the settled question as live)
  - #3045 — "Deploy and configure (Tambo OR AI SDK)"
  - #3046 — "Integrate (Tambo OR AI SDK)"
- A worker on #3044 then recommended Vercel AI SDK against the maintainer's prior directive
- Another worker on #3045 implemented Vercel AI SDK in PR <webapp>#3085 (CLOSED with CI failures)
- Maintainer reaffirmed "Tambo self-hosted please" twice on #3044 (comments 4320899245, 4321143924)
- 2026-04-26: scanner re-fired again, filing #3111 — closed today as Outcome A

Token waste: at least 5 worker dispatches across #3044/#3045/#3085 burning ~80K+ tokens total on the wrong direction.

## Root cause

`auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` checks for the `parent-task` label and the `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` nudge marker. If both are present and parent has no children section/sub-issue graph, it files a decompose request. This is correct for genuinely undecomposed parents.

The bug: when the parent IS decomposed (children exist), the scanner should not re-file. The current check appears to depend solely on the nudge-comment age vs `1-day re-file gate` from `reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`, not on whether decomposition actually exists.

A second, complementary issue: when the parent body's `## Open questions` section names an alternative the maintainer has already chosen against, the decomposer treats it as still-evaluatable. There is no "decision provenance" check.

## Proposed fix

In `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`:

1. **Skip decompose if parent already has children.** Before filing a decompose-parent issue, check:
   - Parent body has `## Children` (or `## Sub-tasks` / `## Child issues`) section with `#NNNN` references, OR
   - Parent has filed sub-issues via GitHub's sub-issue graph (GraphQL `issues(parentIssue:)`)
   - If either is true, do NOT file a decompose request — the parent is decomposed; the auto-decomposer's purpose is satisfied.

2. **Skip decompose during recent maintainer activity window.** If the parent or any child has a maintainer comment in the last 48h, skip — maintainer is engaged and will direct decomposition manually if needed.

3. **(Optional, more invasive) Decision-provenance check on `## Open questions`.** When generating the decompose body, if any prior CLOSED issue with `status:done` from the same repo links back to this parent or shares titular keywords with an open question, surface that in the decompose body so the worker doesn't re-litigate.

(1) and (2) are simple deterministic checks; (3) is the harder semantic check and probably belongs in a follow-up.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` skips parents that already have a `## Children` section listing ≥1 issue ref
- [ ] `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` skips parents with a maintainer comment in the last 48h on parent or any linked child
- [ ] Reproduction case (the <webapp> #3111 / #2547 scenario) does not re-fire after fix
- [ ] Logging: when scanner skips, emit a one-line `[skip:has-children]` or `[skip:recent-maintainer-activity]` to the scanner log so future debug is trivial

## Source repo

<webapp> — see closed #3111 (auto-decompose request) and parent #2547 for the failure trace.

## Related framework rules

- `.agents/AGENTS.md` § "Parent-task decomposition lifecycle (t2442)"
- `.agents/reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` § "AI-Generated Issue Quality (GH#17832-17835)" — same family of "scanner files issue without verifying premise" problem

title: t2891: apply opencode binary validation to active setup-modules/tool-install.sh:1517 (t2888 followup — wrong file)
body:
## What

Apply the t2888 wrong-package detection logic to the ACTUAL active `setup_opencode_cli` function at `setup-modules/tool-install.sh:1517-1570`. The t2888 PR (#21018) restored install logic in `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh` but that file is orphan code — `setup.sh` sources `setup-modules/tool-install.sh` (line 753), not `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh`.

## Why

The active `setup_opencode_cli` short-circuits on `command -v opencode` success without validating the binary is actually anomalyco/opencode:

```bash
# setup-modules/tool-install.sh:1521-1526 (broken)
if command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    local oc_version
    oc_version=$(opencode --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 || echo "unknown")
    print_success "OpenCode already installed: $oc_version"
    return 0
fi
```

On alex-solovyev's runner, `command -v opencode` resolves to `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` (returns `2.1.119 (Claude Code)`) and the function returns 0 without healing. t2887 throttles the spam but cannot fix the binary; t2888 went into the wrong file.

## How

EDIT: `setup-modules/tool-install.sh:1517-1570` — replace the early-return with a validator+heal pattern:

1. Add inlined `_setup_validate_opencode_binary` helper (mirrors t2887 validator semantics: rc=0 valid, rc=1 wrong package, rc=2 missing). Same logic as the function I added to `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh` in PR #21018 — copy and adapt.
2. Replace the `command -v opencode` block with:
   - Resolve current binary
   - Validate via `_setup_validate_opencode_binary`
   - rc=0 → print success and return (current behaviour, but now actually validated)
   - rc=1 → log `Wrong package detected (<version>) — forcing reinstall to heal bin collision`
   - rc=2 → log `Not found — installing`
3. The install path needs to skip the interactive `setup_prompt` when running non-interactive (this is also a bug in the original — but `setup_prompt` returns the default in non-interactive, so OK as-is).
4. After install, re-validate. Persist resolved path to `~/.aidevops/.opencode-bin-resolved`.
5. Fail-open if no installer.

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh:48-167` (PR #21018) — that's the same logic, just in the wrong file. Cherry-pick and adapt.

NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh` — adapt `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-opencode-cli.sh` for the active function.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `setup-modules/tool-install.sh::setup_opencode_cli` validates binary post-`command -v` (no early return on wrong package)
- [ ] On wrong package detected, force-installs `opencode-ai@${pin_ver}` overwriting the bin
- [ ] Smoke test passes: claude CLI shim → triggers reinstall path
- [ ] After running `setup.sh --non-interactive` on alex-solovyev's runner: `opencode --version` returns `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` semver (not `(Claude Code)`)
- [ ] `~/.aidevops/.opencode-bin-resolved` is populated after setup runs
- [ ] Local manual smoke verification: setup.sh non-interactive output includes `OK: OpenCode CLI: <path> (<version>)` from validator path

## Session origin

Discovery during t2888 deployment verification: the deployed `~/.aidevops/.opencode-bin-resolved` file did not get created by `setup.sh --non-interactive`, only by manual `_services.sh` invocation. Tracing showed `setup-modules/tool-install.sh:1517` is the active code path, not `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh:48`. PR #21018 (t2888) is harmless (orphan module is now functional even if unused) but did not heal alex-solovyev's runner.

Relates to t2887 (PR #21001 merged) and t2888 (PR #21018 merged).

title: t2892: fix(security): credential-scrub regex missing word-boundary corrupts task-* identifiers
body:
The credential-scrub regex in shared-constants.sh, contributor-insight-helper.sh, and credential-transcript-scrub.py lacks a word-boundary anchor before the credential prefix alternation. Words like task-failure-handler match sk-failure-handler (which is part of the credential pattern sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}) and get corrupted to ta[redacted-credential]. This actively damages source code in committed files when worker output stream gets written to disk. Evidence: awardsapp/develop has corrupt import statement at packages/api/src/inngest/functions/index.ts:11 — file on disk is task-failure-handler.ts but import string says ./ta[redacted-credential]. Same in __tests__/process-url-capture.test.ts mocks. Fix: anchor the regex with (^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-]) capture and restore via backreference. Add regression tests for task-failure-handler, task-decompose, task-runner, etc.

title: t2894: report all dispatch-dedup blockers in /full-loop gate (followup to t2890)
body:
## What

When a `/full-loop` invocation hits an issue with multiple dispatch-dedup blockers (e.g. `parent-task` AND `no-auto-dispatch` AND a non-self assignee), `_check_linked_issue_gate` only reports the FIRST blocker matched by `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned`. The user has to fix one, retry, hit the next, fix that, retry — instead of seeing all blockers up front.

## Why

Gemini code-assist surfaced this on PR #21027 (the t2890 fix). The merged PR's case statement is correct for the helper's current API contract — `is-assigned` short-circuits on first match by design — but the UX could be better.

Real-world impact:
- aidevops#20518 had `parent-task` + `no-auto-dispatch` + (originally) no assignee. The pre-t2890 gate failed open on the first two. Post-t2890, the gate would block on `parent-task` first; if the user removed that label, the next attempt would hit `no-auto-dispatch`. Two round-trips instead of one.

## How

Two viable approaches:

**Option A: enumerate blockers in the gate** (no helper change)

Call `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned` once, capture its short-circuit signal, then independently check the labels we know are structural blockers (`parent-task`, `no-auto-dispatch`) via `gh api` and report each as a separate `reasons+=` entry.

- Pros: no helper API change, narrow scope
- Cons: duplicates label knowledge between the gate and the helper

**Option B: add an `enumerate-blockers` subcommand to `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`** (helper change)

New subcommand returns ALL applicable signals as newline-separated tokens. The gate iterates and translates each.

- Pros: single source of truth for blocker enumeration; pulse can adopt later for verbose-mode logging
- Cons: broader API surface

Recommendation: Option B — the helper is the canonical source of dispatch-eligibility knowledge; the gate should be the consumer, not a parallel implementation.

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — add `enumerate-blockers <issue> <slug> <runner>` subcommand returning all matched signals
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:230-260` — replace the case statement on `is-assigned` output with iteration over `enumerate-blockers` output
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-gate-pulse-parity.sh` — extend assertions to verify multi-blocker scenarios
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-enumerate-blockers.sh` — model on `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-is-assigned.sh`

## Acceptance

- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh enumerate-blockers <issue> <slug> <runner>` returns all matched blocker signals (newline-separated, empty stdout when no blockers)
- `_check_linked_issue_gate` reports ALL applicable blocker reasons, not just the first
- New test asserts multi-blocker reporting against a fixture or live issue
- Backward compatibility: `is-assigned` API unchanged (callers untouched)

## Tier

`tier:standard` — single helper API addition + gate refactor + 2 test updates. Not simple (judgment in API design), not thinking (clear pattern to follow).

## Source

Followup to PR #21027 (t2890). Gemini code-assist suggestion at https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/21027#pullrequestreview — additive scope per t1382 review-bot-gate rule, filed as separate task.

title: t2893: harness gh signature-gate JS hook errors with misleading message when --body-file is created in same bash call
body:
## Task

Improve `quality-hooks-signature.mjs` JS plugin hook so its blocking error message names the **specific** failure cause (file-not-found, file-unreadable, helper-failure, etc.) instead of the generic catch-all "likely heredoc/cmd-sub/quoting" string. Add explicit guidance for the common "body file created in the same bash call" failure mode.

Full worker-ready spec: `todo/tasks/t2893-brief.md`.

## Why

**Pre-execution race.** `quality-hooks-signature.mjs::checkSignatureFooterGate` runs BEFORE bash executes. When a body file is created later in the same bash command (e.g., `cp ... /tmp/foo.md && gh issue comment --body-file /tmp/foo.md`), `readFileSync` throws ENOENT, `_repairBodyFile` returns null, and the outer hook throws a generic error blaming heredocs/cmd-sub/quoting — none of which apply.

**Cost.** Each worker hitting this wastes ~3-5 tool calls debugging the wrong cause (verifying file content, renaming temp paths, reading hook source) before discovering the wrapper-sourcing workaround documented in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. ~5-15K tokens of pure diagnostic burn per occurrence. Recurs for every worker writing the natural "build comment file inline, post it" pattern in one bash call.

**Anti-mentorship.** The current error blames three causes the worker can verify are NOT the issue without naming the actual cause. Per the t1901 "prompt as mentorship" core principle, error messages must transfer the knowledge needed to fix the issue.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:226-238` — `_repairBodyFile`: return `{status,reason,detail}` structured failure, not null
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:197-214` — `_generateSignature`: same structured-failure pattern
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:299-326` — `tryRepairSignature`: thread structured failure up
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:335-377` — `checkSignatureFooterGate`: format throw using specific reason; targeted same-bash-call hint for FILE_NOT_FOUND
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh:1-50` — header comment: document runtime-vs-pre-execution split between JS hook and PATH shim
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` "Signature footer hallucination (t2685)" — add subsection 8e: same-bash-call gotcha + two correct workflows
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/test-quality-hooks-signature-failures.mjs` — JS test harness, one assertion per FAIL_REASON value

### Reference pattern

`quality-hooks-signature.mjs:178-186` (`_hasUnparseableBody`) — current pattern for distinguishing failure modes via separate predicates. Extend with structured `reason` field.

### Verification

```bash
# Unit test the structured-failure paths
node .agents/scripts/test-quality-hooks-signature-failures.mjs

# Repro the same-bash-call failure mode (should now report FILE_NOT_FOUND specifically)
gh issue comment 99999 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops-test --body-file /tmp/does-not-exist.md 2>&1 | grep -q "body-file not found" && echo PASS

# Regression: pre-created body-file path still works
echo 'test' > /tmp/precreated.md && gh-signature-helper.sh footer >> /tmp/precreated.md
gh issue comment 99999 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops-test --body-file /tmp/precreated.md --dry-run 2>&1 | grep -qv "missing signature footer" && echo PASS

# Regression: wrapper-sourcing path still works
bash -c "source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh && gh_issue_comment 99999 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops-test --body-file /tmp/precreated.md --dry-run" 2>&1 | grep -qv "Hook auto-repair" && echo PASS
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/gh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `.agents/scripts/test-quality-hooks-signature-failures.mjs`
- `todo/tasks/t2893-brief.md`

### Complexity Impact

- `_repairBodyFile` 13→18 lines, `tryRepairSignature` 28→33 lines, `checkSignatureFooterGate` 43→63 lines
- All remain well under 100-line `function-complexity` gate; comfortable buffer to 80-line warning threshold
- No pre-planned refactor needed

## Acceptance

- [ ] JS hook's blocking error names the SPECIFIC failure cause (one of FILE_NOT_FOUND, FILE_UNREADABLE, HELPER_MISSING, HELPER_FAILED, UNPARSEABLE_BODY, BODY_ARG_QUOTING, BODY_ARG_NO_MATCH) instead of generic "likely heredoc/cmd-sub/quoting"
- [ ] FILE_NOT_FOUND error includes targeted hint about same-bash-call race + the two correct workflows (split into two bash calls, OR source `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`)
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Signature footer hallucination (t2685)" gains subsection 8e documenting the gotcha
- [ ] gh PATH shim header comment documents the runtime-vs-pre-execution split
- [ ] Test harness asserts each of the 7 failure-reason returns
- [ ] Regression: pre-created body-file path continues to work
- [ ] Regression: wrapper-sourcing path continues to work

## Why no-auto-dispatch + interactive

JS hook runs on every framework `gh` write. Regression risk warrants maintainer review before dispatch — same precedent as #20918 (PATH shim mutation, sibling concern). Interactive session intends to implement.

- `#20918` (t2861) — PATH shim mutates source file (sibling bug class, distinct)

title: t2895: task-id-guard check-pr mode hangs on PRs with large merge commit sets
body:
## What

Investigate and fix the slow runtime of `task-id-guard.sh check-pr` mode when invoked on PRs that contain a large merge commit set. The Task-ID Collision Guard CI check hangs for 8-21+ minutes on such PRs vs the typical 16-52 second baseline.

## Why

Concrete evidence from PR #20913 (planning PR for t2840, parent #20892):

- **First run** (2026-04-25T19:06): the workflow run failed (run 24938392490 conclusion: failure).
- **Second run** (2026-04-26T11:55:57, after merging origin/main to clear conflict): hung 21 minutes 26 seconds before being cancelled. The PR's merge brought in 143 upstream commits.
- **Third run** (2026-04-26T12:18:08, rerun after cancel): hung 9+ minutes in the "Run task-id collision check" step before being cancelled and the PR admin-merged.
- **Same workflow on other PRs/branches** completed in 16-52 seconds (verified against 5 recent runs: 24956401827=25s, 24956388205=52s, 24956382078=17s, 24956373578=16s, 24956308496=16s).

The hang blocked auto-merge per t2411 (`origin:interactive` from OWNER, all other 35 checks green). Maintainer had to admin-merge to unblock the parent decomposition. Repeating this pattern on future planning PRs that touch many commits will cause similar dispatch-blocking hangs.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/hooks/task-id-guard.sh
- .github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-guard.sh (new tests)

### Approach

1. **Profile first** — add timing instrumentation to `check-pr` mode in `task-id-guard.sh`. Identify whether the bottleneck is per-commit `gh api` calls, regex extraction, or merge-base computation.
2. **Optimize hot path** — likely candidates:
   - Batch `gh api` calls (single GraphQL/REST query for N commits instead of N queries)
   - Skip merge commits explicitly (they cannot introduce new task IDs)
   - Skip commits already on main (they already passed the check there) — use `git log origin/main..HEAD` instead of full PR commit list
3. **Add CI timeout** — `.github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml` should set `timeout-minutes: 5` on the job so a hang fails fast instead of blocking auto-merge for 6 hours.
4. **Add paths-ignore for pull_request** — the workflow currently has `paths-ignore` for push events but NOT for pull_request events. Planning-only PRs (TODO.md, todo/**, README.md, CHANGELOG.md changes) do not need to run this check.

### Reference pattern

Compare runtimes empirically before and after the fix using `time bash .agents/hooks/task-id-guard.sh check-pr <PR>`.

### Verification

- `time bash .agents/hooks/task-id-guard.sh check-pr <PR>` completes in <30s for typical PRs
- For PRs with 100+ commits in the merge: <2 min
- New unit test in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-guard.sh` covers the merge-commit-skip and origin/main-skip optimizations
- CI timeout set to 5 min in `.github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Profiling identifies the dominant cost in `check-pr` mode
- [ ] Optimization brings typical PR runtime under 30s
- [ ] Large-merge PR runtime under 2 min
- [ ] CI workflow has `timeout-minutes: 5` to fail fast on regressions
- [ ] `paths-ignore` added for pull_request event (planning files)
- [ ] Tests cover the optimization paths

Discovered while unblocking PR #20913 (t2840 planning PR for parent #20892). The Task-ID Collision Guard hung 21 min on first run, 9+ min on rerun, blocking auto-merge despite all 35 other checks passing. Maintainer admin-merged to unblock. The hang was infrastructure-level (slow check on large merge), not a real collision — all task IDs in the PR were properly claimed via `claim-task-id.sh`.

title: t2896: lower pulse circuit breaker threshold from 0.30 to 0.05 — REST fallback shifted the calculus
body:
# t2896: lower pulse circuit breaker threshold from 0.30 to 0.05

## What

Reduce `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` from 0.30 (30% / 1500 points reserved) to 0.05 (5% / 250 points reserved).

## Why

The 0.30 threshold was raised from the original 0.05 in t2744 to "preserve headroom for in-flight reads" — a rationale that has since been weakened by t2689 (read-side REST fallback) shipping. With t2574 + t2689 + t2772 covering create/edit/comment/view/list operations via REST when GraphQL is exhausted, the 30% reserve is now mostly preserved for a small set of GraphQL-only mutations (`addSubIssue`, etc.) plus next-pulse-cycle recovery headroom — neither of which requires 1500 points.

### Operational evidence (t2870 session, marcusquinn runtime)

- 43 breaker fires in 4.5 days (~10/day)
- GraphQL still hit 0/5000 with the breaker active — exhaustion happens via in-flight reads which the breaker doesn't gate
- 30% reservation = 36,000 unused points/day
- Cost saved by prevented dispatches: ~$4-11 over 4.5 days (~$30-70/year)
- Cost of reservation: 25% of dispatch budget unavailable for productive work

### Why 0.05 (not 0)

0.05 restores the original t2690 emergency-floor value:

- Still fires in genuine exhaustion (last 250 points)
- Recovers ~25% of GraphQL budget for active dispatch (back to ~9000 points/hr usable)
- Trivial revert path if the lower threshold masks real failures

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` — change `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD=0.30` to `0.05`; append change-history entry
- `.agents/configs/plist-env-overrides.json.txt` — match the new value
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` — update inline docstring referring to "default 0.30 = 30% = 1500/5000"
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` — update "GraphQL budget < 30% (1500/5000 points)" reference in Pulse circuit breaker section
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Changed entry

### Verification

- `shellcheck` clean on the script
- `markdownlint-cli2` clean on AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md
- After deploy + 24-48h: check `pulse-stats.json` `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` counter to confirm the new threshold isn't masking real failures

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All cross-references updated (script docstring, plist override, AGENTS.md)
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under Changed

title: t2899: Fix branch_orphan false-positive: workers complete on main, work discarded
body:
## What

Stop classifying successful worker completions as `worker_branch_orphan` when the worker's final HEAD ends up on the default branch (`main`/`master`). Workers exit cleanly (`exit_code=0`, `output_size=300-450KB`, `result_label=success`) and then get reclassified as orphans because `_worker_produced_output` sees `branch=main` + signal 2 fires (main exists on remote) + no PR linked → returns `branch_orphan`. Claim is released as `worker_branch_orphan` and the run is discarded.

## Why

This is the single largest current throughput sink. Evidence over the last 24h:

- 9 of 10 worker logs show `[lifecycle] worker_branch_orphan session=issue-NNN branch=main` immediately after a successful `handle_run_result_returned ... handle_exit=0 result_label=success`. (90% false-positive rate.)
- `pulse-stats.json` `counters.worker_branch_orphan_count` fired 31 times in 24h.
- `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` failed for every observed case in the same window — recovery is broken too.
- Each false-positive discards 300-450KB of LLM output and several minutes of opus/sonnet compute. At current rate, ~20-30 worker-hours/day are wasted.

Canonical example: `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-20967.log`:

```
[INFO] [lifecycle] handle_run_result_returned session=issue-20967 handle_exit=0 result_label=success
[INFO] [lifecycle] worker_branch_orphan session=issue-20967 branch=main
[INFO] [lifecycle] Orphan recovery failed for session=issue-20967
[INFO] Released claim on #20967 (reason: worker_branch_orphan)
```

## How

Reading `_worker_produced_output` at `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1128-1197`: when `branch_name=="main"`, signal 2 (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`) ALWAYS matches because main exists on the remote. Signal 1 (`origin/main..HEAD` count) is 0 because we ARE on origin/main. Signal 3 (PR linked to issue) is 0 because no PR was opened. The function returns `branch_orphan` — which is semantically wrong: there is no orphan branch, the worker just ended on main.

Two fixes needed:

1. **EDIT `headless-runtime-helper.sh:1158-1166`** — guard signal 2 against the default branch. When `branch_name` matches the repo's default branch (resolve via `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` once and cache, fallback to env `DISPATCH_REPO_DEFAULT_BRANCH`, ultimate fallback `main`), set `has_pushed_branch=0`. Otherwise the signal is meaningless on default branches.

2. **EDIT `headless-runtime-helper.sh:1245-1278`** (`_handle_worker_branch_orphan`) — extend the diagnostic log so the next regression is debuggable. Print: original target branch (from session env if present), final HEAD, count of local commits ahead of origin, and presence of `work_dir` worktree path. This is mentorship for the next session that hits this.

3. **INVESTIGATE separately** why workers end up on main at all. The legitimate orphan is "feature branch + commits + no PR". The current pattern is "main + no commits" — that's `noop`, not `branch_orphan`. Suspected root cause: worktree-creation in `_cmd_run_prepare` is failing silently or `work_dir` is being passed as the canonical repo path. File a follow-up issue once this fix lands and we have clean diagnostic logs.

Reference pattern: `_worker_produced_output` already short-circuits to `noop` at line 1168-1172 when both signals are absent. The fix extends that early-exit logic.

## Acceptance

- After deploy: `worker_branch_orphan_count` over a 24h window drops below 10% of completed workers (current: 90%). Measure: `cat ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json | jq '(.counters.worker_branch_orphan_count | length)'` 24h delta.
- New diagnostic log line on every orphan classification includes target_branch, final_head, ahead_count, work_dir.
- Legitimate orphan path (real feature branch + commits + no PR) still triggers `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr`. Verified by unit test.
- New test file `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh` covers:
  - `branch=main, ahead=0, no PR` → returns `noop`
  - `branch=main, ahead=N, no PR` → returns `noop` (default-branch guard)
  - `branch=feature/tNNN-foo, ahead=N, no PR` → returns `branch_orphan` (unchanged)
  - `branch=feature/tNNN-foo, ahead=N, PR exists` → returns `pr_exists` (unchanged)

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh
- .agents/AGENTS.md

## Complexity Impact

`_worker_produced_output` is 70 lines today (1128-1197). Adding the default-branch guard adds ~10 lines → 80 lines. Within the 80-100 advisory window; no refactor required.

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh
# Then watch for 24h:
jq '.counters.worker_branch_orphan_count | length' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json
```

title: t2900: Eliminate SQLite database lock errors during concurrent worker startup
body:
## What

Eliminate `database is locked (5)` errors during worker startup. Every observed worker log (10 of 10 in last 24h) hits this error during the SQLite migration phase. Workers continue past it, but the error indicates concurrent worker DB races and is correlated with the `worker_branch_orphan` cluster (paired root cause hypothesis: workers without a usable session DB skip persistence and exit on main).

## Why

100% of recent worker startups show:

```
Performing one time database migration, may take a few minutes...
sqlite-migration:done
Database migration complete.
[aidevops] SQLite: Runtime error near line 171: database is locked (5)
```

(See `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-3076.log`, `worker-20987.log`, `worker-20984.log`, `worker-20985.log` — all the same pattern.)

The pulse spawns up to `MAX_WORKERS=24` concurrent workers. The "one time database migration" is being run by EVERY worker startup — not once per machine. Concurrent workers race on the same `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (or per-tenant equivalent), one wins the migration write lock, the rest see `database is locked (5)`.

The lifecycle does isolate per-worker DBs (`db_merged dir=/var/folders/sr/.../aidevops-worker-auth.XXXX`) but the migration appears to run on the shared DB before the merge. That's the race window.

## How

Reading `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:581` (`db_merged dir=...`) and surrounding context. The flow is:

1. Worker starts.
2. Migration runs against shared DB (race window — ALL workers do this).
3. Per-worker isolated DB is created at `$TMPDIR/aidevops-worker-auth.XXXX`.
4. Worker work happens.
5. `db_merged` event — isolated DB is merged back.

Fix candidates (pick one based on architecture review):

A. **File-lock the migration step.** Wrap the migration in `flock` over a per-database advisory lock file. Other workers wait, find migration is `done`, skip. Cost: blocks worker startup briefly. Benefit: zero races.

B. **Skip migration when version matches.** Read the schema version from the shared DB before running migration. If current, no-op. The current code says "one time database migration" but apparently runs unconditionally. Fix: make it actually one-time.

C. **Per-worker isolated DB from the start.** Don't migrate the shared DB at all from a worker context — copy a known-good version, migrate the copy, never touch the shared file. Cost: more disk. Benefit: zero races.

Recommended: **B + A defence-in-depth.** Fix the migration to actually be one-time (B), add flock around the call site as a regression guard (A).

Reference pattern: `pulse-wrapper.sh` already uses `flock` extensively — `acquire_instance_lock`, the `pulse-wrapper.lockdir` pattern. Reuse the same convention.

## Acceptance

- After deploy: zero `database is locked (5)` errors in `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-*.log` for 50 consecutive worker runs.
- Migration log line `sqlite-migration:done` appears at most once per `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` schema version per machine.
- Worker startup time (from spawn to first LLM call) does not regress more than 200ms.
- Add a stress test: `tests/test-concurrent-worker-startup.sh` spawns 8 workers in parallel against a clean DB, asserts no lock errors and exactly one migration line in aggregate.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-concurrent-worker-startup.sh

## Complexity Impact

Both files are large (>1500 lines). Likely 30-50 line addition for migration guard + flock wrapper. Functions involved are around `db_merged` / migration call site. No new function should exceed 100 lines.

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-concurrent-worker-startup.sh
# Then watch for an hour:
grep -c "database is locked" ~/.aidevops/logs/worker-*.log | rg -v ":0$"
# Should be empty.
```

title: t2901: Reduce pulse cycle duration below launchd interval to stop cascading skips and force-kills
body:
## What

Reduce average pulse cycle duration from 25-30 min to under 5 min, OR raise the launchd `StartInterval` (currently 180s) to match measured cycle duration plus headroom. The current 30:1 mismatch (cycle:interval) causes constant "Pulse already running" skips, force-kill recovery at the 1800s ceiling, and repeated session-startup overhead that wastes most of the cycle.

## Why

Direct measurements from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log` over the last 4 cycles:

- `complexity_scan`: 471s, 407s, 471s
- `preflight_ownership_reconcile`: 602s with 124 errors
- `prefetch_state`: 184s
- `preflight_capacity_and_labels`: 134s, 122s
- `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger`: 67s, 97s
- Other stages: ~10-30s each

Aggregate per cycle: ~25-30 min. launchd schedule: 180s. Result:

- Last 24h log tail: 162 `Pulse already running ... skipping` events
- 12 `FORCE-RECLAIMED stale lock from PID NNN (age >1800s)` events in same window — pulses being killed mid-cycle by the 30-min ceiling, then a new pulse starts cold
- `pulse-stats.json` `dispatch_backoff_skipped` and `pulse_dispatch_no_work_breaker_tripped` counters fire when work is queued but pulse can't get to it

The economic effect: every kill discards ~25 min of preflight cleanup, ownership reconciliation, and pre-fetched state. The next pulse re-does it from scratch. We are paying for the same work over and over.

## How

Two-track fix. Both are needed:

### Track 1: shorten the cycle (preferred)

- **Move `complexity_scan` out of the dispatch cycle.** Reading `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1346-1349`, complexity_scan runs inside `_preflight_*` phase, blocking dispatch for 7-8 min. The comment at line 1346 already calls out the problem: "complexity_scan (200-340s) would starve downstream scanners". Current observed: 470s — the budget already overshot. Move to a separate launchd job at `sh.aidevops.complexity-scan.plist`, run hourly (not every 3 min), with its own lock so it cannot block dispatch.

- **Diagnose `preflight_ownership_reconcile` 124 errors.** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1251-...` (`_preflight_ownership_reconcile`). 602s with 124 errors suggests stale data being re-queried per repo. Cache the assignment graph between cycles (TTL ~5 min) — only re-query repos with status-label changes since last cycle. Errors should be classified: rate-limit errors should short-circuit the stage (let circuit breaker handle it), permission errors should be logged once not 124 times.

- **Audit `prefetch_state` 184s.** Likely batch-prefetch already paginating. Verify it actually saves more than its 184s cost.

### Track 2: align the schedule

- Edit `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` `StartInterval` from 180s to 600s (10 min). Reload with `launchctl bootout/bootstrap`. This stops the cascading skips even before Track 1 lands. Document the change in `.agents/configs/launchd-defaults.md` (or equivalent).
- Optionally: switch from `StartInterval` to `StartCalendarInterval` so cycles align to wall-clock boundaries (e.g., :00, :10, :20, ...) which makes log correlation easier.

Reference pattern: `sh.aidevops.contribution-watch.plist`, `sh.aidevops.worker-watchdog.plist` already run on independent schedules — the same pattern works for `complexity-scan`.

## Acceptance

- After Track 1 deploy: average pulse cycle duration drops below 5 min (measured from `pulse-stage-timings.log` rolling 24h average).
- After Track 2 deploy: `Pulse already running ... skipping` events drop below 10 per 24h (current: 162).
- `FORCE-RECLAIMED stale lock` events drop to 0 per 24h (current: 12).
- complexity_scan continues to fire — at its own cadence — verified by `~/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-last-run` being updated within the last hour.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh
- .agents/launchd/sh.aidevops.complexity-scan.plist
- .agents/launchd/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist
- .agents/AGENTS.md

## Complexity Impact

`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` is large; moving complexity_scan out is mostly deletion in that file plus a new helper script + plist. Net delta likely negative (less code in the hot path). New plist + helper is small (<60 lines each).

## Verification

```
# Cycle duration trend after Track 1:
awk -F'\t' '/preflight_ownership_reconcile|complexity_scan|prefetch_state/ {print $1, $2, $3}' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -50

# Skip-event count after Track 2:
rg -c "Pulse already running" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log

# Force-reclaim count:
rg -c "FORCE-RECLAIMED" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log
```

title: t2902: Stop recurring GraphQL budget exhaustion despite REST fallback (t2574, t2689)
body:
## What

Stop the recurring GraphQL budget exhaustion. The GraphQL pool resets to 5000/hour and is being driven to 0 between resets, tripping the pulse circuit breaker (5% threshold) and pausing all dispatch. Observed 11 fires in the last 24h, 47 lifetime. Each fire pauses the entire dispatch path for whatever fraction of the hour remains until reset.

## Why

Right now (snapshot during this session): `gh api rate_limit` returns `{graphql: 0/5000, core: 4256/5000, search: 30/30}`. So:

- Core REST has 4256 of 5000 left — REST-routed ops are healthy.
- Search has 30/30 fresh — `gh search` ops ARE expensive in points (30 budget, 30 in use is unrelated to the GraphQL pool but is a separate scarce resource).
- GraphQL is fully drained.

The framework already has REST fallback for write paths (t2574 — `gh_create_issue`, `gh_create_pr`, etc.) and read paths (t2689 — issue list, PR view). With both routed, GraphQL should NOT be drained. Yet it is. So at least one heavy GraphQL consumer is not using either fallback.

Suspect call sites (need verification):

1. **`gh search issues|prs`** (`pulse-batch-prefetch`, `auto-decomposer-helper.sh`, `pulse-merge.sh`) — `gh search` uses GraphQL Search API and is documented to cost 30+ points per query against the GraphQL pool, not Search's 30/min token bucket. `~/.aidevops/logs/contribution-watch.log` shows this is the failing operation: "[pulse-batch-prefetch] gh search issues failed for owner=marcusquinn: GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded".
2. **`gh pr view --json checks`** — uses GraphQL when checks include status checks + check-runs aggregation.
3. **`preflight_ownership_reconcile` 124 errors** — strong correlation with GraphQL exhaustion. Stage may be re-trying GraphQL queries that already failed earlier in the cycle.

## How

Three steps:

### Step 1: instrument

Add to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (or wherever the auto-router lives) a counter that increments per call site, partitioned by `path` (REST vs GraphQL). Dump to `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json` once per pulse cycle. After 1 cycle of data, we know exactly who the heavy consumer is. Without this we are guessing.

### Step 2: route or cache the offender

Once instrumentation identifies the heavy consumer:

- If it's `gh search`: replace with a per-repo `gh issue list --search "<query>"` REST-backed loop where possible. Cost: more REST calls (cheaper), more wall time. Benefit: no GraphQL pressure.
- If it's `gh pr view --json checks`: split into two calls (`gh pr view --json basic` REST + `gh api repos/.../check-runs/...` REST) and reassemble.
- For repeated reads of slowly-changing data: add a 5-min disk cache keyed by `(owner, repo, op, args_hash)`. Existing pattern: `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt` proves the cache idiom is in use.

### Step 3: lower the floor (operational mitigation, not the fix)

The breaker threshold is 5% (250/5000). Effective when budget is healthy; useless when consumption rate exceeds regeneration. Consider raising the soft fallback threshold (`AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD`, default 1000) to 1500 — earlier REST fallback gives more headroom. This is a one-line config change pending the real fix from steps 1-2.

Reference pattern: `shared-gh-wrappers.sh::_gh_wrapper_auto_route` already inspects rate limits before each write call and routes accordingly. Same logic should apply to read calls and to `gh search` substitution.

## Acceptance

- After fix: `gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining'` stays above 1000 for 24h continuous observation.
- `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` counter increments at most 1x per 24h (current: 11/24h, 47 lifetime).
- `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json` exists and shows GraphQL routes only for ops with no REST equivalent (e.g., addSubIssue, GraphQL-only mutations).

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-helper.sh
- .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf

## Complexity Impact

`shared-gh-wrappers.sh` already has the routing infrastructure (t2574, t2689). Step 1 (instrumentation) is ~30 lines. Step 2 (per-offender routing) is bounded by the number of offenders found — likely 2-3. Step 3 (threshold) is one line. No function should grow past 100 lines.

## Verification

```
# Run a pulse cycle and inspect the new instrumentation:
cat ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json | jq 'to_entries | sort_by(-.value.graphql_calls)'

# 24h GraphQL floor:
while true; do gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining'; sleep 600; done | tee /tmp/gql-floor.log
# Floor should never drop below 1000.

# Circuit fire rate:
jq '.counters.pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken | map(select(. > (now - 86400))) | length' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json
```

title: t2897: pulse per-runner zero-attempt failure circuit breaker
body:
## Task

Per-runner zero-attempt failure circuit breaker that detects stale or broken local installs and triggers a self-healing `aidevops update` after 10 consecutive zero-attempt worker dispatches in a 6h window.

See full brief at `todo/tasks/t2897-brief.md` for the complete state machine, signal definitions, threshold rationale, and integration points.

## Why

One runner running stale or broken code wastes worker dispatches across the entire fleet (incidents: t2076, t2190, t2788). The existing `DISPATCH_CLAIM_MIN_VERSION` filter only protects the OTHER runner; the stale runner keeps burning workers until a human notices. This task makes the runner detect its own degradation and either heal (via the existing `aidevops update` mechanism) or stop wasting dispatches.

## How

NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-runner-health-helper.sh` — 5 subcommands (`record-outcome`, `is-paused`, `pause`, `resume`, `status`). State at `~/.aidevops/cache/runner-health.json`.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — pre-dispatch gate alongside the t2770 no_work breaker; counter `pulse_dispatch_runner_health_breaker_tripped`.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh` — wire `record-outcome no_worker_process` into `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` flow.

NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-runner-health-helper.sh` (15 tests) and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-runner-health.sh` (6 integration tests).

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh` for state-file conventions; `is_no_work_rate_acceptable` (pulse-wrapper.sh:937) for the breaker pattern.

title: t2903: Move complexity_scan from pulse dispatch preflight to standalone launchd plist
body:
## What

Extract `complexity_scan` from the pulse dispatch preflight phase into a dedicated launchd plist (`sh.aidevops.complexity-scan`) running on its own hourly schedule. Remove the `run_stage_with_timeout "complexity_scan"` call from `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1346-1349`.

## Why

`complexity_scan` blocks dispatch for 470s+ (~7.8 min) per pulse cycle. `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log` for 2026-04-26 14:31:20Z shows `complexity_scan	471	0	28101` — 26% of the 1800s pulse stale ceiling consumed by a single stage. The comment at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1346` already calls out the trade-off: "complexity_scan (200-340s) would starve downstream scanners". Observed cost has overshot the planning budget by 40%.

The architectural fix is the same pattern as `sh.aidevops.contribution-watch` and `sh.aidevops.worker-watchdog`: an independent launchd schedule with its own lock so it cannot block dispatch. t2828 (#20866) and t2862 (#20919) apply the same pattern to `pulse-merge`. This issue extends it to `complexity_scan`.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1346-1349` — remove the `run_stage_with_timeout "complexity_scan"` block; leave a one-line breadcrumb comment pointing at the new plist.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh` — standalone wrapper that runs `run_weekly_complexity_scan` with its own file-based lock at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/locks/complexity-scan.lock`. Exit cleanly if a previous instance is still running. Write last-run timestamp to `~/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-last-run`. Model on `worker-watchdog-cmd.sh` and `contribution-watch-helper.sh`.
- NEW: launchd plist content generated by `setup-modules/schedulers.sh`. Label `sh.aidevops.complexity-scan`, `StartInterval=3600` (hourly), `RunAtLoad=true`. Pattern: copy from `_install_contribution_watch_launchd` in `setup-modules/schedulers.sh`.
- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` — add `setup_complexity_scan` and `_install_complexity_scan_launchd` functions (model on `setup_contribution_watch`).
- EDIT: `setup.sh:1198, 1226` — add `setup_complexity_scan` to both interactive and non-interactive install lists. Mirror `setup_contribution_watch` placement.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Scheduled Tasks (launchd/cron)" section — document the new schedule.

### Reference Pattern

- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1257` — `<key>StartInterval</key>` heredoc pattern for contribution-watch plist; copy verbatim and adapt label/binary/interval.
- `worker-watchdog-cmd.sh:504` — alternative launchd plist heredoc pattern for reference.
- `.agents/scripts/contribution-watch-helper.sh` — closest functional analogue: independent schedule, own log file, file-based lock, written for non-overlapping operation.

### Lock Discipline

Independent lock; never share with the pulse lock. Skip cleanly (exit 0) if a previous instance is still running — do NOT stack. The existing `run_weekly_complexity_scan` function should be callable as-is; the helper is mostly a lock+log wrapper.

## Acceptance

- After deploy: `complexity_scan` no longer appears in fresh entries of `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log`.
- After deploy: `~/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-last-run` mtime is within the last hour.
- Average pulse cycle duration (rolling 24h) drops by ~470s.
- `setup.sh --non-interactive` is idempotent — re-running does not reload the plist when content unchanged (uses existing `_launchd_install_if_changed` pattern).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh setup-modules/schedulers.sh` reports zero violations.

## Verification

```bash
# After deploy:
launchctl print "gui/$(id -u)/sh.aidevops.complexity-scan" | grep "run interval"
# Expected: run interval = 3600 seconds

ls -la ~/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-last-run
# Expected: file exists, mtime within last hour

awk '$2 == "complexity_scan"' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -5
# Expected: no entries newer than the deploy timestamp

shellcheck .agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh setup-modules/schedulers.sh
# Expected: zero violations
```

## Complexity Impact

`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` shrinks (delete 4-line block, add 1-line comment). New helper `complexity-scan-helper.sh` ~60-80 lines — well under the 100-line `function-complexity` gate. `_install_complexity_scan_launchd` mirrors existing install helpers (~50 lines). Net delta: dispatch path gets simpler.

title: t2904: Cache assignment graph + classify errors in preflight_ownership_reconcile
body:
## What

Investigate why `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` (in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, around line 1251) takes 602s with 124 errors per pulse cycle. Reduce both: (a) cache the assignment graph between cycles with a 5-minute TTL so unchanged-state cycles short-circuit; (b) classify errors so rate-limit retries trip the circuit breaker once instead of accumulating to 124 per cycle.

## Why

`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log` for 2026-04-26 14:41:46Z: `preflight_ownership_reconcile	602	124	28101` — 602s wall-clock, 124 errors on a single cycle. This is the single largest stage cost after `complexity_scan` (471s) and combined they consume 60% of the 1800s pulse stale ceiling.

124 errors is too high to be repo-coverage. Hypotheses (need confirmation in the diagnostic step below):
1. Rate-limit retries: each 401/403/secondary-rate hits the catch-all path and counts as one error.
2. Permission errors on archived/private repos that get re-queried each cycle.
3. The reconciler re-reads the same data across multiple sub-stages.

A 5-min TTL cache on the assignment graph would cover the case where consecutive pulse cycles see identical state. With t2901 Track 2 raising `StartInterval` to 600s, two consecutive cycles often see no assignment changes — perfect for cache hits.

## How

### Diagnostic First (before implementation)

Add a short-lived debug trace to `_preflight_ownership_reconcile`. Write each error-path event to `~/.aidevops/logs/ownership-reconcile-debug.log` with: timestamp, repo slug, API call (or sub-function), HTTP/exit status, error text. Run for 2-3 pulse cycles. Aggregate:

```bash
awk '{print $4}' ~/.aidevops/logs/ownership-reconcile-debug.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

The top error class drives the design choices below. Remove the trace before merging.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — locate `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` (search for the function definition; line 1251 was the t2901 reference). Add cache check at function entry. Cache key: sha256 of `(repo slug + last status:* label timestamp)` per repo. Cache file: `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/cache/ownership-graph-<sha>.json`, TTL 300s (5 min).
- EDIT: same file — error classification: when an API call fails, check exit code. `gh` exit 4 = rate-limit (set a flag, abort the stage early, let pulse circuit breaker handle). Other non-zero = generic error (log once per repo at WARN level, don't increment the per-call error counter on each retry within a single repo).
- VERIFY (read-only): `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` — confirm what data the ownership reconciler depends on. If these helpers cache their own results inside one cycle, the reconciler may be able to consume that cache instead of re-calling `gh`.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ownership-reconcile-cache.sh` — exercise cache-hit and cache-miss paths with controlled state files. Add to the test runner.

### Reference Pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:752` — `check_repo_pulse_interval` uses a state file with mtime-based TTL. Same shape: read state file, compare mtime to TTL, decide skip vs. re-run.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` — batches multiple `gh` calls and caches results for the cycle. Use this for the cache-miss path: fetch the assignment graph in one batched call, write to cache, return.
- `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — search for `RATE_LIMIT` / exit-code-4 handling for the error-classification pattern: detect once, set a flag, return early.

## Acceptance

- After deploy: `preflight_ownership_reconcile` cost drops below 60s on cycles where no repo has status-label changes (cache-hit path).
- After deploy: error count drops below 10 per cycle (down from 124).
- Cache invalidation is correct: a real assignment change is reflected within one TTL window (manual test: change a status label on a repo, verify reconciler picks it up within 5 min).
- New test passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-ownership-reconcile-cache.sh`.

## Verification

```bash
# Cycle duration trend (after deploy):
awk -F'\t' '$2 == "preflight_ownership_reconcile" {print $1, $3, $4}' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -10
# Expected: most cycles show <60s, error count <10.

# Cache file present after first cycle:
ls -la ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/cache/ownership-graph-*.json
# Expected: 1+ files, mtime recent.

# Test runs:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-ownership-reconcile-cache.sh
# Expected: PASS.

# Lint:
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
# Expected: zero violations.
```

## Complexity Impact

`_preflight_ownership_reconcile` is currently ~80-120 lines (verify by reading). Adding cache-check at entry: ~10 lines. Error classification: ~15 lines. Net delta: +25 lines. If the function would exceed the 100-line `function-complexity` gate post-edit, extract the cache-check into a sibling helper before merging (model on the orchestrator + sub-function pattern in `reference/large-file-split.md`).

title: t2905: Audit prefetch_state cost vs downstream savings (184s/cycle)
body:
## What

Audit `prefetch_state` stage in the pulse cycle (currently 184s per cycle per `pulse-stage-timings.log`). Verify that the work it does saves more than 184s downstream. If not, remove it or downscope it. If yes, document the value-vs-cost trade-off so future audits can find the rationale.

## Why

`pulse-stage-timings.log` shows `prefetch_state` consistently around 184s. That's 3.1 minutes of every pulse cycle. The stage exists to batch-fetch state from `gh` (issues, PRs, labels) so downstream stages don't have to re-fetch. The hypothesis when it was added: cost-amortisation across many downstream stages > one-time fetch cost.

We don't have evidence that this hypothesis still holds. Three classes of work that could invalidate it:

1. **Read-side REST fallback (t2689)**: many downstream `gh` calls now route via REST (the separate 5000/hr pool) when GraphQL is constrained. If REST calls are no longer rate-limited, the prefetch may be saving zero downstream cost.
2. **Cache hits (proposed t2901 Track 1b)**: if the ownership reconciler starts caching its own result, it doesn't need prefetch_state at all.
3. **Dispatch-dedup REST fallback (#20991, t2689)**: dispatch-dedup `is-assigned` already hits REST under load. Same concern.

## How

### Files Scope

- READ-ONLY first: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` — understand what data prefetch_state is actually fetching. Search for the `prefetch_state` stage entry point in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (look for `run_stage_with_timeout "prefetch_state"`).
- READ-ONLY: every downstream stage that consumes prefetched data — `_preflight_capacity_and_labels`, `_preflight_ownership_reconcile`, `_preflight_cleanup_and_ledger`, dispatch loop. Identify by searching for `read_prefetched_state` / `PULSE_STATE_DIR` / equivalent variable.

### Audit (no code changes yet)

Add temporary timing instrumentation:
1. Wrap each downstream consumer call with `time` and log the duration to `~/.aidevops/logs/prefetch-consumer-timings.log`.
2. Run for 5-10 pulse cycles.
3. Sum the consumer time per cycle. Compare to 184s prefetch cost.

If `prefetch_total_consumer_time < 184s` over the sample window: prefetch_state is a net cost — remove it (each downstream consumer makes its own call, possibly with REST fallback).

If `prefetch_total_consumer_time > 184s × 3` (3x rule of thumb for amortised value): prefetch_state is genuinely saving time — leave it, document the savings in the function header comment.

If `184s < prefetch_total < 184s × 3`: marginal value. Lean toward removal because the cost is observable and the savings are small.

### Files Scope (depending on audit outcome)

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — if removing: drop the `run_stage_with_timeout "prefetch_state"` call. If keeping: add a comment block explaining the cost-vs-value rationale measured during this audit.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` — if removing: keep the helper functions but remove the orchestrator. If keeping: no changes.
- EDIT: any downstream consumer that depends on prefetched state — if removing prefetch, switch them to direct calls (likely already supported via cache miss path).

### Reference Pattern

- `pulse-stage-timings.log` is the canonical source for cost measurement.
- `reference/observability.md` describes the OTEL span enrichment pattern; if removing prefetch_state, the OTEL span for the stage will disappear from the logs — this is fine but should be noted in the PR body.

## Acceptance

- One of the following two outcomes is shipped:
  - **Outcome A (remove)**: `prefetch_state` no longer appears in `pulse-stage-timings.log`. Total cycle duration drops by ≥184s. Downstream stages still pass their tests.
  - **Outcome B (keep + document)**: `prefetch_state` remains; `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` orchestrator function header includes a comment block measuring the savings ratio (e.g. "Prefetch costs 184s, saves 600s of downstream calls per cycle = 3.3x value").
- The audit log (`~/.aidevops/logs/prefetch-consumer-timings.log` analysis) is summarised in the PR body so the rationale survives.

## Verification

```bash
# After deploy (Outcome A):
awk '$2 == "prefetch_state"' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -5
# Expected: no fresh entries.

awk '/^[0-9]/ {if (max < $1) max = $1; if (min == 0 || min > $1) min = $1} END {print min, max}' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -5
# Expected: total cycle duration dropped by ~184s.

# After deploy (Outcome B):
grep -A 5 "prefetch_state cost" .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh
# Expected: header comment with measured savings ratio.
```

## Complexity Impact

Outcome A: net deletion (-15 to -30 lines). Outcome B: comment block only (+10-20 lines, no logic change). Either way, well under any complexity gate.

title: t2906: setup.sh leaves 0-byte pulse plist when _generate_pulse_plist_content is interrupted
body:
## What

`setup.sh --non-interactive` can leave the supervisor pulse launchd plist as a 0-byte file (and unload the previous working plist) when the plist-generation step hangs or is interrupted. The framework is then unable to schedule the pulse — `launchctl bootstrap` fails on the empty file with `Bug: xpc_pipe_routine() returned [22: Invalid argument]`, and a user that hits this has no working pulse until they manually reconstruct the plist or rerun setup.

## Why

Hit this directly during the t2901 (#21042) session:

1. Bumped `supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds` from 180 → 600 in settings.json.
2. Ran `setup.sh --non-interactive` to regenerate the plist.
3. After 180s the wrapped command timed out.
4. Found `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` and `*.bak.<timestamp>` both at 0 bytes.
5. The previous plist had already been unloaded by the cleanup step.
6. Had to reconstruct the plist by hand from an earlier capture and `launchctl bootout` + `bootstrap` to recover.

The combination of "unload old before write new" + "non-atomic write" + "no recovery on failure" means a single hang during regeneration takes the pulse offline.

## How

Two cooperating defects in two functions; both need fixing so that the failure is robust no matter which entry point the pulse install goes through.

### Defect A — `_install_pulse_launchd` doesn't use the canonical safe helper

`setup-modules/schedulers.sh:679-713`:

```bash
_install_pulse_launchd() {
    ...
    _cleanup_old_pulse_plists "$pulse_label" "$pulse_plist"          # line 686 — unloads OLD plist
    _generate_pulse_plist_content "$pulse_label" "$wrapper_script" "$opencode_bin" >"$pulse_plist"   # line 689 — non-atomic stdout redirect
    ...
}
```

Every other launchd-installed scheduler in this file (stats wrapper, session-miner, contribution-watch, pr-review, etc.) uses the pattern:

1. Capture full plist content to a shell variable via heredoc command-substitution.
2. Call `_launchd_install_if_changed "$label" "$plist_path" "$content"`.

Reference patterns (already correct, copy from any of these):

- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1085-1124` — stats wrapper
- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1180-1233` — session-miner
- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1268-1326` — guard

Migrate `_install_pulse_launchd` to the same shape:

```bash
_install_pulse_launchd() {
    local pulse_label="$1"
    local wrapper_script="$2"
    local opencode_bin="$3"
    local _pulse_installed="$4"
    local pulse_plist="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${pulse_label}.plist"

    local pulse_plist_content
    pulse_plist_content=$(_generate_pulse_plist_content "$pulse_label" "$wrapper_script" "$opencode_bin")

    # Defensive: if generation produced empty content, refuse to touch the existing plist.
    if [[ -z "$pulse_plist_content" ]]; then
        print_warning "Pulse plist generation produced empty content — leaving existing plist untouched"
        return 1
    fi

    if _launchd_install_if_changed "$pulse_label" "$pulse_plist" "$pulse_plist_content"; then
        # ... existing print_info + _log_plist_env_overrides ...
    else
        print_warning "Failed to load supervisor pulse LaunchAgent"
    fi
    return 0
}
```

This kills the unconditional cleanup-before-write — `_launchd_install_if_changed` only unloads when content has changed and a replacement is ready in memory.

### Defect B — `_launchd_install_if_changed` write is non-atomic

`setup.sh:222-248`:

```bash
# Write new plist and load
printf '%s\n' "$new_content" >"$plist_path"   # line 245 — truncates atomically, write is not
launchctl load "$plist_path" 2>/dev/null || return 1
```

If `printf` is killed mid-write (signal, OOM, terminal closure), the destination is partial. Lower-impact than Defect A because the content is already captured in `$new_content` and content-equality has been checked first, but still violates the atomicity invariant. Replace with tmp + rename:

```bash
# Atomic write: build at sibling path, fsync, then rename.
local tmp_plist="${plist_path}.tmp.$$"
if ! printf '%s\n' "$new_content" >"$tmp_plist"; then
    rm -f "$tmp_plist"
    return 1
fi
# Validate non-empty before installing (defensive — should be guaranteed by content check above)
if [[ ! -s "$tmp_plist" ]]; then
    rm -f "$tmp_plist"
    return 1
fi
mv -f "$tmp_plist" "$plist_path"
launchctl load "$plist_path" 2>/dev/null || return 1
return 0
```

### Files Scope

- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` — rewrite `_install_pulse_launchd` (lines 679-713) to use capture + `_launchd_install_if_changed`
- `setup.sh` — atomic write in `_launchd_install_if_changed` (lines 222-248)

### Reference Pattern

- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1085-1124` (stats wrapper) is the canonical "generate content then install" pattern. Match its structure.
- For atomic write: `printf > .tmp && mv -f .tmp dest` is the standard idiom; no need for `mktemp` since the dest dir is `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` (user-owned, no race partner).

## Acceptance

- Both functions fixed per the patterns above.
- `shellcheck setup.sh setup-modules/schedulers.sh` passes.
- Manual repro: kill `_generate_pulse_plist_content` mid-execution (e.g. wrap in `timeout 0.001`) and verify the existing plist is untouched, the temp file is cleaned, and the function returns non-zero.
- Existing tests still pass: `setup.sh --non-interactive` produces a working plist on a clean run.
- Regression test added if practical (a unit test that mocks `_generate_pulse_plist_content` to fail and asserts the existing plist is preserved).

## Verification

```bash
# 1. Lint clean
shellcheck setup.sh setup-modules/schedulers.sh

# 2. Atomic write — corrupt the temp file, confirm dest is untouched
cp ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist /tmp/baseline.plist
echo > /tmp/empty-content      # simulate generation that produced empty content
# Source schedulers.sh in a test shell, call _install_pulse_launchd with mocked content
# Expect: existing plist is preserved, function returns non-zero
diff -q /tmp/baseline.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist
# Expected: files are identical (no changes)

# 3. Happy path
./setup.sh --non-interactive
plutil ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist
# Expected: "OK" — valid plist content
```

## Related

- t2901 (#21042) — pulse cycle decomposition session that surfaced this
- Sibling observation (NOT in scope here, file separately if pursuing): `setup.sh --non-interactive` itself hung for the full 180s timeout when invoked during the t2901 session. Root cause unclear — could be an aidevops-update-check, a homebrew probe, or a network call. Worth investigating but distinct from the atomic-write defect — fixing this issue does NOT require resolving the hang, only making the failure mode safe.
