## Brief addendum — repo filter for sync iterator

The `mirror sync-workflows` instruction in the original brief is the wrong default for badges. `sync-workflows` runs against every `local_only != true` repo, but badges should only land on repos under user-owned orgs — opening a PR against `WordPress/mcp-adapter` or `swissspidy/wp-performance-action` would be maintainer-overreach.

### Required filter for `aidevops badges sync` and `aidevops badges check`

Three clauses, applied in order:

1. `.local_only != true` (skip local-only — no remote to host SVG)
2. `.slug | split("/")[0]` is in the **owned-orgs allowlist**
3. `.contributed != true` (skip managed forks, even when in an owned org)

### Owned-orgs allowlist (read at runtime; do NOT bake repo names into the helper)

```text
marcusquinn
awardsapp
essentials-com
wpallstars
```

Store as a config constant in the helper (`OWNED_ORGS=("marcusquinn" "awardsapp" "essentials-com" "wpallstars")`). Future expansion: read from `~/.config/aidevops/badge-orgs.conf` if present, fall back to the constant. Don't infer from `repos.json` — flags like `contributed` aren't always set correctly on every entry.

### Equivalent jq for runtime evaluation

```bash
jq -r '
  .initialized_repos
  | map(select(
      .local_only != true
      and (.slug | split("/")[0] | IN("marcusquinn","awardsapp","essentials-com","wpallstars"))
      and .contributed != true
    ))
  | .[] | .slug
' ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json
```

### Target set (computed at runtime — DO NOT precompile)

Approximately 18 repos, mix of public and private. The worker MUST compute this list at runtime from the user's local `repos.json` and MUST NOT log/comment the full slug list to public issues — many entries are private and naming them in a public issue comment is a privacy leak.

For PR-creation logging, use generic phrasing: "opening N PRs against owned-org repos". For per-repo dispatch, log only the slug being worked on at that moment, not the full enumerated set. The PR itself surfaces the slug in its URL anyway, but pre-emptive enumeration in audit comments is the leak path.

### `aidevops badges check` — different scope

The check (drift detection) command should classify ALL non-local-only repos for visibility, not just owned ones. Worker-overreach concern doesn't apply to read-only ops:

- Owned + drifted → suggested action: `aidevops badges sync --repo X --apply`
- Not-owned (`contributed: true` or org not in allowlist) → classification: `EXTERNAL` — informational only, no sync action
- Local-only → `LOCAL-ONLY` — informational

Apply the filter only at sync/install (write) operations, not at check (read) operations.

The same privacy rule applies to `check`: when emitting summary output to a public log/comment, count private repos but do not name them. Per-repo verbose output is fine for local terminal use (`--verbose` flag) but should be guarded against being pasted into public issues.

### Private-repo handling

Self-hosted LOC SVG works on private repos (committed to repo, viewable to authenticated users). Shields.io GitHub-stat endpoints (release, license, stars, last-commit) DO NOT render on private repos because shields.io can't authenticate. The conditional template should detect via `gh repo view --json visibility` and either:

- Skip shields.io-dependent badges on private repos (recommended), OR
- Include them and accept they'll show "no data" externally

Add a `{{?PUBLIC}}` template guard around shields.io badges. Local LOC + Codacy (which has its own auth) can stay outside the guard.

### Acceptance addition

- [ ] Filter applied at sync/install only; check enumerates all repos with `EXTERNAL`/`LOCAL-ONLY` classifications
- [ ] Owned-orgs allowlist either constant or config-file-driven
- [ ] Private-repo guard around shields.io-dependent badges in `badges.md.tmpl`
- [ ] Logging/comment-emitting code paths NEVER enumerate the full slug list when writing to public surfaces — count-only summaries only

title: t2922: fix(pulse-merge): bypass phantom pending checks for owner+origin:worker auto-merge
body:
## What

Pulse-merge auto-merge path checks `mergeStateStatus == CLEAN` and treats `BLOCKED`/`UNSTABLE` as non-mergeable. Many PRs end up `BLOCKED` because non-required check contexts (`CodeRabbit`, `qlty check`, `linked-issue-check`, `maintainer-gate`, `url-allowlist`) report `status: null` indefinitely. These are NOT in `branch_protection.required_status_checks` but still cause `mergeStateStatus = BLOCKED`.

## Why

This blocks the t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge path (origin:worker PRs from owner/member-filed issues). 3+ PRs admin-merged manually in last hour because phantom pending checks blocked them despite all required checks passing. Required: ["review-bot-gate", "Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate", "Complexity Analysis"]. Pulse should distinguish required-pending vs non-required-pending and merge when only the latter remains.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- Locate the `mergeStateStatus` evaluation (in `_check_pr_mergeable` / `_attempt_auto_merge`)
- Before failing on `BLOCKED`/`UNSTABLE`, fetch required check contexts: `gh api repos/$REPO/branches/$DEFAULT/protection/required_status_checks --jq '.contexts[]'`
- Cross-reference `statusCheckRollup` — if all FAILURE/PENDING checks are NOT in required list, treat as mergeable for auto-merge path
- Apply ONLY for owner+origin:worker PRs (preserves contributor security gate)
- Add helper: `_check_required_checks_passing <slug> <pr_num>` returning 0 if all required-by-protection checks are SUCCESS

Reference pattern: existing `_attempt_auto_merge` and `_check_review_state` follow conditional-gate style.

## Verification

```bash

bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
PULSE_VERBOSE=1 .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh check 21075
```

- [ ] Auto-merge path bypasses non-required FAILURE/PENDING checks for owner+origin:worker PRs only
- [ ] Test added: all-required-success / one-required-failure / only-non-required-pending
- [ ] `shellcheck` zero violations

title: t2923: feat(worker): push WIP commits to origin on worker exit/kill — prevent abandoned work
body:
## What

Workers spawned by pulse can die mid-implementation (timeout, OOM, killed) leaving uncommitted/unpushed work in their worktree. Currently 5 aidevops worktrees have `ahead=1..2` with WIP commits that never reached origin. The next dispatch cycle creates a NEW worktree with a fresh worker that re-does the work — wasting tokens.

## Why

Observed during 24-worker concurrency push (Apr 26): 5/9 active worker worktrees had unpushed commits. Worker for t2868 had 2 commits (`3548ccbf7 t2868: inbox triage routine` + `a5db80346 t2868: add triage subcommand`) that died before pushing. Re-dispatch will rewrite the same code from scratch.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` (or `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` if hooks exist there)
- Add EXIT trap: before exit, if `git -C $WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH log main..HEAD` has commits, run:
  - `git push -u origin $branch_name 2>/dev/null || true` (best-effort, fail-open)
  - Log `[lifecycle] worker_exit_pushed_wip branch=$branch ahead=N` to stderr
- Skip if `WORKER_NO_EXIT_PUSH=1` (escape hatch)
- The 300s activity-watchdog kill path (`worker-activity-watchdog.sh`) should also push before SIGKILL

Reference pattern: similar EXIT-trap pattern in `pulse-cleanup.sh::_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` (audit trail on early exit).

## Verification

```bash

shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh

# Manual: kill a running worker via SIGTERM, verify branch has remote
gh api "repos/$slug/branches/$branch" --jq '.name'
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] EXIT trap pushes any local-only commits to origin before worker exits
- [ ] Watchdog kill path also pushes WIP before SIGKILL
- [ ] `WORKER_NO_EXIT_PUSH=1` escape hatch documented
- [ ] No regression on workers that complete normally (push happens once, not twice)
- [ ] Test: kill worker mid-implementation, verify branch on remote with WIP commit

title: t2924: perf(pulse): filter non-dispatchable labels at candidate-build time, not dispatch time
body:
## What

Pulse `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` enumerates 200+ candidates per cycle then iterates them. Each iteration calls `dispatch_with_dedup` which checks dedup layers and returns `rc=1` for non-dispatchable management labels (`parent-task`, `origin:interactive` with assignee, `no-auto-dispatch`). These candidates are RE-EVALUATED every pulse cycle, wasting GraphQL calls and CPU.

## Why

Observed in current pulse run: candidates `#21056` (parent-task), `#20966`, `#20929`, `#20892` (all parent-task) re-checked every iteration. The dispatch loop processes them, fails dedup, skips. Next cycle: same thing. With 201 candidates and ~10s pulse cycle interval, this is hundreds of wasted GraphQL calls per hour.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json`
- Filter OUT issues with non-dispatchable management labels at candidate-build time, not dispatch time
- Specifically exclude (use `--label-not` filter or post-fetch jq filter):
  - `parent-task`
  - `no-auto-dispatch`
  - `needs-maintainer-review`
  - `status:done`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`, `status:claimed`
- Keep dispatch-time check as defense-in-depth (race conditions)

Reference pattern: existing label exclusion in `gh issue list --label-not` calls; check usage in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`.

## Verification

```bash
# Before fix: count non-dispatchable in candidate set
.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels | any(. == "parent-task" or . == "no-auto-dispatch"))] | length'

# After: should be 0
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Candidates with `parent-task`/`no-auto-dispatch`/active-status labels filtered before dispatch loop
- [ ] Dispatch-time `Dispatch blocked: non-dispatchable management label present` log line frequency drops to near-zero
- [ ] `pulse_dispatch_iter_count` per cycle measurably reduced
- [ ] No new dispatch race regressions

title: t2925: feat(security): auto-detect and close bounty-hunter spam PRs from external authors
body:
## What

Auto-detect and close PRs from "automated bounty hunter" spam authors. Pattern observed across multiple repos: PRs with body matching `## 💰 Paid Bounty Contribution`, `Reward: $1`, `Source: GitHub-Paid`, `🤖 Generated via automated bounty hunter`, or similar templated headers. Author posts identical bodies to 20+ unrelated repos (Expensify, NVIDIA-NeMo, anthropics/claude-code, up-for-grabs, etc.).

## Why

These PRs block dispatch on the issue they "address" because the dedup system sees an open PR. Two such PRs (#21077 and #21094 from carycooper777) blocked dispatch on issues #21061 and #20918 today until I manually closed them. Auto-detection saves manual triage.

## How

NEW: `.agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh`

title: t2926: setup.sh: auto-install util-linux on macOS so setsid is available for worker PGID isolation
body:
## What

Workers dispatched by pulse must run in their own process group (PGID) to survive pulse-wrapper restarts. The dispatch path uses `setsid nohup` for this, but **setsid is not part of macOS** — it ships only via `util-linux` from Homebrew. On systems missing `util-linux`, pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh logs `Warning: setsid not found — worker will share pulse's PGID` and falls back to `nohup` only. The result: every pulse cycle's exit sends SIGHUP to its PGID, killing all workers in the same group before they finish.

## Why

This was the **single biggest cause of worker death** observed during 24-worker concurrency testing on Apr 26: 5 of 9 active worker worktrees had unpushed WIP commits, and the pulse log showed 398 cumulative `setsid not found` warnings. Every worker that didn't finish before the next pulse cycle was killed mid-implementation, causing rework on the next dispatch (token waste, throughput cap of ~4 PRs/hr instead of target 24/hr).

After installing `util-linux` via brew (`brew install util-linux && ln -s /opt/homebrew/opt/util-linux/bin/setsid /opt/homebrew/bin/setsid`) and restarting pulse, the warning count dropped to 0 — confirming the fix works. But every other macOS user installing aidevops will hit the same issue silently.

## How

EDIT: `setup.sh::cmd_setup_install_dependencies` (or equivalent dependency-check stage)

Add a setsid availability check + auto-install:

```bash
if ! command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
        log_info "Installing util-linux for setsid (worker PGID isolation)"
        brew install util-linux 2>&1 | tail -3
        # util-linux ships keg-only on macOS; symlink setsid into PATH
        if [[ -x /opt/homebrew/opt/util-linux/bin/setsid && ! -e /opt/homebrew/bin/setsid ]]; then
            ln -s /opt/homebrew/opt/util-linux/bin/setsid /opt/homebrew/bin/setsid
        elif [[ -x /usr/local/opt/util-linux/bin/setsid && ! -e /usr/local/bin/setsid ]]; then
            ln -s /usr/local/opt/util-linux/bin/setsid /usr/local/bin/setsid
        fi
    else
        log_warn "setsid not found — install util-linux package via your distro's package manager"
    fi
fi
```

ALSO: `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` — the existing fallback path (`nohup` without setsid) should be marked as DEGRADED with stronger log severity, not just `Warning:`. Workers in this state will be killed by every pulse exit.

ALSO: `aidevops update` should re-check on every run (not just first install) — homebrew can drift.

## Verification

```bash
which setsid && setsid --version 2>&1 | head -1
# After fresh install: setsid should be in PATH automatically
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `setup.sh` installs util-linux and symlinks setsid on macOS systems missing it
- [ ] `aidevops update` re-checks setsid availability on every run
- [ ] Pulse log line `Warning: setsid not found` upgraded to `ERROR: setsid missing — worker isolation broken; install util-linux`
- [ ] Cross-platform: Linux distros without util-linux get a clear install hint
- [ ] Test: temporarily remove setsid from PATH, run setup.sh, verify it's restored

title: t2927: fix(pulse): FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP cache leaks closed-issue defers — invalidate when issue closes
body:
## What

`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` caches active footprint computations in `_FOOTPRINT_CACHE_DATA` with a 120s TTL. When an issue closes mid-window (PR merges, status:done applied, manual close), the cache still considers it "active" and emits `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP defer #NEW for #CLOSED` defers — blocking dispatch on legitimate work for up to 120s.

## Why

Observed in current pulse log (Apr 26 22:00-22:09): 12+ `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP defer #X for #Y` lines where the referenced "blocking" issues had already closed within the prior cache window. With the deterministic-fill-floor running every ~10s and the dedup pre-pass running on every cycle, this stale cache adds 30-120s latency to every burst-merge wave.

When 5 PRs merge in a 30s window (admin merge bypass), the candidates released for dispatch are deferred for the full 120s TTL because the cache hasn't expired. This cuts effective dispatch throughput by 30-50% during catch-up periods.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`

Add invalidation on issue state change:

1. `invalidate_footprint_cache_for_issue <issue_num>` — removes entries containing the issue from `_FOOTPRINT_CACHE_DATA`
2. Call from these existing pulse paths after any close/merge/status-change:
   - `pulse-merge.sh` after successful merge
   - `pulse-stale-recovery.sh` after status change
   - `pulse-cleanup.sh` after worktree cleanup
   - `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::release_claim` after release

Reference pattern: existing TTL invalidation in `.agents/scripts/shared-cache-helper.sh` (if exists) or implement inline.

ALSO: shorten default TTL from 120s → 30s (still catches the original race condition this was meant to handle, but limits stale-cache blast radius).

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh
# Manual: merge a PR, verify next pulse cycle does NOT defer new dispatches against the closed issue
PULSE_VERBOSE=1 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh --once 2>&1 | grep FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `invalidate_footprint_cache_for_issue` helper added with shellcheck-clean
- [ ] Cache invalidated on PR merge, issue close, status change, claim release
- [ ] TTL default reduced to 30s
- [ ] No regression on the original race condition (concurrent dispatches against same files)
- [ ] Test: close issue, immediately dispatch on its files, verify no FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP defer

title: t2929: perf(pulse): preflight_cleanup_and_ledger 60-133s — stagger and parallelize git fetches
body:
## What

`preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` stage in pulse takes 60-133 seconds per cycle (observed Apr 26). With pulse interval at 180s (default), this stage alone consumes 33-74% of cycle time, leaving little for dispatch + merge work.

The stage runs `git fetch` against every repo in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` (~14 repos), each adding 2-10s. Many repos haven't received commits between pulse cycles.

## Why

Observed in current pulse log:

```text
[stage_timing] preflight_cleanup_and_ledger=133s
[stage_timing] preflight_capacity_and_labels=variable
[stage_timing] reap_zombie_workers=2s
[stage_timing] dispatch_loop=...
```

Even on a 180s pulse interval, 133s preflight means dispatch + merge get only 47s — far short of what's needed to process 24-slot deterministic-fill candidates. Throughput observed: 4 PRs/hr (target: 24/hr).

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh::preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` (or split if it's nested in pulse-init)

1. **Stagger repo fetches across cycles** — fetch only N repos per cycle, rotating through. For 14 repos, fetch 4-5 per cycle (every 540-720s per repo, still well within freshness window for issue/PR data).
2. **Skip repos with no recent activity** — query `gh api graphql` for `pushedAt` once, fetch only if newer than last fetch.
3. **Parallel fetches with bounded concurrency** — 4-way parallel `git fetch` reduces 14×5s to 4×5s ≈ 20s.
4. **Cache fetch results in `~/.aidevops/cache/repo-fetch-state.json`** — `{"slug": "owner/repo", "last_fetch": ts, "head_sha": "abc"}`.

Reference pattern: `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` already implements parallel fetch for issue/PR enrichment — extend the same approach to `git fetch`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
# Measure stage timing before vs after:
grep 'preflight_cleanup_and_ledger=' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -10
# Target: average <30s
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` average <30s per cycle (was 60-133s)
- [ ] Repo fetches rotated across cycles OR parallelized with bounded concurrency
- [ ] Repos with no activity skipped within freshness window
- [ ] Cache file created at `~/.aidevops/cache/repo-fetch-state.json`
- [ ] No regression: workers still see fresh issue/PR data within 1 cycle of update
- [ ] Test: measure 10 consecutive cycles, all <30s preflight

title: feat(t2932): peer-productivity-monitor — also observe claim activity to detect broken peers
body:
## What

`peer-productivity-monitor.sh` (t2932) currently only counts merged
`origin:worker` PRs in the rolling window. A peer whose runner is BROKEN
(claims issues but never merges) appears as "no peers found" because
they never show up in merge data.

## Why

The whole point of the monitor is to detect broken peers and route
around them. The current implementation can detect RECOVERY (peer
starts merging again) but cannot detect REGRESSION (peer was healthy,
now broken).

For the monitor to be useful for the regression case, it must also
observe **claim activity** — open issues with `origin:worker` label
assigned to non-self users — and compute a CLAIM:MERGE ratio.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/peer-productivity-monitor.sh`

In `_observe_repo()` (currently calls `gh pr list --label origin:worker
--state merged`), additionally call:

```bash
gh issue list --repo "$slug" \
  --state open \
  --label origin:worker \
  --assignee '*' \
  --json number,assignees,labels,createdAt
```

For each issue assignee, increment a `peer_claim_count[$login]`.

Then in `_compute_vote()`, compute ratio:
- `merges == 0 && claims >= 2` → `ignore` (broken)
- `merges >= 1` → `honour` (healthy)
- `merges == 0 && claims < 2` → `keep` (insufficient data)

EDIT: `tests/test-peer-productivity-monitor.sh`

Add tests for the claim-but-no-merge regression case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Monitor counts both merges and claims per peer
- [ ] Computes vote based on ratio, not just merge count
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
- [ ] New tests cover claim-only and claim+merge scenarios
- [ ] No flap behavior change (still 3-cycle hysteresis)

## Verification

```bash

shellcheck .agents/scripts/peer-productivity-monitor.sh
```

title: t2936: split files exceeding 1500 lines into focused sub-modules
body:
## Why

`linters-local.sh` blocks every commit to this repo with `File size: 56 blocking violations (threshold: 40)`. The gate's threshold was set when the count was lower; current count is 56 (52 shell + 4 Python). Each commit that touches any repo file (even a one-line doc fix) trips this and forces `--no-verify` or unrelated cleanup, neither of which is acceptable as a steady state.

Beyond CI friction, files >1500 lines:

- waste tokens on every AI-assisted edit (full-file Read becomes mandatory but expensive),
- accumulate dependency cycles that are hard to extract incrementally (pulse-merge.sh documents a 2-cycle co-extraction in its own header — that pattern should be the exception, not the norm),
- discourage focused unit tests because the surface is unbounded.

## How

Per `reference/large-file-split.md`: orchestrator + sub-library pattern, identity-key preservation, known CI false-positive classes, pre-commit hook gotchas. Each split is one PR. Children inherit `tier:thinking` because:

- function-grouping decisions need design judgment (cohesion, call-graph cardinality, future extension),
- identity-key handling for hash-based caches must survive the split,
- the existing nesting-depth gate emits false positives during the split which must be justified or refactored,
- the 100-line `function-complexity` gate and the 40% advisory threshold both fire on long functions that get extracted as-is.

This is the pattern PR #17868 (security hardening) and several earlier splits already followed. Reading the reference doc end-to-end is mandatory before opening any child PR.

title: t2938: convert file-size pre-commit gate from absolute count to ratchet-based
body:
## Why

`linters-local.sh` and the corresponding CI workflow gate file-size with an absolute threshold (`56 blocking violations (threshold: 40)`). This is the canonical anti-pattern that the framework's own t2228 rule warns against:

> Any new pre-commit validator or CI gate MUST be ratchet-based: baseline the violation count at activation, block only on regressions. Absolute-count gating traps pre-existing debt every time a legacy file is touched.

Current behaviour: every commit on the repo trips the gate once the count exceeds threshold. PR #21144 (security fix) had to use `--no-verify` because the absolute gate was triggered by a commit that didn't move the metric. Until the parent decomposition (#21146) finishes — which is multi-week work — every other PR will hit the same trap.

## How

Convert the file-size check to ratchet-based, modeled on:

- `qlty-regression-helper.sh` (t2065) — net-increase gate for qlty smells, docs-only PRs auto-skip
- `qlty-new-file-gate-helper.sh` (t2068) — new-file gate complementary to t2065

Behaviour after the change:

1. Compute baseline count on `origin/<default-branch>` HEAD.
2. Compute head count on the PR branch.
3. Block ONLY if head count > baseline count.
4. New files exceeding 1500 lines are absolute violations regardless of net count (mirrors the qlty-new-file-gate pattern, otherwise the ratchet allows endless drift).
5. Override label `complexity-bump-ok` already exists (t2370) with a justification-section requirement; reuse it for the new-file path.

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` — file-size check section. Replace the absolute count comparison with the ratchet pattern.
- `EDIT: .github/workflows/code-quality.yml` — corresponding CI step uses the same logic. Verify behaviour parity.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/file-size-regression-helper.sh` (optional, if extraction makes the change cleaner — see t2065 helper as the model)
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-file-size-regression-helper.sh` — regression test covering: zero-violation baseline, baseline-equals-head (no regression), head-greater-than-baseline (block), new file >1500 lines (block regardless), docs-only PR (skip).

## Reference pattern

- `reference/shell-style-guide.md` § Gate design (t2228 rule)
- `qlty-regression-helper.sh` (full implementation reference)
- `reference/large-file-split.md` § 4.1 (existing override label semantics)

## Acceptance

- `linters-local.sh` no longer blocks PRs that don't move the file-size violation count.
- New files exceeding 1500 lines are blocked unless `complexity-bump-ok` label + justification section are present.
- CI gate matches local gate behaviour (parity test).
- Regression test passes; existing `qlty-regression-helper.sh` tests continue to pass.
- The 56 → 0 reduction tracked in #21146 progresses incrementally without each PR hitting the gate.

## Tier

`tier:standard`. Pattern is well-documented in two existing helpers; the change is mechanical translation of one to the file-size domain. The new test is small (5 cases). No novel design judgment required.

## Session origin

Filed by interactive session during PR #21144 (t2934) — the security fix that was blocked by this gate. Companion to parent task #21146 which addresses the underlying debt.

title: t2939: feat(pulse): defense-in-depth restart reliability — KeepAlive dict + watchdog plist
body:
## Problem

Pulse is mission-critical infrastructure but currently dies for up to 10 minutes after each cycle exit.

## Root cause

The launchd plist generated by `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:_generate_pulse_plist_content` has:

- `KeepAlive=false` → no auto-restart on crash/SIGKILL/OOM
- `StartInterval=600s` → 10-minute gap after each successful cycle
- No independent watchdog → single point of failure

If pulse dies between StartInterval cycles (deploy, OOM, signal), it stays dead for up to 10 min. `aidevops.sh:710-715` (t2914) calls `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh start` after every update, but that only runs when `aidevops update` is invoked — not between updates.

## Solution: 4 layers of defense-in-depth

### Layer 1: KeepAlive dict with SuccessfulExit=false

Change `KeepAlive` bool to dict form. launchd auto-restarts on crash (within seconds) but respects `StartInterval` on clean exit (preserves 600s rate-limit tuning).

### Layer 2: Independent pulse-watchdog launchd job (every 60s)

New plist `sh.aidevops.pulse-watchdog` runs every 60s. Calls `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh start` (idempotent — no-op when running). Catches launchd registration loss and any failure mode that gets past Layer 1.

### Layer 3: aidevops update verifies plist registration

After every update, check `launchctl print` for the pulse label. If not loaded, force-load. Catches the case where a previous update left the plist file but unregistered.

### Layer 4: Smart watchdog grace logic

Watchdog only revives pulse if it has been dead longer than `(StartInterval + 120s grace)`. Preserves the user's interval tuning while adding redundancy.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:666-672` — KeepAlive dict
- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` — add `_install_pulse_watchdog_launchd` function
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh` — watchdog tick wrapper with grace logic
- EDIT: `setup.sh` — call `setup_pulse_watchdog` after `setup_supervisor_pulse`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — add `verify` subcommand
- EDIT: `aidevops.sh:710-715` — call `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh verify` after start

## Acceptance criteria

1. Pulse plist contains `KeepAlive` dict with `SuccessfulExit=false` (verified via `plutil -p`).
2. `sh.aidevops.pulse-watchdog` plist installed and running every 60s.
3. After `aidevops update`, `launchctl print` shows pulse plist loaded.
4. Watchdog tick is idempotent — no-op when pulse alive within grace period.
5. shellcheck clean on all new/modified scripts.

## Verification

```bash
# Plist contains KeepAlive dict
plutil -p ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist | grep -A 2 KeepAlive
# Expected: KeepAlive => { SuccessfulExit => 0 }

# Watchdog plist registered
launchctl list | grep pulse-watchdog

# Force-kill pulse, wait 65s, confirm watchdog revived it
pkill -KILL -f pulse-wrapper && sleep 65 && pgrep -af pulse-wrapper | head -1
```

## Rationale

User signaled mission-critical reliability over rate-limit conservation. Layered defense ensures pulse always recovers within ~60s of any death mode (crash, SIGKILL, deploy, launchd dropout, OOM).

title: t2937: make maintainer-gate.yml reusable + propagate via aidevops sync-workflows
body:
## What

Make `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml` a reusable workflow (`on: workflow_call:`) and propagate it to all `pulse: true` repos via `aidevops sync-workflows`, the same pattern already shipped for `issue-sync.yml` (t2770).

## Why

The maintainer-gate is the workflow-layer surface that prevents non-collaborator PRs from passing the auto-merge cascade when the linked issue is missing or unlabelled (Check 0). It's the *first* layer of the four-layer defense-in-depth diagram in `.agents/reference/incident-gh17671-supply-chain.md`.

Today, only the framework repo carries this workflow file. Every other `pulse: true` repo relies on the downstream layers alone (`_check_pr_merge_gates` author check + the t2933 function-level guard inside `approve_collaborator_pr`). That's still safe — the t2933 guard refuses approval when the author is not a collaborator regardless of upstream layers — but it means any future code path that bypasses `approve_collaborator_pr` (a direct `gh pr merge --admin` call from a new helper, for instance) inherits zero workflow-layer protection in those repos.

The reusable-workflow architecture (t2770) was specifically designed for this case: ship the canonical workflow logic centrally, distribute a thin caller YAML to every downstream repo, drift-detect via `aidevops check-workflows`, drift-resync via `aidevops sync-workflows`. We already proved the pattern works for `issue-sync.yml`. Reusing it for `maintainer-gate.yml` is mechanical.

## How

1. **Convert** `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml` to expose a reusable variant at `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` (`on: workflow_call:`). Pattern: copy `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` for the workflow-call wrapper structure.

2. **Caller template:** add `.agents/templates/workflows/maintainer-gate-caller.yml` that downstream repos can install. ~45 lines, references `marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml@<ref>`. Pattern: copy `.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml`.

3. **Detector wiring:** extend `aidevops check-workflows` (`.agents/scripts/aidevops/cmd_check-workflows.sh`) to classify each repo's `maintainer-gate.yml` against the new caller template. Same classifications as `issue-sync.yml` (`CURRENT/CALLER`, `DRIFTED/CALLER`, `NEEDS-MIGRATION`, etc.).

4. **Resync wiring:** extend `aidevops sync-workflows` (`.agents/scripts/aidevops/cmd_sync-workflows.sh`) to install/refresh the caller template in target repos. Default `--dry-run`, opt-in `--apply`.

5. **Verify** by running `aidevops check-workflows --json` after the new wiring lands. Every `pulse: true` repo should show either `CURRENT/CALLER` (already migrated), `NEEDS-MIGRATION` (will get it on next `sync-workflows --apply`), or `LOCAL-ONLY` (no remote, skip). The exact list is enumerated dynamically from `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`; do not hard-code repo names in this issue body or in any commit message.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` exists and exposes the same gate logic as `maintainer-gate.yml` via `on: workflow_call:`
- [ ] `.agents/templates/workflows/maintainer-gate-caller.yml` exists and follows the `issue-sync-caller.yml` pattern

title: t2942: reduce STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD default from 24h to 1h to recover pulse productivity faster
body:
Stampless interactive claims currently auto-recover only after 24h via STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD in pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:709. This blocks pulse dispatch on those issues for up to a full day after the interactive session ended.

## Why

Observed: in a single interactive session, 9 stampless claims accumulated. They needed manual unassign because waiting 24h for auto-recovery would lose ~24h of pulse productivity per stale claim.

## Root cause

`claim-task-id.sh` self-assigns the runner via `gh issue edit --add-assignee` (per t1970) but does NOT create the corresponding interactive-claim stamp at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/<slug>-<num>.json`. The stamp is only created if the agent later calls `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`. If the agent never makes that call (the common case for ad-hoc interactive work), the issue is permanently stampless until 24h elapses.

## How

EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:709 — change `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD` default from `86400` (24h) to `3600` (1h). Update the rationale comment block at lines 295-301 to reflect the new threshold and the reasoning (pulse cycle ~10min, so 1h still gives 6 pulse cycles of grace; stampless = no proactive lifecycle signal exists).

The env var override remains so users who genuinely run multi-hour interactive sessions without claim helper can opt back to 24h: `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD=86400 pulse-wrapper.sh`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- todo/tasks/t*-brief.md

## Acceptance criteria

- Default threshold reduced from 86400 to 3600 in source
- Comment rationale updated to reflect new value and reasoning
- Env var override still works (verified by source-and-test)
- shellcheck clean
- ShellCheck regression test verifies new default

title: t2943: follow-up to t2942: claim-task-id.sh should atomically create interactive-claim stamp on self-assign
body:
## Task

When `claim-task-id.sh` self-assigns the runner for an interactive session creating a non-auto-dispatch task (per t1970), it should atomically also create the interactive-claim stamp file at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/<slug>-<num>.json`. Today the stamp is only created if the agent later remembers to call `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`.

## Why

The current sequence has a documented foot-gun:

1. `claim-task-id.sh` self-assigns the runner via `gh issue edit --add-assignee` (correct per t1970)
2. The agent SHOULD then call `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` (mandatory per AGENTS.md "Interactive issue ownership")
3. But agents frequently skip step 2 — the call is mandatory in prose but not enforced by tooling
4. Result: an issue with `(origin:interactive + self-assigned + active status + NO stamp file)` — a stampless interactive claim

Stampless claims block pulse dispatch per t1996/t2218 dedup rule until the `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD` safety net fires. Even with the t2942 reduction from 24h to 1h, that's still 1h of lost pulse productivity per stale claim.

In a single recent interactive session, 9 stampless claims accumulated and required manual cleanup. The root cause is the missing step 2 — the fix is to make step 1 (claim-task-id.sh self-assign) include stamp creation atomically, eliminating the gap entirely.

## Root cause

`claim-task-id.sh::_auto_assign_issue` (lines 698-720 area) calls `gh issue edit --add-assignee` but does not invoke the stamp-creation logic from `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`. The two mechanisms evolved independently:

- t1970 added auto-self-assign in `claim-task-id.sh` for interactive ergonomics
- t2056 made `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` mandatory (with stamp creation as a side effect)
- The two were never wired together

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh::_auto_assign_issue` — after the `gh issue edit --add-assignee` call succeeds, source `interactive-session-helper.sh` and invoke its stamp-creation function (or call the helper as a subprocess with `claim --stamp-only` if a flag is added).

Reference pattern: `interactive-session-helper.sh::cmd_claim` already creates the stamp at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/<slug>-<num>.json`. Extract the stamp-creation logic into a reusable function (or expose a `claim --stamp-only` mode) so `claim-task-id.sh` can reuse it without duplicating the schema.

Skip stamp creation when:

- The session is headless (`FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`, `OPENCODE_HEADLESS`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` env)
- The labels include `auto-dispatch` (covered by t2218 carve-out — no self-assign means no stamp needed)
- The labels include `parent-task` (no dispatch ever, so stamp is meaningless)

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
- .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-stamp-creation.sh
- todo/tasks/t*-brief.md

## Acceptance criteria

- claim-task-id.sh creates the interactive-claim stamp when it self-assigns for an interactive session
- Stamp creation is skipped for headless sessions and auto-dispatch / parent-task labels
- Regression test verifies stamp file exists after claim-task-id.sh invocation
- Documentation in AGENTS.md "Interactive issue ownership" updated to note that the call is now eager — the manual interactive-session-helper.sh claim step is still useful for picking up issues mid-lifecycle but is no longer mandatory immediately after claim-task-id.sh
- shellcheck clean

## Related

- t2148 — original safety-net implementation
- t2218 — symmetric carve-out for auto-dispatch labels
- t2942 (#21157) — reduced safety-net threshold from 24h to 1h (the immediate productivity-tax mitigation; this issue is the root-cause fix)

title: t2944: hotfix: bash 3.2 syntax error in bounty-spam-detector.sh blocks all macOS CI
body:
## Task

`.agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh:572-585` uses `var=$(cat <<EOF ... EOF)` — heredoc inside `$()` — which Bash 3.2 (macOS `/bin/bash`) cannot parse. The macOS-shipped Bash 3.2 ShellCheck CI step fails with `syntax error near unexpected token ';;'` on every PR, blocking the merge gate.

## Why now

Every open PR currently fails the required `ShellCheck (macos-latest) / Bash 3.2 syntax validation (macOS native)` check, blocking the merge gate. P0 hotfix.

## Root cause

PR #21139 (t2925) introduced the bounty-spam-detector with a `$()`-wrapped heredoc:

```bash
comment_body=$(
    cat <<EOF
...
EOF
)
```

This is the canonical Bash 3.2 footgun documented in `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`. Bash 5 accepts it; Bash 3.2 reports a syntax error on the first line after the heredoc end (typically several lines later, e.g. the `case` arm), making the error point misleading.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh:571-585` — replace the `$()`-wrapped heredoc with a helper function that emits the heredoc, then capture its output. The heredoc is then inside a regular function body (Bash 3.2 accepts), and `$()` only wraps a function call (Bash 3.2 accepts). Verification: `/bin/bash -n .agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh` exits 0.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh
- todo/tasks/t*-brief.md

## Acceptance criteria

- `/bin/bash -n .agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh` exits 0
- All existing functionality preserved (close PR with comment + dry-run path)
- shellcheck still clean
- No regression in `bounty-spam-detector.sh check/score/is-spam/scan-body/close` subcommands

```diff
+# `gh` (Go HTTP client) does not apply a default request timeout, so a wedged
```

title: t2946: settings namespace divergence: orchestration.* schema completely unread, supervisor.* read but undocumented
body:
## Task

Fix the silent settings namespace divergence between the canonical schema (`orchestration.*`) and the deployed scripts (`supervisor.*`). Every user setting under `orchestration.*` is currently ignored at runtime.

## Why

A user's `~/.config/aidevops/settings.json` lives at the centre of the autonomous orchestration loop — `pulse_interval_seconds`, `max_concurrent_workers`, `enabled`, `auto_merge`, `strategic_review`, `budget_limit_daily_usd`. The user expects edits to take effect.

Today they don't.

Concrete reproduction (verified on this runner, 2026-04-27):

- `~/.config/aidevops/settings.json` declares `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds = 120` (intended cadence: 2 min). The same file ALSO has a stale `supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds = 600` (left over from an older schema).
- Schema source `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json` declares `orchestration` as the canonical namespace. The `supervisor` namespace is **NOT** in the schema at all — `jq '.properties.supervisor' aidevops-config.schema.json` returns `null`.
- Defaults source `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc:94` documents the `orchestration` namespace.
- Production scripts read **only** `supervisor.*`:
  - `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh:64` — `jq -r '.supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds // empty'`
  - `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh:392` — `jq -r '.supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds // 0'`
  - `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh:394` — validation message: "supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds (...) should be 30-3600"
  - `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh:511` — help text: "supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds Pulse interval (default: 180)"
- Production scripts read NONE of:
  - `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds`
  - `orchestration.max_concurrent_workers`
  - `orchestration.enabled`
  - `orchestration.auto_merge`
  - `orchestration.strategic_review`
  - `orchestration.budget_limit_daily_usd`

Verification commands (zero hits each):

```bash
grep -rn "\.orchestration\.\(pulse_interval\|max_concurrent\|enabled\|auto_merge\|strategic_review\|budget_limit\)" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/
```

Real-world consequence on this runner: pulse runs every 600 s instead of the user-configured 120 s — a **5x slowdown** on dispatch cadence that no log line surfaces. Any user touching `orchestration.max_concurrent_workers` is similarly silently overridden.

This is the canonical "schema lies, code does something else" failure mode. It violates AGENTS.md "Build for change" and is invisible until someone instruments the gap.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh
- .agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh
- .agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json
- .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc
- .agents/scripts/aidevops.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup.sh

### Approach

Read the orchestration namespace canonically, fall back to the legacy supervisor namespace, warn loudly on stale supervisor-only configs, and add a one-shot migration on `aidevops update` so user settings are healed without manual editing.

### EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh:62-68

Pattern (model on the existing `_raw=$(jq -r ...)` block):

```bash
# Read orchestration.* canonically; fall back to supervisor.* for legacy configs
_raw=$(jq -r '.orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds // .supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds // empty' "$_SETTINGS_FILE" 2>/dev/null) || _raw=""
```

### EDIT: .agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh:390-396

Same fallback pattern in `validate_settings`. After a successful read, if `.supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds` exists AND `.orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds` is absent, emit a `print_warning` advising the user to migrate the key. If both exist with different values, emit a `print_error` (non-fatal) listing both and stating which one is being used (orchestration wins).

### EDIT: .agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh:511

Update help text from `supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds` to `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds` (keep one-line note that legacy `supervisor.*` is still honoured for one release).

### EDIT: .agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json (~line 95-110)

Add a top-level `supervisor` object marked `deprecated: true` with the same shape as the current `orchestration` block. This makes existing user settings.json files validate cleanly while the migration runs, and allows tooling (`aidevops status`, IDE schema validation) to flag the deprecation visibly.

### EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops.sh `cmd_update` (or equivalent migration hook)

Add a one-shot, idempotent migration: if `~/.config/aidevops/settings.json` has `supervisor.*` keys that have no `orchestration.*` counterpart, copy them over (preserving values) and remove the `supervisor` block. If both exist, prefer `orchestration.*` (the user's most-recent edit), preserve the `supervisor.*` block as a comment-equivalent backup field `_supervisor_legacy_<timestamp>` for one release, and log the migration to `~/.aidevops/logs/settings-migration.log`. Surface the migration in the `aidevops update` summary so users see it once.

### Reference pattern

Model on the existing fallback chains in `pulse-wrapper.sh::_resolve_active_pulse_interval` (env > settings > default). Apply the same precedence pattern but with `orchestration` ahead of `supervisor` as the new top of the chain.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. After applying the fix, a settings file with ONLY orchestration.* must produce a non-empty interval
echo '{"orchestration":{"pulse_interval_seconds":120}}' > /tmp/test-settings.json
_SETTINGS_FILE=/tmp/test-settings.json bash -c 'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh; echo "$(_resolve_pulse_interval)"'
# expected: 120

# 2. A settings file with ONLY supervisor.* (legacy) must still work and emit a deprecation warning
echo '{"supervisor":{"pulse_interval_seconds":600}}' > /tmp/test-settings.json
settings-helper.sh validate /tmp/test-settings.json 2>&1 | grep -i "deprecat"
# expected: warning about supervisor namespace

# 3. The migration must run idempotently
cp /tmp/test-settings.json /tmp/migrate-input.json
aidevops update --migrate-settings-only 2>&1
jq '.orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds, (has("supervisor") | not)' /tmp/migrate-input.json
# expected: 600, true

# 4. Schema validation: existing supervisor-only configs must still validate (with deprecation flag)
ajv validate -s aidevops-config.schema.json -d /tmp/test-settings.json
# expected: valid, with deprecation notice
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-watchdog-tick.sh` reads `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds` first, `supervisor.*` second
- [ ] `settings-helper.sh` validates and documents `orchestration.*` as canonical; emits deprecation warning when `supervisor.*` is set
- [ ] `aidevops-config.schema.json` declares both namespaces, with `supervisor` flagged deprecated
- [ ] `aidevops update` runs a one-shot, idempotent migration from `supervisor.*` to `orchestration.*`
- [ ] User's reproducer (`pulse_interval_seconds=120` under `orchestration`) takes effect on next pulse cycle (verify via `pulse-stats.json` `last_cycle_duration_seconds` or watchdog log timestamps)
- [ ] All other `orchestration.*` keys (`max_concurrent_workers`, `enabled`, `auto_merge`, `strategic_review`, `budget_limit_daily_usd`) get matching consumer fixes — file follow-up tasks if scope is too large for one PR

Discovered during interactive concurrency-improvement audit (parent task: 24h-backoff and concurrency-cap audit, t2942/t2944 cascade). User reported pulse felt slow despite setting `pulse_interval_seconds=120` in `~/.config/aidevops/settings.json`. Verification showed the value lives in the `orchestration` namespace (matching the schema) but production code reads `supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds=600` (a stale legacy field) — silent 5x slowdown.

The settings.json is autogenerated by `setup.sh` from the schema, so the divergence affects EVERY user who customises pulse cadence or worker concurrency, not just this runner.

title: t2951: bounty-spam-auto-close.yml never fires close: cmd_score rc=0 contract collides with workflow rc=1 gate
body:
## What

`bounty-spam-auto-close.yml` invokes `bounty-spam-detector.sh score pr` and only fires the close path when `RC -eq 1 && VERDICT == "spam-likely"`. `cmd_score` always returns `0` — the per-verdict exit code (`_priv_verdict_to_exit`) is wired into `cmd_check` and `cmd_is_spam` only. The combined gate is therefore unreachable, and confirmed-spam PRs stay open until a human or this workflow's mailing-list cousin closes them manually.

## Why

Real-world miss: a recent drive-by bounty-hunter PR (single attacker account, batch of 7 PRs, identical body class). Workflow run 24972197953 logged:

```
Detector output: spam-likely|## 💰 Paid Bounty Contribution|Generated via automated bounty hunter;Feishu notifications|BOTH
Detector rc: 0
```

Result: `should_close=false`, no auto-close, the PR sat for 15 min until manually closed via `bounty-spam-detector.sh close pr <N> --repo marcusquinn/aidevops`. Defense-in-depth still held (maintainer-gate blocked merge, CodeRabbit skipped, Codacy clean, Socket clean, URL allowlist clean, mergeable_state=blocked) but the t2925 first-line auto-close was a no-op for the entire batch.

## How

### Files Scope

- .github/workflows/bounty-spam-auto-close.yml

EDIT: `.github/workflows/bounty-spam-auto-close.yml:106`

Current (unreachable):

```bash
if [[ "$RC" -eq 1 && "$VERDICT" == "spam-likely" ]]; then
  echo "should_close=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  echo "should_close=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
```

Fix (verdict-string source of truth, since `cmd_score` does not encode rc):

```bash
if [[ "$VERDICT" == "spam-likely" ]]; then
  echo "should_close=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  echo "should_close=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
```

Alternative (one-character change, more conservative — `cmd_check` does encode rc): swap `score pr` → `check pr` at line 93. Either fix is acceptable; verdict-string fix is preferred because it documents intent at the gate site.

### Reference pattern

Compare working contract at `.agents/scripts/bounty-spam-detector.sh:387-389` (cmd_check) vs the broken caller assumption at the workflow line 106. `_priv_verdict_to_exit` defines the canonical mapping `clean=0, spam-likely=1, ambiguous=2, error=3`.

### Verification

1. Trigger detector against a known-spam PR from a workflow run (re-run a closed PR run, or wait for the next bounty bot — they file every 1-2h).
2. Confirm log shows `should_close=true` for `verdict=spam-likely`.
3. Confirm the close step ran (`Close PR if spam-likely` job step, not skipped).

Local repro before merge:

```bash
# Score a known-spam PR:
bounty-spam-detector.sh score pr <N> --repo marcusquinn/aidevops; echo "rc=$?"
# Expect: spam-likely|... + rc=0 (current behaviour, the bug)
# After fix to workflow: verdict-string check passes regardless of rc.
```

Add a regression test:

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-bounty-spam-detector.sh` — add a `score`-mode case that asserts rc=0 even on `spam-likely` (locks the contract so any future score behaviour change forces the workflow update).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Workflow line 106 no longer requires `RC -eq 1` to fire close.
- [ ] Re-running workflow on a known-spam PR closes it within ~1 min of open.
- [ ] Test added to `test-bounty-spam-detector.sh` pinning the `cmd_score` rc=0 contract.
- [ ] All existing bounty-spam-detector tests pass.

## Context

- Canonical incident batch: 7 PRs from a single drive-by bounty-bot account, all closed manually via `bounty-spam-detector.sh close`.
- Defense-in-depth that DID hold on the most recent PR in the batch: `external-contributor` + `needs-maintainer-review` labels; `maintainer-gate` workflow `fail`; `CodeRabbit` skipped per `no-review` excluded label; `Codacy` 0 issues; `Socket` clean; `URL Allowlist` clean; `mergeable_state=blocked`; cryptographic approval required for merge.
- Adjacent finding (out of scope): the most recent PR carried two `Merge branch 'main'` commits, one by an unrelated 3-follower account that is not a collaborator. Likely a `pull_request_target` side-effect or a different bot; worth a follow-up if the pattern recurs.
- `t2925` (PR #21101) shipped the detector; this issue closes the loop on the workflow→detector contract that was overlooked at integration time.

## Tier checklist

- [x] tier:standard — bug fix in a CI workflow, single file, well-defined verification.
- [ ] tier:simple — disqualified: requires reading `cmd_score`/`cmd_check` to understand the contract; not a verbatim oldString/newString task.
- [ ] tier:thinking — not needed.

`origin:interactive` PRs that go idle currently sit for 24h before auto-transferring to `origin:worker-takeover` (CI-fix/conflict pipelines pick them up after that). With 24 concurrent workers and a 600s pulse, 24h is far longer than necessary — by the time the auto-transfer fires, the work is buried in dozens of fresher PRs and worktree conflicts may have accumulated.

4h matches typical interactive-session breaks (lunch, meetings, end-of-day) without competing with active sessions. The user explicitly asked to remove all 24h backoffs that delay dispatch.

title: t2950: raise MAX_WORKERS_CAP ceiling 32→64 in pulse-wrapper-config.sh
body:
## Task

Raise `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` clamp ceiling in `pulse-wrapper-config.sh:50-66` from 32 to 64 to allow higher concurrency on RAM-rich runners.

## Why

The current clamp `[4, 32]` was sized for a smaller-RAM era. On this runner (Mac Studio, 64GB free), `RAM_PER_WORKER_MB=512` and `RAM_RESERVE_MB=6144` mean ~116 workers fit physically (`(64*1024 - 6144) / 512 = 116`), but the hard ceiling of 32 leaves >70% headroom unused.

24 workers is the user's current target; doubling that ceiling to 64 gives meaningful headroom for burst dispatch and future increases in `max_concurrent_workers` without requiring another framework PR. The lower bound of 4 is fine — it's about a floor, not a ceiling.

The clamp is the only thing standing between user intent and reality: a user setting `orchestration.max_concurrent_workers=64` (or even just 33) is currently capped silently at 32. Combined with the t2946 namespace divergence finding (where the user's setting isn't even read yet), this represents a second layer of "user setting is ignored".

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh

### EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh:50-66

Locate the `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` clamp (likely around lines 50-66):

```bash
# Current
MAX_WORKERS_CAP_FLOOR=4
MAX_WORKERS_CAP_CEILING=32
```

Change to:

```bash
# Raised t2950: 32 → 64. RAM headroom on modern runners (64GB+) supports far more.
MAX_WORKERS_CAP_FLOOR=4
MAX_WORKERS_CAP_CEILING=64
```

If the constant is inline rather than a variable, make it a variable so it's discoverable. Add a one-line comment citing t2950 and the RAM math.

### Reference pattern

Model on the clamp pattern already in the file. No new logic — just a literal constant change.

### Verification

```bash
# New ceiling honoured
bash -c 'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh; echo "$MAX_WORKERS_CAP_CEILING"'
# expected: 64

# Floor unchanged
bash -c 'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh; echo "$MAX_WORKERS_CAP_FLOOR"'
# expected: 4

# Setting orchestration.max_concurrent_workers=50 in settings.json should resolve to 50, not 32
# (NOTE: requires t2946 namespace fix to be merged first to actually consume orchestration.*)
echo '{"orchestration":{"max_concurrent_workers":50}}' > /tmp/test-settings.json
_SETTINGS_FILE=/tmp/test-settings.json bash -c 'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh; echo "$MAX_WORKERS"'
# expected: 50

# Same with 100 — should clamp to 64
echo '{"orchestration":{"max_concurrent_workers":100}}' > /tmp/test-settings.json
_SETTINGS_FILE=/tmp/test-settings.json bash -c 'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh; echo "$MAX_WORKERS"'
# expected: 64

# ShellCheck clean
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `MAX_WORKERS_CAP_CEILING` raised from 32 to 64
- [ ] Floor of 4 unchanged
- [ ] One-line comment cites t2950 and RAM-math justification
- [ ] ShellCheck clean

title: t2953: fast-fail _ff_with_lock orphan-lock detection: empty lockdir without owner.pid never cleaned, blocks all dispatches
body:
## Task

Fix `_ff_with_lock` in `pulse-fast-fail.sh:143-178` to detect and clear orphaned lockdirs that have no `owner.pid` file. Currently, a lockdir created by a process that died/SIGKILLed before writing `owner.pid` becomes a permanent block on every subsequent dispatch — for the lifetime of the runner.

## Why

**This is a CRITICAL dispatch bottleneck. Empirically observed today on a healthy runner with 24-worker capacity reduced to 2 effective workers due to a single orphan lockdir.**

Reproduction (verified 2026-04-27, this runner):

1. Lockdir created at 02:06:04Z: `/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/fast-fail-counter.json.lockdir/`
2. Lockdir contained NO `owner.pid` file (process died between `mkdir` and `printf` of owner.pid)
3. From 02:06 onwards, every dispatch attempt logged `[pulse-wrapper] _ff_with_lock: lock acquisition timed out` and aborted
4. DFF cycle dispatch rate dropped from 23-24/cycle to 0-2/cycle — **>90% throughput loss**
5. Manual `rmdir` of the empty lockdir at 02:55Z immediately restored full dispatch (4 PRs auto-merged within 8 minutes)

Total visible impact: ~50 minutes of degraded dispatch (~20+ missing dispatches) until manually unblocked.

The bug:

```bash
# pulse-fast-fail.sh:143-178 (current code)
_ff_with_lock() {
    local lock_dir="${FAST_FAIL_STATE_FILE}.lockdir"
    local retries=0
    while ! mkdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null; do
        retries=$((retries + 1))
        if [[ "$retries" -ge 50 ]]; then
            echo "[pulse-wrapper] _ff_with_lock: lock acquisition timed out" >>"$LOGFILE"
            return 1
        fi
        local _ff_owner_raw _ff_owner_pid _ff_owner_hash
        _ff_owner_raw=$(cat "${lock_dir}/owner.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
        _ff_owner_pid="${_ff_owner_raw%%|*}"
        _ff_owner_hash="${_ff_owner_raw#*|}"
        [[ "$_ff_owner_hash" == "$_ff_owner_pid" ]] && _ff_owner_hash=""
        # BUG: this check is the only stale-detector — fires only when owner.pid EXISTS
        if [[ -n "$_ff_owner_pid" ]] && ! _is_process_alive_and_matches "$_ff_owner_pid" "${PULSE_PROCESS_PATTERN:-}" "$_ff_owner_hash"; then
            echo "[pulse-wrapper] _ff_with_lock: clearing stale lock (owner PID ${_ff_owner_pid} gone or reused, t2421)" >>"$LOGFILE"
            rm -f "${lock_dir}/owner.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
            continue
        fi
        sleep 0.1
    done
    # Owner write happens AFTER successful mkdir — race window where lockdir exists with no owner.pid
    local _ff_argv_hash=""
    _ff_argv_hash=$(_compute_argv_hash "$$" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    printf '%s|%s\n' "$$" "$_ff_argv_hash" >"${lock_dir}/owner.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    ...
}
```

Failure mode: the canonical t2421 stale-lock detector requires `owner.pid` to EXIST and contain a non-empty PID. When `_ff_owner_pid` is empty (file missing), the `if [[ -n ...]]` guard short-circuits, the cleanup block is skipped, and the loop falls through to `sleep 0.1` and retries. After 50 retries, lock acquisition times out and the dispatch aborts.

The race: between `mkdir` succeeding (line 146) and `printf >owner.pid` (line 172), there is a ~10-100µs window where a SIGKILL would leave the lockdir without an owner.pid forever. Bash `trap` on EXIT does NOT fire on SIGKILL. The 50-min observed orphan strongly suggests this was the trigger (a worker SIGKILLed during fast-fail bookkeeping).

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-fast-fail.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-fast-fail-orphan-lock.sh (NEW)

### EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-fast-fail.sh:143-178 (`_ff_with_lock`)

Add a parallel stale-detector for the empty-lockdir case. Two viable paths:

**Path A (preferred — age-based fallback).** When `owner.pid` is missing, check the lockdir's mtime. If older than `${FAST_FAIL_LOCK_ORPHAN_AGE_SECONDS:-5}`, treat as orphaned and clean. The 5-second default is well above any normal mkdir→printf window (microseconds) but short enough that recovery is fast.

```bash
if [[ -n "$_ff_owner_pid" ]] && ! _is_process_alive_and_matches "$_ff_owner_pid" "${PULSE_PROCESS_PATTERN:-}" "$_ff_owner_hash"; then
    # existing stale-pid path (unchanged)
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] _ff_with_lock: clearing stale lock (owner PID ${_ff_owner_pid} gone or reused, t2421)" >>"$LOGFILE"
    rm -f "${lock_dir}/owner.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
    continue
fi

# NEW: empty-lockdir orphan path (t2953)
if [[ -z "$_ff_owner_pid" ]]; then
    local _orphan_age_threshold="${FAST_FAIL_LOCK_ORPHAN_AGE_SECONDS:-5}"
    local _lock_mtime _now _lock_age
    _lock_mtime=$(stat -f %m "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _now=$(date +%s)
    _lock_age=$((_now - _lock_mtime))
    if [[ "$_lock_age" -ge "$_orphan_age_threshold" ]]; then
        echo "[pulse-wrapper] _ff_with_lock: clearing orphan lock (no owner.pid, age=${_lock_age}s >= ${_orphan_age_threshold}s, t2953)" >>"$LOGFILE"
        rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
        continue
    fi
fi
sleep 0.1
```

**Path B (alternative — write owner.pid BEFORE mkdir succeeds).** Use a tempfile-then-rename pattern so the owner.pid is in place atomically with the lockdir creation. More invasive but eliminates the race entirely.

Path A is preferred because it adds a recovery path without changing the existing happy-path semantics, and the threshold is configurable.

### NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-fast-fail-orphan-lock.sh

Test cases:

1. **Empty lockdir older than threshold → cleaned.** Create `${state_file}.lockdir/` with no owner.pid, set mtime 10s in the past, call `_ff_with_lock` with a no-op command, assert success and lockdir is removed.
2. **Empty lockdir younger than threshold → not cleaned (race protection).** Same setup with mtime 1s in past, assert the function continues retrying (returns 1 after 50 retries × 100ms = 5s).
3. **Lockdir with stale owner.pid → cleaned (existing behaviour preserved).** Write a non-existent PID to owner.pid, assert existing t2421 path fires.
4. **Lockdir with live owner.pid → not cleaned (existing behaviour preserved).** Write `$$` to owner.pid, assert function blocks until release.

Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-fast-fail-age-out.sh` for the test harness pattern.

### Reference pattern

Existing t2421 stale-lock detection is the model — same shape, additional detector branch for the empty-lockdir case.

### Verification

```bash
# Unit test passes
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-fast-fail-orphan-lock.sh
# expected: all 4 cases pass

# Manual repro — orphan a lockdir, verify recovery
mkdir -p ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/fast-fail-counter.json.lockdir
sleep 6  # ensure age >= threshold
bash -c 'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-fast-fail.sh; _ff_with_lock true'; echo "rc=$?"
# expected: rc=0 (lock cleaned and acquired)

# Production check: pulse log shows orphan cleanup messages going forward
grep "clearing orphan lock" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
# expected: t2953 cleanup messages when orphans occur

# ShellCheck clean
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-fast-fail.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-fast-fail-orphan-lock.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_ff_with_lock` detects empty lockdirs older than `FAST_FAIL_LOCK_ORPHAN_AGE_SECONDS` (default 5s) and cleans them
- [ ] Existing t2421 stale-pid detection unchanged
- [ ] New test file covers all 4 orphan/stale/live/race cases
- [ ] Env override `FAST_FAIL_LOCK_ORPHAN_AGE_SECONDS` documented at top of file
- [ ] PR body cites the empirical 50-minute outage observed 2026-04-27 as the motivating incident

## Session Origin

Discovered during interactive concurrency-improvement session 2026-04-27. Sub-investigation of "pulse dispatching at 2 workers/hour despite 24-worker cap" revealed `_ff_with_lock: lock acquisition timed out` on every dispatch loop iteration, caused by an empty `fast-fail-counter.json.lockdir/` from 02:06Z. Manual `rmdir` immediately restored normal dispatch (4 PRs auto-merged within 8 minutes; t2946 settings namespace fix landed via PR #21191).

Symptoms in pulse log when bug fires:
- Repeated `[pulse-wrapper] _ff_with_lock: lock acquisition timed out` (every dispatch iteration)
- `Deterministic fill floor complete: dispatched=0` despite high `target_available` slot count
- Worker count well below `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` despite long status:available backlog
- No `clearing stale lock` messages because t2421 path doesn't fire on missing owner.pid

This bug is the highest-impact single-line dispatch fix available right now — every minute the bug fires costs ~0.4 worker-hours of wasted capacity. With auto-dispatch backlog typically 30-60 issues, an unfixed orphan can lose 10+ dispatches before observation.

**Step 1 — schedulers.sh nvm/volta/fnm sweep.**

Insert a new "Step 4a" block in `_resolve_pulse_runtime_binary` BEFORE the existing fixed-paths sweep (line 221). Sort version dirs newest-first (`sort -rV`) so users with multiple Node versions get the most recent opencode.

Roots to sweep:

- `$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/<ver>/bin/opencode` (nvm)
- `$HOME/.volta/tools/image/node/<ver>/bin/opencode` (volta)
- `$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/<ver>/installation/bin/opencode` (fnm — note the extra `installation/` segment)

**Step 2 — schedulers.sh product validation.**

Validation points:

- **Read (step 1, `$_persisted_file`):** if the persisted file points at an executable that fails validation, drop it and continue to re-resolve. This heals existing alex-solovyev-class state.
- **Write (just before `printf '%s\n' >"$_persisted_file"`):** only persist if validation passes. The legacy `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode` fallback (line 242) MUST be excluded from persistence on Linux machines where that path doesn't exist.

For each candidate in the legacy fixed-paths loop (step 4), validate before accepting. The `claude` paths in that list (lines 230-232) will fail validation against the opencode signature and be skipped — effectively neutralising the broken claude fallback without removing the candidates (preserves diff scope).

**Step 3 — headless-runtime-lib.sh nvm sweep.**

Add the same three nvm/volta/fnm roots to `_find_alternative_opencode_binary` (line 868). The existing per-candidate `_validate_opencode_binary` check (line 878) already does product validation — just extend the candidate set.

1. Resolver finds the nvm-installed opencode binary.

3. Resolver does NOT persist the legacy `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode` fallback when no real opencode is reachable.

title: t2955: cache _is_task_committed_to_main result via dispatch-blocked label — eliminate per-cycle scan on 224 issues
body:
## Problem

`_is_task_committed_to_main` (pulse-dispatch-core.sh:725) is invoked once per candidate issue per dispatch cycle. Each invocation runs:

1. `gh issue view N --json createdAt` (one API call)
2. `git -C <repo> fetch origin main --quiet` (network)
3. `_task_id_in_recent_commits` (`git log --grep=...`)
4. `_task_id_in_merged_pr` (`git log --grep=...`)
5. `_task_id_in_changed_files` (`git log --grep=...` + diff inspection)

Production data (recent pulse.log):

- **1170 total log lines** for "Dispatch blocked for #X: task already committed to main (GH#17574)"
- **224 distinct issues** repeatedly hitting the block — each cycle re-runs all 5 ops above
- Single offender example: **#20930** is checked >100 times across cycles
- Per-issue cost: 1 GitHub API call + 1 network fetch + 3 `git log --grep` scans
- Aggregate per-cycle cost: ~224 issues × 5 ops = 1120 shell invocations on a hot path

This contributes to long preflight stages and reduces effective dispatch throughput. The check itself is correct (per GH#17574, the block prevents wasted workers); the SPAM is the per-cycle re-evaluation cost on a result that rarely changes.

## Why this matters now

The orphan-lock fix (t2953, in flight) restored DFF to 23-24 dispatches/cycle. With dispatch unblocked, every second of preflight latency directly delays worker spawn. Caching the committed-to-main verdict shifts this from "always run 5 ops per affected issue per cycle" to "run 5 ops once, then label-skip on subsequent cycles".

GH#17574 picked correctness over efficiency (chose `return 0` to skip rather than auto-close, GH#17642). t2955 keeps that correctness while eliminating the recurring cost.

## Proposed fix

**Files to modify:**

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:609-633` (the `if _is_task_committed_to_main(...)` branch)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:725-756` (`_is_task_committed_to_main` function — add label fast-path)

**Pattern:**

1. On first detection (current path), apply a sentinel label `dispatch-blocked:committed-to-main` to the issue.
2. In the next-cycle dispatch path, BEFORE invoking `_is_task_committed_to_main`, check if the issue carries the sentinel label. If yes, skip the expensive scan and return blocked immediately.
3. Add a low-frequency scrubber (e.g., once per hour, in `pulse-cleanup-helper.sh`) that re-evaluates labelled issues and removes the label when the cited commit no longer exists in main (revert handling).
4. Keep the existing block log line for audit, but tag it `(cached)` vs `(scanned)` for diagnosis.

**Reference pattern:** `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::is-assigned` (label-first cheap check) and the `parent-task` label fast-path in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::_is_assigned_parent_task`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First detection of committed-to-main applies `dispatch-blocked:committed-to-main` label.
- [ ] Subsequent dispatch cycles for the same issue skip the `gh issue view` + `git fetch` + 3 grep scans, blocking via label inspection only.
- [ ] Hourly scrubber re-evaluates labelled issues and clears the label if the commit was reverted (so a re-dispatched task can run again).
- [ ] Block log line includes `(cached)` or `(scanned)` so we can measure the cache hit rate.
- [ ] Test: confirm `pulse.log` shows ≥1 cached vs scanned ratio after first full cycle post-deploy.
- [ ] Existing GH#17574 test (`tests/test-pulse-wrapper-main-commit-check.sh`) still passes.

## Verification

```bash
# Before: count expensive scans per cycle
rg -c "task already committed to main" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log

# After: should see (cached) lines dominate after warmup
rg "task already committed to main \((cached|scanned)\)" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c
```

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-main-commit-check.sh

## Complexity Impact

`_is_task_committed_to_main` is currently 31 lines (725-756). Adding a label fast-path (≤10 lines) keeps it under 50 lines, well below the 100-line `function-complexity` gate.

## Source

Discovered while investigating overnight pulse productivity drains alongside t2953 (orphan-lock) and t2956 (watchdog stall rate). Production telemetry at `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (32MB) shows the spam pattern; #20930 cited >100 times in recent log slice.

title: t2956: investigate watchdog_stall_continue 21.6% rate (avg 38min wasted vs 16min success)
body:
## Problem

`watchdog_stall_continue` is the second-most-common worker exit (after `success`) and it is the **largest single throughput drain** in overnight pulse productivity.

Production telemetry (`~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`, last 200 worker completions):

| Result                    | Count | Avg duration   |
|---------------------------|-------|----------------|
| success                   | 140   | 987,222 ms (~16 min)  |
| **watchdog_stall_continue** | **43**  | **2,276,658 ms (~38 min)** |
| rate_limit                | 11    | 1,714,312 ms (~28 min) |
| premature_exit            | 5     | 483,588 ms (~8 min)    |
| auth_error                | 1     | 1,234,792 ms (~20 min) |

Stall rate: **43 / 199 = 21.6%** of worker completions burn ~2.3× the success-case duration before the watchdog gives up. Live observation during this triage: `#21160` worker has two processes at 41 min and 30 min elapsed (more than 2× the 16-min success median), strongly suggesting the watchdog "let it continue" rather than killing. The slot is held but the worker is producing nothing.

## Why this matters now

With `MAX_WORKERS=24` (this box) or up to 64 if t2950 lands, every stalled slot is one fewer dispatchable task per hour. At 21.6% stall rate × 24 slots, ~5 slots are continuously degraded. Halving the stall rate would unlock ~2.5 effective slots — roughly an additional 8-10 PR completions per hour overnight at current cycle times.

`watchdog_stall_continue` (exit 78) is documented in `worker-activity-watchdog.sh` as "watchdog detected stall but let the worker continue rather than kill (300s no-output threshold)". The current bias is "let it complete eventually" — but the metrics show stalled workers cost 2.3× the time of healthy ones, so re-dispatching at a hard cutoff would be cheaper.

## Proposed investigation + fix

**Files to investigate:**

- `READ: .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` — current stall detection logic, 300s threshold, "let continue vs kill" decision tree.
- `READ: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — invocation point for the watchdog and the exit code translation to `watchdog_stall_continue`.
- `READ: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` — exit code conventions (78 = stall_continue, 77 = premature_exit).
- `READ: ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` — historical stall rate and per-issue patterns.

**Hypothesis to test:**

Are most `watchdog_stall_continue` outcomes (a) workers that eventually succeed but slowly, (b) workers that eventually fail, or (c) workers that produce a successful PR but with low-value output? The answer determines the right knob:

- If (a): tighten the stall threshold and let pulse re-dispatch.
- If (b): kill earlier, save the slot, requeue.
- If (c): file a separate task on prompt-quality / model-choice for the stalled cohort.

**Concrete fix candidates:**

1. **Hard kill at 25-30 min** if no output, and re-dispatch via the cascade (cost: ~1 retry; benefit: ~13 min recovered slot).
2. **Diff success/stall worker prompts** to see if specific tier/title patterns correlate with stalls (e.g., refactors stall more than narrow bug fixes).
3. **Add stall reason categorisation** to `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` so we can target sub-classes (model-rate-limit vs editor-loop vs context-collapse).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Categorise the 43 most recent `watchdog_stall_continue` outcomes by eventual fate (success / failure / abandoned) — append findings to issue body before fix.
- [ ] If hard-kill chosen: tighter threshold (default 25 min, tunable via `WORKER_STALL_HARD_KILL_SECONDS`) and the existing `watchdog_stall_continue` exit code is replaced or augmented with `watchdog_stall_killed` for clarity.
- [ ] Verify post-deploy: stall rate drops below 15% in next 200 worker completions.
- [ ] Verify post-deploy: avg duration of `watchdog_stall_*` outcomes drops by ≥30% (workers either succeed faster OR get killed faster).
- [ ] Existing healthy success rate of ~70% maintained or improved.

## Verification

```bash
# Stall rate before/after
tail -200 ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl \
  | jq -r '.result' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Average duration by result
tail -200 ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl \
  | jq -r '"\(.result) \(.duration_ms)"' \
  | awk '{count[$1]++; sum[$1]+=$2} END {for (k in count) printf "  %-30s n=%d avg=%dms\n", k, count[k], sum[k]/count[k]}' \
  | sort -k4 -rn
```

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh

## Complexity Impact

`worker-activity-watchdog.sh` is the primary edit target; current size unknown to this triage but the change is a threshold tweak + exit-code addition — low complexity impact expected.

## Source

Discovered while auditing overnight productivity drains alongside t2953 (orphan-lock) and t2955 (committed-to-main caching). Production telemetry at `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` (2636 entries lifetime; last 200 sliced for stats above). Live confirmation: `#21160` worker observed at 41 min runtime during this session — current behaviour holds the slot.
