title: t2989: preflight stages: missing per-iteration timeouts cause cycle cadence collapse on dispatch-path regressions
body:
## Task

Add per-iteration timeouts and stage-level circuit breakers so a single hung dedup check, gh API call, or worker enumeration cannot consume an entire 600s preflight stage and degrade pulse cycle cadence from ~3-5 min to ~30-40 min.

## Why

The user-visible symptom — "pulse stops being productive after every aidevops update" — is **caused by per-cycle stage-level timeouts paying their full budget when a single iteration hangs, with no per-iteration cap.** This pattern is independent of any single regression: it is the structural soft underbelly that any subtle dispatch-path bug exploits.

### Evidence (today's pulse.log + pulse-stage-timings.log, 2026-04-27 UTC)

**Stage-timeout pattern across the day** (`preflight_early_dispatch`):

```
00-04Z: 0/7  succeed  → 7 timeouts (4200s wasted, 70 minutes)
05Z:    3/3  succeed  ← regression resolved temporarily
06Z:    3/3  succeed  ← still healthy
07Z:    0/1  succeed  ← regression returns
08-15Z: 0/8  succeed  → 8 more timeouts (4800s wasted, 80 minutes)
```

Same pattern for `preflight_ownership_reconcile` (192 successes / 26 timeouts overall, but recent: ALL TIMING OUT).

**The exact hang signature** (from PID 93191, last cycle):

```
[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: loop iter=20 — _dff_process_candidate rc=1
[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: loop iter=21 — entering body
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: preflight_early_dispatch exceeded 600s (pid 93191)
```

The candidate at iter=21 entered `_dff_process_candidate`'s body. Zero log lines for 600s. Killed by parent stage timeout. **One bad candidate consumed the entire 600s budget.**

**Real cycle timing** (PID 69189, 2026-04-27T15:19-16:00Z):

| Time | Stage | Duration |
|------|-------|----------|
| 15:19:48Z | cycle starts (cleanup_orphans) | — |
| 15:30:42Z | preflight_capacity_and_labels finishes | 654s elapsed |
| 15:40:46Z | **preflight_early_dispatch TIMEOUT** | +600s |
| 15:42:46Z | normalize finishes | +120s |
| 15:51:25Z | **preflight_ownership_reconcile TIMEOUT** | +600s |
| 15:55:00Z | preflight_prefetch_and_scope finishes | +215s |
| 15:59:18Z | **deterministic_merge_pass finishes** (productive!) | +256s |
| 16:00:05Z | refresh_blocked_status_from_graph finishes | +47s |

**Total cycle time: ~40 minutes**, with 1200s (50% of cycle) burned on two timeout events. The productive `deterministic_merge_pass` ran ONLY at the 39-min mark.

**Same hang pattern across 7+ different pulse PIDs today**: 80651, 97144, 58189, 42602, 49152, 93191, 69189. Different candidates, same structural failure.

### User experience

When `aidevops update` deploys new code, any subtle bug in dispatch-path internals (subprocess wait, gh API call without timeout, deadlock in dedup) silently freezes one iteration. The fixed 600s timeout pays in full. Cycle cadence collapses from ~3-5 min to ~30-40 min. The user perceives this as "pulse stopped" because expected merge/dispatch activity drops below visible threshold.

### Why current protections are insufficient

| Protection | Why it doesn't fix this |
|------------|------------------------|
| `run_stage_with_timeout` (600s parent cap) | Pays full 600s even when 22 of 23 iterations were healthy |
| `\|\| true` after each preflight call | Doesn't reduce the wall-clock cost of the timeout itself |
| `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running` | Restarts pulse but new code still has the same per-iteration vulnerability |
| t2690 GraphQL circuit breaker (5% floor) | Triggers only on rate exhaustion, not stage timeouts |
| t2770 no_work rate breaker | Triggers on cross-issue dispatch failures, not stage hangs |
| t2897 zero-attempt breaker | Triggers on consecutive worker-spawn failures, not stage hangs |
| t2984 reconcile time-budget | Per-task budget, not per-iteration; t2988 shows it regressed |

None of the existing breakers fire on "single iteration in a long loop hangs." That gap is what this task closes.

## How

### Phase 1: per-iteration timeout in `apply_deterministic_fill_floor` (highest impact)

The fill-floor loop iterates over candidates calling `_dff_process_candidate` (which delegates to `dispatch_with_dedup`). One bad candidate consumes 600s.

**File**: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`

**EDIT**: `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` (line ~598) — wrap each `_dff_process_candidate` call in `run_stage_with_timeout` with a per-iteration cap (default 30s, env `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT`).

Pattern (model on existing `run_stage_with_timeout` calls):

```bash
local _per_cand_timeout="${FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT:-30}"
run_stage_with_timeout "fill_floor_candidate_${cand_num}" "$_per_cand_timeout" \
    _dff_process_candidate "$cand_num" "$cand_repo" || {
    local _rc=$?
    if [[ "$_rc" == "124" ]]; then
        log_warn "[fill-floor] Per-candidate timeout: skipping #${cand_num} after ${_per_cand_timeout}s"
        # increment pulse_stats counter
        if declare -F pulse_stats_increment >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            pulse_stats_increment "fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    fi
}
```

### Phase 2: per-iteration timeout in `_preflight_ownership_reconcile`

Same structural fix for `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` and `reconcile_issues_single_pass` inner loops. (Note: t2988 covers a specific regression; this task covers the structural protection that prevents future regressions in the same family.)

### Phase 3: stage-level circuit breaker

After 3 consecutive timeouts of the same stage (tracked in `pulse-stats.json`), skip that stage for the next 5 cycles. Surfaces an alert via `aidevops-update-check.sh` advisory channel.

**File**: NEW `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-stage-circuit-breaker.sh`

API:
- `stage_breaker_record_timeout <stage_name>` — increments counter
- `stage_breaker_record_success <stage_name>` — resets counter
- `stage_breaker_should_skip <stage_name>` — returns 0 if 3+ consecutive timeouts, else 1
- `stage_breaker_status` — diagnostic output

Wire into `run_stage_with_timeout` so every stage gets the protection automatically. Bypass: `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_STAGE_BREAKER=1`.

### Phase 4 (consider for follow-up): productive-stage reordering

Currently the cycle runs preflight (15+ stages, 1200s when degraded) BEFORE `deterministic_merge_pass`. Consider running `deterministic_merge_pass` and `dirty_pr_sweep` FIRST (they are productive, free, and cheap when the queue is empty) so even a degraded cycle still produces merge value. This is a more invasive change — file as t29NN follow-up if Phase 1-3 don't fully restore cadence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `apply_deterministic_fill_floor` wraps each candidate in a 30s per-iteration timeout (configurable via `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT`)

title: t2991: fix subagent permission.task entries (4 broken keys + missing Product allowlist)
body:
## Task

Fix four broken `permission.task` propagations from primary-agent YAML frontmatter to `opencode.json`, and add missing subagent allowlist for the `Product` agent.

## Why

`opencode-agent-discovery.py` reads each primary agent's `subagents:` YAML list and writes a `permission.task: {"*": "deny", <subagent>: "allow", ...}` block to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. opencode then uses this to filter the Task tool's available subagents — both narrowing the LLM's choices and **stripping non-allowed subagents from the Task tool description** (since opencode PRs #4773 / #7165, merged 2026-01-07).

Six entries are currently broken:

1. **`automate.md` (4 entries)** — YAML list items contain inline `# comments` that are not stripped before being used as keys. Result: keys like `"github-cli    # gh pr merge, gh issue edit"` propagate to `opencode.json`. Because of `*: deny` precedence, the comment-poisoned key denies the legitimate subagent (the real `github-cli` is never matched).
2. **`legal.md` and `research.md`** — both reference `tools/legal/legal-research` (path-style). opencode flattens nested agent files to basename at deploy time, so the on-disk subagent is `legal-research`. Path-style key never matches → silently denied.
3. **`product.md`** — has NO `subagents:` block at all. Without `permission.task`, opencode includes every discovered subagent (1263 in this install) in the Task tool description. Estimated ~95K tokens leaked per Product session.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/automate.md` lines 5-12 — strip inline `# comments` from 4 list items; convert to standalone YAML comments on preceding lines.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/legal.md` line 7 — `tools/legal/legal-research` → `legal-research`.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/research.md` line 16 — `tools/legal/legal-research` → `legal-research`.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/product.md` lines 1-7 — add `subagents:` block (26 entries) between `mode:` and `tools:`. Include the canonical DESIGN.md system: `design-md`, `brand-identity`, `ui-ux-inspiration`, `design-inspiration`, `colour-palette`, `shadcn`, `ui-skills`. Plus context (`context7`, `augment-context-engine`, `serper`, `keyword-research`), onboarding (`onboarding`, `app-dev-onboarding`, `humanise`), monetisation (`app-dev-monetisation`, `stripe`, `accounts-subscription-audit`), growth (`growth`), UI testing (`pagespeed`, `playwright`, `stagehand`), analytics (`analytics-tracking`, `google-analytics`, `app-dev-analytics`), and built-in (`general`, `explore`).

### Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/build-plus.md` (canonical 39-entry `subagents:` block with category comments).

### Verification

```bash
# Run discovery against worktree (no side effects on deployed config)
python3 -c "
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser('~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/lib'))
from agent_config import discover_primary_agents
_, agents, _ = discover_primary_agents('$PWD/.agents')
for name in ['Automate', 'Legal', 'Research', 'Product']:
    perm = agents[name].get('permission', {}).get('task', {})
    allow = sorted(k for k, v in perm.items() if v == 'allow')
    print(f'{name}: {len(allow)} allow')
    for k in allow:
        print(f'  - {k}')
"
```

Expected output: Automate=7, Legal=6, Research=9, Product=26. No keys containing `#`, no path-style keys (`tools/...`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Automate's `permission.task` block contains 7 clean keys (no inline-comment poisoning).
- [ ] Legal references `legal-research` (basename), not `tools/legal/legal-research`.
- [ ] Research references `legal-research` (basename), not `tools/legal/legal-research`.
- [ ] Product has a `subagents:` block with 26 entries including the DESIGN.md system anchors.
- [ ] All 4 fixes verified via direct `agent_config.discover_primary_agents()` call against the worktree.
- [ ] No new missing-reference warnings introduced (pre-existing `bird` and `heygen-skill` warnings remain — out of scope).

## Files Scope

- .agents/automate.md
- .agents/legal.md
- .agents/research.md
- .agents/product.md
- TODO.md

## Background

Detected by inspecting current `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: 9 of 10 primary agents had `permission.task`, but Product had none. Cross-referenced opencode source to confirm `Wildcard.match()` semantics in `permission.task` (PRs #4773, #7165). PR #7271 was the original feature request — closed unmerged 2026-04-27 because the equivalent functionality had already shipped via #4773 and refactor #7165.

Glob-compression follow-up (e.g., `git*` instead of explicit `github-cli` + `gitlab-cli`) deferred to a separate PR — requires opencode runtime restart to validate that `Wildcard.match()` is actually invoked on `permission.task` keys at filtering time.

title: t2992: post-update cache priming routine to eliminate first-cycle stage cost
body:
## Task

After `aidevops update` deploys new code and restarts the pulse, the first cycle pays the full cold-cache cost: ~210s `prefetch_state` + ~144s `preflight_capacity_and_labels` + ~50s `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` + ~139s `deterministic_merge_pass` ≈ **8-10 minutes minimum** before any productive work happens. Add a separate cache-priming step to `aidevops update` (and a standalone routine) that pre-warms the prefetch caches and pulse state files BEFORE the new pulse starts cycle 1 — so the first post-restart cycle finds warm state and fits within ~3-5 minutes.

## Why

Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log` (last 30 cycles, 2026-04-27):

| Stage | Avg | n | Fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preflight_prefetch_and_scope` | 210s | 5 | 0 |
| `prefetch_state` | 209s | 5 | 0 |
| `preflight_capacity_and_labels` | 144s | 11 | 0 |
| `deterministic_merge_pass` | 139s | 5 | 0 |
| `normalize_active_issue_assignments` | 74s | 4 | 0 |
| `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` | 50s | 11 | 0 |

These are the **healthy** durations (fails=0). t2989 + t2988 fix the *hang* class; this task addresses the *cold-cache* class. They compose: even with all hang protection in place, post-restart cycle 1 still costs ~10 min because every cache file under `~/.aidevops/cache/` and `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/` is stale or missing.

User-visible symptom: "pulse stops being productive after every aidevops update for 10-20 minutes". Root cause: deploy succeeds → pulse restarts → cycle 1 spends 10 min warming → only THEN does merge_pass / fill_floor produce visible work. To the user the system looks frozen.

`prefetch_state` is already delta-aware (t1975, GH#15286 — only fetches items with `updatedAt > last_prefetch`), so a separate priming call doesn't double-fetch the next pulse cycle. It's a near-zero-cost pre-warm for the next cycle's "delta vs last_prefetch" window.

## How

### Phase A: post-deploy priming hook in `auto-update-helper.sh`

After deploy completes but BEFORE pulse restart:

```bash
# auto-update-helper.sh — after agent-deploy.sh succeeds, before pulse restart
if [[ "${AIDEVOPS_SKIP_CACHE_PRIME:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    log_info "Pre-warming pulse caches before restart..."
    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/pulse-cache-prime.sh" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE" || \
        log_warn "Cache priming failed — first cycle may be slow"
fi
"${SCRIPT_DIR}/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh" restart-if-running
```

Honor `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1` (already exists) — if pulse won't restart, priming is wasted.

### Phase B: NEW `pulse-cache-prime.sh`

Single-shot script that:

1. Sources `pulse-prefetch.sh` + `shared-constants.sh` for function access.
2. Calls `prefetch_state` once with current repo list (delta-aware — refreshes the cache and `last_prefetch` timestamp).
3. Calls `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh::_refresh_owner_issues` and `_refresh_owner_prs` directly to populate the per-owner JSON caches.
4. Touches `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-cache-prime-last-run` with epoch timestamp for observability.
5. Exits 0 on success, 1 on partial failure (caller logs but does not abort restart).

Reference pattern: `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` already has the per-owner refresh primitives — this script just orchestrates them outside a pulse cycle.

### Phase C: standalone routine

Add an `r0NN` routine entry in `TODO.md` `## Routines`:

```text
- [x] r0NN [cron(*/30 * * * *)] run:.agents/scripts/pulse-cache-prime.sh
```

Independent of `aidevops update`. Keeps caches warm across long quiet periods (overnight, weekends) so the first post-quiet cycle isn't slow either.

### Phase D: stats counter

Bump `pulse_cache_prime_runs` and `pulse_cache_prime_failures` in `pulse-stats.json` so cache-priming health is visible in `aidevops status`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pulse-cache-prime.sh` exists, ShellCheck zero, parseable.
- [ ] `auto-update-helper.sh` calls it after deploy, before restart, honouring `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_CACHE_PRIME=1` opt-out.
- [ ] After `aidevops update`: first post-restart cycle's `prefetch_state` duration drops by ≥50% (target: <100s vs current 210s) — measure via `pulse-stage-timings.log`.
- [ ] Routine entry registered; runs every 30 min when pulse is idle.
- [ ] `pulse_cache_prime_runs` counter increments on each successful prime.
- [ ] No regression in cycle-1 correctness — same dispatch decisions as without priming.
- [ ] AGENTS.md gains a "## Cache Priming" subsection under "Capabilities" or "Worker Diagnostics".

## Files Scope

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-cache-prime.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh` — call cache-prime before restart
- `EDIT: TODO.md` — register r0NN routine entry
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` — document the priming hook
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cache-prime.sh`

### Complexity Impact

`auto-update-helper.sh::cmd_update` (or equivalent) gains ~8 lines for the priming call. `pulse-cache-prime.sh` is a fresh file with one main function (~30 lines) and a small `main`. Well under all gate thresholds. No refactor required.

## Session Origin

Filed during interactive root-cause investigation of "pulse stops being productive after `aidevops update`" (2026-04-27 t2989 session). t2989 (#21383, PR #21385) fixed the *hang* class (single iteration consuming 600s parent stage). t2988 (#21380, PR #21384, merged) fixed the reconcile budget regression. This task addresses the residual ~10-min post-restart latency that is structural, not a bug — every cache file is cold after restart, and cycle 1 pays the full re-warm cost. User intuition: "if there's a big delay after update / lots of changes, perhaps it needs a separate cache priming routine?" — this task formalises that hypothesis.

Related but distinct from:

- t2989 (#21383) — per-iteration timeout for hung dispatch (deployed in PR #21385)
- t2988 (#21380) — reconcile budget regression (merged PR #21384)
- t2929 (#21153) — preflight_cleanup_and_ledger 47s improvement
- t1975 (GH#15286) — delta prefetch architecture (this task builds on it)

title: t2993: fix(task-id-guard): word-boundary regex to avoid false positives on subagent names like context7
body:
## Task

Tighten the Task-ID Collision Guard's t-ID extraction regex to use word boundaries, eliminating false positives on subagent or library names that contain `t<digits>` as a substring (e.g., `context7`).

## Why

`_extract_tids` in `.agents/hooks/task-id-guard.sh:323` uses `grep -oE 't[0-9]+'` with no anchor. When `_check_pr_title` (line 568) concatenates PR title and body and runs this regex, it picks up incidental matches inside subagent/library names:

- `context7` → `t7`
- `gpt4` → `t4` (would match if `gpt4` ever appeared in a title/body)
- `wp7-cms`, `next13`, etc. — any token where a `t` is followed by digits

In each case the guard then asks "is `t7` a claimed task on this branch / repo / linked issue?", finds nothing (because `t7` is not the t-ID being referenced), and BLOCKS the PR with a `[task-id-guard][VIOLATION]` exit 1.

Concrete failure: t2991 PR #21397. Title contained only `t2991` (legitimately claimed). Body contained `context7` in a Product allowlist composition list. Guard extracted `{t2991, t7}`, validated `t2991` against the claim commit on the branch, then rejected `t7` as unclaimed.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/hooks/task-id-guard.sh:323` — change `grep -oE 't[0-9]+'` to a word-boundary-anchored equivalent that GNU+BSD grep both support. POSIX ERE doesn't support `\b`, so use a leading boundary class. Recommended: `grep -oE '(^|[^a-zA-Z0-9])t[0-9]+\b'` then strip the leading non-alphanumeric character. Or pre-process the input with `sed 's/[a-zA-Z0-9]\(t[0-9]\+\)/\1/g'` to remove suffixes preceded by alphanumerics, then run the existing regex.

- **EDIT:** `.agents/hooks/task-id-guard.sh:336` — the `_extract_xref_issues` regex on this line (`(Resolves|Closes|Fixes|Ref|For)[[:space:]]+#[0-9]+`) is already correctly anchored on the keyword side. No change needed; mention here for cross-reference.

### Reference pattern

The Drizzle migration auto-classifier in `pulse-merge-feedback.sh::_classify_conflicts_by_pattern` uses similar boundary-aware path matching against the `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf` registry. That pattern (anchor + match + de-anchor) is the canonical approach for "match a thing only when it's a standalone token".

### Verification

```bash
# Add a fixture to .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-guard.sh covering:
# - Title: "t2991: fix something using context7"
# - Branch claim commit: "chore: claim t2991"
# Expected: exit 0, no violation. Without this fix, exits 1 with "t7 unclaimed".

# Existing test surface:
```

title: t2994: move pulse cache priming hook into pulse-wrapper.sh boot path
body:
## Task

t2992 wired the cache priming call into `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh::_start`. Verification on the deployed v3.13.2 system shows this never fires under launchd-managed deployments because:

- `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` runs `pulse-wrapper.sh` DIRECTLY
- launchd `KeepAlive` respawns it within ~1s of exit
- `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh::_restart` does `stop → sleep 3 → start`; launchd respawns during the 3-second window
- `_start` sees pulse already running (launchd's respawn won) → early returns → priming skipped

Evidence: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cache-prime.log` was empty after `aidevops update` deployed v3.13.2 + restarted pulse, but populated correctly when invoked manually:

```text
[2026-04-27T18:44:24Z] Starting cache prime (t2992)...
search_calls=0 cache_writes=6 errors=22
[2026-04-27T18:44:49Z] Cache prime succeeded in 25s
```

## Why

The lifecycle-helper hook only catches manually-invoked restarts. Under macOS launchd (and the equivalent on Linux/systemd), the pulse boot path is the launchd plist → pulse-wrapper.sh directly — same architecture other framework users will have. **The priming hook MUST live where every pulse boot is forced through, not where lifecycle-helper happens to call.** That is `pulse-wrapper.sh` itself, after instance-lock acquisition.

## How

### Phase A: relocate priming call

EDIT `pulse-wrapper.sh`: locate the "Instance lock acquired via mkdir" log line. Immediately AFTER it (lock acquired = this invocation owns the pulse for the duration), and BEFORE the main cycle loop begins, call:

```bash
# t2992 cache priming — pre-warm L3 per-owner JSON caches before first cycle.
# Lock-gated: only runs in the actual pulse boot, not duplicate launchd
# invocations that exit on lock contention. Honours AIDEVOPS_SKIP_CACHE_PRIME=1.
if [[ "${AIDEVOPS_SKIP_CACHE_PRIME:-0}" != "1" && -x "$AGENTS_DIR/scripts/pulse-cache-prime.sh" ]]; then
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Pre-warming caches (t2992)..." >&2
    "$AGENTS_DIR/scripts/pulse-cache-prime.sh" || \
        echo "[pulse-wrapper] Cache prime returned non-zero (non-fatal)" >&2
fi
```

EDIT `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh::_start`: REMOVE the t2992 priming call. The duplication was harmless but wasteful (~25s × 2). pulse-wrapper.sh now primes itself.

### Phase B: verify

After deploy + pulse restart:

1. `tail -50 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cache-prime.log` — should show `Cache prime succeeded` with timestamp matching pulse boot time
2. `jq '.counters.pulse_cache_prime_runs | length' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json` — should increment by 1 per pulse boot
3. `tail -30 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` — should show `Pre-warming caches (t2992)` message
4. First post-restart cycle's `prefetch_state` should drop from ~210s to <100s (the original t2992 acceptance criterion)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Priming hook relocated to pulse-wrapper.sh (after lock, before main loop)
- [ ] Lifecycle-helper duplicate priming call removed
- [ ] Honours `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_CACHE_PRIME=1` opt-out
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Pulse cache priming" section updated to reflect pulse-wrapper.sh location
- [ ] After deploy: pulse-cache-prime.log shows entry within 30s of pulse boot
- [ ] First post-restart `prefetch_state` <100s in pulse-stage-timings.log
- [ ] ShellCheck zero on changed files

## Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh — add priming call after lock acquisition
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh — remove duplicate priming from _start
- EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md — update Worker Diagnostics §Pulse cache priming

### Complexity Impact

pulse-wrapper.sh gains ~6 lines for the priming call. pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh::_start LOSES ~8 lines (removing duplicate). Net negative line count. No function complexity gate impact.

## Session Origin

Filed during interactive verification of v3.13.2 deploy (2026-04-27). t2992 PR #21398 merged + deployed but priming log remained empty post-restart. Root cause traced to launchd KeepAlive respawning pulse-wrapper.sh directly, racing the lifecycle-helper's stop→sleep 3→start sequence. The architecture assumption that lifecycle-helper is the universal boot choke point holds for Linux/manual deployments but NOT for launchd/systemd-managed ones.

title: t2996: dispatch_with_dedup hits t2989 30s timeout consistently — too many serial gh calls
body:
## Task

`dispatch_with_dedup` consistently hits the t2989 30s per-candidate timeout on auto-dispatch issues that get deep into the gate pipeline. Reduce the cumulative gh API call count, parallelize independent calls, or pass already-loaded metadata through to downstream gates.

## Why

Empirical evidence from 2026-04-27 cycle (PID 44617):

```text
fill_floor_candidate_3050    33s   rc=124 (timeout)
fill_floor_candidate_3078    32s   rc=124 (timeout)
fill_floor_candidate_3012    32s   rc=124 (timeout)
fill_floor_candidate_21390   32s   rc=124 (timeout)
fill_floor_candidate_21403   32s   rc=124 (timeout)
fill_floor_candidate_21387   32s   rc=124 (timeout)
fill_floor_candidate_3361    31s   rc=1   (just under wire — substantive work, no dispatch)
fill_floor_candidate_3366    31s   rc=1   (just under wire)
fill_floor_candidate_3278    24s   rc=1
```

`pulse-stats.json` shows 37 fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout events.

Root cause hypothesis: `dispatch_with_dedup` makes 10–15 serial gh API calls per candidate that gets past the cheap label checks:

1. `gh issue view --json number,title,state,labels,assignees` (pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1088)
2. `gh issue view --json body` (pulse-dispatch-core.sh:947 — for blocked-by check)
3. `_check_nmr_approval_gate` (`gh api .../comments`)
4. `_check_commit_subject_dedup_gate` (git log + maybe gh)
5. `_issue_needs_consolidation` (`gh issue view --json labels` AND `gh api .../comments --paginate`) — pulse-triage.sh:297, 338
6. `_issue_targets_large_files` (`gh issue view --json labels` AND `gh issue view --json title`) — pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:764, 795
7. `_footprint_check_overlap` (gh search)
8. `check_dispatch_dedup` → dispatch-dedup-helper.sh (more gh calls)
9. `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief` (`gh issue view --json body` again — pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1197)
10. `_run_tier_simple_body_shape_check` (body lookup)
11. `_run_predispatch_validator` (validator helper, may clone repo)
12. `_run_eligibility_gate_or_abort` (final gate)

Each gh call: ~0.5-2s typically; under load can spike to 5s+. 10 calls × 2-3s avg = 20-30s, putting every dispatch on the timeout cliff.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:867-1146` — `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers` and surrounding body-loading helpers
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:747-833` — `_issue_targets_large_files` (extra `gh issue view --json labels/title` calls)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh:292-339` — `_issue_needs_consolidation` (gh issue view + paginated comments)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:489-506` — `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` (timeout enforcement)
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh` — regression test bounding gh call count per dispatch

### Investigation steps

1. **Audit serial vs parallel:** Many of the gh calls are independent. The metadata load (line 1088) already fetches `labels` and `title` — pass that through to `_issue_needs_consolidation` and `_issue_targets_large_files` instead of re-fetching.
2. **Single-call optimization:** Combine `gh issue view --json number,title,state,labels,assignees,body` (one call instead of two) so `_dispatch_issue_body` (line 947) and `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief` (line 1197) share the same body fetch.
3. **Cache by candidate:** Within a single `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers` call, cache the issue body and labels in shell vars so downstream gates don't re-fetch.
4. **Parallelize where safe:** `_check_commit_subject_dedup_gate` (git log) and `_footprint_check_overlap` (gh search) are independent — run in parallel via background subshells with bounded wait.

### Reference pattern

Model on `_pulse_prime_caches_if_stale` (t2994, pulse-wrapper.sh:1477) for the "load once, pass through" pattern. Model the test on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cache-prime.sh`.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh
# Live check after deploy: timeout count should drop to near-zero over 24h
jq '.counters.fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout | length' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json
# Live check: average fill_floor candidate duration should drop below 15s
awk '/fill_floor_candidate/ {sum+=$3; n++} END {if (n>0) print sum/n}' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Number of gh calls per `dispatch_with_dedup` invocation reduced to ≤ 5 (from current 10-15)
- [ ] Regression test bounds gh-call count per dispatch and fails CI if regressed
- [ ] `fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout` counter drops to <5 events per 24h after deploy (vs 37 in last 24h)
- [ ] Average `fill_floor_candidate_*` stage duration drops below 15s
- [ ] No new shellcheck violations

title: t2997: mktemp templates with XXXXXX before extension are BSD-broken — 17+ callsites
body:
## Task

`mktemp` templates with `XXXXXX` followed by a `.ext` suffix (e.g., `.json`, `.log`, `.py`) are silently broken on macOS BSD `mktemp`. The first call returns the literal template name unchanged; subsequent calls fail with `mkstemp failed: File exists`. ~17-20 production callsites are affected. Audit, fix, and add a CI gate.

## Why

Direct evidence reproduced 2026-04-27:

```bash
# macOS BSD mktemp (default) — broken
$ mktemp /tmp/test-XXXXXX.json
/tmp/test-XXXXXX.json    # literal! NOT a random name
$ mktemp /tmp/test-XXXXXX.json
mktemp: mkstemp failed on /tmp/test-XXXXXX.json: File exists

# macOS BSD mktemp — works
$ mktemp /tmp/test-XXXXXX
/tmp/test-gYjQlj         # correct: random suffix
$ mktemp /tmp/test.json.XXXXXX
/tmp/test.json.TW5AIa    # correct: random suffix at end
```

Live impact (today's pulse-wrapper.log): 142 spam lines like:

```text
mktemp: mkstemp failed on /Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/logs/.pulse-tier-last-check-XXXXXX.json: File exists
```

Originating from `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:1107` in `update_repo_tier_check_timestamp`. When multiple pulse-wrapper PIDs are alive briefly during launchd respawn races, all attempt to create the same literal filename → collision.

When the literal-named temp file does get moved/unlinked, the function silently fails for the duration of the race window — meaning tier check timestamps don't get persisted reliably.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:1107` — `update_repo_tier_check_timestamp` (the canonical offender, 142 spam lines/day)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh:69, 204, 267` — pulse-archive, cycle-index, health
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/verify-brief.sh:662` — verify-brief-runtime
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:370` — aidevops-worker-auth (mktemp -d)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:210, 1096` — aidevops-empty-gaps.py, aidevops-canary
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh:399, 467, 780, 1044, 1256` — browser-qa-* mjs scripts
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1455` — pulse-stats-src
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh:75, 165` — pulse-stats
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/codacy-collector-helper.sh:242, 522, 523` — codacy-resp, codacy-sql, codacy-jq
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh:754, 860, 1064` — contest-summaries, contest-score, contest-judges
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/cch-canary.sh:103` — cch-canary-debug
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/document-extraction-helper.sh:461` — classify-XXXXXX.png
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/anti-detect-helper.sh:1034` — warmup_XXXXXX.py
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh:754` — contest-summaries
- (full list — run `rg -nP 'mktemp\s+(?!-d\s+|-u\s+).*X{6}[^X]+'` to confirm scope)
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/lint-mktemp-portability.sh` — CI lint script
- `NEW: .github/workflows/mktemp-portability-check.yml` — CI gate (runs on PR)

### Fix pattern

Two valid forms, choose per callsite:

```bash
# Form A: X's at end (BSD-compatible, GNU-compatible)
mktemp "${dir}/prefix-XXXXXX"

# Form B: extension before X's (BSD-compatible, GNU-compatible)
mktemp "${dir}/prefix.ext.XXXXXX"

# AVOID: extension AFTER X's (macOS-broken)
mktemp "${dir}/prefix-XXXXXX.ext"   # ← do not use
```

Form A is preferred when the caller doesn't need the extension. Form B is preferred when downstream tools require the extension for behaviour (e.g., `python file.tmp.XXXXXX.py` will not be auto-recognized; in that case use `cp tmp tmpname.py` after mktemp).

### Reference pattern

Existing fix elsewhere in the codebase: `pulse-stats-helper.sh:75` already uses `pulse-stats-XXXXXX.json` (broken). Compare with `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` patterns that use `XXXXXX` at end (working). Codify Form A in `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` `§ mktemp`.

### Verification

```bash
# Local check for any remaining offenders
rg -nP 'mktemp\s+(?!-d\s+|-u\s+).*X{6}[^X]+' .agents/scripts/

# Each fixed file should pass shellcheck
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh

# CI gate must reject any new instance of the broken pattern
bash .agents/scripts/lint-mktemp-portability.sh

# Live check after deploy: 0 mktemp errors in pulse-wrapper.log
rg -c "mkstemp failed" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] All ~17-20 production callsites fixed using Form A or Form B
- [ ] CI gate `lint-mktemp-portability.sh` blocks new introductions of the broken pattern
- [ ] `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` documents the pattern under `§ mktemp`
- [ ] Live `mkstemp failed` count drops to 0 over 24h after deploy
- [ ] No new shellcheck violations
- [ ] Test files (`tests/test-*.sh`) excluded from the fix where they are intentionally testing mktemp behaviour

title: t2999: dispatch-ledger-helper: stale-lock recovery (24-day-old lock disabled all registration)
body:
## What

Fix `_acquire_lock` in `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` to detect and recover from stale lock dirs.

## Why

A stale lock dir at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/dispatch-ledger.lock.d` from April 3, 2026 silently disabled dispatch ledger registration for **24+ days** (~1.7M seconds). Every worker dispatch since — both pulse and manual — has emitted "Dispatch ledger registration failed (non-fatal)" warnings.

Operational symptoms observed during the 2026-04-27 GH search-degradation incident recovery:

- Lock dir mtime stuck at Apr 3 17:12 UTC for 24 days
- `mkdir` retry loop in `_acquire_lock` (lines 78-85) loops 50× × 0.1s = 5s timeout, then returns rc=1
- All 3 manual workers dispatched during recovery had to be backfilled into the ledger after manual cleanup
- 233 completed + 396 failed entries in ledger reflect this breakage

Root cause: the mkdir-based fallback path (lines 73-86) has NO stale-lock recovery. `pulse-instance-lock.sh` already has the canonical pattern (PID file inside lock dir + age-based force-reclaim via `PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S=1800`).

## How

1. `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh:66-88` — replace simple busy-wait mkdir loop with stale-detection logic:
   - On mkdir fail: read `${lock_dir}/pid` file
   - If PID alive: short retry loop (current behaviour)
   - If PID dead OR age > `AIDEVOPS_LEDGER_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S` (default 60s — much shorter than pulse-instance because ledger ops are sub-second): `rmdir` + retry mkdir
   - Write `$$` to `${lock_dir}/pid` after successful mkdir (mirror pulse pattern)
2. Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh::_handle_existing_lock` — lines 70-115
3. `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` — add regression tests

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_acquire_lock` detects and recovers from stale locks (PID dead OR age > threshold)
- [ ] Lock dir contains PID file after acquisition
- [ ] Concurrent-access semantics preserved (lock still mutex when live owner present)
- [ ] Regression test added covering: stale-with-dead-PID, stale-with-old-mtime, live-owner-blocks
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh

## Complexity Impact

`_acquire_lock` currently 23 lines (66-88). Adding stale-detection branch will add ~30 lines, projected ~50 lines post-change. Well below 100-line gate. New helper `_handle_stale_ledger_lock` likely 20 lines.

## Session Origin

Filed during interactive recovery from 2026-04-27 GH search-degradation incident. Discovered stale lock blocking ledger registration when investigating "Dispatch ledger registration failed (non-fatal)" warnings on manually-dispatched workers.

title: t3000: dispatch-single-issue-helper: apply pulse-parity ceremony pre-launch
body:
## Task

Extend `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` to apply dispatch ceremony parity with the canonical pulse path before worker launch:

1. Apply `status:queued` (replacing whatever status is present) atomically via `set_issue_status`.
2. Add `origin:worker` and remove `origin:interactive` / `origin:worker-takeover` in the same edit.
3. Add the runner as assignee and remove any prior assignees in the same edit.

This mirrors `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh::_dlw_assign_and_label` exactly.

## Why

Discovered during the 2026-04-27 GitHub search degradation incident: 3 framework workers (#21406/#21407/#21408) launched manually via `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` did NOT receive the dispatch ceremony the pulse normally applies. Concrete failure mode:

- **Pulse double-dispatch risk**: with no status transition, the next pulse cycle saw the issue in its previous state (typically `status:available` with no assignee after the operator unassigned to clear a dedup block) — eligible for dispatch — and could spawn a second worker on top of the running one. I had to manually run `set_issue_status N slug in-progress` after each launch as a stopgap.
- **Origin label drift**: when the operator dispatches a worker via the helper after a `claim-task-id.sh` self-claim, the issue keeps `origin:interactive` even though a worker is now running it. Downstream auto-merge logic and the t2189 idle-handover both branch on origin labels — wrong label = wrong behaviour.
- **Assignee race**: if the issue had a different assignee (e.g. the issue creator), the dispatcher does not normalise to runner-self, leaving co-assignment ambiguity that confuses dedup layer 6 (the same class of bug `_dlw_assign_and_label` was hardened against in pulse).

The helper's top-of-file design comment names a trade-off ("deliberately bypasses 9+ post-claim gates — minimal smoke-test path"). But ownership claim is not a gate — it is the per-launch state mutation that makes a worker visible to dedup. The smoke-test argument doesn't apply.

## Correction from initial filing

This issue was originally filed asking for `status:in-progress` + an interactive claim stamp + ledger registration. After reading the canonical pulse pattern more carefully:

- `status:in-progress` is wrong — pulse uses `status:queued`. Workers transition queued→in-progress themselves when they begin work. Setting `in-progress` from the dispatcher is premature.
- Interactive claim stamps via `interactive-session-helper.sh write-stamp` are not applicable for headless workers — those only apply to interactive sessions. Workers are tracked via the dispatch ledger, which is already registered at line 578.
- Ledger registration already exists in the helper (line 578) — the visible silent failure during the incident was caused by the t2999 stale lock, fixed in PR #21428.

The corrected scope is just the pre-launch label/assignee atomic edit.

## How

Add `_dsi_apply_dispatch_ceremony()` mirroring `_dlw_assign_and_label`. Call it after the dedup check passes and before `_dsi_create_worktree`. Gate behind a `--no-ceremony` flag (default OFF, ceremony default ON).

### Files Scope
- .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh

### Reference patterns
- pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh::_dlw_assign_and_label (lines 80-101) — the canonical ceremony block.
- shared-gh-wrappers.sh::set_issue_status (lines 1646-1700) — atomic status transition with extra-flag passthrough.

### Acceptance
1. Manual launch via dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh applies `status:queued` on the target issue before launch.
2. `origin:worker` is applied; `origin:interactive` and `origin:worker-takeover` are removed in the same edit.
3. Runner is added as assignee; any prior assignees are removed in the same edit.
4. New test `test_dispatch_ceremony` covers all three mutations.
5. `--no-ceremony` flag preserves the current pre-t3000 behaviour (no label/assignee edits).
6. shellcheck passes clean.

### Complexity Impact
Estimate: ceremony block adds ~30 lines (one function `_dsi_apply_dispatch_ceremony` + arg parser update + one call site). dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh body ~737 lines; no function crosses the 100-line gate.

## Files to modify
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh — add `_dsi_apply_dispatch_ceremony()`; add `--no-ceremony` to `_dsi_parse_dispatch_args`; call ceremony before `_dsi_create_worktree` in `cmd_dispatch`.
- EDIT or NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh — add regression test.

title: t3001: Add gh-status-helper for incident detection + incident recovery runbook
body:
## Why

During the 2026-04-27 GitHub-search degradation incident, the pulse cycle
silently degraded for ~50 minutes before it was diagnosed. Symptoms:

- Workers killed at 91-92s with rc=124 (per-candidate timeout).
- Pulse cycles taking 25+ minutes to complete (vs. the normal sub-5-minute).
- `gh search` returning empty results despite open issues being present.

The diagnosis required a human operator to manually visit
`githubstatus.com`, eyeball the incident, and post correlation comments on
each affected issue. There was no programmatic check anywhere in the
framework that says "is GitHub healthy right now?". A passing `gh auth
status` and a returning `gh api rate_limit` are both consistent with a
silently-degrading search backend.

Two follow-on costs:

- The same diagnosis would need to be redone manually at every future
  incident (and there's roughly one degradation event every 1-2 weeks based
  on githubstatus.com history).
- New operators have no canonical recovery runbook — the t2999 ledger lock
  and t3000 manual-dispatch ceremony fixes resolve the failure modes but
  don't document the operator-facing recovery procedure.

## What

Two artefacts:

1. **`.agents/scripts/gh-status-helper.sh`** — shell helper that queries
   `https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/status.json` and
   `https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/incidents/unresolved.json` and
   classifies the response. Subcommands:

   - `check` — single-shot status check; prints one-line summary; exit 0
     `operational` / 1 `degraded` / 2 `outage`. Designed for diagnostics
     scripts and CI gates.
   - `incidents` — list active incidents with name, impact, components,
     started-at, latest update. Empty list when GitHub is healthy.
   - `correlate` — for diagnostic comments on incident-affected issues:
     prints a markdown block that can be appended to an issue/PR comment
     correlating the local symptom timestamp to the GitHub status state
     at that moment.

   Surface the `--json` flag on all subcommands for programmatic callers
   (`pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`, future hooks).

2. **`.agents/reference/incident-recovery-runbook.md`** — operator-facing
   recovery runbook covering:

   - When to suspect a GitHub-platform incident (workers killed at
     ~per-candidate-timeout, pulse cycles >25min, `gh search` empty
     responses, rate_limit healthy but operations failing).
   - How to confirm via `gh-status-helper.sh check` and
     `gh-status-helper.sh incidents`.
   - Stale ledger lock recovery (cross-link to t2999 / PR #21428 and
     `pulse-lock-recovery.md`).
   - Manual single-issue dispatch with pulse-parity ceremony (cross-link
     to t3000 / PR #21430 — `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` with
     ceremony default ON).
   - Posting status-correlation comments on affected issues
     (`gh-status-helper.sh correlate`).
   - Post-incident verification checklist (rate limits recovered, pulse
     cycle time back to baseline, ledger health, downstream-repo dispatch
     resumed).

## How

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/gh-status-helper.sh` — model on
  `memory-helper.sh` (CLI shape with subcommands + `--help` + `--json`).
  Source `shared-constants.sh` for colors / `safe_grep_count` etc. Use
  `curl` (already a framework dependency) — no new deps. Cache the API
  response at `~/.aidevops/cache/gh-status-{status,incidents}.json` for
  60 seconds so repeated `check` calls within a minute don't hit the API
  rate limit (githubstatus.com Statuspage allows ~100 req/min per IP).
  All curl calls go through the existing `allowed-urls.txt` list —
  `www.githubstatus.com` is already there (verified).
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-status-helper.sh` — model on
  `tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (the t3000 test file).
  Mock `curl` via PATH override to return canned API responses
  (operational, single-incident, multi-incident, network-failure).
  At least 8 assertions covering each subcommand and exit code.
- `NEW: .agents/reference/incident-recovery-runbook.md` — model on
  `reference/pulse-lock-recovery.md` (Overview / Behaviour / Audit
  Trail structure). Length budget: ~150 lines, focused on the
  operator's decision tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gh-status-helper.sh check` exits 0 when GitHub is healthy, 1
      when degraded, 2 when outage; one-line summary on stdout.
- [ ] `gh-status-helper.sh incidents` lists active incidents with name,
      impact, components, started-at; empty when healthy.
- [ ] `gh-status-helper.sh correlate` produces a markdown-formatted
      block suitable for `gh issue comment`.
- [ ] All three subcommands support `--json` for programmatic callers.
- [ ] 60-second response cache at `~/.aidevops/cache/gh-status-*.json`
      to avoid hammering the Statuspage API.
- [ ] Test file passes with `bash tests/test-gh-status-helper.sh`
      (≥8 assertions covering all subcommands + cache behaviour +
      network-failure handling).
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations on both new files.
- [ ] `incident-recovery-runbook.md` cross-links pulse-lock-recovery.md,
      t2999 (PR #21428), and t3000 (PR #21430).
- [ ] No new dependencies (uses existing `curl` + `jq` only).
- [ ] `www.githubstatus.com` allowlist entry verified — no
      `allowed-urls.txt` change needed.

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-status-helper.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-status-helper.sh
# exit 0

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-status-helper.sh
# ≥8 assertions, all pass

# Live smoke test (only when not under rate-limit):
.agents/scripts/gh-status-helper.sh check
# operational | degraded | outage + exit code 0/1/2

.agents/scripts/gh-status-helper.sh incidents
# empty when healthy, list when degraded

# Cache verified:
ls -la ~/.aidevops/cache/gh-status-*.json
# Files exist after first check, age <60s
```

## Context

- 2026-04-27 GH-search degradation incident: #21406, #21407, #21408 (all
  closed/merged), #21426 (postmortem).
- Companion fixes:
  - PR #21428 (t2999) — ledger stale lock recovery
  - PR #21430 (t3000) — manual dispatch ceremony parity
- Reference patterns:
  - `.agents/scripts/memory-helper.sh` — CLI shape with subcommands
  - `.agents/reference/pulse-lock-recovery.md` — runbook structure
  - `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` — test
    file model
- Allowlist (already populated): `.agents/configs/allowed-urls.txt`
  contains `www.githubstatus.com`.
- Statuspage API docs: https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2 (the API is
  Atlassian Statuspage, used by GitHub — same JSON schema applies to any
  Statuspage-backed service).

title: t3002: pulse-wrapper singleton lock fails across launchd / aidevops-update concurrency
body:
## Task

Pulse-wrapper.sh's mkdir-based singleton lock fails to prevent multiple concurrent pulse instances when launchd KeepAlive races with `aidevops update` lifecycle calls.

## Why (observed t2999/t3000/t3001 trilogy session 2026-04-27)

Found 4 concurrent pulse-wrapper.sh PIDs running simultaneously. All claimed `[pulse-wrapper] Instance lock acquired via mkdir`. Side symptoms included flooding `mktemp: mkstemp failed on /Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/logs/.pulse-tier-last-check-XXXXXX.json: File exists` errors (those mktemp errors are independently fixed by t2997 / PR #21421, but appearing here proves multiple instances were active concurrently).

Hypothesised root cause: launchd's `KeepAlive` respawned pulse during `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running`'s `stop -> sleep -> start` window, then `aidevops update`'s ensure-running `start` call at the end of `cmd_update` started a SECOND instance because the launchd-respawned one wasn't yet visible to the lock check, OR the lock dir was acquired by the dying pulse but its trap-cleanup hadn't run yet.

Symptoms downstream:
- GraphQL rate-limit pressure 4x normal (each instance prefetches independently, exhausting the read budget)
- Pulse cycle stalls because each cycle competes for read-side caches and ledger locks
- Trilogy auto-merge delayed (pulse couldn't reach the merge stage cleanly)

Killing 3 of 4 instances and letting launchd respawn ONE cleanly resolved the symptoms immediately.

## How

Investigate the lock/respawn interaction in:
- `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — mkdir lock acquisition path; verify the lock survives across SIGTERM and is reclaimed by the respawn.
- `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — `_stop`/`_start`/`restart-if-running` sequencing; verify the helper waits long enough after `_stop` for launchd to NOT have respawned yet.
- `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/aidevops.sh::cmd_update` — the ensure-running idempotent `start` at end of update; verify it's a true no-op when launchd has already respawned.
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` — `KeepAlive`, `ThrottleInterval`, and `RunAtLoad` interaction.

Possible fixes:
1. Lock dir should include PID, and pulse-wrapper.sh should verify the recorded PID is alive at startup; if dead, reclaim; if a different live PID, exit.
2. `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` should `launchctl unload` the plist before stop, then `launchctl load` after start, so launchd doesn't respawn during the stop/start window.
3. Add a "kill duplicates" path: if startup detects another live pulse-wrapper PID via `pgrep -f`, the newer instance exits immediately (older wins).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Reproduce: trigger the race condition (e.g. simulate `aidevops update` while launchd respawns) and observe N>1 pulse instances
- [ ] Lock behaviour: verify only ONE pulse-wrapper.sh PID can hold the lock at any moment
- [ ] Test: regression test that simulates the race and asserts singleton invariant
- [ ] Diagnostic: `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` reports lock holder PID and warns on multiple PIDs
- [ ] No regression: `aidevops update` end-to-end leaves exactly one pulse running

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/aidevops.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-singleton-lock.sh (NEW)

## Complexity Impact

Likely small — adds PID verification on lock dir + duplicate-detection startup check. Estimated <50-line addition.

title: t3003: adaptive per-candidate dispatch timeout based on rolling-window measurement
body:
## Task

Replace fixed `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` (default 30s) with adaptive per-candidate timeout based on rolling-window measurement of recent dispatch attempts. Must ship as v3.13.5 to unblock max-concurrency for all users (alex-solovyev report + this incident: 0 workers spawned for 30+ min because gh API latency drifted from ~2s to ~5s/call after the GitHub search-degradation incident, exhausting the 30s budget).

## Why (incident evidence)

Direct measurements 2026-04-27 23:55Z:

- `gh issue edit 21412 --add-label "tier:standard"` → **3.6s** for ONE label add
- `set_issue_status 21411 ... in-progress + add-label + add-assignee` → **15.4s** for ONE multi-flag edit
- `_dispatch_launch_worker` calls `_dlw_assign_and_label` (multi-flag edit, ~10-15s) + `lock_issue_for_worker` (gh issue lock, ~3-5s) + `_dlw_post_launch_hooks` (more gh calls)
- Cumulative dispatch path: **15-30s under healthy gh latency, 30-90s+ under degraded gh latency**

With a fixed 30s timeout: every candidate hits the cliff, every dispatch posts a `CLAIM_WON` comment that goes nowhere, and zero workers spawn. Manual env override to 90s is per-machine; alex-solovyev and other users have the same regression.

GH API latency is NOT a constant — it varies with global GitHub load, search-index lag, and provider-side incidents. A fixed timeout will always be either:

- Too tight (kills legitimate work during slow periods → 0 workers)
- Too loose (wastes minutes per cycle when one bad candidate hangs)

## How

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh` — core helper with `record`/`recommend`/`stats`/`reset` subcommands.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` calls the helper before timeout, and records outcome after.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh` — surface `dispatch_timing_p50` / `dispatch_timing_p95` / `dispatch_timing_recommended_timeout` counters for observability.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-timing-helper.sh` — regression tests covering: bootstrap default, EWMA convergence, probe-mode escalation, MAX_TIMEOUT clamp, file-corruption recovery.

### Algorithm (probe-and-adapt with EWMA)

State file: `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/dispatch-timing-stats.jsonl` (append-only, one record per attempt).

Record schema: `{"ts":"ISO8601","repo":"owner/repo","issue":NNN,"outcome":"success|timeout|skip","elapsed_ms":N,"timeout_used_ms":N,"probe":bool}`.

`recommend` algorithm:

1. Read last N records (default N=20).
2. Filter to `outcome=="success"` records.
3. If <3 successes in window → return BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT (90000 ms).
4. Else compute EWMA of elapsed_ms (alpha=0.3, weights recent more).
5. recommended = `max(EWMA × 2.0, p95(elapsed_ms))`.
6. If LAST record was a timeout AND no recovery yet → enter PROBE_MODE: recommended = `min(MAX_TIMEOUT, last_timeout_used × 2)`.
7. Clamp: `MIN_TIMEOUT (30000) ≤ recommended ≤ MAX_TIMEOUT (300000)`.

`record` algorithm:

1. Append JSON line atomically (`>> "$file" || ...` with mutex via `mkdir`-lock).
2. Trim file to last 1000 records (rotate to `.1.jsonl` archive on overflow).

### Probe mode

After ANY timeout, the next dispatch is a "probe" — gets `2 × last_timeout_used_ms` budget. If probe succeeds, exit probe mode and re-run EWMA on the now-updated successful records. If probe fails, escalate to `4 × last_timeout_used_ms`, capped at MAX_TIMEOUT. Three consecutive probe failures → emit a stuck-pulse advisory comment via gh-status-helper (t3001).

### Wiring in `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout`

```bash
_dff_dispatch_with_timeout() {
    local issue_number="$1"
    local repo_slug="$2"

    # t3003: adaptive timeout (replaces fixed FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT)
    local timeout_ms timeout_s
    timeout_ms=$(dispatch-timing-helper.sh recommend 2>/dev/null || echo 90000)
    timeout_s=$((timeout_ms / 1000))

    local start_epoch_ms outcome="timeout" elapsed_ms
    start_epoch_ms=$(($(date +%s%N) / 1000000))

    local dispatch_rc=0
    run_stage_with_timeout "fill_floor_candidate_${issue_number}" "$timeout_s" \
        dispatch_with_dedup "$@" || dispatch_rc=$?

    elapsed_ms=$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 - start_epoch_ms ))
    case "$dispatch_rc" in
        0) outcome="success" ;;
        124) outcome="timeout" ;;
        *) outcome="skip" ;;
    esac

    dispatch-timing-helper.sh record \
        --repo "$repo_slug" --issue "$issue_number" \
        --outcome "$outcome" --elapsed-ms "$elapsed_ms" \
        --timeout-used-ms "$timeout_ms" 2>/dev/null || true

    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Adaptive: dispatch_with_dedup rc=${dispatch_rc} elapsed=${elapsed_ms}ms timeout=${timeout_s}s for #${issue_number}" >>"$LOGFILE"

    # ... existing timeout handling ...
    return "$dispatch_rc"
}
```

### Reference patterns

- `pulse-stats-helper.sh` — JSONL append-with-mutex pattern for state files.
- `gh-api-instrument.sh` — TSV append with rotation (similar concern).
- `gh-status-helper.sh` (t3001) — cache-with-TTL pattern for state files.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dispatch-timing-helper.sh recommend` returns a value in `[MIN_TIMEOUT, MAX_TIMEOUT]` regardless of state-file state (clean / partial / corrupted).
- [ ] After 5 successful dispatches at 4s each → recommend ≈ 8000ms (2× EWMA).
- [ ] After 1 timeout → probe-mode kicks in for next attempt with 2× budget.
- [ ] Three consecutive probe failures → advisory comment posted (mock-tested).
- [ ] State file rotation on 1000-record overflow.
- [ ] Concurrent-write safe (two pulse iterations, mkdir lock).
- [ ] `pulse-stats.json` exposes `dispatch_timing_p50`, `dispatch_timing_p95`, `dispatch_timing_recommended_timeout`.
- [ ] No regression: existing `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` env still works as a hard MAX_TIMEOUT override (default 300s ceiling).
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations.
- [ ] Function-complexity gate clean (helper functions <100 lines).
- [ ] Bash 3.2 compatible.
- [ ] Test suite passes (regression test included).

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-timing-helper.sh

## Complexity Impact

- `dispatch-timing-helper.sh`: NEW file, projected ~250 lines split across `cmd_recommend` (~40 lines), `cmd_record` (~30 lines), `cmd_stats` (~30 lines), `_compute_ewma` (~20 lines), `_acquire_lock`/`_release_lock` (~30 lines), CLI dispatch + help (~50 lines).
- `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_dff_dispatch_with_timeout`: currently 17 lines, projected ~30-35 lines after adding adaptive call. Stays well below 100.

## Session Origin

Filed during recovery from 2026-04-27 GitHub search-degradation incident. Discovered when monitoring trilogy auto-merge recovery: pulse spawned 0 workers for 30+ min because every dispatch timed out at 30s while gh API latency was 3-5s/call (vs <2s pre-incident). User explicitly requested an adaptive approach. Must ship as v3.13.5 to unblock all users (alex-solovyev report).

title: t3004: fix: dispatch-timing-helper records probe:false even on escalated probe-mode attempts
body:
## Task

`_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` (in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) does not pass `--probe true` to `dispatch-timing-helper.sh record` when the recommended timeout came from probe-mode escalation. As a result, every record in `dispatch-timing-stats.jsonl` carries `probe:false` even when the timeout was an escalated 2x/4x value after a prior failure.

## Why

Functional behaviour is correct — when a timeout fires, the next attempt gets 2x budget, then 4x if it also fails, capped at MAX_TIMEOUT (300s). Verified in production at 2026-04-28T00:59:02Z: #21433 timed out at 94170ms with timeout_used_ms=90000, and the next dispatch (#20930) used timeout_used_ms=180000 (2x as designed).

But `dispatch-timing-helper.sh stats` cannot tell apart fresh-attempt records from probe-attempt records because every record has `probe:false`. The helper does not currently expose a probe-mode count metric, but if it ever does (or if `pulse-stats-helper.sh` ever surfaces it), the data will be wrong.

This is observability-only — it does NOT affect the timeout escalation logic itself, which works by re-reading the previous record's outcome on each `recommend` call.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` (~5 lines).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh::cmd_recommend` to also output a probe flag when escalating (~3 lines).

### Approach

Option A (preferred — single-source-of-truth in helper):
- `cmd_recommend` outputs two lines: `<timeout_ms>` and `<probe_bool>`. Wire-in reads both via `mapfile` or `read`.
- Drawback: changes helper output format; requires consumer migration.

Option B (caller-side detection):
- Wire-in compares `timeout_ms` to `BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT_MS` and the previous record's `timeout_used_ms`. If `timeout_ms > previous`, set probe=true.
- Drawback: duplicates probe-mode logic between helper and caller.

Recommend Option A for testability.

### Verification

- After deploy, observe `dispatch-timing-stats.jsonl`: a timeout record followed by a probe attempt should have `probe:true` on the second line.
- Test: extend `tests/test-dispatch-timing-helper.sh` with a "probe-flag-roundtrip" case that records a timeout, calls recommend, and asserts `probe:true` is recorded on the next record.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Probe-mode attempts have `probe:true` in the JSONL state file.
- [ ] `dispatch-timing-helper.sh stats` could be extended (separate task) to show `probe_attempts` counter.
- [ ] Test case added.
- [ ] ShellCheck zero NEW.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-timing-helper.sh

## Complexity Impact

- `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout`: currently 53 lines, projected ~55. Stays well below 100.
- `cmd_recommend`: currently ~40 lines, projected ~45. Stays below 100.

## Session Origin

Filed during v3.13.5 release verification (t3003 production observation). Adaptive timeout fired correctly — escalating from 90s to 180s after #21433 timed out — but the resulting record in `dispatch-timing-stats.jsonl` had `probe:false`, masking the probe-mode signal in stats output.

title: t3005: fill_floor parallel dispatch — serial loop caps concurrency at 1-2 workers/cycle
body:
## Task

The `_dispatch_fill_floor` loop in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` processes candidates **serially** — each `_dff_process_candidate` call blocks until completion before the next iteration starts. With ~100s per successful dispatch (most of it in `worktree-helper.sh add`), 24 worker slots take 40 minutes of wall-clock time to fill. With pulse cycle interval of ~7-15min, we never reach the concurrency ceiling.

## Why (incident evidence)

Direct measurements 2026-04-28T01:21Z (after deploying t3003 adaptive timeout v3.13.5):

- `Stage complete: fill_floor_candidate_21436 (0, 109s)` — single dispatch took 109 seconds
- 24 worker slots available, only 2 workers running steady-state
- 132 dispatchable issues across 2 repos, 80% of pulse cycles dispatch 0-1 workers
- Root cause: serial loop at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:816` — `_dff_process_candidate` blocks the loop body

The 109s dispatch breakdown:
- `Stage start` → `Pre-created worktree`: ~100s (worktree-helper.sh add)
- `Pre-created worktree` → `Stage complete`: ~5-9s (gh API ops + nohup spawn)

With serial dispatch:
- Best case: 1 successful dispatch per pulse cycle (~7min) = 8/hour
- Required for 24 concurrency: 48/hour (assuming 30min worker duration)
- **Throughput gap: 6x**

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_dispatch_fill_floor` — parallelize the candidate loop with bounded concurrency (lines ~750-836)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_dff_process_candidate` — make safe for concurrent invocation (state mutations)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh` — regression test for parallel dispatch

### Approach

**Bounded parallelism with shared state file:**

```bash
local _dff_max_parallel=6  # tunable: 6 concurrent dispatches × ~100s each = 1 cycle of 24
local _pids=()

while IFS= read -r candidate_json; do
    if [[ "${#_pids[@]}" -ge "$_dff_max_parallel" ]]; then
        wait -n  # bash 4+: wait for any one to finish
        _pids=("${_pids[@]/$!}")  # remove finished pid
    fi
    if [[ "$dispatched_count" -ge "$_effective_slots" ]]; then break; fi

    # Background dispatch + record outcome via shared state file
    (
        _dff_proc_rc=0
        _dff_process_candidate "$candidate_json" "$self_login" "$available_slots" || _dff_proc_rc=$?
        if [[ "$_dff_proc_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo "success" >> "$_dff_outcomes_file"
        fi
    ) &
    _pids+=($!)
done <"$_dff_candidate_file"

wait  # for remaining
dispatched_count=$(wc -l < "$_dff_outcomes_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
```

**State mutation safety:**

`_dff_process_candidate` mutates module globals (`_DFF_ROUND_DISPATCHED`, `_DFF_THROTTLE_CLEARED`, `_DFF_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER`, `_PULSE_LAST_LAUNCH_FAILURE`). In a backgrounded subshell, these mutations are isolated and lost. Solutions:

1. **Outcomes file** (preferred): aggregate state via shared file, post-loop reconciliation
2. **Drop throttle tracking**: if throttle is rare-path, simpler to remove
3. **flock-based mutex**: atomic increments via `flock` + arithmetic

Outcomes file is simplest: each backgrounded dispatch appends one line indicating success/skip/timeout, post-loop sums. Loses real-time throttle decisions but throttle only matters for SUCCESSIVE-failure detection, which can run on completed batch.

### Reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh::_refresh_owner_*` — already uses backgrounded gh search calls with `wait` for parallel I/O
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh::_acquire_lock` — mkdir-lock pattern for concurrent state writes
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` — fire-and-forget background pattern with PID tracking

### Configuration

New env var: `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` (default 6). Override in plist via `EnvironmentVariables`.
- Set to `1` to retain serial behavior (regression escape hatch).
- Set to `12` for aggressive (~50% utilization while preserving slot accounting).
- Cap at `_effective_slots` (don't dispatch more concurrent attempts than slots).

### Verification

- `tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh` regression: launch N=6 mock candidates, all should complete via `wait`, dispatched_count should match success count
- Live: after deploy, observe `pulse-stage-timings.log` — `_dispatch_fill_floor` total duration should drop from ~10min to ~2min when queue has dispatchable candidates
- Live: workers should ramp from 2 to 24 within 1-2 pulse cycles (currently takes hours)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fill floor processes ≥ 6 candidates in parallel by default
- [ ] State mutations (throttle, dispatched_count) preserved across parallel dispatch
- [ ] No regression: serial mode (`DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL=1`) still works
- [ ] Regression test added covering parallel dispatch + outcome aggregation
- [ ] ShellCheck zero new violations
- [ ] Function-complexity gate: `_dispatch_fill_floor` stays under 100 lines (or refactor to sub-function)
- [ ] Live verification: workers reach 12+ concurrent within 2 pulse cycles after deployment

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh

## Complexity Impact

- `_dispatch_fill_floor`: currently ~120 lines, projected ~140 lines after adding parallel loop. May need extraction to `_dff_dispatch_one_parallel` helper to stay under 100-line gate. Plan refactor pre-implementation.

## Session Origin

Discovered during v3.13.5 verification (t3003 follow-up). Adaptive timeout (180s budget) successfully unblocked individual launches, but serial fill_floor caps total throughput at 8-15 workers/hour. With 24-slot pool and 132 dispatchable issues, the system is structurally incapable of reaching max concurrency. Demo tomorrow requires immediate fix.

title: t3008: fix: concurrent git worktree add races on .git/config lock
body:
## Task

Add retry-with-backoff (or per-repo mkdir-lock) around `git worktree add` in `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh::_dsi_create_worktree` to handle concurrent-creation races on `.git/config` lock.

## Why

Observed t3005 session: 1/8 parallel dispatches failed (#21440) with:

```
error: could not lock config file .git/config: File exists
error: unable to write upstream branch configuration
```

The directory was created but `git worktree list --porcelain` returned empty for that branch (registration partial-write left config in inconsistent state). The script then errored at line 246: `Worktree created but path could not be resolved (branch=<name>)`.

Stored memory: `mem_20260428040301_4986d607` ("Concurrent worktree creation races on .git/config lock").

## How

`EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh:225-251` — wrap the `worktree-helper.sh add` call AND the subsequent `git worktree list --porcelain | awk` query in a retry loop.

Two options (pick one):

**Option A (lightweight, recommended):** retry loop with exponential backoff. 3 attempts at 0.5s/1s/2s sleep. Fails-fast if all three hit lock contention.

**Option B (heavier):** wrap the `git worktree add` call in `mkdir ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/locks/<repo>.lock` (atomic), serializing per-repo worktree creation. Cleaner but adds latency under bursts.

Reference pattern: `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh::_acquire_lock` uses mkdir-lock; copy that idiom for option B. For option A, `shared-gh-wrappers.sh::gh_with_retry` shows the retry-with-backoff pattern.

title: t3010: fix: pulse pile-up under launchctl when cycle exceeds StartInterval
body:
## Task

Fix pulse pile-up under launchctl when cycle duration exceeds `StartInterval`. The mkdir-fallback lock in `pulse-wrapper.sh::main()` serializes execution but does NOT prevent launchctl from spawning new pulse-wrapper instances every 120s — instances accumulate as queued lock-waiters.

## Why

Observed t3005 session (Apr 28 2026): 6 pulse instances detected at one point, lock holder PID 41356 with uptime 06:47, 5 instances queued at uptime 00:00-00:37. `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` flagged "MULTIPLE pulse instances detected (GH#21433) — singleton invariant violated".

The earlier t3002 fix (PR #21437) addressed a different multi-pulse race (concurrent claim conflicts), not this launchctl-respawn pile-up. With cycles taking 9-12 min and StartInterval=120s, every cycle queues 4-5 future instances.

Stored memory: `mem_20260428040259_22e6326b`.

## How

Two fix options:

**Option A (recommended):** make pulse-wrapper.sh exit IMMEDIATELY (fast-fail) when lock is held, so launchctl respawns find no work to do. Currently the second instance blocks on the lock waiting; instead it should `exit 0` with a single `log_info "[pulse-wrapper] another instance running, skipping"`.

`EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — locate the lock-acquire block (search `mkdir.*aidevops-pulse.lock`). Replace `wait-then-acquire` semantics with `try-acquire-or-exit-0`.

**Option B:** raise launchctl `StartInterval` to match observed cycle time (e.g., 600s). But this masks the root cause and prevents recovery if cycle becomes faster.

Pick Option A — it's correct; pile-up is the symptom of treating the second-instance case as legitimate when it's not.

`EDIT: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` may also need adjustment if launchctl reports "service exited too quickly" — check after Option A change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` (possibly)

### Complexity Impact

`main()` lock block currently ~10 lines. Replacement pattern is similar size. No risk of exceeding 100-line gate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] After fix, `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` reports 1 instance (or 0) — never 2+.
- [ ] Locks file inspection shows no queued waiters.
- [ ] `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows new "another instance running, skipping" log lines from launchctl-respawn attempts.
- [ ] Cycle behaviour unchanged (no impact on dispatch throughput).

## Verification

```bash
# After deploy, monitor for 30 min:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status | grep -E "running \([0-9]+ instance"
# Expect: always 1 instance, never multiple
```

## Related

- t3002 (PR #21437) fixed concurrent-claim race, NOT this issue
- This is the launchctl-respawn-during-long-cycle pile-up

title: t3006: framework: add capture-don't-advise + turn-end brevity + proactive memory rules to AGENTS.md
body:
## Task

Add three new framework rules to `.agents/AGENTS.md` to address recurring AI-session failure modes:

1. **Capture-don't-advise discipline** — when the AI identifies a fixable issue, file it as an auto-dispatch task instead of telling the user about it.
2. **Turn-end brevity** — cap status/progress turn-ends at ~200 words, prefer markdown links over prose.
3. **Proactive memory storage** — store breakthroughs immediately (not at session end) so context-compaction can't lose them.

## Why

User feedback (Apr 28 2026 session):

> "you have a habit of telling me things that need doing, but not utilising the todo & issues pipeline to set the fixes in motion"
> "the amount for human reading at each ai turn end, it's a lot... maybe it could be more succinct, and give links"
> "preserving human attention (finite, fallible) and making sure ai takes on the things it knows and has proven it can fix"

Three failure modes observed in t3005 session:

- 4 framework bugs identified but not filed as issues (just listed in turn-end prose).
- Multiple 600+ word turn-ends with paragraph explanations the user could have clicked links to see.
- Lessons stored only at end of session — would have been lost if context compacted mid-stream.

## How

`EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` — add these sections under "Framework Rules":

### Capture-don't-advise discipline (NEW — applies before "Default: do the work")

When you identify a fixable issue (bug, gap, improvement, framework debt), DO NOT just describe it to the user.

- File it as an auto-dispatch issue: `claim-task-id.sh --title "<desc>" --description "<worker-ready body>" --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:standard,bug"`. Worker pipeline picks it up.
- Tell the user ONE LINE: `Filed as #NNN`. Link, no paragraph.
- Anti-pattern (the "advisory trap"): listing N framework bugs in turn-end prose without filing them. The user is busy; the framework has dispatch capacity. Use it.

Applies to: framework bugs, perf issues, missing tests, missing docs, bot review followups, ANY worker-dispatchable task. If genuinely architecture/policy (not auto-dispatchable), say so and ask explicitly.

### Turn-end brevity (NEW — strengthens "Tone and style")

User attention is finite. Every turn-end should:

- Be ≤ 200 words for status/progress reports. Hard cap.
- Use bare markdown links for actionable items: `[#21451](url) BLOCKED` not "PR #21451 was created and is now blocked because...".
- Group by action type — **Done**, **In-flight**, **User-action** — not narrative.
- Skip explanations the user can click links to see.

If turn-end > 200 words: cut. Ask "did the user need to read EVERY part?" If no, link instead.

### Proactive memory storage (NEW — strengthens "Memory recall t2050")

Beyond session-end storage:

- Store lessons IMMEDIATELY after any breakthrough or unexpected discovery — context compaction can wipe an unstored lesson.
- Store-while-fresh triggers: framework bug + workaround pair, race condition discovery, API limit hit + recovery, dispatch-path fix, anything you'd want a future session to know in 1 query.
- Cost is one `memory-helper.sh store` call. Skipping it wastes the lesson.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

### Complexity Impact

Adds ~80 lines of guidance to AGENTS.md. No function complexity impact (Markdown only).

## Acceptance

- [ ] All three new sections present in `.agents/AGENTS.md` under "Framework Rules".
- [ ] Each new rule has: trigger condition, action, anti-pattern call-out.
- [ ] Markdownlint passes: `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Sections fit the existing tone (no emojis, GitHub-flavoured Markdown, ≤ 200 words per section).

## Verification

```bash
markdownlint-cli2 .agents/AGENTS.md && echo "lint passes"
grep -c "Capture-don't-advise" .agents/AGENTS.md  # expect 1+
grep -c "Turn-end brevity" .agents/AGENTS.md      # expect 1+
grep -c "Proactive memory storage" .agents/AGENTS.md  # expect 1+
```
