title: fix(claim-task-id): _ensure_todo_entry_written builds TODO line from --description instead of --title
body:
## Description

`_ensure_todo_entry_written` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh` builds the TODO.md line text from `$description` (the full issue body) instead of `$title` (the short summary). When a caller passes a worker-ready, multi-paragraph description — which is exactly what the t1900 / t2417 worker-ready-body mandate explicitly recommends — the entire body lands in TODO.md as a single mega-line of collapsed whitespace. The longer the description (which is the framework-recommended quality direction), the worse TODO.md gets.

This contradicts the t1900 / t2417 mandate: those rules tell agents to write rich, multi-section descriptions for issue/PR bodies. The TODO.md emitter penalises exactly that quality.

## Expected Behavior

The TODO.md line should be a one-line description matching the issue title — e.g.:

```
- [ ] t344 align 6 downstream briefs with locked t324 enum counts (16/11/11) #deep-research #auto-dispatch tier:standard ref:GH#2107
```

Not the entire issue body collapsed into one line.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (real session, 2026-04-28):

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh \
  --repo-path ~/Git/qs-agency \
  --title "align 6 downstream briefs with locked t324 enum counts (16/11/11)" \
  --description "$(cat /tmp/large-worker-ready-description.md)" \
  --labels "deep-research,tier:standard,auto-dispatch,status:blocked" \
  --no-blocked-by
```

`/tmp/large-worker-ready-description.md` was a ~5 KB worker-ready brief with 7 standard headings (Task / Why / How / Acceptance / Files Scope / Dependencies / Session Origin), per the t1900 / t2417 mandate.

**Actual output** (TODO.md line 2391 after the helper ran):

```
- [ ] t344 ## Task Update 6 downstream task briefs in this repo to reflect the **locked enum counts (N=16, M=11, P=11)** that t324 (PR #2106) ships, per the spec's §9.4 downstream-update table. All 6 briefs were drafted before the t324 Phase 3b-2 override added `forecast` + `event` claim_types and `organization` + `technology` entity types and the `role:` scope prefix. This is a focused planning-edit task — six brief files only, no code touched. Once these briefs are updated, the downstream tasks become dispatch-ready (they're currently blocked on `blocked-by:t324-review` clearing, which happens when t324 PR #2106 merges). ## Why The t324 spine review (§1.5) and Phase 3b-2 override (§1.6) finalised: - **N = 16 claim_types** (originally 14 — added `forecast` and `event` as citable types) - **M = 11 entity types** (originally 9 — added `organization` and `technology`) [...truncated, 3471 chars total on a single line...]
```

The full issue body — paragraphs, headings, bullets, code-fence content, all collapsed to spaces — was inlined as the TODO description. Section headings (`## Task`, `## Why`) and inline code became literal text in the TODO line.

**Expected output**:

```
- [ ] t344 align 6 downstream briefs with locked t324 enum counts (16/11/11) #deep-research #auto-dispatch tier:standard ref:GH#2107
```

i.e., TODO line description should be the `--title` argument (one line by definition), not the `--description`.

## Root Cause

`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh` lines 595-642 (function `_ensure_todo_entry_written`):

```bash
_ensure_todo_entry_written() {
    local task_id="$1"
    local issue_num="$2"
    local description="$3"   # <-- accepts the FULL description body
    local labels="$4"
    local repo_path="$5"
    ...
    # Build the TODO line.
    local safe_desc
    safe_desc=$(printf '%s' "$description" \
        | tr '\n\t' '  ' | sed -E 's/[[:space:]]+/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//')
    [[ -z "$safe_desc" ]] && safe_desc="(no description)"
    local todo_line="- [ ] ${task_id} ${safe_desc}"   # <-- inlines full body
    ...
}
```

Both call sites in `claim-task-id.sh` pass `"$description"` as the third argument:

- `claim-task-id.sh:471-472` (delegation path)
- `claim-task-id.sh:586-587` (bare-fallback path)

`$title` IS in scope at both call sites (it's a top-level `local title=...` in the calling function `create_github_issue`), so the fix surface is small.

`git blame` attributes the safe_desc construction to commit `61c285a248` (t2548 split of claim-task-id.sh — file move), and the GH#20834 blocked-by append at lines 644-649 to commit `421d58bd7c` (which interacts with this function but did not introduce the description-vs-title mismatch). The original t2548 ([PR #20180](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20180)) is the introduction point.

## Suggested Fix

Pass `$title` to `_ensure_todo_entry_written` and use it for the TODO line text. `$description` can still be retained for future cases that need the body (currently nothing in the function reads it after the safe_desc transformation), or removed.

Minimal patch:

```diff
--- a/.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh
+++ b/.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh
@@ -593,9 +593,10 @@ _ensure_todo_entry_written() {
     local task_id="$1"
     local issue_num="$2"
-    local description="$3"
+    local title="$3"
     local labels="$4"
     local repo_path="$5"
+    # Note: 6th arg description previously used; now title is canonical.

     local todo_file="${repo_path}/TODO.md"
@@ -636,8 +637,8 @@ _ensure_todo_entry_written() {

     # Build the TODO line.
     local safe_desc
-    safe_desc=$(printf '%s' "$description" \
+    safe_desc=$(printf '%s' "$title" \
         | tr '\n\t' '  ' | sed -E 's/[[:space:]]+/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//')
     [[ -z "$safe_desc" ]] && safe_desc="(no description)"
     local todo_line="- [ ] ${task_id} ${safe_desc}"

--- a/.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
+++ b/.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
@@ -468,7 +468,7 @@ _create_via_issue_sync_helper() {
         _link_parent_issue_post_create "$issue_num" "$repo_path"
         _ensure_todo_entry_written \
-            "$_task_id_for_todo" "$issue_num" "$description" "$labels" "$repo_path"
+            "$_task_id_for_todo" "$issue_num" "$title" "$labels" "$repo_path"
         echo "$issue_num"
         return 0
@@ -583,7 +583,7 @@ _create_via_bare_gh() {
     # the TODO entry is never written. This call closes that gap idempotently.
     _ensure_todo_entry_written \
-        "$_task_id_for_todo" "$issue_num" "$description" "$labels" "$repo_path"
+        "$_task_id_for_todo" "$issue_num" "$title" "$labels" "$repo_path"

     echo "$issue_num"
```

`$title` is already a `local` in both callers' scope (it's the top-level argument `--title`), so no plumbing required.

A regression test is straightforward: invoke `claim-task-id.sh --title "short title" --description "<long multi-paragraph body>"` and assert the resulting TODO.md line equals `- [ ] t<NNN> short title <tags> ref:GH#<NNN>` byte-for-byte. Existing test harness at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-blocked-by-detection.sh` is the closest pattern to copy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `claim-task-id.sh` with `--description` set to any multi-paragraph string (the t1900 / t2417 worker-ready format guarantees this).
2. Observe `TODO.md` after the helper runs — the appended line will contain the entire description collapsed to a single line, not the title.

Minimum repro:

```bash
cd /tmp && mkdir -p repro && cd repro
git init && git commit --allow-empty -m init
echo "1" > .task-counter && git add .task-counter && git commit -m init-counter
touch TODO.md && git add TODO.md && git commit -m init-todo
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh \
  --repo-path "$PWD" \
  --no-issue \
  --title "short title" \
  --description "$(printf '## Section\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\n## Another\n\nSecond paragraph.\n')"
cat TODO.md
```

Expected last line: `- [ ] tNNN short title ...`
Actual last line: `- [ ] tNNN ## Section First paragraph. ## Another Second paragraph. ...`

## Workarounds Applied

1. **Manual TODO.md cleanup via worktree** — discarded the helper's malformed append, created a separate worktree (`chore/t344-todo-entry`), hand-edited a clean one-liner into the right `## Backlog` section, opened a planning PR (`robstiles/qs-agency#2108`). Cost: ~5 min plus an extra PR/review cycle that wouldn't have been needed.

2. **Stub brief file pointing to the issue** — per the t2417 worker-ready-body heuristic, I created `todo/tasks/t344-brief.md` as a stub linking to GH#2107 as the canonical brief. This is correct framework usage, but it doesn't compensate for the broken TODO line — the TODO mega-line problem is independent of brief file presence.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.13.5 (matches latest; this bug exists in 3.13.5 head)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: robstiles/qs-agency (consumer; not aidevops itself)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.91.0

## Additional Context

- Real-world session: filed task t344 / GH#2107 in robstiles/qs-agency on 2026-04-28 03:45 UTC during interactive Phase 4 review of an unrelated PR. The mega-line landed in TODO.md, was caught by the agent during post-creation verification, and required the worktree workaround above before the planning PR could be opened cleanly.
- The t1900 / t2417 worker-ready-body rules are framework-canonical and well-motivated (better issue bodies → better worker outcomes). The TODO emitter is the only place in the framework that penalises long, structured descriptions. Fixing this aligns the helper with framework intent.
- The fix is one-line-per-call-site (3 lines total) plus a function signature rename. Existing test infrastructure can verify the regression with one new test case.

title: arch(claim-task-id): blocked-by:tNNN auto-emission collides with pre-flight label validation; first-use UX wall in fresh consumer repos
body:
## Description

`claim-task-id.sh` aborts (exit 3) on consumer repos that don't pre-seed per-task `blocked-by:t<NNN>` labels, when the user's `--description` references a predecessor task. The auto-emission introduced in t2823 / [PR #20839](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20839) (detect "blocked-by: t<NNN>" in description text → apply matching label) collides with the pre-flight label-validation guard introduced in t2800 / [PR #20744](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20744) (refuse to advance counter if any requested label doesn't exist). The collision creates a hard wall: the helper detects the predecessor reference, decides to apply the label, and aborts because the label doesn't exist — without an automatic recovery path.

This is filed as an architecture discussion, not a code-fix prescription, because the right resolution depends on framework design intent that maintainers are best placed to weigh.

## Expected Behavior

The user's intent is "this task is blocked by t<NNN>". The helper should record that intent without forcing the user to manually create a label, run with `--no-blocked-by` (which loses the label entirely), or hand-create a label they may not have known they needed.

What the right behaviour IS depends on a deliberate choice between three reasonable options (see Considerations below).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (real session, 2026-04-28 in `robstiles/qs-agency`):

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh \
  --repo-path ~/Git/qs-agency \
  --title "align 6 downstream briefs with locked t324 enum counts (16/11/11)" \
  --description "$(cat description-with-blocked-by-t324.md)" \
  --labels "deep-research,tier:standard,auto-dispatch,blocked-by:t324"
```

The description contained the line `**blocked-by:** t324 PR #2106 must merge first` in its Dependencies section.

**Actual output**:

```
[INFO] Loading project config from .aidevops.json
[WARN] GH#20834: Detected predecessor reference(s) in description; auto-emitting blocked-by:t324. Override with --no-blocked-by.
[INFO] Using remote: origin, counter branch: main
[INFO] Detected platform: github
[ERROR] Pre-flight label validation failed — invalid label(s): 'blocked-by:t324'
[ERROR]   Run: gh label list --repo "robstiles/qs-agency" | grep -i '<name>'
[ERROR]   Claim aborted — counter NOT advanced.
```

(Exit code 3.)

The error message tells the user how to *check* the label, not how to *fix* the situation. The helper has detected a real predecessor reference, intends to record it, and aborts — leaving the user to decide between three non-obvious workarounds, none of which are mentioned in the error output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In any consumer repo that does not have `blocked-by:t<NNN>` labels (i.e., any repo that hasn't been hand-seeded with these labels — most consumer repos at first use).
2. Run `claim-task-id.sh` with `--description` containing any predecessor reference text the t2823 detector recognises (`blocked-by: t<NNN>`, `Follow-up from t<NNN>`, `tracked in #<NNN>`, `after t<NNN> ships|merges|lands`).
3. Helper aborts with `Pre-flight label validation failed`. Counter is not advanced (correct), but no progress is made and the user has no clear next step.

## Workarounds Applied

In the failing session I tried three:

1. `--no-blocked-by` — works, but discards the predecessor information from labels entirely. Body text still contains the blocker reference, and `pulse-dep-graph.sh` (line 541-543) reads body text directly, so the dependency is still tracked for dispatch ordering. But the `blocked-by:t<NNN>` *label* — used by `pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` and other consumers as a fast-filter index — is gone. This is what I shipped on the failing session.

2. `--labels "...,status:blocked"` (substituted a generic blocking label that DOES exist in qs-agency) — works, blocks dispatch, but loses the per-blocker specificity. `status:blocked` is one bit; `blocked-by:t324` carries the blocker identity.

3. `gh label create blocked-by:t324 --repo robstiles/qs-agency` then re-run — works, but requires the user to know the label is needed before they hit the wall, and creates per-task label proliferation that nobody decided to opt into.

The third option is the one a maintainer-aware user would converge on, but the framework gives them no guidance toward it from the error message.

## Context

The relevant interacting commits, in order:

| Commit | Task | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| [#20247](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20247) | t2548 (GH#20224) | Split `claim-task-id.sh` into counter and issue sub-libraries; introduced `_ensure_todo_entry_written` |
| [#20744](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20744) | t2800 | Added pre-flight label validation; abort with exit 3 before counter advance if any requested label doesn't exist |
| [#20839](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20839) | t2823 (GH#20834) | Auto-emit `blocked-by:t<NNN>` labels when predecessor references appear in `--description` |
| [#20863](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20863) | (follow-up) | Case-insensitive normalisation in `_detect_predecessor_refs` |

Each commit is individually correct. The collision emerges from their composition: t2800 says "every requested label must exist or we refuse"; t2823 says "any predecessor reference in description text becomes a requested label". Whether a given consumer repo has the corresponding `blocked-by:t<NNN>` label is path-dependent on whether someone has filed prior cross-task work in that repo, which is unrelated to whether the user's current intent is valid.

`blocked-by:t<NNN>` labels are NOT auto-created by `aidevops init` or any other framework setup step. They accumulate organically when users hit this wall and create them by hand. The first user of cross-task references in a fresh consumer repo will always hit this.

The framework already reads blocker info from body text (`pulse-dep-graph.sh:541-543` for `blocked-by:t<NNN>` and `blocked-by:#<NNN>`; `pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh:149` for `blocked-by:` patterns). Labels are a fast-filter index, not the source of truth. So the cost of "no label, body text only" is real (slower filtering, label-based pulse logic loses the specificity) but not catastrophic (dependencies still resolve).

## Considerations for the Fix Path

Three options, each with trade-offs the maintainer is best placed to weigh:

### Option A — Auto-create missing `blocked-by:t<NNN>` labels in `claim-task-id.sh`

When pre-flight detects a missing `blocked-by:t<NNN>` label requested via t2823 auto-emission, create the label automatically (`gh label create` with a sensible default colour and description) and proceed.

- **Pro**: zero user-visible friction. The label is a deterministic function of the predecessor task ID, so auto-creation is safe.
- **Pro**: aligns with how `tier:*`, `origin:*`, and `status:*` labels are handled at framework init — the label catalogue grows with use, no manual seeding required.
- **Con**: per-task label proliferation. A repo that has worked on 200 tasks accumulates 200 `blocked-by:t<NNN>` labels, most of which become irrelevant once the predecessor merges. Pruning needs a separate sweep.
- **Con**: changes the trust model of pre-flight validation. Currently t2800 means "labels are vetted"; auto-create weakens that.
- **Implementation surface**: small. `claim-task-id-issue.sh` `_validate_labels_pre_flight` (or wherever t2800's check lives) gains an "auto-create exception class" for `blocked-by:t<NNN>` patterns.

### Option B — Skip label application when label doesn't exist; warn but continue

When a `blocked-by:t<NNN>` label is requested via auto-emission and doesn't exist, log a warning ("blocker recorded in body text but no `blocked-by:t<NNN>` label exists in this repo; create with `gh label create blocked-by:t<NNN>` to enable label-based filtering"), drop the label from the apply set, and continue with the claim.

- **Pro**: respects user intent (claim proceeds), preserves t2800's "labels are vetted" trust model (we don't invent labels), and the body text still encodes the dependency for the consumers that read it.
- **Pro**: the warning trains the user toward Option A by hand if they want labelled blockers.
- **Con**: silently degrades the `blocked-by:t<NNN>` label semantic for consumers that DO read the label fast path. If the user expected dispatch-blocking via label, they don't get it.
- **Con**: makes auto-emission a "best effort" feature, which is a different contract from how it's documented.

### Option C — Document the requirement; provide a setup helper

Add to the framework docs that consumer repos should seed `blocked-by:t*` labels on initialization, and provide `aidevops init --seed-blocked-by-labels` (or similar) that creates the catalogue. Keep the current pre-flight refusal.

- **Pro**: simplest framework surface — no new logic, just docs and a setup step.
- **Pro**: keeps the trust model intact.
- **Con**: still a per-task-id label catalogue (200 task IDs → 200 labels) — same proliferation as Option A, just with a different trigger.
- **Con**: shifts the cost to the user. New consumer repos still hit the wall the first time, just with better docs.
- **Con**: doesn't help repos that have already been initialised (most of them).

### Sub-option for any of A/B/C — better error message

Whatever path is chosen, the current error message is unhelpful. It should at minimum say:

```
Pre-flight label validation failed — label 'blocked-by:t324' does not exist in this repo.

This label was auto-emitted by t2823 from a predecessor reference in your --description.
Options:
  (a) Create the label and re-run: gh label create blocked-by:t324 --repo <slug>
  (b) Skip the label: re-run with --no-blocked-by (dependency still recorded in body text)
  (c) Use a different blocking label that exists, e.g. status:blocked
```

This is independently shippable regardless of which Option A/B/C path is chosen.

## My Lean (Optional)

Option B — skip-with-warning — is what I'd choose if it were my call:

- It respects the t2800 trust model (we don't invent labels) while not stalling productive work.
- The warning is the right place to teach the user about Option A as the upgrade path.
- The body-text dependency tracking already works — we're only sacrificing label-fast-filter, not the semantic.
- It's the smallest change.

But I genuinely don't know how heavily `pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` and the rest of the label-fast-path consumers rely on the `blocked-by:t<NNN>` label being present, vs. how often they fall back to body-text parsing. That's the question the maintainer can answer without me.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.13.5
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: robstiles/qs-agency
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.91.0

## Additional Context

- This was hit during interactive Phase 4 review of an unrelated PR while filing a follow-up task with proper t1900 / t2417 worker-ready description (which included the `blocked-by:` reference that triggered auto-emission).
- See-also: sibling issue (TBD) — `_ensure_todo_entry_written` mega-line bug filed in the same session. Different bug, unrelated to this one — but both surfaced in the same `claim-task-id.sh` invocation.

title: bug: sync-workflows-helper.sh and badges-sync-helper.sh leak framework task IDs into consumer-repo commit/PR bodies, blocking the documented one-command remediation
body:
## Summary

`sync-workflows-helper.sh` and `badges-sync-helper.sh` bake their own framework task IDs (`t2779`, `t2975`) into commit and PR bodies on **consumer repos**. Consumer repos that have the task-id-guard pre-commit hook installed (the framework's own `install-task-id-guard.sh`) correctly reject these commits because the framework task ID is meaningless in the consumer's `tNNN` counter space, and the helper exits without applying the resync.

## Symptom

User runs the canonical remediation for [GH#20976](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20976) (the cross-account `secrets: inherit` bug) on their consumer repo:

```bash
$ aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo robstiles/qs-agency

  REPO                                     CLASSIFICATION       ACTION     DETAIL
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[task-id-guard][BLOCK] Commit subject references invented or unclaimed task ID(s):

  Subject: chore: resync framework workflow (DRIFTED/CALLER → CURRENT/CALLER)

  t2779 — numeric ID 2779 > current counter 345, and not confirmed via a linked issue title
  ...
  robstiles/qs-agency                      DRIFTED/CALLER       FAILED     git commit failed
  robstiles/qs-agency                      NEEDS-MIGRATION      SKIPPED    working tree not clean; skipping

[sync-workflows-helper.sh] applied: 0; skipped: 1.
```

The first sync attempt fails. Its file-modification side effect leaves the working tree dirty, so the second sync attempt (for the next workflow) skips with `working tree not clean`. **Net effect: zero workflows synced, despite the user running the documented one-command remediation.**

## Root cause

Two files in the deployed copy at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`:

**`sync-workflows-helper.sh`:**

```text
:268:	printf 'Generated by: aidevops sync-workflows --apply (t2779, GH#20649)\n'
:296:	printf 'Generated by: `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (t2779, GH#20649).\n'
```

These lines are emitted into the commit body (line 268) and PR body (line 296) when the helper applies a sync to a consumer repo. The commit subject (line 390, `chore: resync framework workflow ($_status → CURRENT/CALLER)`) is clean — no task ID — but the body trips the task-id-guard's body scan.

**`badges-sync-helper.sh`:** (same pattern, different ID)

```text
:355:		local _commit_msg="chore: install loc-badge caller workflow (aidevops t2975)"
```

Both helpers were authored under their respective framework tasks (`t2779` for sync-workflows, `t2975` for badges). The author embedded the framework task ID in the helper's output as provenance. That's correct behaviour for the framework's own commits — but the same string ends up in **every consumer repo's commits**, where the framework's task counter is irrelevant and the task-id-guard correctly rejects it.

## Why the guard is right to reject

The task-id-guard's contract is: every `tNNN` referenced in a commit subject or body of *this repo* must either (a) be claimed in this repo's counter, or (b) appear in the title of a linked issue from another repo via a `Resolves/Closes/Fixes/Ref/For owner/repo#NNN` footer. The helper's output satisfies neither — it's a bare `t2779` with no cross-repo qualifier. The guard's behaviour is correct; the helper's output is wrong.

## Reproduction

In any consumer repo with `install-task-id-guard.sh install` previously run (i.e., any repo that follows the framework's recommended setup):

```bash
aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <owner>/<consumer-repo>
# → blocked at task-id-guard with "t2779 > current counter <N>"
```

This will hit every downstream user with the guard installed (which is the recommended default).

## Suggested fix

The helpers should not embed framework task IDs in consumer-repo output. Two acceptable forms:

**Option A — cross-repo qualified reference** (preserves traceability, satisfies guard):

```text
Generated by: aidevops sync-workflows --apply
Ref marcusquinn/aidevops#20649
```

The `marcusquinn/aidevops#NNN` reference passes the guard (the guard scans for `tNNN` patterns, not foreign-repo `#NNN` footers, and would treat `marcusquinn/aidevops#20649` as a cross-repo link rather than a local t-ID claim). It also gives consumers a working hyperlink back to the framework PR/issue that introduced the change.

**Option B — drop the t-ID, keep the upstream reference** (simpler, also fine):

```text
Generated by: aidevops sync-workflows --apply (canonical caller refresh)
See: marcusquinn/aidevops sync-workflows feature
```

Either way, the literal string `t2779` (or any other framework task ID) should not appear in consumer-repo commit/PR bodies emitted by these helpers.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh:268` — replace `(t2779, GH#20649)` with cross-repo qualified ref or drop the t-ID
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh:296` — same as line 268
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh:355` — replace `(aidevops t2975)` with cross-repo qualified ref or drop the t-ID

Header comments and helper source code (lines 7, 117 in `sync-workflows-helper.sh`) are unaffected — those `t2779` references are inside the framework's own repo, where the ID is valid.

## Verification

After fix, in a consumer repo with task-id-guard installed:

```bash
aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <owner>/<consumer-repo>
# → expect: applied: N, skipped: 0 (where N = drifted/needs-migration count)
# → no task-id-guard block, no FAILED rows, working tree returns clean
```

A second run of the same command should be a no-op (`CURRENT/CALLER` for everything previously synced).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No literal `tNNN` (where NNN > 0) framework task ID appears in commit subject or body emitted to consumer repos by `sync-workflows-helper.sh`
- [ ] Same constraint for `badges-sync-helper.sh`
- [ ] `aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <consumer>` succeeds against any consumer with task-id-guard installed
- [ ] Cross-repo provenance is preserved via either `marcusquinn/aidevops#NNN` link or framework-PR URL in the body
- [ ] `shellcheck` passes on both helpers post-edit

## Source repo

Discovered while applying [GH#20976](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20976) downstream in `robstiles/qs-agency` — the resync had to be done manually because the helper itself was blocked. Manual remediation: [robstiles/qs-agency#2110](https://github.com/robstiles/qs-agency/pull/2110).

---
*Detected by framework-routing-helper in `robstiles/qs-agency`.*

body:
## Summary

`sync-workflows-helper.sh` and `badges-sync-helper.sh` bake their own framework task IDs (`t2779`, `t2975`) into commit and PR bodies on **consumer repos**. Consumer repos that have the task-id-guard pre-commit hook installed (the framework's own `install-task-id-guard.sh`) correctly reject these commits because the framework task ID is meaningless in the consumer's `tNNN` counter space, and the helper exits without applying the resync.

## Symptom

User runs the canonical remediation for [GH#20976](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20976) (the cross-account `secrets: inherit` bug) on their consumer repo:

```bash
$ aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo robstiles/qs-agency

  REPO                                     CLASSIFICATION       ACTION     DETAIL
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[task-id-guard][BLOCK] Commit subject references invented or unclaimed task ID(s):

  Subject: chore: resync framework workflow (DRIFTED/CALLER → CURRENT/CALLER)

  t2779 — numeric ID 2779 > current counter 345, and not confirmed via a linked issue title
  ...
  robstiles/qs-agency                      DRIFTED/CALLER       FAILED     git commit failed
  robstiles/qs-agency                      NEEDS-MIGRATION      SKIPPED    working tree not clean; skipping

[sync-workflows-helper.sh] applied: 0; skipped: 1.
```

The first sync attempt fails. Its file-modification side effect leaves the working tree dirty, so the second sync attempt (for the next workflow) skips with `working tree not clean`. **Net effect: zero workflows synced, despite the user running the documented one-command remediation.**

## Root cause

Two files in the deployed copy at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`:

**`sync-workflows-helper.sh`:**

```text
:268:	printf 'Generated by: aidevops sync-workflows --apply (t2779, GH#20649)\n'
:296:	printf 'Generated by: `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (t2779, GH#20649).\n'
```

These lines are emitted into the commit body (line 268) and PR body (line 296) when the helper applies a sync to a consumer repo. The commit subject (line 390, `chore: resync framework workflow ($_status → CURRENT/CALLER)`) is clean — no task ID — but the body trips the task-id-guard's body scan.

**`badges-sync-helper.sh`:** (same pattern, different ID)

```text
:355:		local _commit_msg="chore: install loc-badge caller workflow (aidevops t2975)"
```

Both helpers were authored under their respective framework tasks (`t2779` for sync-workflows, `t2975` for badges). The author embedded the framework task ID in the helper's output as provenance. That's correct behaviour for the framework's own commits — but the same string ends up in **every consumer repo's commits**, where the framework's task counter is irrelevant and the task-id-guard correctly rejects it.

## Why the guard is right to reject

The task-id-guard's contract is: every `tNNN` referenced in a commit subject or body of *this repo* must either (a) be claimed in this repo's counter, or (b) appear in the title of a linked issue from another repo via a `Resolves/Closes/Fixes/Ref/For owner/repo#NNN` footer. The helper's output satisfies neither — it's a bare `t2779` with no cross-repo qualifier. The guard's behaviour is correct; the helper's output is wrong.

## Reproduction

In any consumer repo with `install-task-id-guard.sh install` previously run (i.e., any repo that follows the framework's recommended setup):

```bash
aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <owner>/<consumer-repo>
# → blocked at task-id-guard with "t2779 > current counter <N>"
```

This will hit every downstream user with the guard installed (which is the recommended default).

## Suggested fix

The helpers should not embed framework task IDs in consumer-repo output. Two acceptable forms:

**Option A — cross-repo qualified reference** (preserves traceability, satisfies guard):

```text
Generated by: aidevops sync-workflows --apply
Ref marcusquinn/aidevops#20649
```

The `marcusquinn/aidevops#NNN` reference passes the guard (the guard scans for `tNNN` patterns, not foreign-repo `#NNN` footers, and would treat `marcusquinn/aidevops#20649` as a cross-repo link rather than a local t-ID claim). It also gives consumers a working hyperlink back to the framework PR/issue that introduced the change.

**Option B — drop the t-ID, keep the upstream reference** (simpler, also fine):

```text
Generated by: aidevops sync-workflows --apply (canonical caller refresh)
See: marcusquinn/aidevops sync-workflows feature
```

Either way, the literal string `t2779` (or any other framework task ID) should not appear in consumer-repo commit/PR bodies emitted by these helpers.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh:268` — replace `(t2779, GH#20649)` with cross-repo qualified ref or drop the t-ID
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh:296` — same as line 268
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh:355` — replace `(aidevops t2975)` with cross-repo qualified ref or drop the t-ID

Header comments and helper source code (lines 7, 117 in `sync-workflows-helper.sh`) are unaffected — those `t2779` references are inside the framework's own repo, where the ID is valid.

## Verification

After fix, in a consumer repo with task-id-guard installed:

```bash
aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <owner>/<consumer-repo>
# → expect: applied: N, skipped: 0 (where N = drifted/needs-migration count)
# → no task-id-guard block, no FAILED rows, working tree returns clean
```

A second run of the same command should be a no-op (`CURRENT/CALLER` for everything previously synced).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No literal `tNNN` (where NNN > 0) framework task ID appears in commit subject or body emitted to consumer repos by `sync-workflows-helper.sh`
- [ ] Same constraint for `badges-sync-helper.sh`
- [ ] `aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <consumer>` succeeds against any consumer with task-id-guard installed
- [ ] Cross-repo provenance is preserved via either `marcusquinn/aidevops#NNN` link or framework-PR URL in the body
- [ ] `shellcheck` passes on both helpers post-edit

## Source repo

Discovered while applying [GH#20976](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20976) downstream in `robstiles/qs-agency` — the resync had to be done manually because the helper itself was blocked. Manual remediation: [robstiles/qs-agency#2110](https://github.com/robstiles/qs-agency/pull/2110).

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: bug: aidevops check-workflows reports DRIFTED/CALLER for byte-identical-to-canonical workflows (false positive in _classify_workflow)
body:
## Description

`aidevops check-workflows` (`check-workflows-helper.sh`) reports `DRIFTED/CALLER` for caller-pattern workflows that are byte-identical to the canonical caller templates. Manual byte-comparison (`cmp -s`) and manual reproduction of the helper's own normalization pipeline (`_normalize_wf_for_compare`) both confirm the files match canonical exactly — yet the helper's classifier still emits `DRIFTED/CALLER`.

This makes the drift-checker output unreliable as a CI gate or as a "did my resync land?" smoke test, and produces noisy false alarms after a successful `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (or after a manual byte-for-byte resync).

## Expected Behavior

When a caller workflow is byte-identical to the canonical template at `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/<name>-caller.yml` (after the documented `@<ref>` and `branches: [...]` normalizations), `_classify_workflow` should emit `CURRENT/CALLER`, not `DRIFTED/CALLER`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (run from any consumer repo):

```bash
cp ~/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml      .github/workflows/issue-sync.yml
cp ~/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml .github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml
cp ~/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/maintainer-gate-caller.yml .github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml
aidevops check-workflows --repo robstiles/qs-agency
```

**Actual output**:

```
  REPO [WORKFLOW]                                    STATUS           NOTE
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  [issue-sync] robstiles/qs-agency                   DRIFTED/CALLER
  [review-bot-gate] robstiles/qs-agency              DRIFTED/CALLER
  [maintainer-gate] robstiles/qs-agency              DRIFTED/CALLER

  Summary: 3 entries — 0 current, 3 drifted, 0 needs-migration, 0 no-workflow, 0 local-only, 0 no-template
  Exit code 1
```

**Expected output**: all three `CURRENT/CALLER`, summary `3 current, 0 drifted`, exit code 0.

**Independent byte-identity proof**:

```bash
$ for f in issue-sync review-bot-gate maintainer-gate; do
    cmp -s ".github/workflows/${f}.yml" "$HOME/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/${f}-caller.yml" \
      && echo "  $f: byte-identical to canonical ✓" \
      || echo "  $f: DIFFERS"
  done
  issue-sync: byte-identical to canonical ✓
  review-bot-gate: byte-identical to canonical ✓
  maintainer-gate: byte-identical to canonical ✓
```

**Manual reproduction of the helper's own normalizer** (lines 137-143 of `check-workflows-helper.sh`) confirms the post-normalization strings ALSO match for all three:

```bash
for f in issue-sync review-bot-gate maintainer-gate; do
  ours=".github/workflows/${f}.yml"
  canon="$HOME/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/${f}-caller.yml"
  reusable="${f}-reusable\\.yml"
  norm_ours=$(sed -E "s|(marcusquinn/aidevops/\.github/workflows/${reusable})@[^[:space:]]+|\1@REF|g" "$ours" \
    | sed -E 's|^([[:space:]]+branches:) \[[^]]+\]$|\1 [BRANCH]|')
  norm_canon=$(sed -E "s|(marcusquinn/aidevops/\.github/workflows/${reusable})@[^[:space:]]+|\1@REF|g" "$canon" \
    | sed -E 's|^([[:space:]]+branches:) \[[^]]+\]$|\1 [BRANCH]|')
  [[ "$norm_ours" == "$norm_canon" ]] && echo "  $f: NORMALIZED MATCH" || echo "  $f: NORMALIZED DIFFERS"
done
# All three: NORMALIZED MATCH
```

So the inputs are byte-identical, the helper's own normalizer keeps them identical, but `_classify_workflow` at line 199 (`if [[ "$_wf_norm" == "$_canon_norm" ]]; then`) still falls through to the `else` branch and prints `DRIFTED/CALLER` (line 202).

## Causal code

`.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh`:

- **Lines 137-143** — `_normalize_wf_for_compare`: the normalizer (verified correct by manual reproduction above).
- **Lines 156-205** — `_classify_workflow`: the comparison logic. Lines 199-203 compare `_wf_norm` against `_canon_norm` and emit DRIFTED on mismatch.
- **Line 414** — `_resolve_wf_canonical` pre-computes `_canon_norm` once per workflow type using the same normalizer. The pre-computation path is the suspect: when `_canon_norm_pre` is passed in (line 160, 193-194), the function uses the pre-computed value instead of recomputing. If there's a quoting / escaping mismatch between how `_resolve_wf_canonical` builds `_reusable_escaped` and how the per-row caller computes it, the two normalized strings could differ even though the standalone normalizer reproduction agrees.
- **Lines 405-418** — `_resolve_wf_canonical`: builds `_reusable_escaped` via `printf '%s' "$_reusable_file" | sed 's/\./\\./g'`. Worth checking that `$_reusable_file` matches the per-row equivalent exactly (case, suffix, separator).

A focused diagnostic: instrument `_classify_workflow` to print `_wf_norm` and `_canon_norm` to a tmp file when they differ, then re-run on a known byte-identical caller. The diff will reveal the discrepancy directly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In any repo registered in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` (with `pulse: true`), copy the three caller templates from `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/workflows/` byte-for-byte into `.github/workflows/`.
2. Run `aidevops check-workflows --repo <slug>`.
3. Observe `DRIFTED/CALLER` for all three despite byte-identical inputs.
4. Confirm via `cmp -s` and the manual normalizer reproduction above that the inputs do match.

## Workarounds Applied

None applied during the observing session — the false positive was tolerated because the actual end-to-end functionality works (verified by triggering `gh workflow run issue-sync.yml -f command=enrich`, which exercises the SYNC_PAT pass-through and completes successfully). The drift checker is the only thing reporting drift.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.13.5 (latest)
- **Install method**: unknown (`/home/rob/.local/bin/aidevops`)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: robstiles/qs-agency on main
- **gh CLI**: 2.91.0

## Additional Context

Discovered while verifying [PR #2110 in robstiles/qs-agency](https://github.com/robstiles/qs-agency/pull/2110) — a manual resync of the three framework workflows to canonical caller templates (the resync itself was forced manual because of the separate framework bug filed as marcusquinn/aidevops#21476). After merging the resync, the drift checker continued to report drift, prompting this investigation.

The end-to-end functional fix works correctly (SYNC_PAT now resolves in the cross-account reusable-workflow context — verified live). The bug is purely in the drift-checker's classifier producing false alarms, not in the workflows themselves.

See-also: marcusquinn/aidevops#21476 (the sibling sync-workflows-helper bug that forced manual resync, which surfaced this false-positive).

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

body:
## Unactioned Review Feedback

<!-- provenance:start — workers: skip to implementation below -->
**Source PR**: #21491
**File**: `.agents/scripts/tech-stack-bq-lib.sh`
**Reviewers**: gemini
**Findings**: 1
**Max severity**: high
<!-- provenance:end -->

---

### HIGH: gemini (gemini-code-assist[bot])
**File**: `.agents/scripts/tech-stack-bq-lib.sh:577`
![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current implementation of URL encoding using python3 -c is vulnerable to command injection because the $technology variable is expanded directly into the Python script string. If a technology name contains a single quote followed by Python code, it could be executed. A safer approach is to pass the value via an environment variable, which aligns with the repository's preference for using python3 for robust URL encoding while maintaining security.


title: bug: auto-update-helper.sh status crashes on Linux — systemd NextElapse property does not exist
body:
## Description

`aidevops auto-update status` on Linux with systemd 255 outputs only the header and exits silently — no scheduler info, version, state, or config details are shown. The script crashes mid-execution in `_cmd_status_scheduler` due to an unguarded `grep` pipeline under `set -euo pipefail`.

Related: `aidevops auto-update check` (the remediation command suggested by the "stalled" warning) produces no stdout/stderr output, so users following the hint see nothing happen.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

```
$ aidevops auto-update status

Auto-Update Status
-------------------

```

(No scheduler, version, state, or config lines printed.)

**Expected output:**

Scheduler type, enabled state, unit paths, version, last check time, etc.

**Causal code** (`8696b81c94`, PR #19984, t2403):

`.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh:1220-1221`:

```bash
timer_props=$(systemctl --user show -p NextElapse,LastTriggerUSec "${SYSTEMD_UNIT_NAME}.timer" 2>/dev/null || true)
next_elapse=$(echo "$timer_props" | grep '^NextElapse=' | cut -d= -f2-)
```

`systemctl --user show -p NextElapse` returns nothing on systemd 255 — the property is named `NextElapseUSecRealtime` (or `NextElapseUSecMonotonic`). systemctl silently omits unknown property names.

The `timer_props` fetch at line 1220 is guarded with `|| true`, so it succeeds. But line 1221's `grep '^NextElapse='` finds no match (exit 1), and with `set -euo pipefail` (line 51), the pipeline failure propagates and kills the entire script. `_cmd_status_scheduler` never reaches its `echo` statements, and `cmd_status` never reaches `_cmd_status_state`, the Version line, or any subsequent output.

**Actual systemctl output on systemd 255:**

```
$ systemctl --user show -p NextElapse,LastTriggerUSec aidevops-auto-update.timer
LastTriggerUSec=Tue 2026-04-28 10:13:16 EDT
```

**Correct property name:**

```
$ systemctl --user show aidevops-auto-update.timer | grep -i nextelapse
NextElapseUSecMonotonic=22min 43.306514s
```

**Call-site sweep:** Single affected site — only one `grep '^NextElapse='` in the file. The `LastTriggerUSec` grep on the next line (1222) works because that property exists on all systemd versions.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops on Linux with systemd 255+ (Ubuntu 24.04)
2. Enable auto-update daemon: `aidevops auto-update enable`
3. Run `aidevops auto-update status`
4. Observe: only header printed, no scheduler/state details

## Workarounds Applied

None needed — the daemon itself runs fine, only the `status` display is broken. `health-check` works correctly (uses `is-active`/`is-enabled`, not `show -p`).

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.13.6
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.17.0-22-generic)
- **systemd**: 255 (255.4-1ubuntu8.15)
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.91.0 (2026-04-22)

title: bug: skill freshness check writes cwd-relative — pollutes home dir, project dirs, and re-imports every cycle
body:
## Description

The skill freshness check chain (`auto-update` → `skill-update-helper.sh check --auto-update` → `add-skill-helper.sh add ... --force`) writes skill files to `.agents/<path>` **relative to the calling shell's working directory**. None of the helpers in the chain `cd` to a fixed framework location.

This produces three observable failure modes on end-user installations:

1. The systemd user timer (default `WorkingDirectory=$HOME`) writes skill scaffolds to `~/.agents/` — a stray location not referenced by any framework documentation or `setup.sh` deployment target. The canonical install at `~/.aidevops/agents/` already has the correct content.

2. End users who run `aidevops update` from inside any project directory get the project's `.agents/` populated with framework-level reference content (Cloudflare/HeyGen/Remotion docs, etc.) — content that has nothing to do with their project. These appear as untracked dirs in `git status`.

3. The same skill is re-imported on every 24-hour freshness cycle because of a registry/filename mismatch (see "Bonus bug" below). Each cycle re-clones the upstream repo, re-runs the security scan placeholders, and re-writes the scaffold tree.

This appears to be an architectural assumption that the user runs `aidevops update` only from `~/Git/aidevops/` (the framework maintainer's workflow). End users running from anywhere else hit the failure modes above silently.

## Expected Behavior

The skill freshness check should write to a single canonical location regardless of cwd. The most natural target is the same one `setup.sh` deploys to: `~/.aidevops/agents/services/...` and `~/.aidevops/agents/tools/...`. Alternatively, the skill flow could refuse to run outside `~/Git/aidevops/` to preserve the framework-maintainer assumption explicitly.

The systemd unit should set `WorkingDirectory=` (or the helpers should not depend on cwd at all), so the daemon doesn't pollute `$HOME`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (any end-user install with imported skills):

```
cd ~/Git/<any-project>
aidevops update
git status
```

**Actual output** (24h after first run, or whenever the freshness gate fires):

```
On branch main
Untracked files:
        .agents/services/
        .agents/tools/
```

Inside those dirs: `cloudflare-skill/` (~250 ref files), `heygen-skills-skill/`, `remotion-best-practices-skill/`, `form-cro-skill/` — all framework-level reference content unrelated to the user's project.

**Causal chain** (verified in source):

```
auto-update-helper.sh:cmd_check
  → auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:check_skill_freshness  (24h gate)
    → auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:_run_skill_update     (line 285)
      → skill-update-helper.sh check --auto-update --quiet
        → skill-update-core-lib.sh:471                    ($ADD_SKILL_HELPER add $upstream_url --force)
          → add-skill-helper.sh
            → line 963: target_dir=".agents/$(dirname \"$target_path\")"   ← cwd-relative
            → line 1240: target_file=".agents/${target_path}.md"             ← cwd-relative
```

None of `auto-update-helper.sh`, `skill-update-helper.sh`, `skill-update-core-lib.sh`, or `add-skill-helper.sh` change cwd before the write.

**Three independent pieces of evidence that this is a bug, not intended behavior:**

**1. The framework's own systemd daemon is mis-aimed.**

```
$ systemctl --user show aidevops-auto-update.service | grep WorkingDirectory
WorkingDirectory=!/home/<user>
```

The unit file at `~/.config/systemd/user/aidevops-auto-update.service` has no `WorkingDirectory=` set. systemd defaults user-unit cwd to `$HOME`, so every daily skill freshness run writes to `~/.agents/`. Result on this install:

```
~/.agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-skill/      (created by daemon, not setup.sh)
~/.agents/tools/{browser,git,credentials,...}/    (same)
~/.agents/tools/heygen-skill/                     (same)
```

These directories are not referenced by any framework documentation, `setup.sh` deployment, or `aidevops` CLI command. They're stray.

**2. The canonical install location already exists and has the correct content.**

```
$ ls ~/.aidevops/agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-platform-skill.md
/home/<user>/.aidevops/agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-platform-skill.md
```

That's the one `setup.sh` deploys from the aidevops repo. The freshness check should update THAT path. Instead it runs `add-skill add` from whatever cwd, scaffolding a new copy elsewhere.

**3. The aidevops repo itself commits these scaffolds as canonical, version-controlled content.**

```
$ git -C ~/Git/aidevops ls-files .agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-platform-skill.md
.agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-platform-skill.md
```

Skills are framework-shipped reference content (committed in the framework repo, deployed by setup.sh). They are not user-project data. Users should never see them appear in `git status` for their own projects.

## Bonus bug — registry/filename mismatch causes re-import every cycle

The skill registry at `~/.aidevops/agents/configs/skill-sources.json` records:

```json
{
  "name": "cloudflare-platform-skill",
  "upstream_url": "https://github.com/dmmulroy/cloudflare-skill",
  "local_path": ".agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-platform-skill.md"
}
```

But every freshness cycle, `add-skill-helper.sh` clones `dmmulroy/cloudflare-skill`, detects the skill's self-name as `cloudflare` (from the cloned repo's metadata), and writes to `.agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-skill.md` — a different filename. The registry's `local_path` is never updated to match.

Evidence in `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log`:

```
[add-skill] Skill name: cloudflare
[add-skill] Target path: .agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-skill
[OK] Created: .agents/services/hosting/cloudflare-skill.md
```

…repeated dozens of times across multiple freshness cycles. Because the registry-tracked path `cloudflare-platform-skill.md` is never created, the next cycle's "is this skill out-of-date?" check decides "yes, re-import" and the cycle repeats.

This wastes network bandwidth (re-cloning), wastes CI/local time (re-running security scan placeholders, re-writing ~250 ref files), and produces a misleading `skill_updates_applied` counter in the state file (currently 60 on this install — almost certainly not 60 distinct meaningful updates).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh aidevops install on Linux or macOS with at least one imported skill where the upstream repo's self-name differs from the registry's `name` field (e.g. `cloudflare-platform-skill` registered, upstream identifies as `cloudflare`)
2. Wait 24h for the skill freshness gate to fire (or force it: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh check --auto-update`)
3. Observe in `~/.agents/` (when run by daemon) or in `<cwd>/.agents/` (when run by user from a project dir) — stray scaffold tree appears
4. Wait another 24h. Observe the same scaffold gets re-created — never settles

## Architecture Considerations (for the devs to decide the fix)

The bug touches an architectural assumption — the fix isn't a one-liner. Considerations:

**A. Where should skills live?**

- (i) Always `~/.aidevops/agents/...` (single canonical location, mirrors setup.sh deploy target). Simplest. Possibly breaks the framework-maintainer workflow where edits-in-place from `~/Git/aidevops/` are expected.
- (ii) Always `<framework-repo>/.agents/...` if cwd is the framework repo, else `~/.aidevops/agents/...`. Detects maintainer vs end-user.
- (iii) Refuse to run `add-skill add` outside `~/Git/aidevops/` for end users. Most conservative — but breaks the auto-freshness flow entirely unless the daemon is taught to detect "I'm not in the framework repo, skip."

**B. Should the systemd unit set `WorkingDirectory=`?**

- Independently of (A), the daemon should not have its cwd default depend on user-unit semantics. Options: explicit `WorkingDirectory=%h/.aidevops/agents` (or wherever), or the helpers should `cd` to a known location at script entry.
- launchd unit on macOS likely has the same gap — confirm.

**C. Registry/filename reconciliation (the Bonus bug)**

- Either (i) trust the registry's `name` field and pass it to `add-skill-helper.sh add --name "$registry_name"` so the cloned skill is renamed to match registry expectations, or (ii) update the registry's `local_path` after each successful import so subsequent cycles look at the actual filename.

**D. What about the existing strays?**

- `~/.agents/` and any project-local `.agents/services/` `.agents/tools/` directories created by past versions of this code are now orphaned. A migration path that detects and removes them on update would close the loop. (`aidevops auto-update check` could log a one-time advisory listing detected stray paths.)

## Workarounds Applied

None — investigation only; cleanup pending devs' guidance on intended behavior. The user has not yet deleted the stray directories because we want to confirm whether the design intent makes them legitimate per-project state.

## Cross-reference

Related (filed earlier this session by the same user, different bug, same component): marcusquinn/aidevops#21541 — `auto-update-helper.sh status` crashes on Linux due to a separate `set -euo pipefail` interaction with a non-existent systemd property name. That bug is cosmetic (display only); this bug is functional (data pollution + repeated unnecessary work).

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.13.6
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.17.0-22-generic)
- systemd: 255 (255.4-1ubuntu8.15)
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- gh CLI: gh version 2.91.0 (2026-04-22)

## Affected files (sourced from deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`)

- `auto-update-helper.sh:751` (`cmd_check` entry)
- `auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:281-296` (`_run_skill_update`)
- `auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:298-337` (`check_skill_freshness`)
- `skill-update-core-lib.sh:471, 547, 666` (3 call sites of `$ADD_SKILL_HELPER add ... --force`)
- `add-skill-helper.sh:963` (`target_dir=".agents/$(dirname \"$target_path\")"`)
- `add-skill-helper.sh:1240, 1473, 1561` (3 sites: `target_file=".agents/${target_path}.md"`)
- `~/.config/systemd/user/aidevops-auto-update.service` (no `WorkingDirectory=` set)

title: task-complete-helper.sh assumes '## Done' heading; many repos use '## Completed'
body:
## What

`task-complete-helper.sh` (in `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`) errors out with `## Done section not found in /path/to/TODO.md — cannot move completed task` when the target repo's TODO.md uses `## Completed` instead of `## Done`.

Reproduced in `johnwaldo/ilds` (TODO.md uses `## Completed`):

```
$ task-complete-helper.sh t150 --pr 676
[INFO] Completing task: t150
[INFO] Proof-log: PR #676
[INFO] Verifying PR #676 is merged...
[OK] PR #676 is merged (mergedAt: 2026-04-28T15:04:23Z)
[ERROR] ## Done section not found in /Users/justin/Git/ilds/TODO.md — cannot move completed task
```

## Why this matters

The interactive session-end workflow expects this helper to mark tasks complete. When it fails, the agent has to either:
1. Edit TODO.md by hand (counter-productive — defeats the helper)
2. Skip the TODO update and flag drift in session review (what happened in this session)
3. Open a worktree+PR for one line of TODO content (overkill ceremony)

None of these are good. The helper should be tolerant of the heading variants real repos use.

## Suggested fix

In `task-complete-helper.sh`, accept any of: `## Done`, `## Completed`, `## Complete`, `## Finished` (case-insensitive). Match on first hit. If none found, error with the list of headings tried so the user can pick a convention.

Optional: emit a one-line warning when `## Completed` (or non-canonical) is matched, suggesting the repo migrate to the canonical `## Done` for consistency. Don't block.

## Files Scope

- ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/task-complete-helper.sh (the source — deployed copy lives at ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/)

## Acceptance

- `task-complete-helper.sh tNNN --pr MMM` succeeds against TODO.md files using `## Done`, `## Completed`, `## Complete`, or `## Finished`.
- Existing tests still pass.
- New test case covers each heading variant.

## Source

ILDS session 2026-04-28: t150 completion flow blocked by this. See johnwaldo/ilds#675 + PR#676 for the work that triggered the discovery.

title: Feature request: framework workaround for macOS screenshot Unicode filename bug (U+202F)
body:
## Description

The Claude Code `Read` tool fails on macOS screenshot filenames because macOS inserts a Unicode narrow no-break space (U+202F) before AM/PM in the timestamp portion of the filename.

Example filename: `Screenshot 2026-04-27 at 2.06.27 PM.png` — the space before "PM" is U+202F, not a regular space (U+0020).

When the Read tool encounters this character, it truncates the path and returns:
```
File not found: /Users
```

This is technically a Claude Code (Anthropic) tool limitation, but a framework-level workaround would help all macOS users.

## Expected Behavior

Framework should handle Unicode characters in filenames transparently, or provide a helper that sanitizes filenames before passing to the Read tool.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a screenshot on macOS (Cmd+Shift+4 or similar)
2. File lands in Downloads as e.g. `Screenshot 2026-04-28 at 8.16.59 AM.png`
3. Ask Claude Code to read the file by its full path
4. Read tool fails with `File not found: /Users`

## Workarounds Applied

Current workaround is manual: `cp ~/Downloads/Screenshot*pattern*.png /tmp/clean-name.png` then Read from /tmp. This works but requires the agent to remember to do it every time, and users who drag-and-drop screenshots into chat hit the error repeatedly.

## Suggested Fix

A pre-Read filename sanitizer or helper that:
- Detects U+202F (and potentially other problematic Unicode) in file paths
- Copies to a clean temp path automatically
- Returns the clean path for the Read tool

Or a convention/hook that intercepts Read calls on paths containing known-problematic Unicode and auto-redirects.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.13.6
- **AI Assistant**: Claude Code
- **OS**: macOS 15.7.5
- **Shell**: bash 5.3.9(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.91.0 (2026-04-22)

## Additional Context

This affects any macOS user who takes screenshots and tries to share them with Claude Code agents. The U+202F character is invisible — users have no idea why their file can't be found. The agent typically has to try multiple approaches (glob patterns, wildcards, ls with wildcards) before discovering the issue, burning significant session time.

title: bug: review-bot-gate-reusable check name breaks branch protection contract (regression of GH#5365 in PR #20748)
body:
## Description

`review-bot-gate-reusable.yml` produces a check run named `gate / review-bot-gate` instead of `review-bot-gate`, breaking the documented branch-protection contract for every downstream repo using the canonical caller template.

**Root cause** — PR #20748 (commit `cc44bb231`, 2026-04-24, GH#20727) migrated the workflow from a single-level `jobs.review-bot-gate:` to a caller-reusable pattern with `jobs.gate:` calling `jobs.review-bot-gate:`. GitHub names check runs from reusable workflows as `<caller_job_id> / <reusable_job_id>`, producing `gate / review-bot-gate`.

The canonical caller template (`.agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml:16-17`) and the reusable workflow itself (`.github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml:17-18`) both still document:

> To enforce: add "review-bot-gate" as a required status check in GitHub branch protection settings for each repo.

That contract is now broken. Branch protection requiring `review-bot-gate` (bare) waits forever for a status that will never arrive.

**This is the same bug class GH#5365 fixed in March 2026** (commit `c7081c549`, "fix: remove job name field so check name matches branch protection"). The reusable migration reintroduced it via a different vector — a caller-job wrapper instead of an explicit `name:` field.

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- (a) The reusable workflow posts a `review-bot-gate` commit status directly via `gh api .../statuses/...`, mirroring the maintainer-gate pattern (preferred — restores the documented contract for all downstream repos without requiring branch-protection changes).
- (b) The framework documentation and `aidevops sync-workflows` migrate every downstream repo's branch protection from `review-bot-gate` to `gate / review-bot-gate` (less ideal — every consumer must update their settings).

`maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` chose path (a): Job 1 (`check-pr`, `name: Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`) explicitly posts a `maintainer-gate` commit status via `gh api repos/${REPO}/statuses/${HEAD_SHA}` at lines 115-128, 169-182, 213-218, 231-243, 397-409, 411-423. That is why `maintainer-gate` continues to work as a required status check despite the same caller-job wrapper structure.

`review-bot-gate-reusable.yml` has no equivalent. Verified:

```bash
$ rg -n "statuses" .github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml
67:      statuses: read
```

Only the permission, no posting code.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (any downstream repo with `review-bot-gate` as a required status check, after running `aidevops sync-workflows --apply`):

```bash
gh pr view <PR> --repo <slug> --json mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup
```

**Actual output**:

```json
{
  "mergeStateStatus": "BLOCKED",
  "statusCheckRollup": [
    {"__typename": "CheckRun", "name": "gate / review-bot-gate", "conclusion": "SUCCESS"},
    ...
  ]
}
```

GitHub UI shows: `review-bot-gate — Expected — Waiting for status to be reported`.

```bash
$ gh api repos/<slug>/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks --jq '.contexts'
["review-bot-gate"]

$ gh api repos/<slug>/commits/<head_sha>/status --jq '.statuses[].context'
# (empty — no review-bot-gate StatusContext exists)
```

**Expected output**: a `review-bot-gate` StatusContext or CheckRun matches the branch protection requirement and the PR becomes mergeable.

**Causal code**:

```
$ git log --oneline cc44bb231 -1
cc44bb231 GH#20727: migrate review-bot-gate.yml to reusable-workflow pattern (#20748)
```

The migration commit message documents the SHA-pin drift fix but does not mention check-name preservation. The previous fix (`c7081c549`, GH#5365) is not referenced; its invariant — "the produced check name MUST equal `review-bot-gate`" — was lost in the migration.

**Call-site sweep**:

```bash
$ rg -n 'review-bot-gate' .github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml
17:# To enforce: add "review-bot-gate" as a required status check in
38:  review-bot-gate:

$ rg -n 'review-bot-gate' .agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml
16:# To enforce: add "review-bot-gate" as a required status check in
54:  group: review-bot-gate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In any repo using the canonical `review-bot-gate-caller.yml` (resync via `aidevops sync-workflows --apply`).
2. Add `review-bot-gate` as a required status check in branch protection for `main`.
3. Open a PR. Wait for all checks to complete.
4. PR shows `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` with `review-bot-gate — Expected — Waiting for status to be reported`, even though `gate / review-bot-gate` completed with `SUCCESS`.

Live evidence — robstiles/qs-agency PR #2114 at the time of filing.

## Workarounds Applied

| Workaround | Systemic fix |
|---|---|
| `enforce_admins: false` on `main` lets the repo owner merge PRs despite the missing required check (e.g. PR #2111 merged 2026-04-28 14:30 UTC). | Fix the framework so the `review-bot-gate` status is actually posted; admin bypass should not be the routine merge path. |
| Manually changing branch protection from `review-bot-gate` to `gate / review-bot-gate` (per-repo, per-consumer). | Same as above — one fix in the framework propagates to all consumers via `aidevops sync-workflows`. |

## Files to modify

**EDIT: `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml`** — add a status-posting step that runs `if: always()` after the helper invocation. Mirror the pattern at `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml:115-128` (failure path) and `:213-218` (success path). Pseudocode insertion after the existing `Gate result` step (line 164) and before `Summary` (line 184):

```yaml
- name: Post review-bot-gate commit status
  if: always()
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.event.pull_request.merge_commit_sha }}
    REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    GATE_PASSED: ${{ steps.check.outputs.gate_passed }}
    SKIP_GATE: ${{ steps.skip.outputs.skip }}
    RESULT: ${{ steps.check.outputs.result }}
  run: |
    if [[ "${GATE_PASSED}" == "true" ]] || [[ "${SKIP_GATE}" == "true" ]]; then
      STATE=success
      DESC="Review bot gate passed (${RESULT:-SKIP})"
    else
      STATE=failure
      DESC="Review bot gate WAITING — no real bot review yet"
    fi
    gh api "repos/${REPO}/statuses/${HEAD_SHA}" \
      --method POST \
      -f state="${STATE}" \
      -f context="review-bot-gate" \
      -f description="${DESC}" \
      2>/dev/null || { sleep 5 && gh api "repos/${REPO}/statuses/${HEAD_SHA}" \
      --method POST \
      -f state="${STATE}" \
      -f context="review-bot-gate" \
      -f description="${DESC}"; } || {
      echo "::error::Failed to post review-bot-gate commit status after retry"
      exit 1
    }
```

Note the `HEAD_SHA` fallback — `issue_comment` events do not populate `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, so an explicit lookup may be needed (see `maintainer-gate-reusable.yml:84` for the canonical pattern; that workflow only fires on `pull_request_target` so it can use the simpler form).

**EDIT: `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml:64-67`** — upgrade job-level `permissions: statuses: read` to `statuses: write`.

**EDIT: `.agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml:32-35`** — upgrade caller-level ceiling from `statuses: read` to `statuses: write`. Reusable-workflow job-level permissions cannot exceed the caller's ceiling, so the caller template must match.

**EDIT: `~/Git/qs-agency/.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml:32-35`** (and every other `aidevops sync-workflows`-managed downstream repo) — same caller permission upgrade. Will propagate via `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` after the canonical template is updated.

## Reference pattern

Model on `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml`:
- Status-posting blocks at lines 115-128, 169-182, 213-218, 231-243, 397-409, 411-423 (six call sites — one per gate decision point).
- `permissions: statuses: write` at line 72.
- Caller template `.agents/templates/workflows/maintainer-gate-caller.yml:31` declares `statuses: write` at the ceiling.

## Verification

After implementing the fix:

```bash
# 1. Verify the reusable posts a review-bot-gate commit status:
gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<test-pr-head>/status --jq '.statuses[] | select(.context == "review-bot-gate")'
# Expected: one entry with state=success or state=failure

# 2. Verify on a downstream repo after sync:
aidevops sync-workflows --apply
# (open a test PR in qs-agency or similar)
gh api repos/robstiles/qs-agency/commits/<test-pr-head>/status --jq '.statuses[].context'
# Expected: includes "review-bot-gate"

# 3. Verify branch protection contract is restored:
gh pr view <PR> --repo robstiles/qs-agency --json mergeStateStatus
# Expected: "MERGEABLE" (not "BLOCKED" with phantom required check)
```

## Migration impact for downstream repos

Once the fix lands and downstream repos run `aidevops sync-workflows --apply`, no branch-protection changes are needed — the existing `review-bot-gate` requirement starts being satisfied.

Repos that already changed their branch protection to `gate / review-bot-gate` as a workaround should change it back to `review-bot-gate` after syncing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In any repo with the canonical `review-bot-gate-caller.yml` template (post-PR #20748).
2. Configure branch protection on `main` to require `review-bot-gate` (per the framework's documented contract).
3. Open a PR.
4. Observe: `gate / review-bot-gate` CheckRun completes; `review-bot-gate` StatusContext never arrives; PR is permanently `BLOCKED`.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.13.6
- Latest version: 3.13.6
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: 2.91.0 (2026-04-22)

Not Linux-specific. The bug is in how GitHub names check runs from reusable workflows (caller-job-id prefix), which is a server-side behaviour identical on all platforms.

## Additional Context

- Prior art: GH#5365 (closed) — same bug class, fixed via `name:` field removal in March 2026.
- Prior art: GH#14277 (closed) — `maintainer-gate` had a similar status-not-reporting bug; the fix introduced the explicit `gh api .../statuses/...` posting pattern that this issue proposes adopting for `review-bot-gate`.
- Discovery context: investigating robstiles/qs-agency PR #2114 stuck `BLOCKED` since 2026-04-28 14:30 UTC. PR #2111 merged via owner admin bypass (`enforce_admins: false`); subsequent PRs without bypass cannot merge.
- The migration commit (PR #20748, `cc44bb231`) was reviewed by Gemini Code Assist; the review focused on `check-workflows-helper.sh` performance optimizations and missed the structural check-name regression.
- Suggested label: `bug` (not `enhancement` — this restores a documented contract that was silently broken).

title: t3013: t3013: Fix _pulse_pids false positive — filter pgrep to non-pulse-parent processes
body:
## What

`pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh::_pulse_pids` and the `is-running`/`status` paths report 3-9 "pulse instances" when only 1 is actually running. The naive `pgrep -f` matches every shell whose command line contains `pulse-wrapper.sh`, including subshells of the parent pulse cycle that inherit the parent's command line.

Result: spurious "MULTIPLE pulse instances detected (GH#21433) — singleton invariant violated" warnings every time `is-running` or `status` is called during a busy cycle. This led an interactive session (this one) to mis-diagnose pile-up and run unnecessary `restart` commands.

## Why

Real pile-up detection matters — t3010 fast-fail relies on the lock holder PID, not pgrep. Lifecycle-helper is the human-facing diagnostic surface. False positives here trigger needless restarts, killing the lock holder and any in-flight subshells (e.g., `git fetch` housekeeping mid-stage).

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — `_pulse_pids` function (~line 80-86)

### Reference pattern

Filter pgrep output to PIDs whose PARENT command does not match the pulse pattern. Excludes subshells of any running pulse cycle. Acceptable when pulse is started by:
- launchd (PPID=1)
- setup.sh / aidevops update (PPID=installer process)
- manual `pulse-wrapper.sh` (PPID=user shell)

In all three cases, parent is NOT itself `pulse-wrapper.sh`. The filter is `parent_cmd !~ /pulse-wrapper\.sh/`.

```bash
_pulse_pids() {
  # Get matching PIDs first
  local _pids _pid _ppid _ppid_cmd
  _pids=$(pgrep -f "$_PULSE_PATTERN" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$_pids" ]] && return 0
  while read -r _pid; do
    _ppid=$(ps -p "$_pid" -o ppid= 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
    [[ -z "$_ppid" || "$_ppid" == "0" ]] && continue
    _ppid_cmd=$(ps -p "$_ppid" -o command= 2>/dev/null)
    # Skip PIDs whose parent IS another pulse-wrapper (= subshell)
    [[ "$_ppid_cmd" =~ pulse-wrapper\.sh ]] && continue
    printf '%s\n' "$_pid"
  done <<<"$_pids"
  return 0
}
```

### Verification

```bash
# Should return 1 when one pulse cycle running with subshells:
ps -eo pid,command | rg 'pulse-wrapper.sh' | rg -v 'rg ' | wc -l   # 9 (naive count)
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh is-running    # exit 0
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status        # should report "1 instance" not 9

# Should still detect real pile-up (kill lock holder, second launchd respawn arrives):
kill -9 $(cat ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.lockdir/pid)
sleep 130   # let launchd respawn
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status   # should report "1 instance" (the new one)
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_pulse_pids` returns only PPID-not-pulse pids
- [ ] `is-running` exit 0 with single instance, exit 1 with none, both correct
- [ ] `status` reports accurate count during busy cycle (subshells active)
- [ ] `_stop_all` still SIGTERMs all pulse processes including subshells (use the original pgrep, not the filtered list, in `_stop_all`)
- [ ] Existing tests pass

## Complexity Impact

Adds ~10 lines to `_pulse_pids`. Function stays well under 100-line gate.

title: t3014: Saturate fill-floor to 24 workers — raise parallelism cap + reduce per-candidate ceremony
body:
## Goal

Sustain **>20 concurrent workers** continuously by saturating the deterministic fill-floor to the full slot budget (currently 24).

## Current State (measured 2026-04-28T16:22-16:27Z)

Pulse cycle 21126 dispatched 10 candidates in parallel. Outcomes:

| Issue | Elapsed (ms) | rc | Outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| #21322 | 101,000 | 0 | success |
| #21299 | 103,000 | 0 | success |
| #3443  | 118,908 | 0 | success |
| #3450  | 181,000 | 124 | timeout |
| #21326 | 181,000 | 124 | timeout |
| #3452  | 182,000 | 124 | timeout |
| #21320 | 181,000 | 124 | timeout |
| #3445  | 305,589 | 124 | timeout |
| #3444  | 305,571 | 124 | timeout |
| #3440  | 303,777 | 124 | timeout |

Only **3/10 candidates dispatched successfully**. Steady-state worker count = 4 (out of 24 slot budget).

## Two Independent Bottlenecks

### Bottleneck A — Parallelism cap = 6 (env-default), should be slot-budget (24)

`_dff_compute_max_parallel` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:712-727` defaults `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL=6`. Even with infinite-fast ceremony, parallelism=6 means at most 6 workers/cycle reach the launch step before subsequent iterations begin. Cap is already capped at `effective_slots` so raising the env default is safe.

### Bottleneck B — Per-candidate ceremony 100-305s (often timing out)

`_dff_process_candidate` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:601` calls `dispatch_with_dedup` which makes serial gh API calls per candidate:
- `is-assigned` check
- Origin label set
- `status:in-progress` set
- Worktree pre-creation
- Worker spawn

When gh rate-limit budget is low or GraphQL is congested, these gh calls retry/backoff up to the 300s candidate timeout (`FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT`, t2989). 7/10 candidates in the sample above hit that ceiling.

## Why

P0 client demo tomorrow. Backlog is 60 dispatchable issues, 24 slot budget. At current 4-worker steady state, throughput ≈ 8 PRs/hr; required to clear backlog before demo ≈ 30 PRs/hr (sustainable 20+ workers).

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:712-727` — `_dff_compute_max_parallel`
  - Change default `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL=6` → `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL=24` (or `effective_slots`, since the existing cap clamps it)
  - Document the new default in the function-header comment
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` — investigate ceremony bottleneck
  - Profile gh API calls in `dispatch_with_dedup` (which calls take 100-300s?)
  - Consider: batch issue metadata fetch (one `gh api graphql` per cycle, not per candidate)
  - Consider: skip `is-assigned` if pulse already has the prefetched issue list (delta-only)
- `EDIT: .agents/configs/dispatch.conf` (or wherever `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` is documented) — update default
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` "Worker Diagnostics" section — note the new default

### Reference Pattern

t3005 PR (the original parallelization work) — model on its structure for outcomes file, `wait -n` cap, and module-global state isolation. Use the same idioms when investigating ceremony speedup.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. With patch applied, restart pulse and watch worker climb:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 60
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%MZ)] workers=$(ps -eo command | rg -c 'opencode-ai/bin/.opencode run.*full-loop')"
done

# 2. Success: ≥20 workers within 10 min of pulse restart, sustained for ≥30 min

# 3. No regression: pulse-stage-timings.log shows fill_floor_candidate_* completing in <120s typical, no >300s timeouts
tail -100 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | rg fill_floor_candidate

# 4. Stability: no worker death cascade (stable concurrent count, not flapping)
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` default raised to 24 (or dynamic = effective_slots)
- [ ] `_dff_compute_max_parallel` documents the new default
- [ ] Per-candidate ceremony median <60s (currently 101-305s)
- [ ] Live test: ≥20 workers sustained for ≥30 min after pulse restart
- [ ] Stage timings log shows <10% candidate timeouts (currently 70%)
- [ ] Released as v3.13.7 (or higher), propagating to alex-solovyev runner
- [ ] No worker death regression — workers complete or persist, do not die mid-task

## Complexity Impact

`_dff_compute_max_parallel` change is one-line. `dispatch_with_dedup` profiling/optimization may grow that function — keep under 100-line gate by extracting helpers. New batch-fetch helper would be a NEW file (`pulse-dispatch-batch-fetch-lib.sh`), no existing function bloat.

## Test Plan (full-loop session)

1. Profile current `dispatch_with_dedup` — instrument with timing per gh API call
2. Identify slowest gh call (likely `is-assigned` check or label set)
3. Apply parallelism cap change first (one-line, low risk)
4. Restart pulse, observe — if <20 workers, ceremony is the blocker not cap
5. Apply ceremony speedup (batch fetch / cache-first lookup)
6. Restart pulse, verify 20+ sustained
7. Cut release, full-loop ends
