title: t3015: t3015: Architectural rename — split dispatch_floor + dispatch_max (Option B sweep, follows t3014)
body:
## Status — Sequencing

**BLOCKED behind [t3014 / #21551](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21551).** Do not start until #21551 merges. This task is the follow-on architectural sweep to make the dispatch path's terminology consistent with what the original GH#14471 design intended.

## Goal

Rename and split the conflated "fill floor" mechanism into two clearly-scoped functions per the original GH#14471 intent (see [t3014 floor-vs-max clarification comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21551#issuecomment-4337394391)):

- **`dispatch_floor`** — minimum guarantee under resource constraint (throttle, rate-limit reserve, OAuth budget low). Serial or near-serial. Goal: keep backlog moving when resources are scarce.
- **`dispatch_max`** — saturate to `effective_slots = max_workers - active_workers`. Parallel = effective_slots, no artificial cap. Goal: fill all available capacity when resources are healthy.

This is a **rename + restructure**, not a behaviour change. t3014 will have already implemented the saturate-to-max behaviour; t3015 makes the naming/structure match.

## Why

After t3014 lands, the dispatch path will be doing the right thing but its naming will lie about it: `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` will be saturating to max, and `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` will either be removed or renamed unhelpfully. Future maintainers reading the code will hit the same conceptual confusion that wasted hours this week. Consistency now is cheap; consistency later (after more callers accumulate) is expensive.

This also unblocks **future evidence-based tuning** as a separate concern: once the two paths are clearly named, individual thresholds (floor minimum count, max parallelism level, throttle activation triggers) can be adjusted based on concurrency telemetry, RAM budget, GraphQL/REST rate-limit headroom, and OAuth budget. Today those tunings would have to fight the existing naming.

## How

### Files Scope (the full sweep — 33 files, 310 references)

#### Core implementation (touches behaviour — coordinate with t3014's final state)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — split `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` → `dispatch_max` (default path) + `dispatch_floor` (throttle branch, called from `dispatch_max` when throttle is engaged)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — update call sites (`apply_deterministic_fill_floor` → `apply_dispatch_max`)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — rename references in comments + dedup logic
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh` — `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` → `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` (timeout applies to both floor and max paths)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-backoff-helper.sh` — references in backoff path
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` — confirms the float→floor downgrade path
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` — call sites
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` — comments only
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh` — comments only
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` — diagnostic output strings
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh` — comments only

#### Symbol renames (28 distinct symbols, mechanical)

| Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor()` | `dispatch_max()` | Default saturate path |
| `apply_deterministic_fill_floor()` | `apply_dispatch_max()` | Wrapper called by pulse cycle |
| (new) | `dispatch_floor()` | Throttle-mode minimum, called from `dispatch_max` when throttle engaged |
| `_dff_*` family (24 helpers) | `_dispatch_*` family | Drop the misleading "ff" prefix; use `_dispatch_max_*` / `_dispatch_floor_*` based on which path the helper serves; shared helpers use `_dispatch_*` |
| `_DFF_ROUND_DISPATCHED` | `_DISPATCH_ROUND_DISPATCHED` | Module-global state |
| `_DFF_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER` | `_DISPATCH_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER` | Module-global state |
| `_DFF_THROTTLE_FILE` | `_DISPATCH_THROTTLE_FILE` | Path constant |
| `_DFF_THROTTLE_CLEARED` | `_DISPATCH_THROTTLE_CLEARED` | Module-global state |
| `_DFF_CANARY_CACHE` | `_DISPATCH_CANARY_CACHE` | Cache var |
| `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` | `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` | Env var; provide alias for back-compat one release |
| `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` | (removed if t3014 removed it) or `DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL` | If t3014 leaves the env var in place, rename here |

#### Stats counters (pulse-stats.json) — needs migration handling
- `fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout` → `dispatch_per_candidate_timeout`
- (new from t3014) `dispatch_floor_runs` — increment when throttle path entered
- (new from t3014) `dispatch_max_runs` — increment when saturate path entered
- Migration: keep the old key reading paths for one release for backward-compat with logs/diagnostics

#### Documentation
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/dispatch-architecture.md` — rewrite the dispatch-flow section with the floor-vs-max distinction explicit; update the call diagram
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/incident-recovery-runbook.md` — update references to fill_floor counters
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` "Worker Diagnostics" section if it mentions fill_floor (none found in current grep, but verify)
- `EDIT: CHANGELOG.md` — t3015 entry under [Unreleased]

#### Tests (rename + verify behaviour preserved)
- `RENAME: .agents/scripts/tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh` → `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh` — update symbol references
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-consolidation-phase2.sh` — update symbol references
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-bash32-nul-crash.sh` — update symbol references (likely comments only)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-diagnose-cycle-health.sh` — update fixture timing log entries that say `fill_floor_candidate_*` to match new stage name `dispatch_max_candidate_*`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-runner-health.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh` — update fixtures
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-floor-throttle-engages.sh` — verify floor path activates under throttle and dispatches at minimum count

#### Config
- `EDIT: .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc` — rename keys; document floor + max separately
- `EDIT: .github/workflows/apply-status-available-default.yml` — references to fill_floor concept

#### Historical artifacts (DO NOT EDIT — they document past work)
- `TODO.md` line 924 — t3005 entry references `_dispatch_fill_floor` in past tense; leave as historical record
- `todo/tasks/GH-18830-brief.md`, `todo/tasks/t1996-brief.md`, `todo/tasks/t2157-brief.md`, `todo/tasks/t2392-brief.md` — historical briefs, leave unchanged

### Reference Pattern

When splitting `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` into `dispatch_max` + `dispatch_floor`:

```bash
# After this PR:
dispatch_max() {
    if _dispatch_should_use_floor_path; then
        dispatch_floor "$@"     # throttle/rate-limit/oauth-low → minimum guarantee
        return $?
    fi
    # Default: saturate to effective_slots, parallelism = effective_slots
    _dispatch_max_loop "$@"
}
```

title: t3016: test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh fails 2/4 after #21553 split (Code Quality Analysis red on main)
body:
## What

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` fails 2/4 tests on `main` since #21553 (pulse-wrapper.sh split into bootstrap+cycle sub-libraries):

```
PASS --canary exits 0 (sourcing + self-check + lock passed)
FAIL --canary prints 'canary: ok' checkpoint
       Expected line starting with 'canary: ok'. Exit 0. Output: [config] Cannot read JSONC file: /tmp/.../home/.aidevops/agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc
       [config] Failed to parse defaults — config system unavailable
FAIL _pulse_setup_canary_mode() defined in pulse-wrapper.sh
       Function _pulse_setup_canary_mode() not found in /home/runner/work/aidevops/aidevops/.agents/scripts/tests/../pulse-wrapper.sh
PASS canary short-circuit is after acquire_instance_lock
```

This blocks Code Quality Analysis CI for any PR. Currently red on `main` and on every open PR.

## Why

After #21553 (the 5-way pulse-wrapper.sh split), `_pulse_setup_canary_mode` lives at `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh:121`, but the canary test still greps for it in `pulse-wrapper.sh`. The sandboxed canary run also fails because `pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh::_load_config` requires `~/.aidevops/agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc` to be present, and the test sandbox creates an empty `${sandbox}/home` directory without seeding that config file.

Live evidence:

```
$ grep -rn "_pulse_setup_canary_mode" .agents/scripts/*.sh | head -5
.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh:108:# _pulse_setup_canary_mode
.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh:121:_pulse_setup_canary_mode() {
.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1147:# _pulse_setup_canary_mode, _detect_invocation_source, and
.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1179:	_pulse_setup_canary_mode "$@"
```

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh:36` — `WRAPPER_SCRIPT` is the source of truth for both the runtime invocation (`bash "$WRAPPER_SCRIPT" --canary`) and the static grep checks. Two changes needed:

1. **Test 3 (function existence check, line ~125-133):** the function moved to `pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh`. Update the static grep to look in the bootstrap file:
   ```bash
   local bootstrap_script="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh"
   if grep -q "^_pulse_setup_canary_mode()" "$bootstrap_script"; then
       print_result "_pulse_setup_canary_mode() defined in pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh" 0
       return 0
   fi
   ```

2. **Tests 1 & 2 (sandbox config seeding):** the canary run errors with "Cannot read JSONC file" and "config system unavailable" because the sandboxed `HOME` is missing `~/.aidevops/agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc`. Two acceptable approaches:

   - **Option A (preferred):** seed the sandbox by copying the canonical config file from the worktree before invoking the canary:
     ```bash
     mkdir -p "${sandbox}/home/.aidevops/agents/configs"
     cp "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc" \
        "${sandbox}/home/.aidevops/agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc"
     ```
     This mirrors what `setup.sh` does at install time. Keeps the bootstrap config-loading strict.

   - **Option B (alternative):** make `_load_config` in `pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh` tolerate a missing defaults file when `PULSE_CANARY_MODE=1` is set. Falls back to an in-script default. More invasive but better DX for ad-hoc canary runs from clean homedirs.

Pick A unless there's a reason to weaken bootstrap's config requirements; A is a 4-line test-only change, B touches the bootstrap module.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` passes 4/4 from a clean homedir on macOS and ubuntu.
- `Code Quality Analysis` CI workflow goes green on `main` after this merges.
- The canary test still catches the regression class it was designed for (set -e exit-code propagation in `_pulse_handle_self_check`) — verify by temporarily adding `return 1` to that function and confirming Test 1 fails.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` passes clean.

## Reference Pattern

The split itself: PR #21553 (commit ac1e66635). Look at how `_pulse_setup_canary_mode` was moved in that diff to understand the new ownership boundary between `pulse-wrapper.sh` (entrypoint orchestrator) and `pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh` (sourcing + canary mode + self-check).

The canonical defaults file: `.agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc` — committed, parsed by `pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh::_load_config`.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh

(If implementing Option B, add `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh` to scope.)

title: feat: per-worktree preview subdomains via local proxy (Build+ workflow)
body:
## Why

Interactive AI sessions are required to do all code changes in a linked worktree (`~/Git/<repo>-<branch>/`), keeping the canonical repo on the default branch. The user's local dev server is typically pinned to the canonical directory (one process bound to a fixed port, often proxied via a local hostname like `<webapp>.local`).

That creates a recurring frustration for every web project managed by aidevops:

1. Session creates a worktree, makes changes, opens a PR.
2. User asks "where can I see it?" — and currently the only options are: (a) stop the canonical dev server and restart it from the worktree path, (b) merge the PR first, or (c) read the diff cold.
3. Build+ has no way to surface a preview link in its turn-end summary.

Real example surfaced in a managed private repo: a session created `~/Git/<webapp>-feature-tNNN-…/` with the changes, but the user's `<webapp>.local` was still pointing at the canonical default-branch checkout, so the changes were invisible until they merged the PR. The user explicitly flagged this as a Build+-level workflow gap that should be solved generically across aidevops-managed projects, not patched per-repo.

## What

A "preview proxy" capability so every worktree that contains a runnable dev server gets its own subdomain. When Build+ (or any session) creates a worktree, it allocates a port + registers a proxy route, and surfaces a preview URL in the conversation:

```
Worktree:   ~/Git/<webapp>-feature-tNNN-…/
Preview:    https://<branch-slug>.<webapp>.local (port 3142)
Start dev:  AIDEVOPS_PREVIEW_PORT=3142 pnpm dev:web
```

Same `<webapp>.local` parent the user already has in `/etc/hosts` + a local proxy (e.g. Traefik); just per-branch subdomains.

## How (proposed design)

**1. Port allocator.** New helper `preview-proxy-helper.sh` with state at `~/.aidevops/state/worktree-ports.json`:

```json
{
  "<owner>/<webapp>": {
    "feature/tNNN-<short-desc>": { "port": 3142, "allocated_at": "..." }
  }
}
```

Allocate from a configurable pool (default 3100–3199 per project, fallback 3200–3999 global). Detect collisions (`lsof -ti:<port>`) before assigning. Free on worktree removal.

**2. Pluggable proxy backend.** `~/.config/aidevops/preview-proxy.json` (per-runtime, ignored if absent → fall back to plain `localhost:<port>`):

```json
{
  "backend": "traefik-file",
  "config_dir": "/Users/<user>/.local-dev-proxy/dynamic/",
  "domain_template": "{branch_slug}.{repo}.local",
  "port_pool": { "default": [3100, 3199] }
}
```

Initial backend: **Traefik file provider** (matches the user's existing `~/.local-dev-proxy/`). Each allocation writes a small dynamic file Traefik hot-reloads. Future backends: Caddy on-demand TLS, Nginx, Cloudflare Tunnel for remote previews.

**3. Per-project dev hook.** Optional block in `.aidevops.json` declares how the project's dev server reads its port:

```json
{
  "preview": {
    "command": "pnpm dev:web",
    "port_env": "PORT",
    "default_port": 3100,
    "ready_check": "http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/health"
  }
}
```

Without this block, the helper just allocates a port and prints it — user wires it up manually. With it, the start command can be emitted directly.

**4. Worktree helper integration.**

- `worktree-helper.sh add` (and `wt switch -c`) calls `preview-proxy-helper.sh allocate <repo_slug> <branch>` after the worktree exists; output goes into the helper's stdout summary.
- `worktree-helper.sh remove` calls `preview-proxy-helper.sh free <repo_slug> <branch>` so the proxy entry and port go away with the worktree.
- Both should be best-effort + non-fatal: missing config → log_info skip, never block worktree ops.

**5. Build+ output.** When Build+ announces a new worktree in chat, include the preview URL + start command. Single-line format:

```
Created worktree at ~/Git/<webapp>-feature-tNNN-…/. Preview: https://<branch-slug>.<webapp>.local — start with `AIDEVOPS_PREVIEW_PORT=3142 pnpm dev:web` from that directory.
```

This addresses the exact gap the user flagged: sessions should give the user a working preview link without manual port juggling.

**6. Branch-slug → subdomain.** Sanitize for DNS:

- Strip leading `feature/`, `fix/`, `bugfix/`, `refactor/`, `chore/`, `experiment/`, `release/` prefixes.
- Lowercase, replace `[^a-z0-9-]` → `-`, collapse repeats, trim `-`.
- Truncate to 63 chars (DNS label max). If collision after truncation, append a 4-char hash of the full branch name.

Examples:

- `feature/tNNN-nav-reorder-tasks-ai-activity` → `tNNN-nav-reorder-tasks-ai-activity`
- `fix/tNNN-broken-snapshots` → `tNNN-broken-snapshots`
- `feature/auto-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-ghNNNN` → `auto-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-ghNNNN`

**7. Static fallback.** If no `preview-proxy.json` is present, the helper still allocates a port and emits `http://localhost:<port>`. The proxy registration is the optional layer.

## Acceptance

- `preview-proxy-helper.sh allocate <slug> <branch>` returns `{ port, url, start_hint }` and registers the route.
- `preview-proxy-helper.sh free <slug> <branch>` releases the port and removes the route. Idempotent.
- `worktree-helper.sh add|remove` invoke allocate/free automatically; failure is non-fatal.
- One reference Traefik backend that works with the canonical `~/.local-dev-proxy/` layout (Traefik v3 file provider). Mention setup steps in `reference/preview-proxy.md` (mkcert for HTTPS, hosts/dnsmasq for `*.local`).
- `.aidevops.json` schema documented with the `preview` block.
- Build+ workflow doc (`workflows/build-plus.md` or wherever) explicitly references the preview URL output requirement.
- Works on macOS first; Linux follows.

## Out of scope (good follow-ups)

- HTTPS cert auto-issue (mkcert root CA install). Reference doc covers manual setup.
- Cloudflare Tunnel / ngrok backends for remote previews shared with non-local reviewers.
- Multi-process apps (web + extension + mobile dev servers per worktree). v1 = one preview per worktree.
- Auto-starting the dev server. Print the start hint, let the user run it.

## Files to modify (anchor for the implementer)

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/preview-proxy-helper.sh` — port allocator + backend dispatcher.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/preview-proxy-backends/traefik-file.sh` — Traefik file provider implementation.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` — call `allocate` after `git worktree add`, call `free` on remove. Best-effort, non-fatal.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (or wherever Build+ announces worktrees) — append preview URL + start hint to the announcement.
- `NEW: .agents/reference/preview-proxy.md` — design doc, backends, mkcert/hosts setup steps.
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` — single-paragraph blurb under "Working Directories" / Build+ section pointing to the reference doc.
- `EDIT: .aidevops.json` schema — document the `preview` block (per-project hook).

## Reference patterns

- `worktree-helper.sh` for the existing helper shape (state file, atomic writes, idempotent operations).
- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` for the "best-effort, non-fatal, fail-open" pattern needed when proxy backend is missing.
- A Traefik-on-Docker stack at `~/.local-dev-proxy/docker-compose.yml` (the canonical local-proxy pattern aidevops users are already running) as the first backend target.

## Source

User explicitly requested this as a generic Build+ capability during a session reviewing a managed private repo PR: a worktree was opened for the change, but the user's running dev server still pointed at the canonical default-branch checkout, so the change was invisible. The user proposed: every worktree should get its own subdomain (`https://<branch-slug>.<webapp>.local`) that sessions can hand back as a preview link. They explicitly framed this as belonging in the Build+ part of aidevops, applicable to all aidevops-managed app development — not a per-repo patch.

title: t3017: Add 'aidevops circuit-breaker' CLI subcommand for one-line copy/paste reset
body:
## What

Expose `circuit-breaker-helper.sh` via the top-level `aidevops` CLI so users can reset/inspect the supervisor circuit breaker from a quick copy/paste line, without remembering the deployed-helper path.

## Why

When the supervisor circuit breaker trips (#21556), the auto-generated issue tells the user to run:

```
circuit-breaker-helper.sh reset
```

This requires `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` to be on $PATH (it is, by default) AND for the user to remember the exact helper name. Most other operational entry points (`badges`, `approve`, `issue`, `pulse`, `security`, `stats`) are surfaced via the canonical `aidevops <subcommand>` CLI. Circuit breaker is the missing one in that family.

## How

EDIT: aidevops.sh:~2110 — add a `circuit-breaker | cb)` case in the dispatch switch (model on the existing `approve)` and `issue)` lines that delegate via `_dispatch_helper`).
EDIT: aidevops.sh:~1570 — add a one-line entry in `cmd_help` (model on existing `approve <cmd>` / `issue <cmd>` lines).
EDIT: aidevops.sh:~1755 — add a worked example block in `_help_detailed_sections` (model on the `Secrets:` / `Knowledge Plane:` block right above).
EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md — add `circuit-breaker` to the Quick Reference CLI line.
EDIT: .agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh:~570,~720 — update `Resolution` instruction in the GH issue body and `cmd_help` usage block to recommend `aidevops circuit-breaker reset` first, with the helper path as fallback.

### Files Scope

- aidevops.sh
- .agents/AGENTS.md
- .agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh

### Reference pattern

`approve)` / `issue)` cases at aidevops.sh:2110-2111 — single-line `_dispatch_helper` delegation.

## Acceptance

- `aidevops circuit-breaker status` prints the breaker state (matches `circuit-breaker-helper.sh status`).
- `aidevops circuit-breaker reset` resets the breaker and closes the GH issue.

title: t3018: Self-heal stale rate-limit stamp when no live pulse lock holder (post-#21557 defense in depth)
body:
## What

Add self-healing to the entry-point rate-limit gate in `pulse-wrapper.sh` so a stale 'last run' timestamp left behind by a crashed cycle does NOT lock pulse out for `PULSE_MIN_INTERVAL_S` seconds.

## Why

The t3016/#21557 emergency surfaced a class of failure where:

1. A cycle starts, writes the rate-limit timestamp at line 1261 of pulse-wrapper.sh.
2. The cycle dies silently mid-way (e.g., source-gate regression, stage crash, OOM).
3. The lock is released by EXIT trap, but the timestamp persists.
4. Subsequent launchd respawns (every 60s) hit the rate-limit at line 1257 ('last run 60s ago < 90s threshold') and skip the cycle.
5. Pulse appears 'alive' (launchd keeps respawning) but no actual work happens until the timestamp ages past `PULSE_MIN_INTERVAL_S`.

The current logic writes the timestamp BEFORE doing any cycle work, so a fast crash creates a 90-second lockout. With `PULSE_MIN_INTERVAL_S=90` and launchd respawn=60s, this means at most 1 attempt per 90s window — a steep recovery rate when other users are affected.

Bonus self-healing: catches all future failure modes that leave a stale timestamp (not just t3016).

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1244-1262` — when the rate-limit threshold fires, ALSO check the instance lock state. If `pulse-wrapper.lockdir/pid` is missing, contains a non-numeric value, or refers to a dead process, the timestamp is 'ghost-recent' (left behind by a crashed cycle). Clear the timestamp file, log the recovery, and proceed with the cycle.

The lock check is the same primitive used elsewhere in pulse-wrapper.sh (line ~1216-1232) — read pid, validate is integer, `kill -0`. Fail-open: any error in the live-lock check defaults to 'no live lock' (proceed), since the cost of a false-positive proceed is much smaller than the cost of false-negative skip (the existing bug).

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh

### Reference pattern

Existing `kill -0` pattern in pulse-wrapper.sh:1227 (lock-staleness check) and pulse-instance-lock.sh.

## Acceptance

- A pulse-wrapper.sh invocation with timestamp 30s old AND no live lock holder PID clears the stamp and proceeds (logs '[pulse-wrapper] Rate-limit stamp <N>s old but no live lock holder — clearing stale stamp and proceeding').
- A pulse-wrapper.sh invocation with timestamp 30s old AND a live lock holder PID skips as before (existing rate-limit behaviour preserved for steady state).
- A pulse-wrapper.sh invocation with timestamp >= PULSE_MIN_INTERVAL_S behaves as before (no new behaviour).
- Shellcheck clean on pulse-wrapper.sh.
- test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh still 4/4 pass.

## Origin

Filed by the interactive session that diagnosed the post-PR-#21553 production breakage. Source-gate fix shipped via t3016/#21557; this is the layered defense against the same failure mode reoccurring.

title: Code Quality Analysis: Pulse Wrapper Canary flaky on main (blocks unrelated PRs)
body:
## Premise

`Pulse Wrapper Canary (GH#18790)` step inside `Code Quality Analysis` → `Framework Validation` is flaky on `main`. Recent runs:

- 2026-04-28T17:59:59Z — failure
- 2026-04-28T18:01:14Z — failure
- 2026-04-28T19:42:48Z — failure
- 2026-04-28T19:51:25Z — **success**
- 2026-04-28T19:57:29Z — running

PR #21569 (a CLI plumbing change that touches `aidevops.sh` + `circuit-breaker-helper.sh` + `AGENTS.md`, none of which are in `pulse-wrapper.sh` or the canary's reach) inherited this flake on first run.

## Symptom

```
FAIL --canary prints 'canary: ok' checkpoint
       Expected line starting with 'canary: ok'. Exit 0. Output:
       [config] Cannot read JSONC file: /tmp/tmp.m15lKa6QNX/home/.aidevops/agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc
       [config] Failed to parse defaults — config system unavailable

FAIL _pulse_setup_canary_mode() defined in pulse-wrapper.sh
       Function _pulse_setup_canary_mode() not found
```

The `--canary` flow appears to depend on `aidevops.defaults.jsonc` being readable in the test sandbox. The `/tmp/tmp.XXXX/home/.aidevops/agents/configs/` path suggests the test stages a fake `$HOME` and copies/symlinks framework files into it — when the copy step races or skips the JSONC, the config layer collapses and `_pulse_setup_canary_mode()` is never defined (because pulse-wrapper.sh aborts before reaching the function definition during sourcing? unclear — needs investigation).

## Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` — likely fixture/sandbox setup is the bug
- `READ-ONLY: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — to understand `--canary` and `_pulse_setup_canary_mode()` lifecycle
- `READ-ONLY: .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc` — to understand what the test must stage
- Possibly `EDIT: .github/workflows/code-quality.yml` — Framework Validation step that invokes the test

## Why

Flaky CI gate blocks unrelated PRs. PR #21569 is a small CLI plumbing change with zero connection to pulse-wrapper.sh; failing it on this canary forces a re-run cycle that costs time and CI minutes for every unrelated change.

## How

1. Reproduce: run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` locally a few times. If deterministic locally, the bug is in test setup; if non-deterministic locally, there's a race in `pulse-wrapper.sh --canary` itself.
2. Inspect the test's sandbox-setup logic — it stages a fake `$HOME` somewhere under `/tmp/tmp.XXXX/`. Confirm whether `aidevops.defaults.jsonc` is consistently copied/symlinked.
3. If the JSONC copy is missing on failure paths, fix the staging step. If the JSONC IS present but `_pulse_setup_canary_mode()` is still undefined, the early-abort path in pulse-wrapper.sh's sourcing is masking the function definition — investigate `set -e` interaction with the config layer.
4. Add a sanity check at the top of the test: assert `aidevops.defaults.jsonc` exists in the staged `$HOME` before invoking `--canary`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Test passes 10 consecutive times locally
- [ ] 5 consecutive `Code Quality Analysis` runs on `main` are green
- [ ] Root cause documented in commit message (was it sandbox setup, set -e, or something else?)

## Reference Pattern

Model on `test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh`'s own structure — the test framework is fine, just one specific assertion is racy. Compare working sandbox setup in sibling tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.

title: bug: tool-version-check.sh brew category gate skips all brew-origin tools on Linux (residual from #6762)
body:
## Description

`tool-version-check.sh` correctly detects outdated brew-origin tools (gh, glab, jq, shellcheck) on Linux and generates platform-aware update commands (apt-get/dnf), but the category-level gate at `_check_all_categories` (line 528) skips the entire "Homebrew" category when `brew` is not installed. The leaf functions fixed by PR #6815 (for #6762) never execute.

Separately, `_update_check_tools()` in `aidevops.sh` (line 419-425) has a gh-specific GitHub API fallback that correctly detects the version gap — so `aidevops update` reports `gh (2.91.0 -> 2.92.0)` — but the "Run full tool update check?" prompt delegates to `tool-version-check.sh --update`, which hits the same category gate and skips gh.

## Root Cause

Two locations, same underlying issue:

**1. `tool-version-check.sh:528` — category gate blocks all brew-origin tools on no-brew systems:**

```bash
# _check_all_categories(), line 528:
if command -v brew &>/dev/null && [[ ${#BREW_TOOLS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    check_category "Homebrew" "${BREW_TOOLS[@]}"
fi
```

`command -v brew` is false on Linux without Homebrew → entire category skipped. But the functions INSIDE the category already handle no-brew correctly:

- `get_brew_latest()` (line 346-366): falls back to GitHub Releases API for gh, glab, jq, shellcheck, wt
- `_brew_upgrade_cmd()` (line 89-95): generates `apt-get install --only-upgrade` / `dnf upgrade` when brew absent
- `check_tool()` → update path: would run the platform-aware command if it reached it

The gate was introduced at commit `3bcbbe38b8` (2026-02-22) before the platform-aware leaf functions were added by PR #6815 (2026-03-27). The PR fixed the leaves but didn't update the gate.

**2. `aidevops.sh:419-425` — detection works but update delegates to the broken path:**

```bash
# _update_check_tools(), line 419-425:
if [[ -n "$brew_bin" && -x "$brew_bin" ]]; then
    latest=$(_timeout_cmd 30 "$brew_bin" info --json=v2 "$brew_pkg" | ...)
elif [[ "$brew_pkg" == "gh" ]] && command -v gh &>/dev/null; then
    latest=$(get_public_release_tag "cli/cli")  # ← works on Linux
fi
```

This correctly detects the gap via the `elif` fallback, but the subsequent "Run full tool update check?" just calls `bash "$tool_check_script" --update` which hits issue #1.

## Expected Behavior

On Linux without brew, `tool-version-check.sh --update` should check and update brew-origin tools using the system package manager (apt-get/dnf), since both the version detection and update commands already support this.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
aidevops update
# Reports: "1 tool(s) have updates: gh (2.91.0 -> 2.92.0)"
# User answers "y" to "Run full tool update check?"
# tool-version-check.sh --update runs but gh is not updated
# Re-running aidevops update shows the same gh version gap
```

**Causal code**:

```bash
git blame .agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh -L 528,529
# 3bcbbe38b8 (Marcus Quinn 2026-02-22) if command -v brew &>/dev/null && ...
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Linux system with gh installed via apt (standard Debian/Ubuntu method), no Homebrew
2. gh has an available update (e.g. 2.91.0 → 2.92.0)
3. Run `aidevops update` — correctly reports the version gap
4. Accept "Run full tool update check?" — gh is not updated
5. Run `tool-version-check.sh --update` directly — same result, brew category skipped entirely

## Workarounds Applied

Manual `sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y gh` to update gh.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.13.6
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.91.0 (installed via apt, `/usr/bin/gh`)
- **brew**: not installed

## Additional Context

- Prior issue: #6762 (closed as done via PR #6815). That fix added `_brew_upgrade_cmd()` with apt/dnf support and `get_brew_latest()` with GitHub API fallback — but missed the category gate.
- The category name "Homebrew" is now a misnomer since the tools within it support apt/dnf. Renaming to "System Packages" or similar would clarify intent, though the functional fix is just relaxing the gate.

title: t3019: Auto-install commit-msg task-id guard during setup.sh
body:
## Task

`setup.sh`, `aidevops.sh`, and `agent-deploy.sh` do not invoke `install-task-id-guard.sh install`. Fresh clones and existing repos updated via `aidevops update` have **zero client-side enforcement** of the rule that t-IDs in commit subjects must come from `claim-task-id.sh`. The CI gate (`.github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml`) catches violations server-side, but only after a push has already burned dev cycles.

## Why

Memory recall on the canonical t2377 collision incident (Apr 2026): "sessions may skip the helper and hardcode IDs from stale counter reads." The commit-msg hook is the cheapest defence layer — it blocks at write time, before push, before CI. Closing the install gap converts opt-in to opt-out and brings every runner up to the same baseline without each user having to know about it.

This is consistent with the existing `install-pre-push-guards.sh` install convention (privacy / scope / dup-todo / complexity guards).

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/setup.sh
- .agents/scripts/agent-deploy.sh
- .agents/scripts/aidevops.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-installs-task-id-guard.sh (NEW)

EDIT: identify the canonical hook-install location in `setup.sh` (search for existing `install-pre-push-guards.sh` invocation or the post-deploy hook block) and add an idempotent call: `bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/install-task-id-guard.sh" install || log_warn "task-id guard install failed (non-fatal)"`. Honour `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_TASK_ID_HOOK=1` for opt-out parity with the other hook installs.

Reference pattern: `install-pre-push-guards.sh install` invocation site in `setup.sh` — copy the surrounding pattern (idempotency check, env-var skip, log_info on success).

### Complexity Impact

Single function modification, no growth past complexity gate. Estimated function-complexity delta: +5 lines per touched script.

## Acceptance

1. Fresh clone + `bash setup.sh --non-interactive` → `.git/hooks/commit-msg` exists and is executable.
2. `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_TASK_ID_HOOK=1 bash setup.sh --non-interactive` → hook is NOT installed (opt-out works).
3. Re-running setup with hook already installed → idempotent (no error, no duplicate install).
4. Test: `git commit --allow-empty -m "t99999: bogus"` after install → hook blocks with the existing "not claimed" error message.

## Verification

```bash
# In a fresh worktree
rm -f .git/hooks/commit-msg
bash ~/Git/aidevops/setup.sh --non-interactive
test -x .git/hooks/commit-msg && echo PASS-installed

# Opt-out
rm -f .git/hooks/commit-msg
AIDEVOPS_SKIP_TASK_ID_HOOK=1 bash ~/Git/aidevops/setup.sh --non-interactive
test ! -e .git/hooks/commit-msg && echo PASS-optout

# Idempotency
bash ~/Git/aidevops/setup.sh --non-interactive
bash ~/Git/aidevops/setup.sh --non-interactive  # should not error

# Functional check
git commit --allow-empty -m "t99999: unclaimed" 2>&1 | grep -q "not claimed via claim-task-id" && echo PASS-functional

# Lint
shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup.sh .agents/scripts/agent-deploy.sh .agents/scripts/aidevops.sh
```

title: t3020: Add brief-filename guard to block unclaimed t-IDs in todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md
body:
## Task

Brief files at `todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md` can currently be created and committed with **any** t-ID — including IDs that have never been allocated via `claim-task-id.sh`. The existing commit-msg guard (`install-task-id-guard.sh`) blocks unclaimed t-IDs in commit *subjects*, but does nothing about t-IDs that appear only in brief *filenames*. This is a parallel bypass vector that the t2377 post-mortem batch did not close.

## Why

Memory recall on the t2377 incident: a parallel session created `todo/tasks/t2377-brief.md` plus 7 companion issues without ever running `chore: claim t2377` — the brief file was the entry point, not a commit subject. The commit-msg guard would not have caught this, because no commit subject contained "t2377". Closing the surface where t-IDs first appear (filenames) hardens the same invariant the commit-msg guard already enforces.

The defence is symmetric: client-side hook for cheap rejection, optional CI gate for server-side coverage. The hook is the cheaper half.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/hooks/brief-filename-guard.sh (NEW)
- .agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh (EDIT: register new guard)
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-filename-guard.sh (NEW)

NEW: pre-commit hook that iterates staged files matching `^todo/tasks/t[0-9]+-brief\.md$`. For each, extract the t-ID and verify either (a) a commit `chore: claim tNNN` exists anywhere in `git log --all --grep`, or (b) the file is being deleted (allow cleanup). Block on any miss with a mentoring error message naming the unclaimed ID and the `claim-task-id.sh` remediation.

Reference pattern: `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` (hook scaffolding, staged-file iteration, exit code conventions). Install/uninstall integration: `.agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh` (existing four-guard registry).

### Complexity Impact

New file ≈ 80-100 lines (under the 100-line `function-complexity` gate). One new function in `install-pre-push-guards.sh` (~15 lines) for registration. No growth past gate.

## Acceptance

1. Staging `todo/tasks/t99999-brief.md` (no claim commit) and committing → blocked with mentoring error.
2. Staging a brief file for a legitimately claimed t-ID → passes.
3. Deleting a brief file (any t-ID) → passes (cleanup must work).
4. `git commit --no-verify` → bypasses (standard pre-push convention).
5. Test suite: ≥6 assertions covering valid/invalid/delete/bypass/multi-file-stage/no-brief-files-staged cases.

## Verification

```bash
# Install
bash .agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh install

# Reject unclaimed
echo "test" > todo/tasks/t99999-brief.md
git add todo/tasks/t99999-brief.md
git commit -m "wip: unclaimed brief" 2>&1 | grep -q "not claimed" && echo PASS-reject
git restore --staged todo/tasks/t99999-brief.md && rm todo/tasks/t99999-brief.md

# Accept claimed (use any tNNN with a known claim commit)
KNOWN_CLAIMED=$(git log --all --grep='chore: claim t' --oneline | head -1 | grep -oE 't[0-9]+' | head -1)
echo "test" > "todo/tasks/${KNOWN_CLAIMED}-brief.md"
git add "todo/tasks/${KNOWN_CLAIMED}-brief.md"
git commit -m "wip: claimed brief" && echo PASS-accept
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Test suite
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-filename-guard.sh && echo PASS-tests

# Lint
shellcheck .agents/hooks/brief-filename-guard.sh .agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh
```

```
{"ts":1777397345,"session_key":"issue-21320","model":"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6","result":"rate_limit","exit_code":143,"duration_ms":1205576}
{"ts":1777397359,"session_key":"issue-21315","model":"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6","result":"rate_limit","exit_code":143,"duration_ms":1203140}
```

3 workers killed simultaneously at the 20-minute mark, all opus-4-6, all rate_limit. Pattern: Anthropic returns 429 on the FIRST API call, the client (opencode) silently retries for ~20 min, watchdog finally kills as `idle`. Worker consumed a dispatch slot, produced zero output, kept the issue lock for 20 min.

## Why it matters

Each rate-limited zombie blocks one slot for 20 min. With 24 slots, 4 zombies = 16% throughput loss. With cascading rate limits, the system enters thrash where every dispatch slot is occupied by a zombie.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — function that monitors opencode subprocess output (search for `run --print-logs`). 

- Tail opencode stderr for the FIRST 30s of execution.
- If stderr contains `429`, `rate_limit`, `anthropic.*overloaded`, or HTTP 5xx within first 30s, send SIGTERM to opencode, write metric `{result:"rate_limit_fast", exit_code:0, duration_ms:<actual>}`, exit cleanly so the dispatch slot frees.
- DO NOT trigger NMR backoff — this is a transient API condition, not an issue-level failure.

## Reference pattern

`worker-activity-watchdog.sh` already polls opencode logs for activity signals; copy the polling cadence (30s tick) and stderr pattern matching.

## Verification

```

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=invalid headless-runtime-helper.sh run --issue 99999 --model anthropic/claude-opus-4-6
# Should exit within 60s, not 20min
```

## Acceptance

- Rate-limit detected within 30s of first API call
- Worker exits with code 0 (not 143), result="rate_limit_fast"
- No NMR backoff applied to the issue
- duration_ms in metric < 60000
- Watchdog kill rate drops sharply for opus-4-6 workers

title: t3022: Cap concurrent opus-4-6 dispatches at N per Anthropic account to prevent rate-limit cascade
body:
## Problem

Single Anthropic account sustains many concurrent sonnet workers but only ~3-4 concurrent opus before triggering 429 rate limits. Currently no per-model concurrency cap exists in dispatch logic. When fill_floor + cascade-elevation both push opus-tier dispatches, all simultaneous opus workers hit 429 within seconds and become 20-min zombies (see GH#21570 follow-up).

Evidence: 3 opus-4-6 workers killed at the same minute with rate_limit (`headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` ts=1777397345-1777397359). Sonnet workers in the same pool succeeded.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — function `_dff_compute_max_parallel` (~line 712-727). Add a per-model concurrency check:

```bash
# Count in-flight workers by model from active worker process list
local opus_inflight
opus_inflight=$(pgrep -f 'opencode.*-m anthropic/claude-opus' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
local opus_cap=${AIDEVOPS_OPUS_CONCURRENCY_CAP:-4}
if (( opus_inflight >= opus_cap )); then
    # Skip opus-tier candidates this cycle; sonnet candidates still dispatch
    return $opus_cap
fi
```

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` near line 1119 — when a candidate's resolved model is opus AND opus_inflight >= cap, defer with reason="opus_concurrency_cap" instead of dispatching.

NEW: per-model cap config in `.agents/configs/dispatch-model-caps.conf`:
```
opus-4-6=4
opus-4-7=4
sonnet-4-6=24
```

## Reference pattern

`shared-gh-wrappers.sh` rate-limit threshold logic is conceptually similar: probe budget before action, defer when below threshold.

## Verification

```

for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do (exec -a 'opencode -m anthropic/claude-opus-4-6' sleep 600 &); done
# Run pulse cycle
pulse-wrapper.sh --canary
# Log should show 'opus_concurrency_cap' deferrals for issues that would have used opus
```

## Acceptance

- Concurrent opus workers never exceed the cap (default 4)
- Sonnet dispatch unaffected
- Cap is overridable via `AIDEVOPS_OPUS_CONCURRENCY_CAP` env
- Deferred candidates retry next cycle (not NMR'd)

select(.body_start | startswith("Dispatching worker"))

Fix:

title: t3026: P0 — per-candidate ceremony exceeds adaptive 180s timeout, dispatched=0/148
body:
## Severity P0

Production pulse is failing to dispatch ANY candidates. `pulse.log` shows the deterministic fill_floor cycle iter=62 evaluating 148 candidates and dispatching ZERO due to per-candidate timeout. Workers exist but new dispatches are blocked.

## Evidence

`pulse.log` 2026-04-28T22:30Z:

```
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: fill_floor_candidate_21303 exceeded 180s (pid 76562)
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: fill_floor_candidate_21302 exceeded 180s (pid 85363)
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: fill_floor_candidate_21314 exceeded 180s (pid 85551)
[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: loop body finished — processed=0 dispatched=0 mode=parallel(24)
[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor complete: dispatched=0 (0 triage + 0 implementation), processed=0/148, target_available=24
```

CLAIM_WON fires for #21547, #21329, #21303, #21302, #21314, #21289, #21286 — ceremony reaches claim acquisition (~120s in). Adaptive 180s timeout fires before `dispatch_with_dedup` returns.

Earlier successful dispatch (#3366) used 300s timeout and completed at 289s — barely under wire. Adaptive logic dropped to 180s after some 'fast' cycles, then can't recover.

## Root cause hypotheses (rank by likelihood)

1. Adaptive logic in `dispatch-timing-helper.sh` undercounts long ceremonies — exit code 124 (timeout) may be excluded from learning samples, so adaptive average doesn't rise after timeout cycles.
2. Ceremony genuinely takes >180s for: gh issue view + brief check + eligibility validators + pre-dispatch validators + CLAIM_WON audit comment write + body composition with footer + worker spawn (npm install / node startup). Total: ~75-160s baseline; with backpressure adds 20-40s.
3. Adaptive cap is too low at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:519`.

## Fix options (cheapest first)

**Option A (immediate, safest):** floor adaptive timeout at 360s.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh:334-401` — clamp calculated timeout: `if (( calc_timeout < 360 )); then calc_timeout=360; fi`. Add env override `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT_FLOOR` (default 360).

**Option B:** include timeout outcomes in adaptive learning. When stage exits rc=124, record `elapsed_ms=timeout_value` AND mark sample as 'underestimate', shift adaptive p95 upward.

**Option C (future):** speed up ceremony by parallelising independent gh API calls.

## Acceptance

- Per-candidate timeout floors at 360s
- After deploy, fresh pulse cycles dispatch >0 candidates per cycle
- `pulse-stats.json` `fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout` counter stops growing
- `gh pr list --state merged --search 'merged:>=NOW-30M'` returns >5 worker PRs after the fix is live

## Verification

```bash
tail -F ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -E 'dispatched=|Stage complete:|Stage timeout:'
```

## Reference

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:54` — default `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT=30`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:513-540` — adaptive timeout calc + run_stage_with_timeout

title: t3027: P0 — pulse burns GraphQL budget on idle cycles (1456/2065 today, 70%) — add orchestration-level idle backoff + budget-aware throttle
body:
## Severity P0

70% of pulse cycles today produced ZERO dispatches but still consumed full GraphQL budget for prefetch_state, batch search, dedup checks. With no idle-detection at the orchestration level, the pulse keeps cycling at 120s while GraphQL exhausts every hour. When budget hits 0, ALL ceremony falls back to slower REST paths, per-candidate timeouts fire (see #21583), and the system spirals.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -c 'dispatched=0' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
1456
$ grep -c 'dispatched=' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
2065
```

`pulse-health.json` always shows `idle_skips=0` — the field exists in telemetry but the counter is never incremented. There is NO idle-skip pathway in the code.

`pulse-stats.json` shows `prefetch_calls=null, prefetch_cache_hits=null, prefetch_cache_miss=null` — prefetch caching counters are never recorded. Either the caching is not wired up or the increment paths are broken.

`~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` exists but is EMPTY — t2902 instrumentation is deployed but not capturing data, so we cannot identify top GraphQL spenders.

## Why existing protections aren't enough

- t2574, t2689, t2744 handle EXECUTION-level fallback (REST when GraphQL low) — they don't conserve budget
- t2690 circuit breaker pauses dispatch when GraphQL <250pts — but the cycle ITSELF still runs prefetch_state, burning budget while breaker holds dispatch
- t2992/t2994 cache priming runs only on stale sentinel — doesn't help during normal cycles
- t2830 ETag tickle layer (just merged in PR #21577) — counters not visible; effectiveness unknown

## Required additions

### 1. Idle backoff (orchestration-level)

When N consecutive cycles have `dispatched=0` AND `workers_active=0`, exponentially extend cycle interval:

- N=3: interval ×2 (240s)
- N=6: interval ×4 (480s)
- N=9: interval ×8 (max, e.g. 900s)

Reset interval to baseline on first `dispatched>0` or `workers_active>0`.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` after cycle complete — track consecutive idle cycles in a sentinel file (`~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-idle-counter`); next `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` call reads the counter and applies the backoff window.

### 2. GraphQL-budget-aware orchestration throttle

When `graphql.remaining` < orchestration_skip_threshold (e.g. 500), skip prefetch_state entirely for this cycle (use stale cache); skip batch search; only run essential cleanup + dispatch with cached candidates.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` — at top of `run_cycle`, query `gh api rate_limit` (1 call cost), branch to lightweight path if budget low.

### 3. Wire up cache hit/miss telemetry

Investigate why `pulse-stats.json` counters are null. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` — ensure `pulse_stats_increment 'prefetch_cache_hit' / 'prefetch_cache_miss'` is called on every cache lookup. Add corresponding counter on every actual REST/GraphQL fetch.

### 4. Wire up gh-api-calls.log capture

Investigate why `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` is empty. Verify `gh-api-instrument.sh` is being called from gh wrappers. May be a sourcing path issue.

### 5. Canonical-recovery routine (addresses Q1: stale-local-main without release)

The pulse-canonical-recovery escalation (advisory file at `~/.aidevops/advisories/canonical-recovery-aidevops.advisory`) currently requires user intervention. Add a ROUTINE entry to TODO.md (r-prefix) that runs every 10 min, detects the advisory, attempts safe stash + pull, removes the advisory if recovery succeeds. This decouples recovery from release cadence.

NEW: `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/scripts/r004.sh` (or framework-shipped `canonical-recovery-routine.sh`).

## Acceptance

- After deploy + sustained idle period: cycle interval extends to 480s+ within 9 cycles of inactivity
- After deploy + GraphQL exhaustion: pulse skips prefetch_state with log line `[pulse-wrapper] GraphQL budget low (N remaining), skipping prefetch_state`
- After deploy: `pulse-stats.json prefetch_cache_hits` increments on every cycle
- After deploy: `gh-api-calls.log` accumulates entries
- After deploy: 24h post-merge, ratio of `dispatched=0` to total cycles drops to <30% (from current 70%)
- Canonical-recovery routine r-prefixed entry present in framework TODO.md

## Verification

```bash
# Watch idle backoff fire:
tail -F ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -E 'idle_skip|backoff_extend|GraphQL budget low'

# Confirm cache hits flowing:
watch 'jq .prefetch_cache_hits ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json'

# Confirm budget retained:
watch 'gh api rate_limit | jq .resources.graphql.remaining'
```

## Reference

- t2574 / t2689 / t2744: REST fallback layers (execution-level)
- t2690: dispatch circuit breaker (worker spawn)
- t2902: gh-api instrumentation (apparently broken — investigate)
- t2830 / PR #21577: L1 ETag tickle (just merged, counters unverified)
- t2992 / t2994: cache priming hook
- This task adds the missing orchestration-level layer above all of the above

P0 demo tomorrow. The t3026 fix (#21583) addresses per-candidate timeout but won't help if pulse keeps exhausting GraphQL on idle cycles before any candidate runs. Filed from interactive root-cause session (2026-04-28T23:38Z).

title: t3028: fix: setup.sh fails when caller exports SCRIPT_DIR (schedulers.sh module path bug)
body:
## What

`setup-modules/schedulers.sh` lines 42-48 only initializes SCRIPT_DIR if unset:

```bash
if [[ -z "${SCRIPT_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    _sched_orch_lib_path="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}"
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_sched_orch_lib_path" && pwd)"
fi
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/schedulers-pulse.sh"
```

When the parent (setup.sh or another sourcing script) exports SCRIPT_DIR pointing elsewhere (e.g. `.agents/scripts/` from prior agent-deploy sourcing), the source line tries to load `.agents/scripts/schedulers-pulse.sh` — which doesn't exist (sub-library is in `setup-modules/`). Setup aborts.

## Why

`setup.sh --non-interactive` is the canonical post-merge deployment path. As of t3026 (PR #21585) deploy attempt, it fails:

```text
./setup-modules/schedulers.sh: line 56: /Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/schedulers-pulse.sh: No such file or directory
```

Workaround used to deploy t3026: rsync `.agents/` directly to `~/.aidevops/agents/`, then `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running`. Bypasses other setup hooks.

## How

EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` lines 42-48 — make SCRIPT_DIR resolution unconditional inside this sub-library context. Always derive from ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}, independent of inherited SCRIPT_DIR. Reference pattern: `setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` or any other setup-modules/*.sh that resolves its own location reliably.

Verification: `./setup.sh --non-interactive` from a clean shell (no SCRIPT_DIR pre-exported) should complete. Also test from inside a script with its own SCRIPT_DIR set to verify isolation.

### Files Scope
- setup-modules/schedulers.sh

### Complexity Impact
Trivial — replacing 7-line conditional with 3-line unconditional resolution.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `setup.sh --non-interactive` succeeds when called from a shell with SCRIPT_DIR pre-exported
- [ ] Fresh-shell setup runs unchanged
- [ ] No new shellcheck warnings

title: t3031: fix dispatch counter accounting (subshell stdout pollution at engine.sh:902)
body:
## What

Cycle summary `Deterministic fill floor complete: dispatched=N (M triage + K implementation), processed=X/Y` reports `dispatched=0` even when `Dispatched worker PID NNN` lines fire in the same cycle. Root cause: subshell stdout pollution leaks through the parallel-loop function's stdout, corrupting the `read -r dispatched_count processed_count` capture in the caller.

## Root cause analysis

`_dff_dispatch_loop_parallel` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:848-920` runs candidates in backgrounded subshells:

```bash
# pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:900-910
(
    local _rc=0
    _dff_process_candidate "$candidate_json" "$self_login" "$available_slots" || _rc=$?
    # ... outcome write to $outcomes_file
) &
```

The subshell's stdout is INHERITED from the parent function. `_dff_process_candidate` calls `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` (line 681) which calls:

```bash
# pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:558-559
run_stage_with_timeout "fill_floor_candidate_${issue_number}" "$timeout_seconds" \
    dispatch_with_dedup "$@" || dispatch_rc=$?
```

`dispatch_with_dedup` is invoked UNCAPTURED. Any echo/printf to stdout (not explicitly `>>"$LOGFILE"`) inside the dispatch chain — `dispatch_with_dedup`, `_dlw_nohup_launch`, `check_dispatch_dedup`, jq error noise on null inputs (cf. t3025), gh API stderr leakage on rate-limit retries — flows up through:

1. `dispatch_with_dedup` → `run_stage_with_timeout` (which uses `"$@" &` — inherits stdout)
2. → `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` (no capture)
3. → `_dff_process_candidate` (no capture, `return rc`)
4. → backgrounded subshell at line 902 (no redirection)
5. → parent function's stdout (mixed with the `printf '%d %d\n'` at line 918)
6. → `loop_output=$(_dff_dispatch_loop_parallel ...)` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1119` captures EVERYTHING
7. → `read -r dispatched_count processed_count <<<"$loop_output"` reads only the FIRST line
8. → if first line is pollution (e.g. `null`, `jq error`, anything non-numeric), regex check at line 1124 (`[[ "$dispatched_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || dispatched_count=0`) zeros both counters
9. → cycle summary reports `dispatched=0/N` while logs show real dispatches

## Files

- EDIT: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:900-910` — wrap the subshell body to redirect stray stdout to LOGFILE
- VERIFY: `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1119-1132` — caller capture/regex; should not need changes if subshell is sealed
- REFERENCE PATTERN: existing redirection style elsewhere in same file: `>>"$LOGFILE" 2>&1` or `>/dev/null 2>&1` for pure outcome paths

## How

Apply the smallest-correct change. Two viable options:

**Option A (preferred): seal the subshell body**

```bash
# pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:900-910 (current)
(
    local _rc=0
    _dff_process_candidate "$candidate_json" "$self_login" "$available_slots" || _rc=$?
    # ...
) &

# After fix:
(
    local _rc=0
    _dff_process_candidate "$candidate_json" "$self_login" "$available_slots" >>"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 || _rc=$?
    # ...
) &
```

This appends any stdout/stderr from the dispatch chain to LOGFILE (where it belongs) without changing `_dff_process_candidate`'s contract.

**Option B (broader): seal at run_stage_with_timeout layer**

Redirect inside `_dff_dispatch_with_timeout` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:558-559`. Risky — touches more code paths used outside the parallel loop.

Option A is the minimum-blast-radius fix.

## Verification

```bash
# Trigger a fill_floor cycle (any cycle with target_available > 0 + open issues)
# Then read cycle summary and outcomes file:
LATEST_CYCLE=$(grep -nE "loop body finished" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -1 | cut -d: -f1)
START=$((LATEST_CYCLE - 50))
sed -n "${START},${LATEST_CYCLE}p" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log

# Compare counts:
DISPATCHED_FROM_SUMMARY=$(sed -n "${LATEST_CYCLE}p" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -oE "dispatched=[0-9]+" | cut -d= -f2)
ACTUAL_PIDS=$(awk -v line="$LATEST_CYCLE" 'NR <= line && NR > line-100 && /Dispatched worker PID/' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | wc -l)
test "$DISPATCHED_FROM_SUMMARY" -eq "$ACTUAL_PIDS"  # must match
```

After fix: 10 consecutive cycles must show `dispatched_from_summary == actual_PIDs` (±0).

## Why

- Per Pillar 1 of parent (Ref #21598): trustworthy data
- Currently impossible to diagnose pulse health from logs (summary contradicts evidence)
- Blocks t3027 (idle backoff) from working correctly — N=consecutive_idle counter would mis-fire
- Blocks pulse-health.json correctness (depends on same counter chain)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_dff_dispatch_loop_parallel` subshell body redirects stdout/stderr to LOGFILE
- [ ] `shellcheck pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` passes clean
- [ ] Verification command above shows `dispatched_from_summary == actual_PIDs` over 10 cycles
- [ ] `_dff_count_outcomes` outcomes file still receives correct success/fail lines (regression check)

title: t3033: pulse-wrapper self-respawn-on-source-mtime-change
body:
## What

`pulse-wrapper.sh` does not detect when its source file has been modified by `aidevops update` / `setup.sh`. It continues running pre-deploy bytecode in memory until the process exits and launchd respawns it. Result: post-deploy fixes don't take effect for up to several hours (until the existing process happens to die for unrelated reasons).

## Evidence

During the t3026 deploy in this session:
1. Hot-deployed via `rsync -a --delete .agents/ ~/.aidevops/agents/` at session-time T+0
2. Existing `pulse-wrapper.sh` instance (PID X, started pre-deploy) continued running OLD code with the buggy 30s timeout
3. `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running` was needed to force re-exec
4. Without it, `setup.sh` would have shipped the fix to disk but not into the live process

This makes hot-deploys brittle and obscures whether a fix is actually live.

## Files

- EDIT: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add mtime check at top of main loop
- REFERENCE PATTERN: bash re-exec on update is a well-known idiom:
  ```bash
  if [[ "$(stat -f %m "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$SCRIPT_PATH")" != "$LOADED_MTIME" ]]; then
      log "source modified — re-executing"
      exec "$SCRIPT_PATH" "$@"
  fi
  ```
- REFERENCE: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh::main()` — current main loop structure.

## How

1. Capture `SCRIPT_MTIME` once at top of main:
   ```bash
   SCRIPT_PATH="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
   SCRIPT_MTIME=$(stat -f %m "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
   ```
2. At end of each cycle (before sleep), compare current mtime to captured:
   ```bash
   _current_mtime=$(stat -f %m "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
   if [[ "$_current_mtime" != "$SCRIPT_MTIME" && "$_current_mtime" -gt 0 ]]; then
       echo "[pulse-wrapper] Source modified ($SCRIPT_MTIME -> $_current_mtime) — re-execing for fresh code" >>"$LOGFILE"
       exec "$SCRIPT_PATH" "$@"
   fi
   ```
3. Also check sourced helpers if they're large/critical (`shared-constants.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, etc.) — store mtimes in array and check together.
4. Use `exec` (not respawn) — preserves PID, lock, and launchd attachment.

## Edge cases

- **Lock**: `exec` preserves the FD lock if held by the script. Verify the lock acquisition path is at the top of `main` and not inside a sourced helper that gets re-evaluated.
- **In-flight workers**: `exec` happens between cycles, so no in-flight dispatch is interrupted. Worker processes are detached via setsid (per `_dlw_exec_detached`), so they survive parent re-exec regardless.
- **Singleton interaction (C1)**: must coordinate with the singleton lock fix — re-exec must NOT release the lock, only the parent script body changes.
- **launchd**: `exec` preserves the PID, so launchd KeepAlive sees no exit. Safe.

## Verification

```bash
# 1. Stat the deployed script
ORIG_MTIME=$(stat -f %m ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh)
ORIG_PID=$(~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status | grep "Lock holder PID" | awk '{print $4}')

# 2. Touch the script (simulate aidevops update)
touch ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
NEW_MTIME=$(stat -f %m ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh)

# 3. Wait one cycle (default 120s)
sleep 130

# 4. Verify same PID, fresh mtime acknowledged in log
NEW_PID=$(~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status | grep "Lock holder PID" | awk '{print $4}')
test "$ORIG_PID" -eq "$NEW_PID"  # PID preserved via exec
grep -q "Source modified.*re-execing" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

## Why

- Per Pillar 2: pipeline hygiene — eliminate stale-process-running-old-code class of failures
- Eliminates the need for `restart-if-running` calls in setup.sh / aidevops update (t2914 ensures-running becomes redundant)
- Faster fix-deploy turnaround for pulse bugs

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-wrapper.sh` re-execs on source mtime change at end of each cycle
- [ ] PID is preserved across re-exec (verified via `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` before/after)
- [ ] `shellcheck pulse-wrapper.sh` passes clean
- [ ] Lock is preserved (no SIGSTOP/orphan duplication)
- [ ] Verification command above passes

title: t3034: 360s ceiling timeout investigation — per-stage ceremony instrumentation
body:
## What

After t3026 (PR #21585) raised the per-candidate timeout floor to 360s, fresh `exceeded 360s` events still appear in logs. Need to identify which ceremony sub-stage occasionally exceeds the budget so we can either (a) optimize that stage, (b) raise the floor with justification, or (c) split ceremony into faster + slower phases.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -c "exceeded 360s" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
8  # (post-deploy, ~30 min window)

$ grep "exceeded 360s" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -3
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: fill_floor_candidate_3128 exceeded 360s (pid 28704)
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: fill_floor_candidate_3125 exceeded 360s (pid 22603)
[pulse-wrapper] Stage timeout: fill_floor_candidate_3126 exceeded 360s (pid 22605)
```

`dispatch-timing-helper.sh` has EWMA + p95 metadata per repo, but the granular per-stage breakdown (gh issue view vs brief check vs eligibility vs CLAIM_WON comment vs body composition vs worker spawn vs npm install) is not currently captured.

## Files

- EDIT: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::dispatch_with_dedup` — add per-stage timing instrumentation
- EDIT: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh::_dlw_*` — add per-stage timing for spawn ceremony
- NEW: `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` — per-stage timing log
- REFERENCE PATTERN: `gh-api-instrument.sh` (t2902) for TSV-style per-call instrumentation; same pattern here.

## How

1. Wrap each major ceremony sub-stage with timing markers:
   ```bash
   _stage_start=$(date +%s%N)
   # ... stage work ...
   _stage_elapsed_ms=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - _stage_start) / 1000000 ))
   echo -e "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)\t#${issue_number}\t${repo_slug}\t<stage_name>\t${_stage_elapsed_ms}" >> ~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv
   ```
2. Stages to instrument (in order they appear in dispatch_with_dedup):
   - `dedup_check` (Layer 1-6 in `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers`)
   - `gh_issue_view` (full metadata fetch)
   - `large_files_gate` (file size / function complexity check)
   - `eligibility_validators` (pre-dispatch validators per t2424)
   - `claim_won_comment` (gh API comment post)
   - `body_composition` (prompt assembly + footer)
   - `worker_prewarm_db` (`_dlw_prewarm_opencode_db`)
   - `worker_spawn` (`_dlw_exec_detached` setsid+nohup)
   - `worker_validation` (`check_worker_launch` 15-20s poll)
3. Run for 1 cycle on a quiet repo, identify p95 of each stage.
4. File follow-up tasks for any stage exceeding 60s p95.
5. If sum of medians < 360s but tail behavior pushes above, document and size the floor accordingly.

## Hypothesis to validate

Strongest hypothesis given t3026 evidence: `gh issue view` + `gh api` rate-limit retries stack into the 360s envelope when GraphQL is exhausted (REST fallback path also has retry+backoff). Secondary hypothesis: `_dlw_prewarm_opencode_db` migration step on cold isolated DB.

## Verification

```bash
# 1. After 50 dispatches, compute per-stage p95:
awk -F'\t' '{print $4 "\t" $5}' ~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv | \
    sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | \
    awk -F'\t' '
    { stage[$1]=stage[$1] " " $2; count[$1]++ }
    END { for (s in stage) {
      n=split(stage[s], arr, " "); p95_idx=int(n*0.95);
      print s, "p95=" arr[p95_idx] "ms (n=" count[s] ")"
    }}'
# 2. Identify top-3 stages by p95
# 3. File follow-up tasks for each
```

## Why

- Per Pillar 2: pipeline hygiene — make the budget conscious of where time goes
- Without per-stage data, raising the floor is shooting in the dark
- Data feeds future optimization tasks (e.g., parallelize independent ceremony sub-stages)

## Acceptance

- [ ] All ceremony sub-stages instrumented with TSV timing log
- [ ] Per-stage p95 + p99 computed from 50+ dispatches
- [ ] Top-3 slow stages filed as follow-up tasks (not in scope here)
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on edited files

title: t3035: orphan worker reaper for workers whose parent pulse died
body:
## What

When pulse-wrapper.sh dies (crash, OOM kill, manual `kill -9`), worker processes it spawned via `setsid+nohup` survive — they are explicitly detached via `_dlw_exec_detached` (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:421`). Surviving workers continue running but without a parent to:

1. Update their dispatch ledger
2. Reap them on completion
3. Detect early-exit and post recovery comments

These become "orphan workers" — running real work but invisible to the framework. Need a reaper to either reattach them or terminate them safely.

## Evidence

Workers are launched with `setsid nohup ... &` (line 422). Worker PGID differs from pulse PGID (intentional, per t2814 — prevents pulse SIGTERM from cascading). On pulse crash, `worker-lifecycle-common.sh::list_active_worker_processes` still returns them as active, but the dispatch ledger / claim stamps don't reflect their state.

Currently observed during t3026 deploy: 25 opencode child processes were running, but the new pulse instance (post-restart) had no record of them in its dispatch ledger.

## Files

- NEW: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/orphan-worker-reaper.sh` — periodic detector + reaper
- EDIT: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh::main()` — call reaper at start of each cycle
- REFERENCE: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh:730` — `list_active_worker_processes` (canonical detector)
- REFERENCE: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh::_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` — existing cleanup pattern for early-exit (different scenario but similar bookkeeping)

## How

1. **Detection**: at start of each cycle, list active workers via `list_active_worker_processes`. For each worker:
   - Extract issue number from process command line (`WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER=NNN` env var or `--session-key issue-NNN`)
   - Check dispatch ledger for matching entry
   - If NOT in ledger → orphan candidate
2. **Classification**:
   - **Reattachable**: ledger has stale entry (PID points to dead process) but issue is still active. Update ledger PID to current worker.
   - **Unreattachable**: no ledger entry at all (dispatched by previous pulse instance whose ledger is gone).
3. **Action**:
   - Reattachable: update ledger, log `[pulse-wrapper] Reattached orphan worker PID NNN to issue #NNN`.
   - Unreattachable: post recovery comment to issue ("worker resumed by new pulse instance after parent restart"), reattach to current ledger.
   - Truly stuck (running >2h with no PR/comment activity): escalate to `worker-activity-watchdog.sh kill` with reason `orphan_stuck`.
4. **Idempotency**: reaper must be safe to run every cycle. Tracking via PID+start_time tuple (PID can be reused).

## Verification

```bash
# 1. Note current workers
BEFORE=$(~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh::list_active_worker_processes | sort)

# 2. Kill pulse-wrapper.sh
pkill -9 -f "pulse-wrapper.sh"

# 3. Wait for launchd respawn (≤120s)
sleep 130

# 4. Reaper runs on first cycle of new pulse
sleep 60

# 5. Verify orphans are now in ledger:
DURING=$(~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh::list_active_worker_processes | sort)
test "$BEFORE" = "$DURING"  # all original workers still running
grep "Reattached orphan worker" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | wc -l  # should be > 0
```

## Why

- Per Pillar 2: pipeline hygiene — workers shouldn't be invisible
- Helps debugging (workers in ledger can be queried, killed, escalated)
- Prevents zombie state where workers run forever without watchdog supervision
- Bonus: makes pulse-wrapper.sh restarts safer (workers gracefully reattach)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `orphan-worker-reaper.sh` runs at start of each pulse cycle
- [ ] Workers detached from previous pulse are detected and reattached to ledger
- [ ] Truly stuck orphans (>2h) are killed with audit comment
- [ ] `shellcheck orphan-worker-reaper.sh` passes clean
- [ ] Verification command above passes

title: t3036: fix: pulse-merge-routine never installs and crashes when invoked — green PRs sit unmerged for 30+ hours
body:
## Summary

Investigating a managed private webapp's PR backlog (12 open, all aged 0-1 days, mostly origin:worker) revealed three compounding aidevops bugs that prevent the t2862 'fast-cadence merge routine' from EVER working on existing systems. Net effect: PRs only merge when the full pulse cycle's deterministic_merge_pass runs, which currently happens 1-2x per 24h (not every 2 min as designed).

## Evidence

```text
$ launchctl list | grep pulse-merge-routine
(empty)

$ ls ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.pulse-merge-routine.plist
ls: No such file or directory

$ ls ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge-routine.log
ls: No such file or directory

$ PULSE_START_EPOCH=$(date +%s) ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh --dry-run --repo <private-webapp-slug>
.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh: line 326: PULSE_START_EPOCH: unbound variable
$ # (Even with PULSE_START_EPOCH exported, the routine hangs without producing output.)

$ tail -200 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.merged > 0)' | tail -3
{"ts":"2026-04-26T09:55:02Z","merged":1,...}
{"ts":"2026-04-27T17:45:07Z","merged":2,...}
{"ts":"2026-04-29T00:23:33Z","merged":4,...}
```

Three pulse merge cycles in ~50 hours. Designed cadence: every 120s.

## Root causes (independent, all need fixing)

### Bug 1 — Setup.sh chicken-and-egg gate (BLOCKER, P0)

`setup.sh:1364` gates `setup_pulse_merge_routine` behind `_should_setup_noninteractive_scheduler`. That helper (setup.sh:374-393) returns 0 ONLY IF the scheduler is ALREADY installed. For a feature added AFTER initial install, this gate is permanently false — the launchd plist never installs.

The same risk was identified for stats-wrapper (t2418, GH#20016 — '11-day staleness'). Fix there: add `_should_setup_noninteractive_stats_wrapper` (setup.sh:402-419) with a 'pulse-dependency escape hatch' that returns 0 if the supervisor pulse is enabled. pulse-merge-routine is in the same dependency class — it is the merge-side of pulse — but never received the equivalent escape hatch.

### Bug 2 — Routine crashes on PULSE_START_EPOCH unbound (BLOCKER, P0)

`pulse-merge.sh:326` references `PULSE_START_EPOCH` (set by `pulse-wrapper.sh:180`). `pulse-merge-routine.sh` is a standalone script that does NOT initialize `PULSE_START_EPOCH`. Under `set -euo pipefail` (line 39) this is a hard fail.

Even if Bug 1 were fixed, every launchd invocation would crash immediately. The test harness already works around this (`tests/test-pulse-merge-parent-task-keyword.sh:106-107` exports PULSE_START_EPOCH manually). The routine must do the same.

`pulse-simplification-*.sh` has 4 more sites with the same dependency — confirm they only run from pulse-wrapper.sh, or audit.

### Bug 3 — Routine hangs even with PULSE_START_EPOCH set (BLOCKER, P0)

After exporting `PULSE_START_EPOCH`, `pulse-merge-routine.sh --dry-run` produces no output and hangs past 100s. Needs reproduction with `bash -x` and timeout instrumentation. Likely cause: a sourced helper waits for input, or a function call expects pulse-wrapper.sh state (lock files, prefetch state, dependency graph cache) that the routine doesn't bootstrap.

## Compounding factors (downstream, NOT framework bugs but amplify impact)

1. **Mixed PR check-name collision** — when a PR contains both planning files (`TODO.md`, `todo/**`, `*.md`) and code, both `planning-fast-path.yml` and `ci.yml` fire. Both emit "Lint"/"Typecheck"/"Format" check names. Whichever runs second becomes the latest result for the rule. ci.yml runs longer, so its (often-failing) result overrides planning-fast-path's success → the PR gets blocked even when the intent was a fast-path skip. Fix is downstream-side (workflow yaml mutual exclusion) but framework should consider shipping a canonical `planning-fast-path-reusable.yml` (mirroring t2770/issue-sync-reusable) so this is fixed once and inherited everywhere.
2. **Worker PRs trip on pre-existing lint debt** — workers fix bug X correctly but ESLint surfaces accumulated debt in the same files. The `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker` recovery path exists (pulse-merge-feedback.sh:279) but the merge cycle that would invoke it isn't running often enough — see Bug 1.
3. **`pulse-wrapper.log` is 7.5 GB** — causes grep timeouts when diagnosing. Log rotation isn't aggressive enough for fast-cadence pulse.
4. **Workflow-only PR self-blocking** — when a PR's only diff is `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `paths-ignore` filters skip ci.yml, leaving required checks permanently unfullfilled under main-protection rulesets. Needs documented `gh pr merge --admin` workaround OR a ruleset bypass for workflow-only PRs.

## Why this matters

When the merge routine works as designed, fast PRs merge in 2-3 min (CI complete + 120s heartbeat). When it doesn't, PRs queue up until the next full pulse cycle (~5-10 min ideally, 30+ hours observed). On a fast-paced repo (10-20 PRs/day), that means a 12-PR backlog accumulates within hours.

## Files to fix

- `setup.sh` — add `_should_setup_noninteractive_pulse_merge_routine` escape hatch (model on `_should_setup_noninteractive_stats_wrapper` at lines 402-419). Update line 1364 to call it.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh` — initialize `PULSE_START_EPOCH=$(date +%s)` in env-bootstrap section (before sourcing pulse-merge.sh).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh` — instrument with timeout/strace and identify hang root cause; fix.
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh` (NEW) — assert routine completes `--dry-run` against a fixture in <30s.

## Acceptance

1. After `aidevops update` on existing system, `launchctl list | grep pulse-merge-routine` returns the loaded label.
2. `pulse-merge-routine.sh --dry-run` exits 0 within 30s on idle repos.
3. `pulse-merge-routine.sh run` writes a timestamp to `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge-routine-last-run`.
4. Standalone routine test passes in CI.
5. Pulse cycle index shows merge passes every 2-5 min during business hours, not 30h gaps.

## Worker Guidance

Implement Bug 1 (setup escape hatch) and Bug 2 (PULSE_START_EPOCH init) first — these are 5-line fixes that unblock 80% of the impact. Bug 3 (hang) needs investigation and may not have a one-line fix; treat as a separate phase, file as t3036-phase2 follow-up if needed.

Discovered while investigating a managed private webapp's PR backlog (12 PRs, 0-1 day stale, observed 2026-04-29).
