title: worktree-helper.sh: localdev proxy YAML write fails on macOS without PyYAML + BSD sed regex error (non-fatal)
body:
## What

When running `worktree-helper.sh add feature/<branch>` on macOS, two non-fatal errors print to stderr immediately after port allocation:

```
[ERROR] YAML corruption in /Users/<user>/.local-dev-proxy/conf.d/<repo>--<branch>.yml (Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml') — removing
Localdev branch route creation failed (non-fatal)
sed: 1: "s|.*[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+?)( ...": RE error: repetition-operator operand invalid
```

The worktree itself is created correctly; only the localdev-proxy route registration fails. Output is misleadingly labelled `[ERROR]` for a non-fatal path, and BSD sed (macOS default) chokes on the slug-extraction regex regardless of PyYAML state.

## Why

1. `python3 -c 'import yaml'` is invoked inline but PyYAML isn't guaranteed on macOS — many users only have stdlib python3. Should fall back to a pure-shell/stdlib writer, or skip with a single `[INFO]` log when PyYAML missing (not an `[ERROR]` traceback).
2. The `sed` slug-extraction expression uses Perl-flavoured regex syntax (`+?` non-greedy) that BSD sed (macOS default) doesn't support. Should use `sed -E` with portable POSIX-ERE, or bash parameter expansion `${var##*/}`.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` — localdev-proxy YAML write block: detect PyYAML availability before invocation, skip with `[INFO]` log when missing.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` — slug-extraction `sed`: switch to portable POSIX-ERE (`sed -E`) or bash parameter expansion. Current regex `s|.*[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+?)(...)` uses non-greedy `+?` which is a GNU/Perl extension.

### Verification

```
worktree-helper.sh add feature/test-localdev
# On macOS without PyYAML: should print no [ERROR] lines.
# Either proxy YAML is written cleanly, or skipped with one [INFO] log.
# No "sed: RE error: repetition-operator operand invalid" output.
```

### Acceptance

- [ ] No `ModuleNotFoundError` traceback on macOS without PyYAML
- [ ] No `sed: RE error` on macOS BSD sed
- [ ] Worktree creation continues to succeed (already does — this is purely cosmetic + UX)
- [ ] If localdev-proxy YAML write is skipped, log level is `INFO` not `ERROR`

## Reproduction

Reproduced on macOS Darwin 2026-04-29 during ILDS interactive session creating `feature/t153-remove-header-pricing-line` worktree. macOS default python3 (no PyYAML), default `/usr/bin/sed` (BSD).

## Tier

`tier:simple` — one file, two narrow edits (PyYAML guard + sed portability).

title: t3057: add interval-sampled CPU to _watchdog_tree_cpu (lifetime-avg false-defer fix)
body:
## What

Replace lifetime-average CPU measurement in `_watchdog_tree_cpu` with interval-sampled CPU so the stall-defer check measures recent activity, not lifetime average.

## Why

PR #21784 (resolves #21781) added `_watchdog_tree_cpu` using `ps -p $pid -o %cpu=`. On macOS BSD `ps` and Linux procps, `%cpu` reports `total_cpu_time / total_elapsed_lifetime` — a lifetime average, not a recent-interval rate.

Failure mode: a worker that ran hot for 10 min then froze at 0% CPU reports ~30% lifetime average. The defer check (`>= STALL_CPU_THRESHOLD`, default 2%) passes, kill is deferred. Combined with the deferred-marker self-feedback (sibling task t3058), stuck workers survive until the 1500s `HARD_KILL_SECONDS` cap — extending dispatch-slot occupancy ~5x for true positives.

This bug substantially weakens the kill-rate fix the PR claims to deliver. Phase 2 measurement will catch it after the fact, but a pre-emptive fix lets the metric move on first deploy.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh:178-208` — `_watchdog_tree_cpu` function
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh` — add interval-sample assertion

### Reference patterns

Two viable approaches:

1. **Two-sample delta** (cross-platform): grab `ps -o time=` (cumulative cpu time) at T=0 and T=5, compute delta-cpu-seconds / 5. Portable across macOS BSD ps and Linux procps.
2. **`top` interval** (per-platform): `top -l 2 -pid <pid>` on macOS, `top -bn2 -p <pid>` on Linux — second iteration shows interval CPU. Requires platform branch.

Recommend approach 1 for portability. Model on the time-delta pattern at `worker-lifecycle-common.sh:283` (which uses `ps -o %cpu=` for periodic sweeps where lifetime avg is acceptable — different use case).

### Verification

title: t3058: separate WATCHDOG_STALL_DEFERRED marker from monitored OUTPUT_FILE
body:
## What

Stop writing the `[WATCHDOG_STALL_DEFERRED]` marker into the worker's `OUTPUT_FILE`. Use a separate sentinel path or `LIFECYCLE_LOG` instead.

## Why

PR #21784 (resolves #21781) added a CPU-aware stall-defer path. When the watchdog defers a kill, it writes a marker to `OUTPUT_FILE`:

```bash
printf '[WATCHDOG_STALL_DEFERRED] timestamp=%s cpu=%s%% ...\n' ... \
    >>"$OUTPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
stall_seconds=0
```

`OUTPUT_FILE` is the file Phase 2 monitors for growth. Writing to it grows the file. Next iteration: `current_size > last_size` → `stall_seconds=0` and `last_size` advances.

Failure mode: the deferred write *itself* falsely-resets the stall counter as a side-effect of being written to the monitored file. Combined with t3057 (lifetime-CPU bug), this means every defer cycle gives a fresh 600s window AND erases evidence of the prior stall. The stall counter never reaches `STALL_TIMEOUT` again until the worker is genuinely killed by `HARD_KILL_SECONDS` (1500s).

Effect: the documented 600s `STALL_TIMEOUT` becomes meaningless for any worker that ever defers — the 1500s hard-kill is the only real cap.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh:491-495` — the `[WATCHDOG_STALL_DEFERRED]` write site

### Reference patterns

Two options, recommend option B:

- **A.** Write the marker to `${OUTPUT_FILE}.deferred_log` (a sentinel adjacent to OUTPUT_FILE but NOT monitored).
- **B.** Write to `LIFECYCLE_LOG` — same destination as `[lifecycle] worker_killed` lines, so Phase 2 aggregation finds defer events alongside kill events. Format: `[lifecycle] worker_stall_deferred pid=<N> cpu=<X>% stall_seconds=<S> deferred_total=<D> ts=<ISO>`.

Model on the `[lifecycle] worker_killed` pattern at `worker-activity-watchdog.sh:303-309` (already writes to LIFECYCLE_LOG).

### Verification

- Regression test in `tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh`: assert that after a defer, `last_size` is unchanged from before the defer (i.e., OUTPUT_FILE wasn't grown by the watchdog itself).
- Confirm Phase 2 aggregation query also picks up defer events:
  ```bash
  grep "worker_stall_deferred\|worker_killed" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log | awk ...
  ```
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` clean

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Defer markers written to LIFECYCLE_LOG, not OUTPUT_FILE
- [ ] OUTPUT_FILE size unchanged across a defer cycle (verified by test)
- [ ] Phase 2 aggregation query finds defer events
- [ ] No new ShellCheck violations

## Complexity Impact

3-line change. No complexity risk.

## Tier

`tier:simple` — straightforward path change; `oldString`/`newString` is exact.

title: t3059: walk full descendant tree in _watchdog_tree_cpu (BFS, not one-level)
body:
## What

Replace one-level `pgrep -P` in `_watchdog_tree_cpu` with full-tree BFS via `_get_descendant_pids` from `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`.

## Why

PR #21784 (resolves #21781) added `_watchdog_tree_cpu`:

```bash
for pid in $(pgrep -P "$root_pid" 2>/dev/null) "$root_pid"; do
```

Comment says "One level deep covers the typical opencode worker chain (bash → node → opencode binary)". But the typical chain is deeper: a node runtime spawns subprocesses for shellcheck, biome, jq, ripgrep, file reads, etc. — these grandchildren do real CPU work that the one-level scan misses entirely.

Effect: the CPU defer check undercounts CPU activity. Workers doing heavy tool-call work via subprocesses (the exact case the defer is meant to protect) may register as 0% CPU at the root + direct children level, get killed despite being legitimately busy.

This is the inverse of t3057 — t3057 fixes false-defer (lifetime avg too high), this fixes false-kill (subprocess CPU undercounted).

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh:178-208` — `_watchdog_tree_cpu` function
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh:1-15` — source `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` if not already

### Reference patterns

`_get_descendant_pids` at `worker-lifecycle-common.sh:294-321` already does iterative BFS expansion via `pgrep -P` per level. Reuse it:

```bash
local pid_list
pid_list=$(_get_descendant_pids "$root_pid")
for pid in $pid_list "$root_pid"; do
    ...
done
```

### Verification

- Regression test: spawn `bash -c 'while :; do sha256sum /dev/zero >/dev/null; done' &` (3-level deep CPU work), measure tree CPU. Without fix: ~0% (root bash idle, child sha256sum sees 100%). With fix: ~100%.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh` — passes
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` clean

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_watchdog_tree_cpu` walks full descendant tree, not one level
- [ ] Reuses existing `_get_descendant_pids` (no new BFS implementation)
- [ ] Regression test asserts grandchild CPU is included in tree sum
- [ ] No new ShellCheck violations

## Complexity Impact

Reduces line count (calls existing helper). No complexity risk.

`tier:simple` — replace one helper call with another, exact `oldString`/`newString`.

title: t3060: enum-prefix kill_reason setters in pulse-watchdog.sh classifier
body:
## What

Replace prose-string-matching kill_reason classifier in `pulse-watchdog.sh` with enum-prefix coupling at the kill_reason setter sites. Phase 2 aggregation depends on stable reason classes.

## Why

PR #21784 (resolves #21781) added a kill_reason classifier in `pulse-watchdog.sh::_run_pulse_watchdog`:

```bash
case "$kill_reason" in
*"stale threshold"*) _pw_reason_class="wall_clock_stale" ;;
*"cold-start stalled"*) _pw_reason_class="cold_start_timeout" ;;
*"stalled for"*) _pw_reason_class="progress_timeout" ;;
*"idle for"*) _pw_reason_class="idle_timeout" ;;
*"Stop flag"*) _pw_reason_class="stop_flag" ;;
esac
```

The classifier substring-matches the human-readable kill_reason prose. Any future refactor that changes the prose ("idle for" → "has been idle for", "stalled for" → "has stalled at") silently breaks the classifier — falls through to `pulse_unknown`, corrupting Phase 2 aggregation.

The Phase 2 measurement target (94% → ≥50% wait_status=0) depends on these classifications being correct. A stealth refactor that breaks the classifier without breaking the test makes the metric unreliable.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:418-518` — kill_reason setter sites in `_run_pulse_watchdog`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:524-535` — the classifier case statement

### Reference patterns

Two mechanisms compose well:

1. **Enum-prefix at setter site:** every `kill_reason="<prose>"` becomes `kill_reason="<ENUM_CLASS>:<prose>"`. Example: `kill_reason="WALL_CLOCK_STALE:Wall clock exceeded ${PULSE_STALE_THRESHOLD}s"`.
2. **Classifier reads the prefix, not the prose:**
   ```bash
   local _pw_reason_class="${kill_reason%%:*}"
   _pw_reason_class="${_pw_reason_class,,}"  # lowercase
   ```

Model on `worker-activity-watchdog.sh:294-300` which already uses prefix-based classification (`phase1:*`, `hard_kill:*`, `stall:*`).

### Verification

- Regression test: assert each `kill_reason` setter site uses an `ENUM_CLASS:` prefix, and the classifier extracts via `${var%%:*}`.
- Run pulse cycle locally, grep `pulse-dispatch.log` for `worker_killed` lines, confirm `reason=` field never has `pulse_unknown`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh` clean

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All kill_reason setter sites in `pulse-watchdog.sh` use enum prefix
- [ ] Classifier extracts via `${var%%:*}`, not substring matching
- [ ] No `pulse_unknown` entries in test pulse cycle
- [ ] No new ShellCheck violations

## Complexity Impact

Adds ~5 lines per setter site (5 sites = ~25 LOC growth in `_run_pulse_watchdog`, currently ~150 lines per t3056 acknowledgement). Stays under 100-line gate. Net: classifier shrinks from 8 lines to 3.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — multiple setter sites need consistent rewriting; small judgment call about enum names.

title: t3062: add trusted-issue-author allowlist to bypass t2449 gate for peer-runner-filed issues
body:
## Task

Eliminate the per-issue cryptographic approval ceremony required when a peer runner (e.g. alex-solovyev) files an issue that a worker then resolves. Currently every such PR sits at `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` until the maintainer runs `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` to add a crypto signature, because the t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge gate at `pulse-merge-process.sh:585` only honours `OWNER`/`MEMBER` author_association — peer runners are `COLLABORATOR`.

## Why

Observable backlog accumulation. As of 2026-04-29, 7 of 11 open PRs in marcusquinn/aidevops were `BLOCKED` because their linked issues were authored by alex-solovyev (COLLABORATOR), johnwaldo (CONTRIBUTOR), or robstiles (NONE). PR #21767 (t3052) extends the gate to honour crypto-approval as a bypass — but crypto-approval is still per-issue maintainer toil. A trusted-author allowlist removes the toil entirely for known peer runners.

## Background

- t2449 gate: `pulse-merge-process.sh:585` checks `author_association in {OWNER, MEMBER}`
- t3052 (PR #21767): adds crypto-approval bypass — necessary for genuinely external contributors
- Peer runners aren't external — they're trusted operators on different machines/accounts. The trust model is missing this category.

## How

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/configs/` — NEW: `trusted-issue-authors.conf` (one GitHub login per line, `#` comments, blank lines ignored). Model on `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:582-611` — after fetching `issue_author_assoc`, also check whether the issue author login is in the trusted-authors config. If yes, treat as MEMBER-equivalent and proceed (log: `...passing via trusted-issue-author allowlist (t<this-task>)`).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh` — add 2 cases: (n) COLLABORATOR author + login in allowlist → passes; (o) COLLABORATOR author + login NOT in allowlist + no crypto → blocked. Total expected: 15/15.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md` — document the trusted-author bypass in the t2449 section.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — extend the t2449/t3052 reference line to mention the allowlist.

Reference pattern: `pulse-merge-process.sh` already loads several config files via `source`/`while read`; copy the simplest pattern (e.g. how `self-hosting-files.conf` is consumed by `pulse-dispatch-detector.sh`).

### Files Scope

- .agents/configs/trusted-issue-authors.conf
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh
- .agents/reference/auto-merge.md
- .agents/AGENTS.md

## Acceptance

2. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` clean.
3. With `alex-solovyev` in the allowlist, an issue authored by alex-solovyev resolves the gate without crypto signature; without the allowlist entry, it still blocks (regression of t3052 behaviour).
4. Empty/missing config file = no allowlist entries = pure t2449/t3052 behaviour preserved.

## Verification


title: t3063: add kill_reason field to [lifecycle] worker_exited line
body:
## What

Add `kill_reason` field to the `[lifecycle] worker_exited` line in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` so Phase 2 aggregation finds reason class on the same line as `wait_status`, no PID-join required.

## Why

PR #21784 (resolves #21781) emits `[lifecycle] worker_killed` lines at all 5 SIGTERM sites — but these are written by the watchdog at kill time. The `[lifecycle] worker_exited pid=<N> wait_status=<S>` line, where the canonical `wait_status=143` (SIGTERM) vs `wait_status=0` (clean exit) signal lives, is emitted separately by `worker-lifecycle-common.sh::worker_exited` (or wherever this line originates).

Phase 2 aggregation currently has to JOIN by PID across two log lines from two scripts to know "this 143 was caused by no_output_stall". This is fragile:

- The pulse-dispatch.log has interleaved entries from many concurrent workers
- PID reuse across log rotations breaks the join
- Workers killed by paths that don't emit `worker_killed` (e.g. OOM, parent crash) show as `wait_status=143` with no kill_reason

Issue #21781's `Files Scope` explicitly listed this file. The PR skipped it without justification.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — wherever the `[lifecycle] worker_exited` line is emitted (search: `worker_exited pid=`)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — if it owns the worker_exited emission instead

### Reference patterns

Read the kill_reason from the same `LIFECYCLE_LOG` file (or a sentinel `${EXIT_CODE_FILE}.kill_reason`) and embed it in the worker_exited line:

```bash
local kill_reason_class="natural"
if [[ -f "${EXIT_CODE_FILE}.kill_reason" ]]; then
    kill_reason_class=$(<"${EXIT_CODE_FILE}.kill_reason")
fi
log_info "[lifecycle] worker_exited pid=${pid} wait_status=${ws} kill_reason=${kill_reason_class}"
```

Where `kill_reason_class` is one of `natural` (clean voluntary exit), `no_output_stall`, `hard_kill_stall`, `phase1_zero_output`, `process_guard_*`, `stage_timeout_*`, `wait_loop_timeout_*`, `wall_clock_stale`, `cold_start_timeout`, `progress_timeout`, `idle_timeout`, `stop_flag`.

The kill sites in PR #21784 already emit these classes — they need to write them to the sentinel file as well, OR the classifier needs to scan LIFECYCLE_LOG by PID at exit time.

### Verification

- Pulse-dispatch.log query produces complete reason classification in one pass:
  ```bash
  grep "worker_exited" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log \
    | sed -E 's/.*wait_status=([0-9]+).*kill_reason=([a-z_0-9]+).*/\1 \2/' \
    | sort | uniq -c
  ```
- Acceptance target: 0% of `wait_status=143` lines have `kill_reason=unknown`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` clean

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[lifecycle] worker_exited` line carries `kill_reason` field
- [ ] All known kill paths populate kill_reason; default is `natural` for clean exits
- [ ] Phase 2 query returns 0 `wait_status=143` lines with `kill_reason=unknown`
- [ ] No new ShellCheck violations

## Complexity Impact

~10 lines added to one function. Well under gates.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — needs to thread kill_reason through the lifecycle library; small design decision about sentinel file vs log-scan.

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/21837/head:recovered-21837
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick 161321ed93eb5f2b53e6275e0afc1ea05ab79751
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

title: t3064: extend PR #21733 fix — use gh_issue_edit_safe in remaining hot-path body updates
body:
## Task

Apply the `gh_issue_edit_safe` REST-fallback fix from PR #21733 to the remaining bare `gh issue edit --body` call sites in pulse-driven hot paths. PR #21733 fixed only `stats-health-dashboard.sh:179`; three identical call sites elsewhere have the same failure mode and are equally susceptible to GraphQL rate-limit silent-failure.

## Why

Bare `gh issue edit --body` always uses GraphQL. When the 5000/hr GraphQL budget is exhausted, the call silently fails — error is logged to LOGFILE but the body update is lost until the budget resets (up to 1h). The wrapper `gh_issue_edit_safe` (defined at `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:218`) falls back to REST `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{N}` which uses the separate 5000/hr core API budget that stays available even when GraphQL is exhausted. Same root cause as PR #21733; same fix applies to three more sites.

All three sites run on pulse-driven hot paths — exactly when GraphQL pressure is highest:
- `post-merge-review-scanner.sh:814` — runs every pulse cycle to refresh stale review-followup issue bodies.
- `pulse-merge-conflict.sh:1019` — runs on merge-close path (t2118 carry-forward of PR diff into linked issue body).
- `pulse-merge-feedback.sh:168` — runs on every PR feedback routing (review/CI feedback append).

## How

All three files transitively source `shared-constants.sh` (which sources `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` → `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:218` defining `gh_issue_edit_safe`) — the wrapper is reachable, drop-in compatible, and validated by 28 unit tests in `tests/test-gh-edit-safety.sh`.

title: Migrate statusCheckRollup from GraphQL to REST check-suites endpoint
body:
## Task
Replace `gh pr list --json statusCheckRollup` (GraphQL, ~230KB per cycle) with per-PR REST `/commits/{sha}/check-suites` calls (~1.3KB each) in pulse prefetch and related scripts.

## Why
`statusCheckRollup` is the single heaviest GraphQL consumer in the pulse:
- 11 open PRs × ~70 checks × ~300 bytes = **230KB per cycle**
- 20 cycles/hr × 230KB = **4.6MB GraphQL/hr** on one field
- GraphQL budget (5000 points/hr) is shared with all other ops — statusCheckRollup crowds out issue creation, PR management, search
- REST budget (5000/hr) is **separate** and currently ~80% unused

## Research findings (GH#21774 session)

| Approach | Endpoint | Budget pool | Size/PR | 11 PRs total | Gives PASS/FAIL/PENDING? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Current** | GraphQL `statusCheckRollup` | GraphQL (shared) | ~21KB | 230KB | Yes, client-side |
| REST check-runs | `/commits/{sha}/check-runs` | REST (separate) | ~111KB | 1.2MB | Yes, but heavier |
| **REST check-suites** | `/commits/{sha}/check-suites` | REST (separate) | **~1.3KB** | **~15KB** | **Yes** |
| REST combined status | `/commits/{sha}/status` | REST (separate) | ~0.1KB | ~1KB | Legacy status only |

**Winner: REST check-suites** — 15x smaller payload, uses separate REST budget, returns conclusion+status per suite (enough to derive PASS/FAIL/PENDING).

### Derivation logic (proven in session):
```bash
gh api "repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/$sha/check-suites" --jq '
  if (.check_suites | length) == 0 then "none"
  elif (.check_suites | all(.conclusion == "success" or .conclusion == "skipped" or .conclusion == "neutral")) then "PASS"
  elif (.check_suites | any(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "timed_out" or .conclusion == "cancelled")) then "FAIL"
  else "PENDING"
  end'
```

## How
Scripts that use `statusCheckRollup`:
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:119-121` — replace `--json number,statusCheckRollup` with per-PR REST check-suites loop
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:153-169` — simplify jq (checks_json now has pre-computed summary, not raw rollup)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:72,81` — same migration
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-queue-governor.sh:56,66-67` — same migration
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:683-687` — single-PR check, use check-suites
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-data.sh:202,262` — same migration
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:609,653` — same migration
- Requires `headRefOid` (commit SHA) per PR — already available from `gh pr list --json headRefOid`

## Acceptance
- `rg 'statusCheckRollup' .agents/scripts/ --type sh | grep -v tests | grep -v '#'` returns zero code lines
- GraphQL budget consumption drops measurably (check `gh api rate_limit` before/after pulse cycle)
- Pulse dashboard still shows correct PASS/FAIL/PENDING per PR
- `shellcheck` clean on all modified files

title: t3065: worktree-helper.sh remove emits BSD sed regex error after cleanup
body:
## Symptom

Running worktree-helper.sh remove on macOS prints (after the SUCCESS messages):

    sed: 1: "s|.*[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+?)( ...": RE error: repetition-operator operand invalid

The error appears after the worktree is fully removed and localdev cleanup completes — functional behaviour is unaffected, but the trailing error is misleading (looks like cleanup failed when it succeeded).

## Root cause hypothesis

BSD sed (macOS default) does not support extended-regex `?` (zero-or-one) repetition the way GNU sed does. The pattern `([^/]+/[^/]+?)` uses non-greedy `?` semantics which BSD sed rejects.

## Files to modify

EDIT: ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh — locate the sed invocation matching `s|.*[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+?)`. Likely in the post-cleanup origin-slug parse path. Replace with a portable form: either `sed -E` with explicit greedy form, or use bash parameter expansion (preferred — no sed needed for slug parsing).

## Reference pattern

shared-constants.sh defines portable helpers (_file_mtime_epoch etc.). Apply same portability discipline to sed: either avoid sed for path manipulation (use bash `${var##*/}` etc.) or guard with `case "$(uname)" in Darwin*) ...`.

## Verification

After fix, run: ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh add feature/test-sed-fix && ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh remove feature/test-sed-fix --force

Should produce zero `sed:` error lines in output.

## Discovery context

Observed during t3058 (PR #21797) worktree cleanup on macOS Darwin.

title: t3066: extend approve_collaborator_pr to honour crypto-approval as CONTRIBUTOR-author bypass (sibling of t3052)
body:
## Why

PR #21733 (author `superdav42`, CONTRIBUTOR) sat with maintainer cryptographic approval (`APPROVE:issue:marcusquinn/aidevops:21733`) at `2026-04-29T22:09:47Z`, but the pulse kept refusing to auto-approve it with:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #21733 in marcusquinn/aidevops — author superdav42 is not a collaborator
```

The skip is upstream of `approve_collaborator_pr` — `pulse-merge.sh:187` short-circuits in `_check_pr_merge_gates` (or its caller) when `_is_collaborator_author "$pr_author" "$repo_slug"` returns false. Even if it reached `approve_collaborator_pr`, that function self-validates author at `pulse-merge-gates.sh:402-405` (GH#17671 / t2933 hardening) and refuses regardless of crypto-approval.

t3052 (PR #21767) extended the t2449 worker-briefed gate to honour crypto approval. This issue extends the **same trust signal** to the deterministic merge cascade. Without it, `sudo aidevops approve` on a CONTRIBUTOR-authored PR is effectively a no-op — the maintainer's explicit cryptographic consent cannot satisfy the author-association gate.

## What

Extend the maintainer-collaborator gate in the deterministic merge path so that a verified cryptographic approval signature on either the linked issue OR the PR itself counts as maintainer consent — equivalent to `_is_collaborator_author` succeeding for trust purposes.

The GH#17671 defence-in-depth is preserved: crypto-approval is a stronger signal than author-association (it requires root-owned SSH key, which workers cannot forge), so honouring it does not weaken the supply-chain protection that the original guard exists to provide.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh`
- `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md`
- `.agents/reference/incident-gh17671-supply-chain.md`

### Implementation pattern (model on t3052 / PR #21767)

1. **EDIT `pulse-merge-gates.sh:402-405`** — `approve_collaborator_pr`. Before refusing on `! _is_collaborator_author "$pr_author"`, check for a crypto-approval signature on the PR or its linked issue:
    ```bash
    # Crypto-approval bypass: a verified maintainer signature on the PR or
    # its linked issue is a stronger trust signal than author-association.
    # See t3052 (PR #21767) for the symmetric extension to the worker-briefed gate.
    if _has_maintainer_crypto_approval "$pr_number" "$repo_slug"; then
        echo "[pulse-wrapper] approve_collaborator_pr: PR #$pr_number author (@$pr_author) is not a collaborator on $repo_slug, but maintainer crypto-approval found — proceeding (t3063)" >>"$LOGFILE"
        # fall through to the approval block
    elif [[ -n "$pr_author" ]] && [[ "$pr_author" != "unknown" ]] && ! _is_collaborator_author "$pr_author" "$repo_slug"; then
        echo "[pulse-wrapper] approve_collaborator_pr: PR #$pr_number author (@$pr_author) is not a collaborator on $repo_slug — refusing to auto-approve (GH#17671 defense-in-depth, t2933)" >>"$LOGFILE"
        return 0
    fi
    ```

2. **EDIT `pulse-merge.sh:187`** (and any sibling check in `_check_pr_merge_gates`) — apply the same crypto-bypass at the upstream merge-pass skip. The skip line currently reads `Merge pass: skipping PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} — author ${pr_author} is not a collaborator`. Wrap the skip in the same `_has_maintainer_crypto_approval` check.

3. **NEW helper `_has_maintainer_crypto_approval`** — locate or extract from t3052 worker-briefed gate. Should:
    - Search `gh api repos/$slug/issues/$N/comments` for `aidevops-signed-approval` HTML marker.
    - Verify the signature using existing `aidevops approve verify` machinery if available, else trust the marker (downstream verification already exists).
    - Check both PR comments AND linked-issue comments (issue extraction via existing `_extract_linked_issue` regex).

4. **EDIT `test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh`** — add cases:
    - (n) CONTRIBUTOR author + crypto-approval on PR → approves
    - (o) CONTRIBUTOR author + crypto-approval on linked issue → approves
    - (p) CONTRIBUTOR author + NO crypto-approval → still refuses (preserves Case B regression guard)

5. **EDIT `reference/auto-merge.md`** — document the crypto bypass under "Author-association gate" as symmetric with t3052.

6. **EDIT `reference/incident-gh17671-supply-chain.md`** — add a "t3063 update" section noting the crypto bypass is a stronger signal (root-owned SSH key vs author-association alone), preserving the four-layer defence.

### Verification

```bash
# Tests must pass — including new cases (n)(o)(p)
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-approve-collaborator-guard.sh
# Existing tests must NOT regress
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `approve_collaborator_pr` in `pulse-merge-gates.sh` honours `_has_maintainer_crypto_approval` as bypass for `_is_collaborator_author` failure
- [ ] Upstream skip in `pulse-merge.sh:187` also honours crypto bypass
- [ ] New test cases (n)(o)(p) added and passing
- [ ] Case B regression guard (CONTRIBUTOR + no crypto = refuse) still passes
- [ ] `reference/auto-merge.md` and `reference/incident-gh17671-supply-chain.md` updated
- [ ] PR body references this issue with `Resolves #NNN`

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-29 — diagnosed PR #21733 stuck despite user crypto-approval. Sibling of t3052 (PR #21767) which fixed the worker-briefed gate; this fixes the deterministic merge gate.

## Complexity Impact

`approve_collaborator_pr` is currently ~70 lines. Adding the crypto-bypass branch will add ~10 lines — projected ~80 lines, below the 100-line `function-complexity` gate. No refactor needed.

title: t3067: interactive-session-helper.sh release applies status:available to CLOSED issues
body:
## Task

`interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <slug>` unconditionally applies `status:available` to the issue, regardless of whether the issue is OPEN or CLOSED. When called on a closed issue (e.g. after a manual merge that didn't go through pulse-merge.sh), the result is a CLOSED issue tagged `status:available` — a label state that means nothing for closed issues and adds noise to label queries.

## Why

Mismatched label state pollutes `gh issue list --label status:available` queries (used by triage and dashboards) and confuses scanners that expect `status:done` or `status:resolved` on closed issues. Observed today on GH#21788 after a direct `gh pr merge` instead of pulse-merge.sh — the helper applied `status:available` to a CLOSED issue.

## How

EDIT: .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh — locate the `release` subcommand handler. Before applying `status:available`, check the issue state via `gh issue view <N> --repo <slug> --json state --jq .state`. If state is `CLOSED`, either:

  (a) Apply `status:done` instead (matches the framework's closed-issue convention used by `task-complete-helper.sh`), OR
  (b) Skip the status label change entirely and only release the local claim stamp.

Reference pattern: `task-complete-helper.sh` already handles the OPEN→CLOSED label transition correctly — model on its closed-issue branch.

title: t3068: kick pulse-merge cycle when sudo aidevops approve posts a verified signature (eliminate up-to-120s latency)
body:
## Why

Currently, `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` posts a cryptographically-signed approval comment, but the next pulse-merge cycle is up to ~120s away. For a maintainer who just approved a stuck PR, this latency is invisible (no feedback that the approval landed in the merge queue) and burns ~2 minutes per stuck-PR session.

Concrete scenario from interactive session 2026-04-29: 17+ open PRs accumulated in marcusquinn/aidevops, several blocked behind various gates. After diagnosing root causes and deploying t3052 (PR #21767), the user crypto-approved 8+ stuck PRs/issues in sequence. Each had a 0-120s wait before the next pulse cycle picked it up. The user explicitly asked: "shouldn't `sudo aidevops approve` re-trigger the merge pass?"

This is a UX gap, not a correctness gap — the approvals always eventually take effect — but ~2min × N PRs adds up, and the lack of feedback makes the maintainer uncertain whether the approval was effective.

## What

When `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` (or `aidevops approve pr <N>`) successfully posts a verified signature, kick the pulse to immediately re-evaluate the linked PR(s) — eliminating the 0-120s latency.

Two implementation options (recommend Option A):

- **Option A (touch-file marker)**: Approve helper writes `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-merge-trigger.txt` with the slug + issue/PR number. Pulse-wrapper main loop checks this marker at the top of each cycle and runs an out-of-band `pulse-merge.sh` pass on JUST those PRs before the normal cycle. Simple, crash-safe, idempotent.
- **Option B (webhook-driven)**: Reuse the t3038 webhook-driven pulse-merge infrastructure (PR #21657). Approve helper publishes a `merge-eligible` event for the target.

Option A is preferred — Option B couples to webhook infra that may not be configured in all environments.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-approve.sh` (or wherever `aidevops approve issue` is implemented)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md`

### Implementation pattern

1. **EDIT `aidevops-approve.sh`** — after the signature comment posts successfully, write a touch-file:
    ```bash
    local trigger_file="$HOME/.aidevops/cache/pulse-merge-trigger.txt"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$trigger_file")"
    # Append; pulse drains and clears
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$repo_slug" "$issue_or_pr_num" >> "$trigger_file"
    ```

2. **EDIT `pulse-wrapper.sh::main()`** — at the top of each cycle (after locks, before normal cycle work):
    ```bash
    _drain_merge_trigger_file_if_present
    ```
    Where `_drain_merge_trigger_file_if_present` reads the file, atomically clears it, and for each `slug<TAB>num` line invokes `pulse-merge.sh` scoped to that single PR.

3. **EDIT `pulse-merge.sh`** — accept an optional `--only-pr <repo_slug> <num>` flag that bypasses the full PR-list scan and processes just one PR. Reuse all existing gate logic.

4. **NEW test `tests/test-approve-kicks-pulse.sh`**:
    - Approve writes trigger file
    - Pulse drains and clears trigger file
    - Trigger file with malformed lines is handled (fail-open, log warning)

5. **EDIT `reference/auto-merge.md`** — document the new latency: "After `sudo aidevops approve`, the next pulse cycle picks up the approval within seconds (formerly up to 120s)."

### Verification

```bash
# Unit test new behaviour
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approve-kicks-pulse.sh
# Manual smoke test: approve a stuck PR and observe pulse acts within ~5s
sudo aidevops approve issue NNN
tail -f ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep "pulse-merge.*--only-pr.*NNN"
shellcheck .agents/scripts/aidevops-approve.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `aidevops approve` writes a trigger file on successful signature post
- [ ] `pulse-wrapper.sh` drains the trigger file each cycle (top of `main()`)
- [ ] `pulse-merge.sh --only-pr <slug> <num>` works as a scoped single-PR pass
- [ ] Trigger file is cleared atomically (no double-processing on race)
- [ ] Test passes; existing pulse tests do not regress
- [ ] Latency from approval to pulse action drops from up to 120s to <5s
- [ ] PR body uses `Resolves #NNN`

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-29 — user explicitly asked: "shouldn't `sudo aidevops approve issue/pr` re-trigger the merge pass?" after observing ~120s latency between approving a PR and the pulse acting on it. Sibling improvement to t3063 (gate fix); this is the latency fix.

## Complexity Impact

`pulse-wrapper.sh::main()` adds ~5 lines (drain call). `pulse-merge.sh` adds ~15 lines (--only-pr branch). `aidevops-approve.sh` adds ~3 lines (touch file). All well below complexity gates.

title: t3069: harden issue_num extraction against multi-line gh_create_issue output (TODO.md append silently fails)
body:
## Why

Filing two issues via `claim-task-id.sh` in 2026-04-29 interactive session both produced output like:

```text
[INFO] Skipping auto-assign for #2157
21803 — auto-dispatch entry is worker-owned (t2218)
awk: newline in string - [ ] t3066 extend a... at source line 1
[INFO] t2548: appended TODO entry for t3066 (ref:GH#2157
21803)
[OK] Created issue: GH#2157
21803
ref=GH#2157
issue_url=https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/2157
```

The actual issue created was 21803 (correct). 2157 is an unrelated MERGED PR from 2026-02-22 ("fix: suppress Homebrew auto-update globally"). Both numbers ended up concatenated via newline in `$issue_num`, which:

1. Caused awk to error out parsing the TODO line.
2. Caused the TODO.md append to silently fail (no entry landed).
3. Reported the wrong `ref=GH#2157` to the caller (truncated at first newline).

Failure mode reproducible on first issue (#21803) and second (#21806).

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:535`:

```bash
issue_num=$(echo "$issue_url" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')
```

When `$issue_url` is multi-line (which happens when `gh_create_issue` falls back from `issue-sync-helper.sh push` to bare `gh` creation, accumulating both warning output and the final URL), `grep -oE '[0-9]+$'` matches digits-at-end-of-line for EVERY line. Older lines may contain unrelated issue numbers from log output.

The user observed prior `[WARN] issue-sync-helper.sh push returned no issue number, falling back to bare creation` immediately above the failure, confirming the multi-line accumulation path.

## What

Make `issue_num` extraction robust to multi-line `$issue_url`:

- Take the LAST GitHub URL line, then extract its trailing digits — never accept multiple matches.
- Validate `issue_num` is a single positive integer before passing to `_auto_assign_issue` and `_interactive_session_auto_claim_new_task`.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-multiline-url.sh` (NEW)

### Implementation pattern

EDIT `claim-task-id.sh:535`:

```bash
# Before: issue_num=$(echo "$issue_url" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')
# After: extract from the LAST GitHub issue/PR URL in the output, then take only the trailing digits.
local _last_url
_last_url=$(echo "$issue_url" | grep -oE 'https://github\.com/[^[:space:]]+/(issues|pull)/[0-9]+' | tail -n1)
issue_num=$(echo "$_last_url" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')

# Validate single integer (reject empty, non-numeric, or multi-line)
if [[ -z "$issue_num" || ! "$issue_num" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    log_warn "Failed to extract single issue number from gh_create_issue output: $issue_url"
    return 1
fi
```

NEW `tests/test-claim-task-id-multiline-url.sh`:

- Stub `gh_create_issue` to emit a known multi-line output (warning line + 2 unrelated URLs + final new-issue URL).
- Source the extraction logic and assert `issue_num` matches the LAST URL's number, not earlier lines.
- Negative test: stub returns no URL → return 1, no issue_num.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-multiline-url.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
# Smoke test: claim a new task, verify TODO.md entry lands and ref=GH#NNN matches the actual issue.
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `claim-task-id.sh:535` extraction handles multi-line `$issue_url` correctly
- [ ] New test asserts last-URL extraction with multi-line input
- [ ] No regression on single-line URL case (existing happy path)
- [ ] TODO.md entry lands successfully when claim is invoked from interactive session
- [ ] No `awk: newline in string` error in normal output

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-29. Surfaced while filing t3066 and t3068 — the systemic fixes for the PR merge backlog. Both claims emitted the multi-line bug; both TODO entries failed to land. Issues themselves were created correctly, but traceability via TODO.md was lost.

## Complexity Impact

Adds ~7 lines to `claim-task-id.sh:535`. Function body is currently ~140 lines (well under 100-line gate already approaches). Net size unchanged or slightly larger. No refactor required.

title: Research caveman-style token optimization for aidevops
body:
## What

Research [JuliusBrussee/caveman](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman) (50K+ stars) — a Claude Code skill that cuts ~75% output tokens via compressed communication style. Evaluate whether its techniques could complement or improve aidevops's existing token-efficiency rules.

title: t3070: switch pulse-merge to GitHub native auto-merge for sub-30s green-to-merged latency
body:
## Why

Measured push→merge latency on 7 recent pulse-merged PRs (2026-04-29):

| PR    | Author        | push→merge |
|-------|---------------|-----------:|
| #21797 | marcusquinn (owner)   | 3m 8s |
| #21792 | alex-solovyev (peer)  | 12m 10s |
| #21767 | alex-solovyev (peer)  | 21m 45s |
| #21769 | alex-solovyev (peer)  | 70m 34s |
| #21768 | alex-solovyev (peer)  | 73m 13s |
| #21766 | alex-solovyev (peer)  | 89m 50s |
| #21778 | alex-solovyev (peer)  | 99m 33s |

70-100 min cases were t2449 backlog draining post-t3052 deploy (one-time). Excluding those, baseline is **3-22 min** for green-CI → merged. The dominant component is the **~120s pulse poll cycle**: pulse detects "all green now" only at the next tick.

Current `pulse-merge.sh` calls `gh pr merge` (or REST PUT) only when CI is **already green** at the moment the cycle inspects the PR. There's no way to "merge as soon as CI goes green" without polling.

GitHub's native auto-merge feature (`gh pr merge --auto`) does exactly this: when invoked on a PR with all gates passing **except** still-pending CI, GitHub watches and merges autonomously within seconds of green. Repo-level `allow_auto_merge: true` was just enabled (2026-04-29) on 10 pulse-managed repos.

## What

When pulse-merge has evaluated all non-CI gates as PASS but CI is still pending or in-progress, switch from "skip and revisit next cycle" to "set GitHub native auto-merge and move on". GitHub then merges within ~5-30s of green (down from up to 120s polling overhead, down further from 4-10 min historical t2411 cooldown).

This is the SAME approval/gate logic — just delegating the "when to actually merge" trigger to GitHub. All existing safety (review-bot-gate, maintainer gate, complexity gate, crypto-approval check, etc.) is preserved because it runs BEFORE setting auto-merge.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-native-auto.sh` (NEW)

### Implementation pattern

1. **EDIT `pulse-merge-process.sh`** — in `_process_single_ready_pr` (or the function that decides the merge call), check `allow_auto_merge` on the repo via cached `gh api repos/$slug --jq '.allow_auto_merge'`. If true AND all non-CI gates pass:
    - When CI is `pending`/`in_progress` and otherwise mergeable → set GitHub native auto-merge via `gh pr merge --auto --squash` (or REST `PUT /repos/.../pulls/N/merge` with `auto_merge: true`).
    - When CI is already `success` → existing fast path (immediate merge).
    - When CI is `failure` → existing skip path.

2. **EDIT `pulse-merge.sh`** — extend `process_pr` to recognise that GitHub auto-merge has already been set (PR has `auto_merge` non-null). Skip re-setting; let GitHub handle.

3. **NEW test `test-pulse-merge-native-auto.sh`**:
    - Stub PR with all-green gates + CI pending → asserts `gh pr merge --auto` invocation.
    - Stub PR with all-green gates + CI success → existing fast path (no `--auto`).
    - Stub PR with `auto_merge` already set → no-op.
    - Stub repo with `allow_auto_merge: false` → falls back to polling path (existing behaviour).

4. **EDIT `reference/auto-merge.md`** — add "Native Auto-Merge" section between t2411 and webhook subsections. Document that the polling cycle is now the backstop; native auto-merge is the fast path when repo allows it. Include the `gh api -X PATCH repos/SLUG -F allow_auto_merge=true` enablement command.

5. **NEW config helper or reuse existing** — when a new repo is added via `aidevops init`, optionally enable `allow_auto_merge: true` if the repo allows it (idempotent, fail-soft on permission denied).

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-native-auto.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
# Smoke test: open a trivial owner PR, observe pulse sets --auto on first cycle, GitHub merges within 30s of CI green
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-merge-process.sh` checks `allow_auto_merge` and uses `gh pr merge --auto` when CI is still pending but all other gates pass
- [ ] Existing fast-path (immediate merge on green CI) preserved
- [ ] PRs with `auto_merge` already set are not re-set on subsequent cycles
- [ ] Repos with `allow_auto_merge: false` fall back to polling path
- [ ] New test passes; existing pulse-merge tests do not regress
- [ ] Documentation updated in `reference/auto-merge.md`
- [ ] Measured push→merge latency drops from 3-12 min (owner/peer green PRs) to <2 min on a smoke-test PR

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-29 — user explicitly asked "green PRs still seem very slow to merge, any way to speed that up?" after observing 3-22 min latencies on recent merges. Native auto-merge is a strict speedup with zero infrastructure cost (vs t3038 webhook which needs cloudflared tunnel + secret + GitHub webhook config). Repo flag enabled across 10 pulse repos on 2026-04-29.

## Complexity Impact

`_process_single_ready_pr` adds ~20 lines (one new branch). Currently ~80 lines, post-change ~100 — at the function-complexity gate. Refactor advisable: extract `_set_native_auto_merge_or_skip` helper to keep the main function lean.

title: t3071: audit framework for t3058-class watchdog self-write anti-pattern (monitor X, write marker to X)
body:
## Premise

PR #21797 (t3058) discovered a critical class of silent bug in `worker-activity-watchdog.sh`:

> When a watchdog monitors file X for stalls (via byte-delta, line-count, or mtime), and the same code path writes status markers (defer/heartbeat/info) into file X, those self-writes register as "progress" — silently neutering the timeout for the very condition the marker was meant to instrument.

**Concrete instance fixed by t3058**: defer marker writes were going to `$OUTPUT_FILE` (the file the watchdog monitors). Result: `STALL_TIMEOUT` was effectively a no-op for any CPU-busy worker — only `HARD_KILL_SECONDS=1500` was a real cap. The bug shipped silently for an undetermined period — easily a year or more given the file's age.

This audit scans the framework for OTHER instances of the same anti-pattern.

## Why

- t3058 is one fix, but the pattern shape is generic: **monitor X, write marker to X**
- Any other instance has the same silent-neuter property: a timeout becomes a no-op with no observable failure mode
- Watchdogs, stall detectors, CI progress monitors, recovery loops are all candidates
- Single high-leverage scan; each finding gets a small targeted fix per the t3058 routing model
- Codifying the rule once prevents future reintroduction

## What

- **Phase 1**: Mechanical scan for the anti-pattern signature across `.agents/scripts/`
- **Phase 2**: Classify each suspect (GENUINE / DEFENDED / UNRELATED) with one-line rationale
- **Phase 3**: File a separate auto-dispatch fix issue per GENUINE finding (one PR per fix, mirroring t3058)
- **Phase 4**: Codify the rule in `reference/shell-style-guide.md` so future code can't reintroduce it

## How

### Phase 1 — scan signature

Find scripts containing BOTH:

- A loop that polls a file for activity (`last_size`, `prev_size`, `byte_delta`, `wc -l "$f"`, `wc -c "$f"`, `stat ... %z`, mtime polling)
- A write statement targeting that same file (`>>"$file"`, `tee "$file"`, `printf ... >"$file"`)

Concrete starting scan:

```bash
# Find scripts with byte-delta-style monitoring
rg -l 'last_size|prev_size|byte_delta|previous_size|file_size_prev' .agents/scripts/

# For each, identify the monitored file variable and check for writes to it
for f in $(rg -l 'last_size|prev_size|byte_delta' .agents/scripts/); do
  echo "=== $f ==="
  rg -nN '(last_size|prev_size|byte_delta).*\$\{?([A-Z_]+)' "$f" -r '$2' | sort -u
done
```

Then for each candidate `(file, monitored_var)` pair, run:

```bash
rg "(>>|tee|printf.*>).*\$\{?$VAR\}?\b" "$file"
```

Any non-empty result is a SUSPECT requiring Phase 2 classification.

### Files to start with (known watchdog/progress-polling logic)

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` — t3058 fixed the defer-marker write; **check the other marker writes in this file** (kill marker, classification marker, recovery marker, hard-kill announcement) for the same pattern
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh` — `_watchdog_check_progress` watches `$LOGFILE` via byte-delta; verify nothing in `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` writes status markers to `$LOGFILE` during the watched window
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` — `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor` and `run_pulse` both write to `$LOGFILE`; cross-reference with `pulse-watchdog.sh` monitored vars
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — `tee "$output_file"` with downstream byte-delta monitoring (this is where t3058 lived); check for sibling writers to `$output_file`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` and `headless-runtime-provider.sh` — sub-libraries split from `headless-runtime-helper.sh`; same monitor-and-write contract surface
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — has byte-delta and progress-stall logic; verify
- All other matches from the Phase 1 regex

### Phase 2 — classification

For each suspect, classify as:

- **GENUINE**: monitor watches X, the same code path writes to X with no defensive countermeasure (no sentinel filter, no separate file routing) → file fix issue
- **DEFENDED**: writer uses a sentinel pattern the monitor explicitly excludes (e.g., grep -v before counting), or the write happens outside the watch window → safe, document the contract in a comment
- **UNRELATED**: false positive from the regex (e.g., monitoring is for size accounting, not stall detection)

Document classification in a comment on this issue with one-line rationale per suspect.

### Phase 3 — fix per GENUINE

Pattern from t3058 (PR #21797), applied verbatim:

```bash
# Before (anti-pattern):
echo "$marker" >>"$OUTPUT_FILE"   # OUTPUT_FILE is the file the watchdog monitors

# After (fix):
echo "[lifecycle] marker_<event>" >>"$LIFECYCLE_LOG"   # separate file, never monitored
```

The fix is always: **route the marker to a sibling log that the watchdog does NOT consult**. `$LIFECYCLE_LOG` (defaults to `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log` per `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`) is the canonical destination for lifecycle markers; pick a different sibling if the marker is conceptually different.

Each GENUINE finding becomes its own auto-dispatch issue with: scope = the one offending file, fix = one-line redirection, regression test = the t3058 model (`tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh` Test 4b shows the pattern).

### Phase 4 — codification

Add to `reference/shell-style-guide.md` a section:

```markdown
## Watchdog Self-Write Anti-Pattern (t3058 + t<this>)

If a script monitors file X for activity as a stall signal (byte-delta, line-count, mtime), the SAME script MUST NOT write status markers to X. Self-writes register as progress and silently neuter the timeout. Route markers to `$LIFECYCLE_LOG` (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log`) instead.

Canonical examples:
- worker-activity-watchdog.sh:570-583 (PR #21797 fix)

CI gate: TBD — scan PRs for `>>"$X"` where the same file contains a `last_size=$(stat ... "$X")` polling loop.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Phase 1 scan completed; full suspect list posted as a comment on this issue
- [ ] Phase 2 classification: every suspect labeled GENUINE / DEFENDED / UNRELATED with one-line rationale (in comment)
- [ ] Phase 3 fix issues filed per GENUINE finding, each with `auto-dispatch` and `tier:simple` (the fix shape is mechanical once classified)
- [ ] Phase 4: anti-pattern rule added to `reference/shell-style-guide.md`
- [ ] Memory note stored: `memory-helper.sh store --confidence high` capturing the pattern for future review sessions

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` (re-audit other markers)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh`
- All other scripts under `.agents/scripts/` returned by the Phase 1 regex
- `reference/shell-style-guide.md` (Phase 4)

## Complexity Impact

Audit-only — no functions added or grown. Phase 4 adds ~20 lines to `reference/shell-style-guide.md` (markdown, not shell). Each Phase 3 fix is single-line redirect; complexity-bump-ok not anticipated.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — Phase 2 classification is per-file judgment (not regex-decidable). Phase 4 needs a clear, durable rule statement.

## Reference

- t3058 / PR #21797 — canonical fix establishing the routing pattern; worker-activity-watchdog.sh:570-583 is the before/after diff
- `LIFECYCLE_LOG` env var (default `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log`) — canonical sibling-log destination
- `tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh` Test 4b — regression-test model for fixes

title: git_safety_guard.py: enforce canonical-workspace protection on Edit|Write across all default-branch names
body:
## Task

Make `git_safety_guard.py` enforce the **canonical-workspace protection** rule (framework rule "t1990: ALL work goes through a linked worktree") for Edit/Write tool calls, regardless of whether the canonical repo is on `main`, `master`, `develop`, or any other branch.

Today the hook silently allows Edit/Write on the canonical workspace whenever the canonical is checked out on any non-`main`/`master` branch — even when those edits violate the documented framework rule. This was discovered when an interactive session resumed against a canonical that a prior session had left on `feature/t620-billing-rls-phase1`; the agent edited canonical-tree files directly and no hook fired.

## Why

Three independent gaps allow the rule to be violated mechanically:

1. **`install-hooks-helper.sh` registers `git_safety_guard.py` on the `Bash` matcher only.** `~/.claude/settings.json` ends up with:
   ```json
   { "matcher": "Bash",       "hooks": ["...git_safety_guard.py"] },
   { "matcher": "Edit|Write", "hooks": ["...complexity_advisory_pre_edit.py"] }
   ```
   The hook's own code (`.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py:343-348`) handles Edit/Write — but that branch is unreachable under the installed config. Dead code.
2. **`git_safety_guard.py:287` hardcodes `("main", "master")`** as the protected branch set. Some registered repos use `develop` (or any other name) as their default branch. On a non-`main`/`master` default branch, the hook returns `None` ("not protected") and allows arbitrary writes — even the `README.md`/`TODO.md`/`todo/**` allowlist is never consulted.
3. **`pre-edit-check.sh` exit 3 is a non-blocking warning.** When the canonical is off the default branch, the script prints "Options: 1. Create worktree..." and exits 3 — but no PreToolUse hook calls `pre-edit-check.sh` before Edit/Write, and exit 3 doesn't translate to a `permissionDecision: deny` regardless. So the script is purely advisory and only invoked manually.

The combined effect: an interactive agent can silently edit a canonical workspace that's stale on any branch other than `main`/`master`, with zero enforcement. The documented rule ("ALL work goes through a linked worktree") relies entirely on agent discipline.

Reproduction: in any repo whose default branch is not `main`/`master` (e.g. `develop`), leave the canonical checked out on `feature/foo` (e.g. from a prior session that didn't reset). Open a fresh interactive session and call Edit on a tracked file. No hook fires; the edit lands. This was observed today against a managed private repo (default branch `develop`) left on a prior session's feature branch — interactive Edit/Write succeeded with no protection.

## How

Three coupled changes to make the install + hook honour the t1990/t1712 rule semantics ("canonical workspace + non-default branch + non-allowlisted path = deny") instead of the literal `main`/`master` check.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py`
- `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh` (NEW)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh` (only if existing assertions need to follow the renamed semantics)
- `AGENTS.md` (one paragraph under "Pre-edit rules" / t1712 reference, if the rule wording shifts)

### EDIT: `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py`

1. **Add `_get_default_branch(repo_root: str) -> str`** that returns the configured default branch, in priority order:
   - `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (strips `origin/` prefix), wrapped in subprocess with timeout, fail-soft
   - fallback: `git config --get init.defaultBranch`
   - fallback: literal `"main"`
   Cache the result per-`repo_root` for the lifetime of the hook process (a single Edit/Write call) — do NOT cache across invocations (mtime-stable enough for one tool call, but per-run otherwise).

2. **Replace the hardcoded check at line 287** (`if branch not in ("main", "master"): return None`) with:
   ```python
   default_branch = _get_default_branch(repo_root)
   if branch == default_branch:
       # On default branch: existing main-allowlist logic governs
       if _is_linked_worktree(repo_root) or _is_main_allowlisted(file_path, repo_root):
           return None
       return _build_deny(...)  # reuse the existing deny dict structure
   else:
       # Off default branch in canonical workspace: allow only inside a linked worktree
       if _is_linked_worktree(repo_root):
           return None
       return _build_canonical_off_default_deny(file_path, branch, default_branch)
   ```

3. **Add `_build_canonical_off_default_deny()`** that returns a clear deny dict explaining: "Canonical workspace is on `<branch>` (default is `<default_branch>`). Per t1990, all work goes through a linked worktree. Either: (a) `wt switch -c <type>/<name>`, or (b) reset canonical: `git switch <default_branch>`." Match the formatting of the existing main-allowlist deny so error messages are consistent.

4. **Keep the `MAIN_BRANCH_ALLOWLIST`** (`README.md`, `TODO.md`, `todo/`) — it still applies for headless sessions that legitimately edit planning files on the default branch. Do NOT extend the allowlist to off-default-branch edits in canonical; the rule there is "linked worktree, full stop."

5. **Headless-session carve-out**: when `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`, `OPENCODE_HEADLESS`, or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set in the environment, retain today's behaviour for the default-branch path (allowlist-only writes). Off-default-branch writes from headless workers should already happen inside their own worktrees, but if any headless path needs the carve-out, document it and add a guarded escape via env var (`AIDEVOPS_SKIP_CANONICAL_GUARD=1`) for explicit override.

### EDIT: `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh`

1. **Register `git_safety_guard.py` on the `Edit|Write` matcher in addition to `Bash`** (lines ~759 and ~769 currently set `hook_entry` for Bash and `complexity_advisory_entry` for Edit|Write). Either:
   - Add a third matcher entry that registers `git_safety_guard.py` for Edit|Write, OR
   - Append the git_safety_guard command to the existing Edit|Write matcher's `hooks` array alongside `complexity_advisory_pre_edit.py`.
   Prefer option 2 (single Edit|Write matcher with both hooks) to keep the settings.json compact.

2. **Update the `has_hook()` / removal logic** (lines ~717-721, ~798-804, ~867-879) so that:
   - Install is idempotent: rerunning `install` on a settings.json that already has the new layout doesn't duplicate entries.
   - Uninstall removes `git_safety_guard.py` from BOTH the Bash and Edit|Write matchers.

3. **Update the status check** (`_check_status` around line ~958) to verify the hook is registered under both matchers and report missing registration explicitly.

4. **Update the docstring/comments at top of file** (lines 7-17) to reflect the broader scope.

### NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh`

Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh` for structure (init temp git repo, run hook with crafted JSON stdin, assert exit-code + JSON output). Cover at minimum:

1. **Default-branch detection** — repo with `origin/HEAD -> origin/develop`: hook reports `develop` as default; allowlist-deny still works on `develop`; non-allowlisted Edit on `develop` is denied.
2. **Off-default-branch in canonical** — repo on `feature/foo`, NOT in a linked worktree, Edit to a non-allowlisted path: hook returns `permissionDecision: deny` with the canonical-off-default reason.
3. **Off-default-branch in linked worktree** — same repo, Edit invoked from a linked worktree path: hook allows (returns no output / exit 0).
4. **Default-branch allowlist preserved** — repo on default branch, Edit to `README.md` / `TODO.md` / `todo/foo.md`: allowed.
5. **Default-branch non-allowlisted** — repo on default branch, Edit to `src/foo.ts`: denied (existing behaviour).
6. **Bash matcher unchanged** — destructive `rm -rf` and `git reset --hard` still denied; safe `git checkout -b` still allowed.
7. **Repo without `origin/HEAD` set** — falls back to `init.defaultBranch` then `main`; doesn't crash.
8. **Headless env var bypass** — `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=1` set: off-default-branch writes still denied (workers should be in their own worktrees) OR allowed per the carve-out chosen during implementation. Test must match the implemented behaviour.

### EDIT: `AGENTS.md` (small)

If the wording around t1712/t1990 references "main-branch file allowlist" specifically, broaden it to "default-branch file allowlist (default branch is auto-detected from `origin/HEAD`)". Do not change the rule itself — the rule is unchanged; only the implementation now matches the documented intent.

## Reference pattern

- Default-branch detection: model on `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` if it has a similar helper, else inline the subprocess call as in `_get_current_branch()` (line 166 of `git_safety_guard.py`).
- Deny dict format: reuse the structure from `_check_main_branch_allowlist()` (lines 295-309) — the user-facing reason text is the most important part, since that's what the agent reads when blocked.
- Test harness: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh` already builds a temp git repo + runs the script; copy that scaffold and adapt for the Python hook (invoke via `python3 .agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py < <(echo "$json")`).

## Verification

```bash
# 1. Lint passes
shellcheck .agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh
python3 -m py_compile .agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py

# 2. New tests pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh

# 3. Existing tests still pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-install-hooks-validator-preflight.sh

# 4. Round-trip install works
.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh install
jq '.hooks.PreToolUse[] | {matcher, hooks: [.hooks[].command]}' ~/.claude/settings.json
# Expect: git_safety_guard.py registered under BOTH Bash and Edit|Write matchers

# 5. Manual reproduction of the original gap is now blocked
cd ~/Git/aidevops  # or any repo
git switch -c tmp/canonical-guard-test
# In a Claude Code session at this path, attempt to Edit a non-allowlisted file
# Expect: Edit blocked with "Canonical workspace is on tmp/canonical-guard-test (default is main)..."
git switch main
git branch -D tmp/canonical-guard-test
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `install-hooks-helper.sh install` registers `git_safety_guard.py` under both `Bash` and `Edit|Write` matchers in `~/.claude/settings.json`; running install twice produces no duplicates.
- [ ] `git_safety_guard.py` detects the default branch from `origin/HEAD` (with documented fallbacks) and applies branch-aware deny logic; no `("main", "master")` literal remains in the protected-branch check.
- [ ] In any repo, an Edit/Write tool call from the canonical workspace (not a linked worktree) on a branch that is NOT the default branch is denied with a clear reason, regardless of the path. Exception: linked-worktree paths always allowed.
- [ ] On the default branch in canonical, the existing `MAIN_BRANCH_ALLOWLIST` (`README.md`, `TODO.md`, `todo/**`) governs; everything else is denied. (Existing behaviour preserved.)
- [ ] Inside a linked worktree, the hook always allows. (Existing behaviour preserved.)
- [ ] New test file `test-git-safety-guard.sh` covers the eight cases listed in How. Existing `test-pre-edit-check.sh` and `test-install-hooks-validator-preflight.sh` continue to pass.
- [ ] Hook uninstall (`install-hooks-helper.sh uninstall`) cleanly removes the entry from both matchers.
- [ ] `shellcheck` zero violations on modified scripts; `python3 -m py_compile` succeeds.

## Tier rationale (`tier:standard`)

Multiple files (Python hook + shell installer + new test file + small doc edit), branch-detection logic with fallbacks, security-boundary change with asymmetric risk (too-aggressive blocks user writes; too-lenient = current state). The design is clear from this brief, so `tier:thinking` is not warranted, but the brief assumes design decisions a `tier:simple` worker shouldn't be making (e.g. headless-session carve-out behaviour, single-vs-dual matcher entry).

## Session origin

Discovered in an interactive session against a managed private repo on 2026-04-30. The canonical workspace had been left on a feature branch by a prior session; the agent edited tracked files (a marketing page component plus four locale JSON files) directly in the canonical workspace before recognizing the violation, then migrated changes to a proper linked worktree and shipped them as a PR in the originating private repo. Investigation traced the gap to the three independent issues above. See memory `mem_20260430001606_82e05938` for the full debrief.
