title: consolidated: fix worker exit classifier — SIGTERM/zero-session kills misclassified as clean (root cause for #21707 cycle)
body:
_Supersedes #21754 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix the worker exit classifier so signal-killed workers (SIGTERM/SIGKILL before producing an opencode session) are no longer misclassified as `reason=clean`. Three coordinated changes in `headless-runtime-failure.sh` + `headless-runtime-helper.sh` + `pulse-cleanup.sh`.

## Why

Canonical failure: marcusquinn/aidevops#21707 — 6+ worker dispatches on `tier:thinking` (opus-4-6) all reported `exit=0 reason=clean session_count=0`, were re-dispatched, and eventually escalated NMR. The maintainer had to take over interactively (PR #21741). Logs show every worker actually died with `wait_status=143` (SIGTERM) but the EXIT trap never saw that status.

This is a generalised classifier bug, not a #21707-only symptom: any worker killed externally between `wait` and the EXIT trap (rate-limit monitor missing the 429 keyword, sandbox timeout, OOM, manual kill, lost-race against watchdog sentinel) lands in the same false-`clean` bucket. Because `reason=clean` skips the fast-fail counter and the orphan-worktree path classifies the empty branch as `no_work` (which `escalate_issue_tier` short-circuits as "transient infra"), the system loops at the same tier indefinitely, invisible to the cost circuit breaker until stale-recovery threshold (2 ticks) trips NMR.

Pulse log evidence (deployed copy, `/tmp/pulse-marcusquinn-aidevops-21707.log`):

```
[lifecycle] worker_exited pid=56021 wait_status=143
[exit-trap] session=issue-21707 exit=0 reason=clean session_count=0
Released claim on #21707 (reason: clean)
```

`wait_status=143` (SIGTERM) + `session_count=0` (no opencode session row created) is **definitively not clean**. The classifier reports it as such because the EXIT trap reads `$?` after the wrapper functions cleanly return 0 — losing the actual worker exit status that was captured in a local variable.

Additionally (per @alex-solovyev observation, comment 2 on #21754): tier escalation was being skipped for this class of failure because `no_work` exits are treated as infrastructure failures. This confirms the masking effect: the orphan-worktree → `no_work` path produces believable-looking failure comments while the root cause (signal-kill misclassification) goes unfixed.

## How

### Fix 1 — propagate worker wait_status to EXIT trap

`EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:638-640` — after `wait "$worker_pid" 2>/dev/null || _wait_status=$?`, persist `$_wait_status` to a sentinel file the EXIT trap can read:

```bash
local _wait_status=0
wait "$worker_pid" 2>/dev/null || _wait_status=$?
print_info "[lifecycle] worker_exited pid=$worker_pid wait_status=$_wait_status"
# t3050: persist worker wait_status so the EXIT trap can classify signal kills.
# Without this, the trap reads $? at script exit (always 0 after clean cleanup)
# and classify_worker_exit returns "clean" for SIGTERM/SIGKILL kills.
if [[ -n "${exit_code_file:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$_wait_status" >"${exit_code_file}.wait_status" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
```

`EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:247-265` — in `_exit_trap_handler`, prefer the persisted wait_status over `$?`:

```bash
_exit_trap_handler() {
    local session_key="$1"
    local exit_status=$?
    # t3050: prefer the worker's actual wait_status (persisted by _invoke_opencode)
    # over $? — by the time EXIT fires, the wrapper functions have cleanly
    # returned 0 even when the worker subshell was SIGTERM'd.
    local _wait_file="${_WORKER_EXIT_CODE_FILE:-}.wait_status"
    if [[ -f "$_wait_file" ]]; then
        local _w
        _w=$(<"$_wait_file" 2>/dev/null) || _w=""
        if [[ "$_w" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_w" -gt 0 ]]; then
            exit_status="$_w"
        fi
        rm -f "$_wait_file" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    ...
```

This requires exporting `_WORKER_EXIT_CODE_FILE` from `_invoke_opencode` so the trap can find the file. Pattern matches the existing `_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH` global.

### Fix 2 — treat (exit_status=0, session_count=0) as `worker_noop_zero_output`

`EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:130-133` (`classify_worker_exit`) — extend the `wait_status == 0` clean branch to first verify session creation:

```bash
# Clean exit (unusual in EXIT trap context — trap is normally cleared on success)
if [[ "$wait_status" == "0" ]]; then
    # t3050: a clean exit with zero opencode sessions means the wrapper
    # returned 0 cleanly but the worker never produced model output. This is
    # a startup-phase failure (sandbox crash, OpenCode init failure, prompt
    # parse error before tool use), not a successful run.
    local _shared_db="${HOME}/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db"
    local _db="${_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH:-$_shared_db}"
    if command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$_db" && "$start_epoch_ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$start_epoch_ms" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local _cnt
        _cnt=$(sqlite3 "$_db" "SELECT count(*) FROM session WHERE time_created >= ${start_epoch_ms}" 2>/dev/null) || _cnt=""
        if [[ "$_cnt" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_cnt" -eq 0 ]]; then
            printf '%s' "worker_noop_zero_output"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    printf '%s' "clean"
    return 0
fi
```

The `worker_noop_zero_output` reason is already recognised downstream in `_maybe_reclassify_worker_failed_as_no_work` (worker-lifecycle-common.sh:1107) and `escalate_issue_tier` — this fix just ensures the reason is emitted authoritatively from the trap instead of being inferred later from orphan-worktree state.

### Fix 3 — orphan-worktree classifier escalates on repeated zero-session failures

`EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:428-450` (`_record_orphan_crash_classification`) — before posting `crash_type=no_work` from orphan detection, check whether the most recent CLAIM_RELEASED comment on the issue already carries `session_count=0` AND its predecessor was also `session_count=0`. If yes, escalate the failure mode rather than retry:

```bash
# t3050: per-issue infra-failure escalation. If the last 2 CLAIM_RELEASED
# comments both carry session_count=0, the issue is repeatedly killing
# workers in setup (sandbox crash, OpenCode init failure, prompt parse
# error). Re-dispatching at the same tier produces the same failure.
# Apply needs-maintainer-review with a dispatch-infrastructure-failure
# marker so auto_approve_maintainer_issues PRESERVES NMR (see t2386).
if _consecutive_zero_session_failures "$orphan_issue_num" "$repo_slug_age" 2; then
    gh_issue_edit_safe "$orphan_issue_num" --repo "$repo_slug_age" \
        --add-label "needs-maintainer-review" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    gh_issue_comment "$orphan_issue_num" --repo "$repo_slug_age" \
        --body "$(_dispatch_infra_failure_advisory "$orphan_issue_num" "$repo_slug_age")" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    return 0
fi
```

`_consecutive_zero_session_failures` is a new helper that reads recent issue comments and counts trailing `CLAIM_RELEASED.*session_count=0` lines. `_dispatch_infra_failure_advisory` writes a worker-mentoring body per t1900: includes the last 5 worker log file paths, suggests sandbox/auth/OpenCode plugin diagnostics, and explicitly does NOT re-dispatch.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:638-640`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1681-1690` — persist + export wait_status sentinel
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:120-182, 247-288` — classifier reads sentinel, treats clean+session_count=0 as worker_noop_zero_output
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:428-460` — per-issue infra-failure escalation when N consecutive zero-session releases
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-exit-classifier-signal-kill.sh` — regression test covering all three fixes
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document the new `worker_noop_zero_output` classification path

### Reference pattern

- `_maybe_reclassify_worker_failed_as_no_work` at `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh:994-1050` — existing reclassification helper; this work makes the upstream classifier emit the same reason directly instead of relying on downstream rescue.
- `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` at `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:792-840` — pattern for the new `_consecutive_zero_session_failures` helper (same comment-scan idiom).
- `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` NMR-preservation markers at `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` — `cost-circuit-breaker:fired` and `stale-recovery-tick:escalated` are the established NMR-preservation markers; new advisory should use `dispatch-infrastructure-failure` in the same family.

### Complexity Impact

`_record_orphan_crash_classification` currently 30 lines, projected 50-60 with the new escalation branch — well below the 100-line `function-complexity` gate. New helpers `_consecutive_zero_session_failures` (~25 lines) and `_dispatch_infra_failure_advisory` (~30 lines) are net new functions, not extensions. `classify_worker_exit` grows from 65 to ~85 lines — close to the 80-line advisory but below the 100-line gate; acceptable.

### Verification

```bash
# Regression test must pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-exit-classifier-signal-kill.sh

# Static checks
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh \
    .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh \
    .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh

# Manual verification — simulate SIGTERM during worker run
# (test fixture should stub _invoke_opencode to send SIGTERM mid-call,
#  assert exit-trap line shows reason=signal_killed:15 not reason=clean)
grep "reason=signal_killed:15" /tmp/test-output.log

# Confirm the live #21707 symptom no longer reproduces:
# A signal-killed worker should now post:
#   CLAIM_RELEASED reason=signal_killed:15 exit=143 session_count=0
# instead of:
#   CLAIM_RELEASED reason=clean exit=0 session_count=0
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Worker SIGTERM'd before producing a session emits `reason=signal_killed:N` (not `clean`) in the CLAIM_RELEASED comment
- [ ] Worker that exits 0 with zero opencode sessions emits `reason=worker_noop_zero_output` (not `clean`)
- [ ] After 2 consecutive `session_count=0` CLAIM_RELEASED comments on the same issue, pulse-cleanup applies `needs-maintainer-review` with `dispatch-infrastructure-failure` marker instead of re-dispatching
- [ ] Regression test in `test-exit-classifier-signal-kill.sh` covers all three paths (signal kill, noop-zero, repeated-zero escalation)
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations on touched files
- [ ] `worker-diagnostics.md` documents the new classifications and the per-issue infra-failure escalation
- [ ] No `.watchdog_killed`/`.rate_limit_fast` sentinel paths regress — they continue to take precedence over the new wait_status sentinel

## Context & Decisions

- This bug was masked for an unknown duration because the orphan-worktree → `no_work` path produced believable-looking failure comments. Operationally, every "Worker failed: orphan worktree detected (crash_type=no_work, 0 commits)" comment for the past several months may correspond to a signal kill that the classifier missed.
- The fix preserves the existing `clean` classification for genuinely-successful runs (session_count > 0, exit 0) and the existing `signal_killed:N` path for kills caught at the wait boundary. It only changes behaviour for the silent-loss path.
- This is a dispatch-path change (`headless-runtime-helper.sh`, `headless-runtime-failure.sh`, `pulse-cleanup.sh` all in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`). Per t2920 / t2819, dispatch-path tasks now auto-dispatch with auto-elevation to opus-4-7.
- Per @marcusquinn (comment 1 on #21754): self-hosting tier override applied `model:opus-4-7` upfront — issues modifying the dispatch path are self-referential, starting at opus-4-6 wastes 1-2 cascade attempts. The `model:opus-4-7` label on this consolidated issue ensures the same elevation applies at dispatch.
- Per @alex-solovyev (comment 2 on #21754): tier escalation was being skipped (`no_work` path) for this class of failure. Fix 3 addresses this directly: consecutive `session_count=0` releases now trigger `needs-maintainer-review` with `dispatch-infrastructure-failure` marker rather than silently re-dispatching — closing the loop that caused #21707's 6-dispatch spiral.

For #21707

## Contributors

@alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

body:
## Consolidation target: #21805

**Parent issue:** #21805 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t3067: interactive-session-helper.sh release applies status:available to CLOSED issues
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,origin:worker,tier:standard,framework,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #21805. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #21805 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #21805:**

```bash
gh issue comment 21805 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 21805 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 21805 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #21805 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #21805** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Task

`interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <slug>` unconditionally applies `status:available` to the issue, regardless of whether the issue is OPEN or CLOSED. When called on a closed issue (e.g. after a manual merge that didn't go through pulse-merge.sh), the result is a CLOSED issue tagged `status:available` — a label state that means nothing for closed issues and adds noise to label queries.

## Why

Mismatched label state pollutes `gh issue list --label status:available` queries (used by triage and dashboards) and confuses scanners that expect `status:done` or `status:resolved` on closed issues. Observed today on GH#21788 after a direct `gh pr merge` instead of pulse-merge.sh — the helper applied `status:available` to a CLOSED issue.

## How

EDIT: .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh — locate the `release` subcommand handler. Before applying `status:available`, check the issue state via `gh issue view <N> --repo <slug> --json state --jq .state`. If state is `CLOSED`, either:

  (a) Apply `status:done` instead (matches the framework's closed-issue convention used by `task-complete-helper.sh`), OR
  (b) Skip the status label change entirely and only release the local claim stamp.

Reference pattern: `task-complete-helper.sh` already handles the OPEN→CLOSED label transition correctly — model on its closed-issue branch.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-helper.sh (or new test file)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `release` on an OPEN issue still applies `status:available` (existing behaviour preserved).
- [ ] `release` on a CLOSED issue does NOT apply `status:available` — instead applies `status:done` OR skips status label change.
- [ ] Regression test asserting both branches.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-helper.sh
```

title: t3072: runtime-health-audit routine: surface operational bugs the supervisor blind-spots
body:
## Task

Add a `runtime-health-audit` routine that examines the running pulse system the way an interactive operator does — and files issues for what it finds. The supervisor LLM session triages GitHub state but never inspects processes, logs, or `pulse-stats.json` trend deltas. This is a structural blind spot that has cost multiple operator-discovered bugs (#21729, #21756, #21761, #21762, #21763, #21781, #21811) over the last 24h that the supervisor itself never raised.

## Why

**Premise:** the framework relies on the supervisor LLM cycle for autonomous self-improvement. Observed reality (this session): every operational bug surfaced today came from an interactive operator running `ps`, `pgrep`, `pmset -g log`, `jq` over `pulse-stats.json`, and reading `pulse-wrapper.log` directly. The supervisor doesn't do any of those — its inputs are issue lists, PR status, label state, scanner findings.

**Concrete evidence (4h window around t3056 deploy at 22:28Z 2026-04-29):**

- `fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout`: 18 → 0 (real fix landed)
- `pulse_cycle_skipped_graphql_low`: 4 → 12 (new bottleneck)
- `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken`: 4 → 13 (3× regression)

The bottleneck shift from "workers die" to "GraphQL quota exhaustion" is invisible to the supervisor. No routine surfaces it; no scanner files an issue. An interactive `jq` query found it in 30 seconds.

## How

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/runtime-health-audit-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/runtime-audit-rules/*.sh` (one rule per detector, registry-style)
- EDIT: `TODO.md` — add `r-runtime-audit` routine entry under `## Routines`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/routines.md` — document the new routine

### Reference patterns

- **Routine structure:** model on existing `r001`/`r002` entries in `TODO.md` and `.agents/reference/routines.md`.
- **Helper structure:** model on `.agents/scripts/quality-feedback-helper.sh` — finding-emit pattern with `<!-- aidevops:generator=runtime-audit -->` marker so `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` can re-validate before dispatching workers on findings.
- **Rule registry pattern:** model on `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf` (declarative one-record-per-line) for the detector list.

### Initial detector set (Phase 1)

Each is a small bash function that returns 0 (no finding) or 1 (file an issue):

1. **counter-trend-delta** — read `pulse-stats.json`, compute 4h-vs-prior-4h ratio for each counter array; flag any 3× regression with `tier:standard`.
2. **process-count-anomaly** — `ps -ax -o command | grep -c "pulse-wrapper.sh$"` should be ≤ 2 (parent + at-most-one child); >5 = leak signal.
3. **deployed-vs-source-mtime-drift** — for hot files (`pulse-wrapper.sh`, `pulse-merge.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, etc.), compare `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/<f>` mtime to `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/<f>` git commit time; >24h drift = warning.
4. **log-pattern-novelty** — tail last 1000 lines of `pulse-wrapper.log`, group by template (strip PIDs/timestamps), flag any new template appearing >5× in the window that wasn't present in the prior 24h.
5. **idle-state-stuck** — read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.pid`; if it shows `SETUP:<pid>` and that PID is dead, file `idle-state-stale-pid` issue.

### Issue body shape

Each filed finding gets a t1900 worker-ready body: file paths, reference patterns, verification commands. Marker: `<!-- aidevops:generator=runtime-audit -->`. Pre-dispatch validator (`pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh`) MUST be extended to re-run the detector before worker spawn — many of these will resolve themselves between detection and dispatch.

### Routine cadence

- `repeat: cron(*/30 * * * *)` — every 30 min (matches qlty-scanner cadence)
- `run: scripts/runtime-health-audit-helper.sh`
- Initial rollout: dry-run mode for 48h to calibrate noise before enabling issue creation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runtime-health-audit-helper.sh --dry-run` prints findings to stdout, files no issues.
2. `runtime-health-audit-helper.sh --apply` creates auto-dispatch issues with the generator marker.
3. Pre-dispatch validator skips dispatch when the detector no longer fires (re-validation passes).
4. At least 3 of the 5 Phase 1 detectors land + ship; `counter-trend-delta` is mandatory.
5. `r-runtime-audit` registered in `TODO.md` under `## Routines` with `[ ]` (disabled) initially; flip to `[x]` after 48h dry-run.
6. Documentation entry in `reference/routines.md` covering: trigger conditions, dry-run behaviour, escalation path for novel patterns.
7. Regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-audit-detectors.sh` covering each of the 5 detectors with synthetic fixtures.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-audit-detectors.sh` — all detectors exit-code-correct against fixtures.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/runtime-health-audit-helper.sh .agents/scripts/runtime-audit-rules/*.sh` — zero violations.
- `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/reference/routines.md` — clean.
- Manual smoke: run `--dry-run` against current system; confirm at least the GraphQL-regression finding above is detected.

## Notes / Anti-patterns to avoid

- **Don't make this a giant single-script.** One rule per file in `runtime-audit-rules/`, registry-driven. Easy to add new detectors without editing the orchestrator.
- **Detector body cap:** each rule ≤ 50 lines. Larger = split into a sub-helper.
- **No GraphQL calls inside detectors** (would amplify the very problem we're trying to surface). Read local files only.
- **Ratchet, not absolute (t2228 class):** counter-trend-delta should compare to prior window, not absolute thresholds. Otherwise it false-positives every quiet period.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #21555 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #21555

**Parent issue:** #21555 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t3015: t3015: Architectural rename — split dispatch_floor + dispatch_max (Option B sweep, follows t3014)
**Parent labels:** `refactor,status:queued,priority:high,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,model:opus-4-7`

> You do **NOT** need to read #21555. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #21555 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #21555:**

```bash
gh issue comment 21555 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 21555 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 21555 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #21555 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #21555** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Status — Sequencing

**BLOCKED behind [t3014 / #21551](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21551).** Do not start until #21551 merges. This task is the follow-on architectural sweep to make the dispatch path's terminology consistent with what the original GH#14471 design intended.

## Goal

Rename and split the conflated "fill floor" mechanism into two clearly-scoped functions per the original GH#14471 intent (see [t3014 floor-vs-max clarification comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21551#issuecomment-4337394391)):

- **`dispatch_floor`** — minimum guarantee under resource constraint (throttle, rate-limit reserve, OAuth budget low). Serial or near-serial. Goal: keep backlog moving when resources are scarce.
- **`dispatch_max`** — saturate to `effective_slots = max_workers - active_workers`. Parallel = effective_slots, no artificial cap. Goal: fill all available capacity when resources are healthy.

This is a **rename + restructure**, not a behaviour change. t3014 will have already implemented the saturate-to-max behaviour; t3015 makes the naming/structure match.

## Why

After t3014 lands, the dispatch path will be doing the right thing but its naming will lie about it: `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` will be saturating to max, and `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` will either be removed or renamed unhelpfully. Future maintainers reading the code will hit the same conceptual confusion that wasted hours this week. Consistency now is cheap; consistency later (after more callers accumulate) is expensive.

This also unblocks **future evidence-based tuning** as a separate concern: once the two paths are clearly named, individual thresholds (floor minimum count, max parallelism level, throttle activation triggers) can be adjusted based on concurrency telemetry, RAM budget, GraphQL/REST rate-limit headroom, and OAuth budget. Today those tunings would have to fight the existing naming.

## How

### Files Scope (the full sweep — 33 files, 310 references)

#### Core implementation (touches behaviour — coordinate with t3014's final state)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — split `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` → `dispatch_max` (default path) + `dispatch_floor` (throttle branch, called from `dispatch_max` when throttle is engaged)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — update call sites (`apply_deterministic_fill_floor` → `apply_dispatch_max`)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — rename references in comments + dedup logic
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh` — `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` → `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` (timeout applies to both floor and max paths)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-backoff-helper.sh` — references in backoff path
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` — confirms the float→floor downgrade path
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` — call sites
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` — comments only
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh` — comments only
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` — diagnostic output strings
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh` — comments only

#### Symbol renames (28 distinct symbols, mechanical)

| Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor()` | `dispatch_max()` | Default saturate path |
| `apply_deterministic_fill_floor()` | `apply_dispatch_max()` | Wrapper called by pulse cycle |
| (new) | `dispatch_floor()` | Throttle-mode minimum, called from `dispatch_max` when throttle engaged |
| `_dff_*` family (24 helpers) | `_dispatch_*` family | Drop the misleading "ff" prefix; use `_dispatch_max_*` / `_dispatch_floor_*` based on which path the helper serves; shared helpers use `_dispatch_*` |
| `_DFF_ROUND_DISPATCHED` | `_DISPATCH_ROUND_DISPATCHED` | Module-global state |
| `_DFF_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER` | `_DISPATCH_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER` | Module-global state |
| `_DFF_THROTTLE_FILE` | `_DISPATCH_THROTTLE_FILE` | Path constant |
| `_DFF_THROTTLE_CLEARED` | `_DISPATCH_THROTTLE_CLEARED` | Module-global state |
| `_DFF_CANARY_CACHE` | `_DISPATCH_CANARY_CACHE` | Cache var |
| `FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` | `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT` | Env var; provide alias for back-compat one release |
| `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` | (removed if t3014 removed it) or `DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL` | If t3014 leaves the env var in place, rename here |

#### Stats counters (pulse-stats.json) — needs migration handling
- `fill_floor_per_candidate_timeout` → `dispatch_per_candidate_timeout`
- (new from t3014) `dispatch_floor_runs` — increment when throttle path entered
- (new from t3014) `dispatch_max_runs` — increment when saturate path entered
- Migration: keep the old key reading paths for one release for backward-compat with logs/diagnostics

#### Documentation
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/dispatch-architecture.md` — rewrite the dispatch-flow section with the floor-vs-max distinction explicit; update the call diagram
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/incident-recovery-runbook.md` — update references to fill_floor counters
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` "Worker Diagnostics" section if it mentions fill_floor (none found in current grep, but verify)
- `EDIT: CHANGELOG.md` — t3015 entry under [Unreleased]

#### Tests (rename + verify behaviour preserved)
- `RENAME: .agents/scripts/tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh` → `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh` — update symbol references
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-consolidation-phase2.sh` — update symbol references
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-bash32-nul-crash.sh` — update symbol references (likely comments only)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-diagnose-cycle-health.sh` — update fixture timing log entries that say `fill_floor_candidate_*` to match new stage name `dispatch_max_candidate_*`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-runner-health.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` — update fixtures
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh` — update fixtures
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-floor-throttle-engages.sh` — verify floor path activates under throttle and dispatches at minimum count

#### Config
- `EDIT: .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc` — rename keys; document floor + max separately
- `EDIT: .github/workflows/apply-status-available-default.yml` — references to fill_floor concept

#### Historical artifacts (DO NOT EDIT — they document past work)
- `TODO.md` line 924 — t3005 entry references `_dispatch_fill_floor` in past tense; leave as historical record
- `todo/tasks/GH-18830-brief.md`, `todo/tasks/t1996-brief.md`, `todo/tasks/t2157-brief.md`, `todo/tasks/t2392-brief.md` — historical briefs, leave unchanged

### Reference Pattern

When splitting `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` into `dispatch_max` + `dispatch_floor`:

```bash
# After this PR:
dispatch_max() {
    if _dispatch_should_use_floor_path; then
        dispatch_floor "$@"     # throttle/rate-limit/oauth-low → minimum guarantee
        return $?
    fi
    # Default: saturate to effective_slots, parallelism = effective_slots
    _dispatch_max_loop "$@"
}

dispatch_floor() {
    # Resource-constrained guarantee: dispatch at most floor_count candidates,
    # serial or low-parallelism, prioritizing the simplest/cheapest issues
    _dispatch_floor_loop "$@"
}

_dispatch_should_use_floor_path() {
    # True when:
    # - throttle file present (.aidevops/cache/dispatch-throttle)
    # - GraphQL budget < threshold
    # - OAuth budget < threshold
    # - rate-limit reserve flag present
    [[ -f "$_DISPATCH_THROTTLE_FILE" ]] && return 0
    # ... other constraint checks
    return 1
}
```

The constraint checks should be cheap (file existence, env var, single arithmetic comparison). The actual throttle-engagement decisions remain in their existing helpers — `_dispatch_should_use_floor_path` is just the boolean dispatcher.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Symbol search confirms no leftover fill_floor / _dff_ / DFF references in active code
git grep -nE "(fill_floor|_dff_|_DFF_|DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR|FILL_FLOOR_PER)" -- '.agents/scripts/' '.agents/reference/' '.agents/AGENTS.md' '.agents/configs/' '.github/workflows/'

# 2. All tests pass

.agents/scripts/run-tests.sh tests/test-pulse-diagnose-cycle-health.sh

# 3. ShellCheck zero new violations
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh

# 4. Live behavior preserved
# After deploy: pulse cycles should dispatch identically to t3014's behavior
# pulse-stats.json should show dispatch_max_runs and (rarely) dispatch_floor_runs
# stage timings log entries should now say "dispatch_max_candidate_*" not "fill_floor_candidate_*"

# 5. Back-compat env var alias works
FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT=120 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh --dry-run
# expected: warning logged ("FILL_FLOOR_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT is deprecated, use DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT"), value honored
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dispatch_max` and `dispatch_floor` functions exist and are documented in their function-header comments
- [ ] Throttle path activates `dispatch_floor`; default path uses `dispatch_max`
- [ ] All 28 symbols renamed per table; module-globals follow new naming
- [ ] `pulse-stats.json` counters renamed; old keys still readable for 1 release
- [ ] Stage timings log entries use `dispatch_max_candidate_*` / `dispatch_floor_candidate_*`
- [ ] `dispatch-architecture.md` rewritten with floor-vs-max diagram
- [ ] All tests rename + pass
- [ ] No leftover `fill_floor` / `_dff_` / `_DFF_` / `FILL_FLOOR_*` references in active code (historical TODO/brief files allowed)
- [ ] No behaviour regression — pulse dispatches identically to post-t3014 behaviour
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md t3015 entry under [Unreleased]
- [ ] Released as v3.13.8 (or higher), propagating to alex-solovyev runner

## Complexity Impact

This is a **rename + restructure**, not new logic. The `dispatch_max` body is what `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` already is post-t3014. The `dispatch_floor` body is the existing throttle branch extracted. Net function-line change: small. Module size unchanged.

Risk: PR will touch 33 files with ~310 line changes. Use a single PR (the renames are mechanically coupled — partial PR leaves the codebase in a half-renamed state). ShellCheck regression risk is the main exposure.

## Sequencing With Other Work

- **Blocks until:** [t3014 / #21551](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21551) merges
- **Followed by (separate concern):** evidence-based threshold tuning — once telemetry from `dispatch_floor_runs` and `dispatch_max_runs` accumulates, tune floor minimum count, max parallelism level, throttle activation thresholds, OAuth budget threshold. File when there's at least 1 week of post-t3015 telemetry to inform the tuning. Likely tasks: t30XX (floor minimum tuning), t30XX (throttle threshold tuning), t30XX (OAuth-budget-aware downgrade).

## Test Plan (full-loop session)

1. Verify t3014 has merged and v3.13.7 (or later) is deployed
2. Run the full grep inventory above — confirm scope hasn't drifted
3. Apply renames in dependency order: implementation → call sites → tests → docs → config
4. Run shellcheck on every modified shell file before next edit (write-time enforcement)

title: t3074: fix duplicate Code Audit Routines dashboard issues — fail-closed dedup + title-prefix fallback + self-healing sweep
body:
## Task

Fix the recurring duplicate-creation bug in the daily quality sweep dashboard. Four "Code Audit Routines" issues currently exist (#2632, #20409, #20845, #21670) — one new duplicate created roughly every 3-4 days from a peer runner (`alex-solovyev`). The dedup is fail-open and the cache is per-machine.

## Why

Each duplicate steals attention, breaks the "single rolling dashboard" invariant the `persistent` label promises, and pollutes pulse search results. Prior class-fix #10308 addressed dashboard-vs-supervisor parallel creation; THIS bug is dashboard-vs-dashboard from cross-runner machines.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh:51-130` — `_ensure_quality_issue()`. Three changes:
  1. **Fail-closed label search** (line 79-84): capture `gh issue list` exit code. If `gh` exits nonzero (rate limit, network blip, auth flake), abort the sweep entirely with a logged error — do NOT proceed to create. Currently `2>/dev/null || echo ""` swallows the error and proceeds to create, which is the documented failure path.
  2. **Title-prefix fallback** (after line 84, before line 87): if label search returns empty AND exit code is 0, run a secondary search by title prefix `in:title "Code Audit Routines" is:open is:issue` against the same repo. Labels can be stripped by reconcilers; the title prefix is invariant. Only proceed to create if BOTH the label search and the title-prefix search confirm zero matches.
  3. **Post-create defensive dedup sweep** (after line 124, before the `# Cache` block): after a successful create, run the same label+title search for siblings; close all but the newest (the one we just created), with a closing comment `> Auto-closed: superseded by #NEW as duplicate quality dashboard.`. This is the self-healing path that reclaims any duplicates created during prior failures.

- **EDIT:** same file `_ensure_quality_issue()` cache-validation block (line 69-76): if `gh issue view` errors transiently, do NOT invalidate the cache — only invalidate when the API returns a definitive non-OPEN state. Currently any transient failure invalidates the cache and forces the script through the search path, where the label-search bug then fires.

- **NEW (one-time):** runs as part of the same PR — close 3 of the 4 existing dupes via `gh issue close`. Keep #21670 (most recent, latest stats). Close #2632, #20409, #20845 with a closing comment linking #21670. Implementation: a single shell block at the top of the PR description executable by the maintainer, OR (better) a `.agents/scripts/cleanup-quality-dashboard-dupes.sh` one-shot.

### Reference pattern

Model the fail-closed pattern on `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::is-assigned` — that helper exits 1 on any `gh` error rather than fall through to "no claim". Same principle: dedup queries are safety-critical; fail-open creates duplicates.

For the post-create defensive sweep, model on `pulse-merge.sh::_close_superseded_prs` (closes older PRs with comment when a newer one wins).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-quality-dashboard-dupes.sh` (NEW, optional one-shot)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh` (NEW, regression coverage)

### Complexity Impact

`_ensure_quality_issue()` is currently 80 lines. The three changes add ~40 lines (exit-code capture, title-prefix fallback, post-create sweep). Projected post-change: ~120 lines, exceeding the 100-line `function-complexity` gate. **Pre-planned refactor required:** extract three helpers — `_quality_issue_label_search()`, `_quality_issue_title_search()`, `_quality_issue_close_duplicates()` — keeping the orchestrator `_ensure_quality_issue` under 60 lines. See `reference/large-file-split.md §0` for the canonical extract pattern.

## Acceptance

1. `_ensure_quality_issue()` aborts (returns 1) if `gh issue list` fails for any reason; pulse-wrapper.log records the abort. No new issue is ever created on transient API failure.
2. Title-prefix fallback search runs after label search returns empty; only when BOTH return zero matches does the create path execute.
3. Post-create defensive sweep: after creating a new dashboard, all sibling open issues matching `title:"Code Audit Routines"` get closed with a `superseded by #NEW` comment.
4. One-time cleanup: #2632, #20409, #20845 all closed with comment linking to #21670.
5. Regression test `test-stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh` covers: (a) label-search-fails-do-not-create, (b) title-prefix-fallback-finds-existing, (c) post-create-sweep-closes-siblings.
6. Function-complexity gate passes (`_ensure_quality_issue` ≤ 100 lines, no nesting-depth regression).

### Verification

```bash
# Lint
shellcheck .agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh

# Test
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh

# Confirm dupes closed
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops \
  --label quality-review --label persistent --state open \
  --json number --jq 'length'
# Expected: 1
```

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-30 — user reported workers creating duplicate "Code Audit Routines" issues, asked for root cause + systemic fix.

## Notes

- Prior fix #10308 (closed Mar 2026) was a DIFFERENT bug class — dashboard issue racing with supervisor-created actionable issues. This bug is dashboard-vs-dashboard across runners.
- The `alex-solovyev` runner is a peer pulse runner per `~/.config/aidevops/dispatch-override.conf`. Per-machine cache (`~/.aidevops/logs/quality-issue-marcusquinn-aidevops`) means cross-runner dedup relies entirely on the GitHub-side label search, which is the path that fails open.
- Issue #21670 is the most recent dashboard and should be the survivor.

body:
## What

Tighten `claim-task-id.sh` issue dedup so it catches the case where multiple worker sessions hit the same unfixed bug and each files a fresh issue under a different `tNNN` task ID.

## Why

Observed canonical chain: aidevops#21737 → #21760 → #21770 → #21747 — four issues filed for the **same** `claim-task-id.sh` stderr-capture bug, each with a different `tNNN` prefix. PR #21771 merged the fix at 23:08 on 2026-04-29, but #21747 (filed 17:18 same day) was still dispatching workers afterward, all 4 of which crashed `no_work` and triggered NMR escalation. Workers wasted dispatch cycles on a bug already fixed. The repeat-filing pattern is the framework debt.

Two orthogonal dedup paths exist but neither catches cross-`tNNN` duplicates:

1. `_check_duplicate_issue` (`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh:348`) extracts the `tNNN:` prefix from the title and queries `gh issue list --search "${task_id_prefix}: in:title"`. Each new task gets a fresh `tNNN`, so the search never matches. Dedup is "I'm not filing my own duplicate", not "this bug isn't already filed by someone else".

2. `_pre_claim_discovery_pass` (`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:1142`) searches **PRs** via `_pc_search_related_prs`. It does not search OPEN ISSUES. When the bug is filed but no PR is in flight yet, no match returns.

The combination means: worker A files issue #N1, worker B's session hits the same bug 30 min later, claims a fresh `tNNN`, runs both dedup paths (issue dedup misses on `tNNN` prefix mismatch, PR dedup misses because no PR exists), files #N2.

## How

Add a third dedup path: a body-and-file-keyword search across **open issues** with a sliding-window age cap.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:1138-1161` (`_pre_claim_discovery_pass` orchestrator)

- After `_pc_search_related_prs` and before returning, also run a parallel `_pc_search_related_issues` over `gh issue list --search "$keywords in:body in:title" --state open` with `--limit 10`.
- Filter results by recency (`AIDEVOPS_CLAIM_DEDUP_DAYS` already exists, default 14 days).
- If issues match, treat them like PR hits: feed them into `_pc_prompt_or_warn` so the human sees the conflict and can decline filing.
- Headless mode (current behaviour): warn-only is acceptable; do not block. The signal in worker logs lets the next pulse cycle catch it via the issue-sync path.

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:1044-1062` (add sibling `_pc_search_related_issues` next to `_pc_search_related_prs`)

- Same shape as `_pc_search_related_prs`: `gh issue list --repo "$repo_slug" --state open --search "..." --json number,title,body,createdAt --limit 20`.
- Reuses `_pc_filter_relevant_prs` keyword scoring (rename to `_pc_filter_relevant_items` if needed for clarity, both PRs and issues have the same JSON shape).

NEW: test case in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id.sh`

- Mock `gh issue list` to return a fixture with one open issue whose body mentions `claim-task-id.sh` and `phantom number`.
- Run the discovery pass with title containing the same keywords.
- Assert that the existing issue surfaces in the warn output.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id.sh`

### Complexity Impact

`_pre_claim_discovery_pass` is currently 20 lines. Adding the issue-search branch will add ~15 lines (one more search call, one more filter+prompt invocation). Projected post-change ~35 lines — well under the 100-line `function-complexity` gate, no warning needed.

## Acceptance

- `_pre_claim_discovery_pass` searches both open issues AND PRs (was: PRs only).
- When an open issue matches the keyword fingerprint within `AIDEVOPS_CLAIM_DEDUP_DAYS`, it appears in the `_pc_prompt_or_warn` output exactly like a PR hit does today.
- Reproduction: file two issues back-to-back with substantially-overlapping titles on the same file, claiming separate `tNNN` IDs. Second filing emits a warn referencing the first issue.
- ShellCheck clean on all three edited files.
- Existing tests in `test-claim-task-id.sh` continue to pass; new test case for issue dedup passes.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id.sh
```

## Tier Checklist

- [ ] tier:simple — NO (touches 3 files, requires new test case, extends a function with new branch logic)
- [x] tier:standard — YES (1-2h, narrative brief is enough, uses existing patterns)
- [ ] tier:thinking

## Discovery context

Filed during interactive triage of aidevops#21747 (closed as duplicate of #21770). Memory lesson stored: `mem_20260430012933_4a36a676`.

**Parent issue:** #21762 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #21762 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #21762:**

```bash
gh issue comment 21762 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 21762 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 21762 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #21762 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #21762** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

A worker dispatched by the pulse can disappear without leaving a `[lifecycle] worker_exited pid=NNN wait_status=N` entry in `pulse.log`, breaking post-mortem debugging. Specifically observed today: PID 88900 was launched on aidevops [#21729](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21729), then vanished — no exit line, no `/tmp/worker-issue-21729*.log` file, no kill signal in pulse.log.

## Symptom evidence

```
$ grep "88900" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -vE "^\{|tool_use"
[dispatch_worker_launch] Issue #21729: worker PID=88900 PGID=66689 (setsid detached from pulse PGID=66689; FDs 3-9 closed for t2814)
[dispatch_with_dedup] Dispatched worker PID 88900 for #21729 in marcusquinn/aidevops

$ ps -p 88900
(no such process)

$ ls /tmp/worker-issue-21729* 2>&1
zsh: no matches found

$ grep "88900" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -E "exit|killed|wait_status"
(no matches)
```

For comparison, healthy workers DO emit lifecycle exit lines:

```
[INFO] [lifecycle] worker_exited pid=88845 wait_status=0
```

## Why

- Stuck-worker detection relies on the lifecycle exit log to distinguish "worker still running" from "worker died silently".
- Watchdog and stalled-worker reaper paths in `pulse-cleanup.sh` use this signal indirectly.
- Without an exit line, post-mortem questions like "did the worker actually do anything?" or "what was the exit code?" are unanswerable from logs alone.
- Forensic incidents (like #21729's runaway-log diagnosis) become harder when worker death is invisible to the log.

## Hypothesis

`worker-lifecycle-common.sh` or the `setsid`-detached child shell in `dispatch_worker_launch` only emits the `worker_exited` line on certain code paths. Possible gaps:

- The `setsid`-detached worker exits before its `wait` parent has set up the lifecycle trap.
- The detach pattern (`setsid` + FDs 3-9 closed for t2814) may sever the parent-child reaping relationship that the lifecycle helper relies on.
- A `trap EXIT` is registered in the parent but the detached child is not in the parent's process group anymore (FBO `setsid`).
- The `[INFO]` prefix in `lifecycle worker_exited` suggests it's emitted by `log_info` from the *worker's own shell*, but if the worker's `exec` chain doesn't preserve the trap, no exit line is emitted on abnormal termination.

## How

### Files to investigate

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — primary suspect; this is where `worker_exited` should be emitted. Verify the emit path covers all exit modes (normal, SIGTERM, SIGKILL, exec failure, immediate exit).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — `dispatch_worker_launch` is the launcher; verify it registers a parent-side `wait` and lifecycle log on the worker PID, independent of the worker's own emit.
- `EDIT?: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — main loop that processes worker completions; verify a parent-side `worker_exited` is logged when the cycle reaps the PID, even if the worker itself didn't emit one.

### Reference pattern

- The current `[INFO] [lifecycle] worker_exited pid=88845 wait_status=0` line shows the *expected* shape. Make sure every dispatch path emits this, ideally from the parent (pulse) side via `wait` + `log_info`, not relying on the detached child to emit on its own.
- For setsid-detach behaviour, see `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` `--detach` mode — it uses `nohup` + `&` and writes to `/tmp/worker-${session_key}.log`. Consider whether the pulse's `setsid` path should follow the same `/tmp/worker-issue-<NNN>.log` discipline so worker stdout/stderr is recoverable.

### Acceptance

- Every worker PID dispatched by `dispatch_worker_launch` has a corresponding `worker_exited pid=N wait_status=M` line in pulse.log within 60s of the worker terminating.
- Failure modes (worker exec failure, SIGKILL by OOM, exit 143 from watchdog, normal exit 0) all produce the lifecycle line; only the `wait_status` differs.
- Regression test: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-lifecycle-exit-emit.sh` dispatches a synthetic worker that immediately `exit 7` and asserts the matching `worker_exited pid=*N* wait_status=7` line lands in the test log.

## Verification

```bash
# Empirical baseline (pre-fix): count dispatches without matching exits over last 24h
DISPATCHED=$(grep -cE "Dispatched worker PID [0-9]+" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log)
EXITED=$(grep -cE "worker_exited pid=[0-9]+" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log)
echo "dispatched=$DISPATCHED exited=$EXITED gap=$((DISPATCHED - EXITED))"
# Goal: gap should be near zero (delta = currently-running workers only)
```

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-lifecycle-exit-emit.sh` (NEW)

### Complexity Impact

`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::dispatch_worker_launch` is in the canonical self-hosting set (`.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`). Any new emit path or wait-trap inside this function should not exceed the 80-line warning threshold; if a clean implementation requires growth past 80 lines, factor the new emit path into a small helper in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`.

## Session Origin

Observed while diagnosing PID 88900's fate after the [#21729](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21729) wait-loop runaway recovery on 2026-04-29 ~18:37Z. The dispatch was successful (rc=0, 146s ceremony, claim comment posted), but the worker vanished without an exit signal — making it impossible to determine whether it completed work, hit auth failure, OOMed, or was killed by the runaway log eating disk.

title: consolidated: t3067: interactive-session-helper.sh release must not apply status:available to CLOSED issues
body:
_Supersedes #21805 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix `interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <slug>` to check issue state before applying `status:available`. When the target issue is CLOSED, the release subcommand must either apply `status:done` (matching the framework's closed-issue convention) or skip the status label change entirely — never apply `status:available` to a closed issue.

## Why

`release` unconditionally applies `status:available` regardless of whether the issue is OPEN or CLOSED. When called on a closed issue (e.g., after a manual `gh pr merge` that bypassed `pulse-merge.sh`), the result is a CLOSED issue tagged `status:available` — a label state that is meaningless for closed issues and injects noise into:

- `gh issue list --label status:available` queries (used by triage and dashboards)
- Scanners that expect `status:done` or `status:resolved` on closed issues

**Observed incident:** GH#21788 — after a direct `gh pr merge` instead of `pulse-merge.sh`, `release` applied `status:available` to a CLOSED issue.

## How

**EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` — locate the `release` subcommand handler.

Before applying `status:available`, insert a check:

```bash
local issue_state
issue_state=$(gh issue view "$issue_num" --repo "$slug" --json state --jq '.state' 2>/dev/null || echo "OPEN")

if [[ "$issue_state" == "CLOSED" ]]; then
  # Apply status:done (framework convention for closed issues) instead of status:available
  set_issue_status "$issue_num" "$slug" "done"
  # OR: skip status label change entirely (option b)
  return 0
fi
# existing: set status:available for OPEN issues
set_issue_status "$issue_num" "$slug" "available"
```

**Reference pattern:** `task-complete-helper.sh` already handles the OPEN→CLOSED label transition correctly — model on its closed-issue branch for the `status:done` convention.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-helper.sh` (existing or new test file)

### Complexity Impact

Minimal — adding a 3-line guard before one `set_issue_status` call. No function restructuring required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `release` on an OPEN issue still applies `status:available` (existing behaviour preserved)
- [ ] `release` on a CLOSED issue does NOT apply `status:available` — instead applies `status:done` OR skips status label change
- [ ] Regression test asserting both branches (OPEN → `status:available`, CLOSED → `status:done` or no label change)
- [ ] ShellCheck clean: `shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-helper.sh
```

## Context & Decisions

- **Tier assignment (per @marcusquinn, automated):** Issue was initially filed as `tier:simple` but auto-downgraded to `tier:standard` pre-dispatch because the Files Scope contains >2 file references — the `tier:simple` hard disqualifier. Worker dispatches at `tier:standard`.
- **Dispatch history (per @alex-solovyev, automated):** One prior dispatch attempt classified as `no_work` (stale_timeout during worker setup, not an engagement failure). Tier escalation was correctly skipped — a more expensive model cannot fix an infrastructure boot issue. Task stays at `tier:standard` for retry.
- **Implementation choice:** Option (a) `status:done` is preferred over option (b) skip — it produces a clean, consistent label state on closed issues and aligns with the `task-complete-helper.sh` convention already used by the framework.

## Contributors

/cc @marcusquinn @alex-solovyev

title: t3076: pulse: circuit breaker auto-files root-cause meta-issue and dispatches systemic-fix worker
body:
## What

Extend the existing per-issue circuit breakers (t2007 cost, t2769 no_work) so that when they trip, they **also** auto-file a root-cause meta-issue with failure forensics and dispatch a `tier:thinking` worker against it. Original issue gets `blocked-by:#<meta>` and clears automatically when the meta-issue's PR merges.

## Why

Existing breakers (`worker-lifecycle-common.sh:855-905` for t2769, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:716,934,1453` for t2007) halt dispatch and apply `needs-maintainer-review` after N failures. NMR is a maintainer-queue dead-end — it surfaces the problem but doesn't move it forward. The user pays attention cost; the system stays stuck.

This task converts the trip into a self-healing cycle: breaker fires → forensics gathered → meta-issue filed with hypothesis → worker dispatched on meta-issue → fix lands → original unblocks automatically.

Canonical incidents motivating this:

- #21707: 6+ failed dispatches all `reason=clean session_count=0`, NMR'd, maintainer took over interactively (PR #21741). Six wasted opus dispatches before human intervention.
- #21782, #21793 (Apr 30 2026): system eventually solved them via PRs #21837/#21838/#21839, but only after multiple silent-death attempts AND filed duplicate PRs (#21793 has two competing PRs because dispatch dedup didn't see the first). A working systemic loop would have caught these after 2-3 failed attempts and filed a meta-issue diagnosing the dispatch-dedup gap.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh:855-905` — in the t2769 NMR-application block, after applying NMR, call new `_file_circuit_breaker_meta_issue $issue $repo $reason $failure_count`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:716,934,1453` — in the t2007 cost circuit-breaker trip block, same call.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` — composes meta-issue body and files via `gh_create_issue`. Body must include:
  - Original issue link + breaker type (cost/no_work)
  - Failure forensics: dispatch count, PIDs, exit codes, last 50 pulse.log lines mentioning the issue
  - `dispatch-stages.tsv` slice for the original
  - Hypothesis section: "workers terminate at stage Y with classification Z"
  - File hint: known-related issues (#21818 classifier, #21762 lifecycle log gap)
  - Labels: `auto-dispatch tier:thinking model:opus-4-7 bug pulse framework circuit-breaker-meta`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` (NMR comment composition) — add `Blocked-by: #<meta>` line + link to the meta-issue.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (or `pulse-merge-feedback.sh`) — when a meta-issue's PR merges, find the original (parsed from meta-issue body), remove `blocked-by:#<meta>` label, remove `needs-maintainer-review` only if no other NMR markers remain.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` — synthetic NMR trip, assert meta-issue created with expected sections, assert original gets `blocked-by` label, simulate meta-PR merge, assert original unblocks.

### Reference pattern

- Existing t2769 NMR-application path in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh:864-905` for the trip→label→comment flow.
- `pulse-nmr-approval.sh::_nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip` for the marker-recognition pattern (extend with `circuit-breaker-meta-filed`).
- Consolidation parent/child linkage in `pulse-triage.sh` for the blocked-by lifecycle.

### Acceptance

1. After 3 consecutive `no_work` failures (or t2007 cost breaker trip), a meta-issue is filed within 60s.
2. Meta-issue body contains: failure forensics, hypothesis, file hint, link to original.
3. Original issue gets `blocked-by:#<meta>` + existing NMR comment updated with meta-link.
4. Meta-issue dispatches normally on next pulse cycle (`auto-dispatch tier:thinking`).
5. When meta-PR merges, original's `blocked-by` clears; if no other NMR markers, NMR also clears.
6. Idempotent — second trip on same original does NOT file a duplicate meta-issue.
7. Test `test-circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` passes.

### Configuration

- `AIDEVOPS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_META_FILE_DISABLE=1` — bypass for emergencies.
- `AIDEVOPS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_META_LABELS` — override labels applied to meta-issue.

### Verification

```bash
# Smoke test: synthetic trip
AIDEVOPS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TEST_MODE=1 ./test-circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh
# Expect: meta-issue created, original blocked, simulated merge clears it
```

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` (NEW)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh`

- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` similar ~30-line addition at three call sites.

title: t3077: pulse: LLM-driven periodic pass detects fix-the-fixer tasks and adds extra observability
body:
## What

Add a periodic LLM-driven pulse pass that scans pending dispatches, classifies each as fix-the-fixer (touches dispatch system itself) or normal, and adds extra observability flags to fix-the-fixer tasks before workers spawn. Closes the cyclical-trap window where workers fixing the dispatch system are killed by the very bug they're fixing, with no visible failure mode.

## Why

The deterministic t2819 self-hosting detector auto-elevates dispatch-path issues to opus and adds advisory comments by pattern-matching paths in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`. But determinism cannot catch:

- Tasks that touch dispatch indirectly via shared lib changes (e.g. `shared-constants.sh` updates that cascade into the dispatch path).
- Tasks where the brief implies dispatch-system risk without naming files (e.g. "fix the worker exit semantics" with no `Files Scope` block).
- Combination tasks where one part is dispatch-system and another is unrelated.

Canonical: #21818 fixes the worker exit classifier. If the worker dispatched to fix it gets SIGTERM'd at 600s before producing output, classification is wrong (the very thing being fixed), failure is invisible to the existing logs, and re-dispatch loops indefinitely. The maintainer eventually has to take over interactively (precedent: #21707 → PR #21741, six wasted opus dispatches first).

A periodic LLM pulse pass closes this gap. The framework's deterministic pulse runs every cycle; an LLM-driven pass on a slower cadence (default 1h) is cheap enough to add. A thinking-tier model reads pending dispatches' briefs + linked issues + recent failure history, applies `fix-the-fixer` label where appropriate, and the dispatch path picks it up to enable extra observability flags + tighter watchdog timeouts.

This is the LLM-driven layer that catches what deterministic rules miss — same principle as the existing t2402 LLM judgement pattern in pulse triage.

## How

### Files to modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh` — invoked by the LLM pulse cycle (or as a standalone routine). For each pending `auto-dispatch` issue:
  - Read brief + linked issue body + recent dispatch-stages history (last 24h)
  - Call `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --tier haiku --prompt "..."` with binary classification prompt
  - Apply `fix-the-fixer` label + post advisory comment if positive
  - Idempotent — skip issues that already carry the label
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (or new routine entry) — register the periodic pass; default 3600s interval, gated by sentinel staleness check (mirroring t2992 cache priming pattern).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — when `fix-the-fixer` label present, set env vars before spawning worker:
  - `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE=1`
  - `WORKER_STALL_TIMEOUT=180` (vs 300s default)
  - `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PREFLIGHT_SENTINEL=1`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — honour `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PREFLIGHT_SENTINEL`: write to `~/.aidevops/cache/worker-preflight-<pid>.txt` before launching opencode; abort dispatch with clear error if write fails. Catches sandbox/FD issues before model invocation.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — when `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE=1`, emit additional checkpoints:
  - `worker_started`
  - `opencode_session_created`
  - `first_tool_use`
  - `first_commit_attempted`
  - `first_push_attempted`
  - Each line includes timestamp + PID + session_key.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh` — synthetic dispatch with the label, assert all 5 checkpoints emitted in pulse.log within 30s.

### Reference pattern

- `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` for the pattern of "periodic helper invoked by pulse-wrapper main loop with sentinel staleness gate".
- `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` (t2389) for the pattern of "scan pending dispatches → classify → annotate before dispatch".
- Workflow drift detector (t2778, `aidevops check-workflows`) for the shape of an LLM-friendly classification helper that returns a verdict per item.
- t2402 pulse triage LLM judgement integration for the prompt + parsing pattern.

### Acceptance

1. Periodic pass runs on default 1h interval (configurable via env).
2. For each pending `auto-dispatch` issue without `fix-the-fixer` label, classifier produces yes/no + 1-line rationale.
3. Issues classified yes get `fix-the-fixer` label applied with advisory comment naming the rationale.
4. Workers dispatched on `fix-the-fixer` tasks emit ≥5 verbose lifecycle checkpoints visible in pulse.log.
5. Workers fail fast (within 10s) if preflight sentinel write fails — visible in pulse.log with clear error message.
6. Empirical: at least one previously-silent failure mode becomes visible in pulse.log on a fix-the-fixer task.
7. Detector dry-run on 10 historical issues: ≥80% precision, ≥70% recall against ground-truth (which actually touched dispatch system, judged manually).
8. Test `test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh` passes.

### Configuration

- `AIDEVOPS_LLM_PULSE_FIX_THE_FIXER_INTERVAL` (default 3600).
- `AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_DETECTOR_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-4-5` — cheap; classifier is simple binary).
- `AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_DETECTOR_DISABLE=1`.
- `AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE_TIMEOUT` (default 180 — stall timeout for fix-the-fixer workers).

### Verification

```bash

AIDEVOPS_FIX_THE_FIXER_DETECTOR_DRY_RUN=1 \
  ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --limit 10
# Expect: per-issue verdict + rationale on stdout, no labels applied

# Smoke test: synthetic worker
./tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh
# Expect: 5 lifecycle checkpoints visible in test log within 30s
```

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh` (NEW)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`

title: route pulse-watchdog informational writes away from monitored LOGFILE (t3058-class fix)
body:
## Task

Route pulse-watchdog informational writes away from the monitored `$LOGFILE` to prevent false-progress signals in the stall detector.

## Why

t3071 audit (GH#21811) found two instances of the t3058-class "monitor X, write marker to X" anti-pattern in `pulse-watchdog.sh`. Both are informational echo statements that write to `$LOGFILE` — the same file `_watchdog_check_progress` monitors via byte-delta for stall detection. Each write creates one 60s poll of false progress, delaying stall detection by one poll interval per stall cycle.

Severity: minor (not self-sustaining, but the same class of silent correctness bug as the t3058 canonical fix in PR GH#21797).

## How

### Fix pattern (from t3058 PR GH#21797)

Route informational writes to a separate log file that the byte-delta monitor does not consult.

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:378` — change `>>"$LOGFILE"` to `>>"${PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG:-${LOGFILE}.watchdog}"` (or a `LIFECYCLE_LOG` equivalent for the pulse context)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:426` — same redirect

### Specific changes

**Line 378** (`_watchdog_check_progress`):
```bash
# Before (anti-pattern):
echo "[pulse-wrapper] Progress resumed after ${WD_PROGRESS_STALL_SECONDS}s stall (log grew by $((current_log_size - WD_LAST_LOG_SIZE)) bytes)" >>"$LOGFILE"

# After (fix):
echo "[pulse-wrapper] Progress resumed after ${WD_PROGRESS_STALL_SECONDS}s stall (log grew by $((current_log_size - WD_LAST_LOG_SIZE)) bytes)" >>"${PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG}" 2>/dev/null || true
```

**Line 426** (`_watchdog_check_idle`):
```bash
# Before (anti-pattern):
echo "[pulse-wrapper] Pulse active again (CPU ${tree_cpu}%) after ${WD_IDLE_SECONDS}s idle — resetting idle counter" >>"$LOGFILE"

# After (fix):
echo "[pulse-wrapper] Pulse active again (CPU ${tree_cpu}%) after ${WD_IDLE_SECONDS}s idle — resetting idle counter" >>"${PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG}" 2>/dev/null || true
```

**Add `PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG` initialization** near the top of the file (alongside `LOGFILE`):
```bash
PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG="${PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG:-${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/pulse-watchdog.log}"
```

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh
# Verify no writes to $LOGFILE remain in _watchdog_check_progress or _watchdog_check_idle:
rg '>>".*LOGFILE' .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh | grep -E '(check_progress|check_idle)' && echo "FAIL: self-write remains" || echo "PASS"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Lines 378 and 426 in `pulse-watchdog.sh` write to `$PULSE_WATCHDOG_LOG`, not `$LOGFILE`
- [ ] `shellcheck` passes clean on `pulse-watchdog.sh`
- [ ] No other writes to `$LOGFILE` exist inside `_watchdog_check_progress` or `_watchdog_check_idle`

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`

## Complexity Impact

Two single-line redirects changed. No function growth. No complexity bump needed.

## Reference

- t3058 / PR GH#21797 — canonical fix in `worker-activity-watchdog.sh:570-583`
- t3071 / GH#21811 — parent audit that discovered these instances
- `_watchdog_check_progress` (pulse-watchdog.sh:364) — progress stall monitor
- `_watchdog_check_idle` (pulse-watchdog.sh:412) — CPU idle monitor

title: t3082: fix: bash 3.2 heredoc parser fails on apostrophe in counter-trend-delta runtime audit rule
body:
## Task

The runtime-audit detector at `.agents/scripts/runtime-audit-rules/counter-trend-delta.sh:96` contains the literal `supervisor's` (ASCII apostrophe U+0027) inside an unquoted heredoc body. Bash 3.2 (macOS default at `/bin/bash`) tracks single-quote state across unquoted heredoc bodies — total of 3 single quotes in the body of `<<MARKDOWN ... MARKDOWN` causes "unexpected EOF while looking for matching `'`" at parse time.

The result: the file fails `bash -n` syntax validation on macOS, blocking the `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` CI job for every PR merged into main since #21824 (commit `e96814335`, t3072 parent landing). Currently blocking PR #21825 from merging green.

## Why

Bash 3.2 vs 4+ heredoc parser difference. Bash 4+ doesn't track quote state inside unquoted heredocs the same way; bash 3.2 does. The framework's bash 3.2 compatibility rule (see `reference/bash-compat.md`) catches this on the macos-latest runner — but it's not a required check, so the broken commit was able to land. This is a regression that was masked by a missing required-check on macos-latest shellcheck.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runtime-audit-rules/counter-trend-delta.sh:96` — replace ASCII apostrophe `'` with Unicode right single quotation mark `'` (U+2019, UTF-8 `e2 80 99`). Bash does not treat U+2019 as a quote character; the heredoc parses cleanly. Grammar preserved.

Reference pattern: this is the canonical "apostrophe in unquoted heredoc" fix; see `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` "Heredoc apostrophe portability" section if it exists, or document the workaround there as a follow-up.

Verification: `/bin/bash -n .agents/scripts/runtime-audit-rules/counter-trend-delta.sh` must exit 0 with no output. Also run `shellcheck` to confirm no shellcheck regression.

### Files Scope
