title: t3197: Per-issue launch-failure cooldown: prevent same-issue tight retry loops after no_worker_process
body:
## Task

After `recover_failed_launch_state` releases an issue with `failure_reason=no_worker_process`, write a `<!-- dispatch-cooldown-until:<ISO> -->` audit comment (default 30 min from now) on the issue. Wire `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::is-assigned` to short-circuit with `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE` while a recent cooldown comment is unexpired.

## Why

Currently after `recover_failed_launch_state` runs `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released`, the issue is set to `status:available` and is **immediately** eligible for re-claim on the next pulse cycle. Same broken runner picks it back up within 30-90 minutes (whatever its tick rate is), produces another `no_worker_process` failure, releases, repeats. Sample evidence: a managed private repo issue #NNN — 5 retries from `runner=alex-solovyev` over 3.5 hours, every retry ~95-99s lifespan. The pattern repeats across 31+ issues simultaneously when the runner is broken.

A 30-min cooldown gives the broken runner's `t2897` per-runner breaker a chance to accumulate enough signal to trip (10 events / 6h), and gives healthy peers a chance to claim the issue first.

This is **complementary** to t2769 (per-issue 3-consecutive-no_work circuit breaker → NMR): t2769 fires after 3 stacked failures, but only against the SAME issue+runner pair within a tight window. With multiple issues rotating, t2769 rarely arms because each issue only sees 1-2 failures before the runner moves on.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-cooldown.sh`

### Implementation

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh::_post_launch_recovery_claim_released`** (current lines 971-1013) — when `failure_reason == "no_worker_process"`, after the existing CLAIM_RELEASED comment, post a SECOND short comment containing only the marker:
  ```
  <!-- dispatch-cooldown-until:<ISO+30min> reason=no_worker_process runner=<self_login> -->
  ```
  Use a separate comment rather than modifying the existing CLAIM_RELEASED body to keep the regex parse path simple in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`. Env: `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_AFTER_LAUNCH_FAILURE_SECONDS` (default 1800).

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::is-assigned`** — add a new `_is_assigned_check_dispatch_cooldown` function (model on `_is_assigned_check_no_auto_dispatch` at line ~440 area). Scans last 10 comments for the cooldown marker; if found and ISO is in the future, return `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE`. Insert the call into the layer cascade after `_is_assigned_check_no_auto_dispatch`. The existing `LAYER_RESULT` codes/printer pattern is followed.

- **NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-cooldown.sh`** — three cases:
  1. Issue with future cooldown marker → `is-assigned` returns 0 with `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE`.
  2. Issue with past (expired) cooldown marker → `is-assigned` returns normal result.
  3. Issue with no cooldown marker → unchanged behaviour.

### Reference pattern

`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::_is_assigned_check_no_auto_dispatch` (NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED short-circuit, t2832 — same shape: scan label/comment, short-circuit, named outcome). Marker comment style: existing `<!-- ops:start/end -->` pattern.

### Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-cooldown.sh` returns 0.
- Manual: post a `<!-- dispatch-cooldown-until:<future-ISO> ... -->` comment on a real issue, run `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned <num> <slug>` and verify `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE` outcome.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` passes clean.

## Acceptance

- Cooldown applied only on `failure_reason=no_worker_process` (not `cli_usage_output`, `stale_timeout`, etc. — these are real-attempt failures, not infra).
- Cooldown window configurable via env (default 1800 s).
- Both broken runner and healthy peers respect the cooldown (any pulse run reading `is-assigned` honours it — no per-runner partitioning).
- Cooldown auto-expires; no cleanup needed.
- Tests added.

## Session Origin

Same review as the cross-runner peer quarantine task (sister issue). Per-issue cooldown is the local-issue protection; peer quarantine is the cross-runner protection. Both are needed: cooldown alone leaks a broken runner's claims to peers; peer quarantine alone leaves the issue available for the broken runner's next tick. Together: the issue cools, the broken peer is ignored, healthy peers can pick up.

title: t3198: pulse-runner-health-helper.sh diagnose: cross-check breaker state vs observed pulse log
body:
## Task

Add `pulse-runner-health-helper.sh diagnose [--json]` subcommand that cross-checks recorded breaker state against observed pulse log evidence and surfaces wiring gaps before the operator notices the symptom.

## Why

Evidence (Apr 2026, managed-private-repo): a single peer runner produced ≥30 `recover_failed_launch_state` events with `failure_reason=no_worker_process` over ~4 hours — well past the t2897 per-runner threshold of 10/6h. Yet the issues kept being dispatched, suggesting either (a) the breaker tripped but `cmd_is_paused` only gates `apply_dispatch_max` and not other dispatch entry points, (b) the deployed `_record_runner_health_zero_attempt` wiring isn't being called, or (c) `_rh_window_expired` resets the counter too aggressively when failure spacing exceeds the window.

Without a self-diagnostic command, the only way to investigate is to read three files manually (`runner-health.json`, `pulse-wrapper.log`, the source). A `diagnose` subcommand turns 30 minutes of operator forensics into one command.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-runner-health-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-health-diagnose.sh`

### Implementation

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-runner-health-helper.sh`** — add `cmd_diagnose` and wire into `main()` dispatch (current line 570-587). The function:
  1. Reads `runner-health.json` for `consecutive_zero_attempts`, `window_started_at`, `circuit_breaker.state`.
  2. Greps `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` for `recover_failed_launch_state` invocations + extracted `failure_reason=no_worker_process` events since `window_started_at`.
  3. Computes `expected_counter = count_of_observed_events_since_window_start`.
  4. Compares `expected_counter` vs recorded `consecutive_zero_attempts`. If `expected - recorded > 2` → `WIRING_GAP` finding (recorder not being called).
  5. If `recorded >= threshold` but `state == "closed"` → `TRIGGER_MISSED` finding (trip evaluation broken).
  6. If `recorded < threshold` and `state == "closed"` → `HEALTHY` (or BUILDING).
  7. If `state == "tripped"` and `now - tripped_at > 24h` and outcome is `failed` → `STUCK_TRIPPED` (manual resume needed).
  8. Print human-readable table by default; `--json` emits structured object.
- Update `cmd_help()` text and the dispatch table.

- **NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-health-diagnose.sh`** — fixtures with synthetic state files + log snippets exercising each finding (HEALTHY, BUILDING, WIRING_GAP, TRIGGER_MISSED, STUCK_TRIPPED).

title: t3199: add ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE classification to t2987 conflict-pattern registry
body:
## Task

Add an `ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE` classification to the t2987 conflict-patterns registry so when two PRs both create the same new file (and the second one to merge gets DIRTY), the conflict-fix-worker brief tells the worker exactly how to resolve it instead of a generic "files conflicted, rebuild on develop."

## Why (real incident)

GH#21799 introduced `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` as a NEW file. While that PR was in review, GH#21884 (a follow-up) ALSO created `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` — slightly evolved (string-literal cleanup) — and merged first. GH#21799 then had an `add/add` conflict on the same file:

```
CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh
```

Today's t2987 conflict-pattern registry does NOT classify this. It falls through to `CODE` ("hand-resolve required, no guidance block"). A worker rerouted by `_dispatch_conflict_fix_worker` would get only the generic cherry-pick guidance — which doesn't apply to add/add conflicts (cherry-picking the original commit just re-creates the same conflict).

The correct resolution is: **delete the local copy, accept the version that landed first on the default branch, then re-apply any unique additions on top.** This is mechanical and worker-tractable IF the brief tells the worker.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT: `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf`** — add a new record. Format from the file's header comment is `CLASSIFICATION | GLOB_PATTERN | RESOLUTION_COMMAND | GUIDANCE_TEXT`. Add this record (place it BEFORE the `CODE | * | ...` catch-all):

  ```text
  ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE | __SPECIAL_ADD_ADD__ | git checkout --ours <path> && git add <path> && git rebase --continue | Both your PR and a previously-merged PR added the same new file. The version on the default branch (--ours during rebase) is canonical — accept it. If your version had unique additions not in main's version, append them on top in a follow-up commit AFTER the rebase completes.
  ```

  The `__SPECIAL_ADD_ADD__` glob is a sentinel — actual `add/add` detection happens in step 2 below, NOT via filename glob (since add/add conflicts can occur on any path).

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh`** — `_classify_conflicts_by_pattern()` (look near line 534, before `_emit_pattern_guidance_blocks`). Currently it iterates conflicting files and matches each path against globs. Extend it to ALSO inspect git's conflict type — `add/add` is detected via `git status --porcelain` showing `AA` (both added):

  ```bash
  # Detect add/add conflicts BEFORE glob matching — they need a different
  # resolution shape than content conflicts on existing files.
  local add_add_files
  add_add_files=$(git -C "$repo_path" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null \
      | awk '/^AA / {print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ')
  if [[ -n "$add_add_files" ]]; then
      echo "ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE:${add_add_files}"
      # Don't return here — also emit any glob-based classifications for
      # other conflicting files that aren't add/add.
  fi
  # ... existing glob-loop continues for non-add/add conflicts ...
  ```

  Then `_emit_pattern_guidance_blocks` (already iterates classifications) picks up the new record from `conflict-patterns.conf` and emits the guidance block normally.

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-conflict-pattern-detection.sh`** — add cases:
  1. Single `add/add` conflict on a `.sh` file → `ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE` classification.
  2. Mixed: one `add/add` + one content conflict on `pnpm-lock.yaml` → emits BOTH `ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE` and `LOCKFILE` blocks.
  3. Single content conflict on existing `.sh` file → `CODE` (existing behaviour, unchanged).

- **EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md`** — under the existing "Conflict Resolution Patterns (t2987)" table, add the new row:

  ```markdown
  | `ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE` | any `add/add` (both branches created the file) | `git checkout --ours <path>` during rebase; re-apply unique additions on top as follow-up commit. The first-merged version is canonical. |
  ```

### Reference patterns

- Pattern registry format and existing examples: `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf` (file header has the schema).
- Pattern matching code: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh::_classify_conflicts_by_pattern`.
- Existing tests to model on: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-conflict-pattern-detection.sh`.
- Real-incident proof point: GH#21799 add/add conflict on `shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` — recoverable via `git checkout --ours` (verified manually in the canonical PR).

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-conflict-pattern-detection.sh   # 0 failures
markdownlint-cli2 .agents/AGENTS.md
```

## Acceptance

- `ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE` classification appears in `conflict-patterns.conf`.
- `_classify_conflicts_by_pattern` detects add/add via `git status --porcelain` (`AA` rows), independent of filename glob.
- Mixed conflicts (add/add + lockfile + content) emit one guidance block per non-CODE classification.
- 3 new test cases pass alongside the existing test suite.
- AGENTS.md "Conflict Resolution Patterns" table updated.
- ShellCheck clean.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-conflict-pattern-detection.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

### Complexity Impact

The new add/add detection is ~6 new lines in `_classify_conflicts_by_pattern`; existing function size ~30 lines. Stays well below the 80-line advisory and 100-line CI gate.

title: t3193: pulse: stuck-merge detector + zero-progress circuit breaker (mergeable-but-unmerged)
body:
## What

Add a **stuck-merge detector** to the pulse so PRs that are merge-eligible (APPROVED + MERGEABLE + no `hold-for-review`) but stay unmerged past a threshold get classified, escalated to investigation issues, and (where safe) auto-routed to a fix-worker — instead of silently re-evaluating every cycle until a human notices.

## Why

The pulse has rich deterministic merge gates and **two narrow stuck-state nudges** (`_post_rebase_nudge_on_interactive_conflicting`, `_post_rebase_nudge_on_contributor_conflicting`), but **no general "merge-eligible but stuck" detector**. When a PR sits APPROVED + MERGEABLE for hours with non-required checks failing, a transient `branch-protection API` 401, or repeated `update-branch` failures, the pulse just re-runs the same gates every 120s. No issue is filed, no worker is dispatched, no counter trips a circuit breaker.

Concrete current evidence (a managed private webapp repo, snapshot 2026-04-30 ~14:00Z):

- **8 open PRs stuck**, idle 9–29h.
- **6 of them** share an **identical CI failure fingerprint**: `Format` + `Lint` + `Typecheck` + `Secret Detection` + `Dependency Audit` + `Merge E2E Reports` all FAILURE, frequently at the **`Setup` step** (pre-execution env break). Six PRs failing the *same* checks is a **broken-base signal**, not six independent PR bugs — but no detector fires this finding.
- **2 of them** are docs/migration PRs with only Socket Security checks (1 SUCCESS + 1 NEUTRAL) and `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY`. They are functionally green but conflicting; `update-branch` fails, `_close_conflicting_pr` metadata-fetch fails (transient 401), and they sit. No nudge fires (rebase-nudge requires `origin:interactive`/contributor; these have neither label).
- **The default branch (`develop`) has no protection** — `gh api .../branches/develop/protection` → HTTP 404. `_check_required_checks_passing` (`pulse-merge-process.sh:687-762`) emits `branch protection API failed (exit 1) — failing closed (t2922)` repeatedly because the 404 path collapses into the generic API-error branch instead of the `no required contexts → allowing` branch. So the worker-briefed gate refuses to evaluate even when the answer should structurally be "allow".
- **No `pulse-stats.json` counters** exist for `pulse_merge_eligible_stuck_pr_count`, `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles`, or `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips`. The pulse cannot self-diagnose its own merge-throughput collapse.

User intent: surfaced 8 stuck PRs and explicitly asked whether the pulse / pulse LLM / circuit breaker layer should detect and route them autonomously. Self-healing is the explicit framework mission.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — main merge loop; emit per-cycle eligible-stuck count + zero-progress counter; call into new stuck-merge module.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-stuck.sh` — new module, sourced by `pulse-merge.sh`. Houses the detector, classifier, escalation/dispatch logic, and dedup markers. Mirrors layout of existing `pulse-merge-conflict.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:687-762` — `_check_required_checks_passing`: differentiate HTTP 404 (no protection → return success/0) from real API errors (auth fail, network) before falling through to `failing closed`. The existing line-714 "no required contexts → allowing" path is reachable only when `gh api …/protection` exits 0 with empty `required_status_checks.contexts`; a 404 currently hits line 708 instead.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh` (or wherever `pulse-stats.json` keys are written — confirm via `rg pulse_merge_ ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`) — add the four new counters listed below.
- `EDIT: .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` (or new `.agents/configs/pulse-merge-stuck.conf`) — surface threshold env vars: `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_STUCK_AGE_MINUTES` (default 240 = 4h), `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES` (default 5), `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_PATTERN_MIN_PRS` (default 3).
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh` — fixture-driven tests for each classifier branch and dedup marker.

### Reference patterns

Model on:

- **`pulse-merge-conflict.sh:75-143`** (`_post_rebase_nudge_on_interactive_conflicting`, `_post_rebase_nudge_on_contributor_conflicting`) — exact pattern for one-shot nudge with HTML-comment marker (`<!-- pulse-rebase-nudge -->`) + `_gh_idempotent_comment`. Reuse the same idempotency primitive.
- **`shared-claim-lifecycle.sh::release_interactive_claim_on_merge`** (t2413/t2429/t2811) — pattern for "fire once on a state transition, dedup on a marker".
- **`pulse-merge-feedback.sh::_dispatch_conflict_fix_worker`** + the `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf` registry (t2987) — declarative pattern → guidance lookup. Apply the same shape to **failure-fingerprint patterns** (e.g. `Format+Lint+Typecheck all fail at Setup → likely broken base/lockfile drift`).
- **`pulse-merge.sh:571-585`** — existing t2922 origin:worker bypass — extend the same conditional logic (require all *real* required contexts pass) for the new "no branch protection" path.

### Implementation outline

`pulse-merge-stuck.sh` exposes:

1. `_classify_stuck_pr <pr_number> <repo_slug>` — returns one of:
   - `STUCK_CHECKS_FAILING` (≥1 FAILURE in rollup, no conflict)
   - `STUCK_CONFLICT_NO_NUDGE_LABEL` (CONFLICTING but neither `origin:interactive`/contributor — current gap)
   - `STUCK_BRANCHPROTECT_404` (default-branch unprotected; t2922 mis-fires)
   - `STUCK_BRANCHPROTECT_API_ERROR` (transient 401/5xx from protection API)
   - `STUCK_AUTH` (`gh` auth-failed signature)
   - `STUCK_OTHER` (mergeable + approved + idle but no signal)
2. `_detect_pattern_outage <repo_slug>` — groups all stuck PRs in the repo by failure fingerprint (sorted set of FAILURE check names). If ≥`AIDEVOPS_MERGE_PATTERN_MIN_PRS` share a fingerprint, file ONE investigation issue per outage signature with `auto-dispatch` + `tier:thinking` (broken base/CI infra needs reasoning) and label `source:merge-stuck-detector`. Dedup marker: `<!-- merge-stuck:pattern:<sha256_of_fingerprint> -->` so the issue is filed once per outage, not once per cycle.
3. `_escalate_individual_stuck_pr` — for `STUCK_CHECKS_FAILING` past `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_STUCK_AGE_MINUTES` *and* not part of an outage cluster, post a one-shot worker-ready comment on the PR's linked issue with the failing check names + a "model on existing CI fix patterns" pointer. Marker: `<!-- merge-stuck:individual -->`.
4. `_handle_stuck_branchprotect_404` — call `_check_required_checks_passing` in a "treat 404 as no-protection allow-list" mode and let the existing rollup gate decide; if rollup is all-pass, merge.
5. `_handle_stuck_conflict_no_nudge_label` — extend the existing rebase-nudge family with a label-agnostic variant that fires once for any APPROVED + CONFLICTING PR idle past the threshold. Use the same `<!-- pulse-rebase-nudge -->` marker (already idempotent per PR) so it doesn't double-fire.
6. **Circuit-breaker counter:** in `pulse-merge.sh` per-cycle, after the merge pass, compute `eligible_unmerged = count(APPROVED + MERGEABLE + !draft + !hold-for-review)`. If this is non-zero AND no PR was merged this cycle, increment `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles`. When it crosses `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES`, file ONE meta-issue (dedup marker `<!-- merge-stuck:zero-progress -->`) describing the throughput collapse with a snapshot of all stuck PRs and their classifications. Reset to 0 on any successful merge. Disable the meta-issue path during active circuit-breaker trip (`pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken=true`) to avoid noise during GraphQL exhaustion.

### Counters added

- `pulse_merge_eligible_stuck_pr_count` (gauge, current cycle)
- `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles` (counter, resets on merge)
- `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips` (counter, monitors t2922 mis-fires until t2922 fix lands)
- `pulse_merge_stuck_escalations_filed` (counter, by classification)

### Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-stuck.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` passes clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh` passes 0 failures.
- Manual smoke: `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_STUCK_AGE_MINUTES=0 pulse-merge.sh --once --dry-run` (or equivalent) prints classification table for currently-stuck PRs and shows ≥1 `STUCK_BRANCHPROTECT_404` + ≥1 pattern-cluster finding when run against a repo with the symptom.
- After landing, the t2922 404→fail-closed log line should disappear from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge.log` for repos whose default branch is intentionally unprotected.
- One meta-issue should appear within one pulse cycle of the threshold being hit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` exists, sourced by `pulse-merge.sh`, exports the six classifier outcomes listed.
- [ ] `_check_required_checks_passing` distinguishes HTTP 404 (no protection) from API error and returns success when the default branch is unprotected.
- [ ] At least one one-shot escalation comment fires per individual stuck PR past `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_STUCK_AGE_MINUTES`, deduped by HTML marker.
- [ ] At least one meta-issue is filed when ≥3 stuck PRs share a failure fingerprint, deduped by fingerprint hash.
- [ ] `pulse-stats.json` exposes the four new counters; values are non-zero against the captured snapshot (verifiable end-to-end).
- [ ] All four `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_*` env-var thresholds documented in `reference/auto-merge.md` (or a new `reference/pulse-merge-stuck.md`).
- [ ] `tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh` exercises every classifier branch + dedup-marker behaviour.
- [ ] No regression: existing rebase-nudge paths still fire exactly once per CONFLICTING `origin:interactive`/contributor PR.

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-30 — user surfaced 8 stuck PRs in a managed private webapp repo and explicitly asked whether the pulse / pulse LLM / circuit breaker layer should detect and route them autonomously. Investigation traced the gap to: (a) stuck-PR detection scoped only to CONFLICTING + (interactive|contributor); (b) `_check_required_checks_passing` collapsing 404 into generic API-error fail-closed; (c) no merge-throughput counter / zero-progress circuit breaker. Filed per t3006 capture-don't-advise (autonomous self-healing is the explicit framework mission).

## Complexity Impact

- `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` is a NEW file — no existing function exceeds the 100-line `function-complexity` gate.
- `pulse-merge.sh` per-cycle wiring adds ~20 lines (counter increment + `pulse-merge-stuck.sh::run_pass` call). No existing function in `pulse-merge.sh::process_pr` family is at risk of crossing 80 lines.
- `_check_required_checks_passing` 404-distinguish change is ~5 lines inside an already-modular function; the function stays well under 80 lines.

## Dispatch-Path Classification (advisory)

This task EDITS `pulse-merge.sh` and `pulse-merge-process.sh` (canonical self-hosting set per `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`). Per t2920, default is `auto-dispatch` with t2819 auto-elevation to `model:opus-4-7`. Worker worktree isolation + the t2690 5% GraphQL circuit breaker provide the safety cascade. No `no-auto-dispatch` opt-out needed — interactive opt-out is not warranted here.

<!-- conflict-feedback:PR21916 -->
## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #21916)

The previous worker's PR #21916 (`t3193: pulse stuck-merge detector + zero-progress circuit breaker`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (5 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/configs/pulse-merge-stuck.conf
.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-stuck.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `2ef505496a6e7f75f06db7a949380be051bde756`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/21916/head:recovered-21916
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick 2ef505496a6e7f75f06db7a949380be051bde756
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #21916's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`.

_Routed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)._

title: sync-workflows --apply does not inject runner override into CURRENT/CALLER workflows
body:
## What

`aidevops sync-workflows --apply --repo <slug>` does not inject `with: runner: <label>` into CURRENT/CALLER workflows when `repos.json` gains a new `runner` field. The command reports "no actionable repos/workflows (all CURRENT or NO-WORKFLOW)" and makes no changes.

## Why

`_list_actionable_repos` (line ~281) filters to `DRIFTED/CALLER` and `NEEDS-MIGRATION` only. When a repo's callers are structurally current (matching the canonical template), `check-workflows-helper.sh` classifies them as `CURRENT/CALLER` — correctly, because `_normalize_wf_for_compare` strips the `runner:` line before comparison.

The runner injection code in `_sync_one_workflow` (lines 506-509) fires only for repos that pass the actionable filter. CURRENT callers never reach it.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Start with a repo whose callers are CURRENT/CALLER and no runner field
aidevops check-workflows --repo robstiles/qs-agency
# → CURRENT/CALLER for all callers

# 2. Add runner to repos.json
jq '(.initialized_repos[] | select(.slug == "robstiles/qs-agency")).runner = "ubicloud-standard-2"' \
  ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json > /tmp/r.json && mv /tmp/r.json ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json

# 3. Run sync — expects runner injection, gets nothing
aidevops sync-workflows --repo robstiles/qs-agency --apply
# → "no actionable repos/workflows (all CURRENT or NO-WORKFLOW)."
```

## Suggested Fix

In `_list_actionable_repos`, also include repos classified as `CURRENT/CALLER` when `_read_runner_field "$slug"` returns a non-empty value AND the on-disk caller does not already contain `runner:` in a `with:` block. This triggers the sync path which already has the injection code.

Alternative: add a `--force` flag that includes CURRENT repos in the actionable set.

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh:263-295` — extend `_list_actionable_repos` to include CURRENT/CALLER repos needing runner injection
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows-runner-normalise.sh` — add a test case for the sync-after-runner-add scenario

## Impact

Low — workaround is to manually add the `with: runner:` block (3 lines per caller). But the whole point of GH#21877 was to make this automatic via `repos.json` + `sync-workflows`.

title: check-workflows normaliser leaves bare with: block when runner is EOF (GH#21877 follow-up)
body:
## What

`_normalize_wf_for_compare` in `check-workflows-helper.sh` fails to strip an empty `with:` block when it is the LAST line of the file. This causes callers with `runner:` as the only `with:` entry (e.g. `maintainer-gate.yml`, `review-bot-gate.yml`) to be classified as `DRIFTED/CALLER` even when `repos.json` correctly declares the `runner` field.

Callers where `with:` has other children (e.g. `issue-sync.yml` which also has `command:`) are unaffected.

## Root Cause

The awk block (lines 153-168) buffers a `    with:` line as `pending` and discards it if the next line is not a 6-space-indented child. But the `END` block at line 167:

```awk
END { if (pending != "") print pending }
```

re-emits the buffered `with:` when it is the last line of the file (no next line to trigger the discard path). The empty `with:` then shows up in the diff against the canonical template which has no `with:` block.

## Fix

Change line 167 from:

```awk
END { if (pending != "") print pending }
```

to:

```awk
END { }
```

or simply remove the `END` block. A pending `with:` at EOF is always empty (the `runner:` line was already deleted by sed). There is no legitimate scenario where a `with:` as the last line of a caller should survive normalisation.

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh:167` — remove or empty the awk `END` block

title: t3200: full-loop-helper.sh: detect shallow clone before rebase to avoid add/add conflict cascade
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` calls `git rebase origin/main` without first checking whether the local clone is shallow. On a shallow clone, intermediate commit objects between the clone-depth boundary and origin/main tip are missing locally. The rebase then fails to find a merge-base and produces 'add/add' conflicts on every file in the diff (hundreds of files for a one-file PR), printing a wall of conflict noise that looks like a force-push or history rewrite. The session loses minutes investigating a non-incident.

## Why

Multi-runner aidevops setups frequently produce shallow clones (initial setup speed, CI clone defaults). When the operator's interactive session uses such a clone, the FIRST rebase against an active main fails dramatically. The current commit-and-pr error message is 'Rebase conflict. Resolve conflicts, then run: git rebase --continue', which is misleading — the conflicts cannot be resolved because the merge-base is genuinely absent locally; the operator must unshallow the clone first. Without explicit detection, every operator hits this once and burns ~10-30 min misdiagnosing.

## How

EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh — in cmd_commit_and_pr, before `git rebase origin/main`:
- Call `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`. If true, log warning and run `git fetch --unshallow origin` (or refuse with an actionable message: 'Local clone is shallow; rebase requires full history. Run: git fetch --unshallow origin').
- Reference pattern: model on the existing pre-rebase 'fetch origin main' invocation in the same function (search for 'Rebasing onto origin/main').

EDIT: .agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh — same shallow-clone detection at session start; warn once per session if the active worktree's repo is shallow.

EDIT: .agents/reference/bash-compat.md or a new note in .agents/reference/git-hygiene.md — document the symptom + recovery pattern so future operators recognise it instantly. Recovery sequence: `git format-patch -1 <commit> --stdout > /tmp/save.patch`, `git reset --hard origin/main`, `git am /tmp/save.patch`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh
- .agents/reference/git-hygiene.md (NEW, optional)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` on a shallow clone either auto-unshallows OR exits 1 with the message 'Local clone is shallow; run git fetch --unshallow origin' BEFORE attempting rebase.
- [ ] Test: clone the repo with `--depth=1`, make a one-line edit, run commit-and-pr → no add/add cascade, clear error or auto-recovery.
- [ ] Memory lesson 'Shallow git clones masquerade as force-pushed history' (already stored 2026-04-30) is referenced from the doc.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops /tmp/aidevops-shallow-test
cd /tmp/aidevops-shallow-test && echo 'test' >> README.md
.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue X --message wip --title wip --summary wip --testing wip --decisions wip
# Expected: clean error or auto-unshallow, NOT add/add cascade
```

## Tier

tier:standard — touches a dispatch-adjacent helper but is purely defensive guard logic; no judgment calls. Use cascade dispatch starting at simple if brief allows.

## Session origin

Surfaced during interactive work on issue #21860 (t3086 doc add): `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` rebase produced 200+ add/add conflicts that initially looked like a force-push to origin/main. After `gh api compare` confirmed remote history was healthy, `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returned true. `git fetch --unshallow` resolved everything. Cost ~15 min of session debugging.

title: t3201: investigate: worker stuck-loop pattern force-pushes + review_dismissed + close on PR (canonical: #21876)
body:
## What

Investigate the recurring failure mode where a headless worker dispatched against an issue (canonical: #21860) opens a PR, gets approved, but then force-pushes 4-5 times before its own runner closes the PR with simultaneous `auto_merge_disabled` + `head_ref_deleted`. Each force-push dismisses the prior approval, creating a loop the pulse cannot exit. The PR ultimately stays `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` despite `mergeable=MERGEABLE` + all CI passing + multiple approvals.

## Why

Single-incident #21876 burned a worker session, then triggered re-dispatch cascade on issue #21860 with WORKER_BRANCH_ORPHAN classifications on subsequent dispatches. Each re-dispatch costs tokens and attention without progress. The same pattern likely affects other issues silently. Without identifying the trigger, the loop will keep happening — the cost compounds across issues.

## How (investigation)

This is a parent / research task — DO NOT auto-dispatch a worker to 'fix' it without first identifying the root cause.

EDIT: read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge.log` and `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` filtered to PR 21876 across the 07:00-08:00 UTC 2026-04-30 window. Pulse-diagnose-helper currently does not have an `issue` subcommand; that is a separate lacuna (see ## Sub-tasks below).

EDIT: trace timeline of PR #21876 via `gh api /repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/21876/events?per_page=100`. Confirmed shape: 5x `head_ref_force_pushed` interleaved with `review_dismissed` (because dismiss_stale_reviews=true on main branch protection), terminating in `closed` + `auto_merge_disabled` + `head_ref_deleted` from `alex-solovyev` actor.

EDIT: search `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` and `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` for code paths that force-push + close an open PR they own. The kill signature suggests `_handle_worker_branch_orphan` (line 522) OR `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` is firing while the worker is mid-pushing.

EDIT: examine `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` close criteria. The PR was approved + mergeable; what made it 'dirty'?

EDIT: examine watchdog (`worker-activity-watchdog.sh`) — the worker was clearly producing activity (5 force-pushes in 30min), so why didn't watchdog kill earlier or, conversely, if watchdog DID kill, why did the cleanup close the PR rather than letting it stand for human triage?

## Hypotheses to verify

1. **Watchdog timeout + cleanup path**: worker watchdog killed the worker for some reason (maybe stuck on a single review-feedback cycle) and the cleanup path closed + deleted branch unconditionally. Cleanup should preserve the PR for triage when CI was passing.
2. **Review-feedback retry loop**: worker is re-running the review-feedback loop on each `review_dismissed` event even though the PR is already approved by pulse. Self-cancelling: each push dismisses its own approval.
3. **Cross-runner approval visibility lag**: pulse on alex-solovyev's machine doesn't see pulse-merge approvals from marcusquinn runner; worker thinks it's still pre-approval and keeps fixing.
4. **`pulse-dirty-pr-sweep` mis-classification**: PR with multiple force-pushes + dismissed reviews matches a 'dirty' heuristic and gets closed as cleanup.

## Sub-tasks (file after triage)

- [ ] `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` lacks an `issue <N>` subcommand. Add one.
- [ ] Apply explicit dispatch-loop counter on issue: kill cascade after N retries on the same issue with same failure class.
- [ ] If hypothesis 3 is the root cause: cross-runner approval state must be visible across runners (not just per-runner cache).

## Investigation result

### Root cause

The #21876 loop was caused by the worker-output classifier relying on GitHub Search to decide whether a worker had opened a PR. The worker branch `feature/auto-20260430-062441-gh21860` already had PR #21876 open, but the classifier still emitted `worker_branch_orphan` repeatedly because the previous PR-existence probe could miss recently-created PRs. Each redispatch reused the same issue/branch, pushed again, and branch-protection dismissed the previous pulse approval on the next force-push.

### Evidence

- PR #21876 events show repeated `head_ref_force_pushed` events at 05:34, 05:44, 06:18, 06:32, and 07:18 UTC; the last two are paired with `review_dismissed` because stale approvals are dismissed after push.
- PR #21876 reviews show pulse approvals at 06:23, 06:53, and 07:22 UTC; the first two were dismissed by later pushes.
- Issue #21860 comments show repeated `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_branch_orphan` and `WORKER_BRANCH_ORPHAN branch=feature/auto-20260430-062441-gh21860` at 04:35, 05:41, 05:48, 06:30, 06:41, and 07:32 UTC while PR #21876 existed.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge.log` on the maintainer runner shows the merge pass repeatedly considered PR #21876 mergeable, passed worker-briefed auto-merge gates, approved it, then deferred because auto-merge was already set.
- Current code now contains the corrective helper `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh::_pr_exists_for_branch_or_issue`, which checks `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` before falling back to search; this shipped in PR #21902 for #21889.

### Hypothesis decision

Correct root cause: **review-feedback / orphan-recovery retry loop driven by stale PR-existence detection**. It is closest to hypothesis 2, but the trigger was not a bot review-feedback loop; it was the orphan classifier failing to see an existing PR and re-queueing the same issue/branch.

Rejected hypotheses:

- **Watchdog cleanup path**: not supported by local evidence; no local watchdog metrics matched #21876, and the repeated issue comments were `worker_branch_orphan`, not watchdog kill markers.
- **Cross-runner approval visibility lag**: not primary. The marcusquinn runner saw and approved PR #21876 repeatedly; the destructive loop was the worker side re-pushing the branch after orphan misclassification.
- **`pulse-dirty-pr-sweep` close criteria**: not primary. PR #21876 was not old enough for the default 7-day dirty close threshold, and the PR comments do not contain dirty-sweep close markers.

### Follow-up tasks filed

- #21889 / PR #21902 — fixed the immediate classifier bug by probing PRs via `--head` before search fallback.
- #22045 — add `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <N>` so issue-level cascades can be diagnosed from one command.
- #22049 — add a dispatch-loop counter for repeated `worker_branch_orphan` on the same issue + branch.

### Single-line guard

A guard equivalent to "if `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` returns a PR, classify as `pr_exists`, not `branch_orphan`" would have prevented the #21876 cascade. That guard is now implemented by PR #21902.


## Children

- #22041 — Reconstruct PR #21876 worker-loop timeline.
- #22045 — Add `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <N>` for issue-level worker/PR timelines.
- #22049 — Add a dispatch-loop counter for repeated `worker_branch_orphan` on the same issue branch.

## Acceptance

- [x] Root cause of PR #21876 closure documented in this issue's body
- [x] Decision recorded: which of the 4 hypotheses (or new one) is correct, with evidence link
- [x] Sub-task issues filed for each independent fix that emerges from the investigation
- [x] If a single-line guard would have prevented #21876, file that as #auto-dispatch with brief

## Tier

tier:thinking — investigation requires reading multiple log streams, correlating timestamps across runners, and understanding multi-process state. Not appropriate for tier:simple or tier:standard auto-dispatch. Prefer `#parent` to block dispatch until human triage decides scope.

## Session origin

Surfaced during interactive work on issue #21860 (t3086 doc add). PR #21876 was filed by alex-solovyev's worker for the same issue earlier this session and got into the cascade. PR #21898 (this session's PR) is now active with the same scope; if it hits the same cascade, this investigation becomes urgent.

title: pulse-wrapper singleton lock: MULTIPLE instances regression after t3002 fix (GH#21433)
body:
## What

`pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` reports 2 live pulse-wrapper instances minutes after a clean restart, with the lifecycle helper emitting `MULTIPLE pulse instances detected (GH#21433) — singleton invariant violated`. PR [#21437](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/21437) (t3002) shipped the lock-race fix on 2026-04-28; the symptom returned by 2026-04-30, observed in v3.13.12.

Reproduction (live, after a fresh restart):

```
$ ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart
[OK] Pulse started (PID: 95560)

$ sleep 60 && ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status
Pulse: running (2 instances)
  Lock holder PID: 45682
  PID 40800 (uptime 04:53)
  PID 45682 (lock holder) (uptime 04:45)
[WARN] MULTIPLE pulse instances detected (GH#21433) — singleton invariant violated
[WARN] Recommendation: pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart
```

`pulse-diagnose-helper.sh cycle-health` shows low all-time churn (`Acquired lock: 92, Exited early: 1, Churn: 1%`), so the lock primitive itself works *most* of the time — but the singleton invariant is observably breached in steady state.

## Why

A 1% churn rate on a lock that fires hundreds of times per day still produces multiple-instance windows daily. While the lock release between cycles (t2774 — released for LLM dispatch) is intentional, the lifecycle helper's `status` subcommand still reports the violation because two `pulse-wrapper.sh` processes are alive at the same time. Either:

(a) the t3002 fix is incomplete — there's a remaining race window between launchd `KeepAlive` respawn timing and the existing instance's lock-release cycle window, or
(b) the t3002 fix is sufficient but the lifecycle-helper warning logic is now over-eager — it shouldn't flag two-process-coexistence when one is in the legitimate release window.

The premise check is non-trivial and the worker should verify which case is true before patching.

## How

### Premise check (do FIRST, before writing code)

1. Read `pulse-instance-lock.sh` to understand the post-t3002 lock semantics — when is the lock acquired, when released, when is a new respawn allowed.
2. Read `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh::status` (or wherever the "MULTIPLE pulse instances detected" warning is emitted) to see what condition triggers it.
3. Decide: is the warning correct (two processes ARE racing), or stale (warning fires on legitimate release-window coexistence)?

If (b) — warning is stale: fix the warning logic to consider lock-release-window coexistence legitimate, AND keep a guard that flags genuine duplicate-lock-holders.

If (a) — race remains: identify the window. Likely candidates: launchd respawn during `aidevops update` script invocation, two simultaneous `pulse-wrapper.sh` invocations from setup.sh + launchd KeepAlive racing during deploy.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh` (if real race)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` (if stale warning)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (if either fix touches the call site)
- TESTS: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-instance-lock-*.sh` (extend existing)

### Reference

- Read PR #21437 diff for the t3002 fix scope
- Read `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh:827` for the wrapper-churn telemetry that informs the verification

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Restart pulse cleanly
.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart

# 2. Wait 5 minutes for steady state, then check
sleep 300
.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status
# Expected: "Pulse: running (1 instance)" — no MULTIPLE warning

# 3. Run aidevops update mid-cycle and re-check
aidevops update
sleep 30
.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status
# Expected: still 1 instance after the update cycle settles
```

## Acceptance

- After 5 min of steady state, `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` reports exactly 1 instance
- After `aidevops update` mid-cycle, status returns to 1 instance within the next pulse cycle
- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh cycle-health` `Wrapper churn` percentage stays at or below current 1%
- Test added that fails on the multi-instance race condition or the false-positive warning, depending on which case applies

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — premise verification required (real race vs stale warning), launchd interaction, lock primitive semantics. Worker must read the t3002 fix before patching.

## Related

- Original: GH#21433 (closed, t3002)
- Fix PR: GH#21437 (merged 2026-04-28)
- Observed regression: 2026-04-30, v3.13.12, multiple operators

title: claim-task-id.sh: HTTPS push hangs indefinitely; needs timeout + SSH fallback
body:
## What

`claim-task-id.sh` hangs indefinitely when pushing the `.task-counter` advance to GitHub via HTTPS. Observed in this environment (macOS 14.x, gh CLI authenticated, `origin` URL is HTTPS): the helper completes ID allocation locally, attempts `git push origin main` to advance the canonical counter, and stalls past 90 seconds with no output. Counter `+1` commit lands locally; remote never advances; no GitHub issue gets created.

Reproduction (this session, t3077 follow-up):

```
$ ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh \
    --title "ai-research-helper: invalid Anthropic model IDs..." \
    --description "..." \
    --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:simple,bug,framework"
[INFO] Loading project config from .aidevops.json
[INFO] Using remote: origin, counter branch: main
[INFO] Detected platform: github
# (hangs >90s, no further output, no remote ref advance)

$ git remote get-url origin
https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops.git
```

Workaround that succeeds in this environment:

```bash
# Step 1: claim ID offline (succeeds)
claim-task-id.sh ... --offline
# task_id=t3191, ref=offline

# Step 2: push counter via SSH (succeeds in seconds)
git push --no-verify git@github.com:marcusquinn/aidevops.git HEAD:refs/heads/main

# Step 3: file issue directly
gh issue create --repo OWNER/REPO --title "..." --body-file body.md --label "..."
```

The HTTPS hang is reproducible across multiple `claim-task-id.sh` and `git push origin` invocations in this session. SSH push succeeds every time. `gh` CLI commands (which use the gh-managed token, not git credential helper) also succeed.

## Why

Cross-session memory has a recorded lesson (`mem_20260430054453_5f0d112e`) on this exact failure mode. The hang appears to be in git's HTTPS credential negotiation — `git credential approve` is invoked but never returns, possibly because the credential helper is waiting for input that never arrives, or the gh-managed token isn't being surfaced to git's HTTPS layer in this environment.

This blocks the canonical claim flow. Every interactive task creation must currently use `--offline` + SSH workaround. Workers may also be affected if they use HTTPS remotes and the credential helper races.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- EDIT (likely): `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (for shared push helper)
- TESTS: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-*.sh`

### Premise check (do FIRST)

1. Reproduce the hang on a clean session (`gh auth refresh`, fresh terminal, no agent overrides).
2. Confirm the hang is in `git push` and not earlier — strace/dtruss the helper if needed.
3. Confirm SSH push works in the same environment for the same remote.

If hang reproduces: implement timeout + auto-fallback (see "The fix" below).
If hang does NOT reproduce on a clean session: file as environment-specific (close with reproduction instructions for affected runners).

### The fix (if premise confirmed)

Add a configurable timeout + automatic SSH fallback to the push step:

```bash
# In claim-task-id.sh push logic:
if ! timeout 30 git push --no-verify "$remote" "HEAD:refs/heads/$counter_branch"; then
  log_warn "HTTPS push timed out after 30s — retrying via SSH"
  local ssh_url
  ssh_url="$(git remote get-url "$remote" | sed -E 's|https://github.com/|git@github.com:|; s|\.git$|.git|')"
  if ! timeout 30 git push --no-verify "$ssh_url" "HEAD:refs/heads/$counter_branch"; then
    log_error "SSH push also failed — leaving claim offline"
    # Fall through to existing offline-mode behaviour
  fi
fi
```

Apply the same pattern to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` push helper if one exists, so the fallback is shared across helpers (issue-sync, version-manager, etc.).

### Reference

- Cross-session memory: `mem_20260430054453_5f0d112e` (HTTPS push hung; SSH workaround verified)
- Pattern to copy: any helper with `timeout` + fallback (e.g., `headless-runtime-helper.sh::_execute_run_attempt` retry pattern)

### Verification

```bash
# 1. With --offline counter advance pending, run:
claim-task-id.sh --title "test claim push hang" --description "verify HTTPS+SSH fallback" --labels "test"
# Expected: completes within 60s with HTTPS hang transparent (warning logged + SSH fallback succeeds)

# 2. Force HTTPS to fail (e.g., add invalid credential), verify SSH fallback:
GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/false claim-task-id.sh --title "..." --description "..." --labels "test"
# Expected: HTTPS fails fast, SSH fallback succeeds, GitHub issue created

# 3. Test on clean SSH-less environment:
# Expected: HTTPS path works (no fallback needed), or both fail with clear error
```

## Acceptance

- `claim-task-id.sh` push step has a configurable timeout (default 30s)
- On HTTPS push timeout, helper auto-retries via SSH URL derived from remote
- If both HTTPS and SSH fail, helper falls through to existing offline-mode warning, never hangs
- Test added that simulates HTTPS hang (e.g., `GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/false`) and verifies SSH fallback path
- Memory `mem_20260430054453_5f0d112e` referenced in the fix's commit message

## Tier

`tier:standard` — single helper script, well-defined fix, deterministic verification. Cross-cutting if the same fix is ported to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`.

title: t3202: version-manager release fails non-deterministically on marketplace.json update
body:
## What

`version-manager.sh release patch` fails non-deterministically at the marketplace.json validation step. First attempt: `_update_json_version_field` reports SUCCESS for marketplace.json (sed-inplace + grep-q both pass), but moments later `_check_marketplace_json` (validate-version-consistency.sh) sees the file with the OLD version. After the failure exit, the file content is back to the old version with no rollback code in any script. Re-running the same command immediately afterwards succeeds.

## Why

Causes spurious release failures requiring a manual retry. Wastes maintainer cycles. Real-world hit: v3.13.13 release on 2026-04-30 — first attempt failed, second succeeded with no code change.

## Repro

1. `version-manager.sh release patch` from clean main with all version files at v3.13.X
2. Observe `Updated .claude-plugin/marketplace.json` followed by `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json shows '3.13.X', expected '3.13.X+1'`
3. `git status` shows clean working tree (changes appear to roll back, but no rollback code exists)
4. Re-run `version-manager.sh release patch` — succeeds.

## How

Files to investigate:

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/version-manager-files.sh:139-153 — `_update_json_version_field` reports success based on grep-q immediately after sed-inplace, but file may not be flushed to disk before validator reads it.

title: t3204: issue-sync close path drops signature footer + summary on auto-close
body:
## Task

Restore the rich closing comment on the issue-sync auto-close path. Currently when the issue-sync helper closes an issue from a TODO.md `[x]` push, it emits only `"Completed via [PR #N](url). Task tNNN done in TODO.md."` — no signature footer, no implementation summary. Compare:

- #21892, #21889 (auto-closed by `github-actions` via `_close_comment`): one-liner, no `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`.
- #21888, #21877, #21880 (closed manually by an interactive agent): rich body + signature footer.

This violates the framework rule (AGENTS.md "Signature footer hallucination", t2685): *"Every gh issue create, gh issue comment, gh pr create, and gh pr comment body MUST end with the helper's output."*

## Why

- Audit trail: signature footer carries runtime, version, model, tokens, and session-time metadata. Auto-closes lose all of it.
- Discoverability: when reading a thread, the close comment is the most useful summary anchor. A bare one-liner forces the reader to click through to the PR to learn what shipped.
- Consistency: agent-closed issues already have the rich format; auto-closed ones look stub-like by comparison.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh`
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-close-signature.sh`

### Implementation

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh::_close_comment`** (lines 86-105). Currently emits bare `echo "Completed via..."`. Change to:
  - Compose the body in a temp file (heredoc), then append `gh-signature-helper.sh footer --solved --issue "$repo#$issue_number"` output. Pattern: `reference/secret-handling.md` and the same-bash-call avoidance from t2893 (build file in step 1, attach in step 2).
  - Threading the signature requires `_close_comment` to know `$repo` and `$issue_number` — currently it only takes `task_id text pr_num pr_url`. Update the signature to accept those, update callers (`_do_close` line 170 is the only one).
  - The body should remain short (one line of summary like today) but ADD the signature footer block. Don't try to synthesise a long implementation summary in the close path — the PR title + description already contains that, and the close comment links to it. The fix is signature-only.
- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh::cmd_reopen`** (lines 340-341): the reopen comment likewise lacks a footer. Append `gh-signature-helper.sh footer --issue "$repo#$ref_num"` (no `--solved` since reopening is not a solved state).
- **EDIT: `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`**: search for any `gh issue close ... --comment` or `gh issue comment` calls in the workflow YAML that compose comment bodies inline. If present, route them through the `gh` PATH shim (already in `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh`) by ensuring `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` is first in PATH before the call; OR explicitly call `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` and append. The shim auto-injects, but only when it's in PATH. CI runners need the agents/scripts dir prepended.
- **NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-close-signature.sh`**: 3 cases — (a) `_close_comment` output for a normal completion contains `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`; (b) cancelled-task variant contains the marker; (c) `cmd_reopen` reopen comment contains the marker.

### Reference pattern

- `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` invocations elsewhere: `rg -n 'gh-signature-helper.sh footer' .agents/scripts/ --files-with-matches | head -10`. Canonical caller: `claim-task-id.sh` and the wrappers in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh::_gh_wrapper_auto_sig`.
- The PATH shim at `.agents/scripts/gh` is the simplest path for the workflow YAML.

### Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-close-signature.sh` returns 0.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh` passes clean.
- Manual: locally run `cmd_close <task-id>` against a test fixture, confirm output contains `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` followed by `[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh)`.
- Post-merge: next auto-closed issue (e.g. via TODO.md `[x]` push) has a comment ending in `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_close_comment` output ends with `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` marker for completed, cancelled, deferred, and declined task variants.
- [ ] `cmd_reopen` reopen comment ends with `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`.
- [ ] `issue-sync-reusable.yml` close/comment paths produce signed comments (either via PATH shim or explicit helper call).
- [ ] New regression test passes (3 cases).
- [ ] No shellcheck violations.

## Session Origin

User reported during interactive review of #21892: "we used to have a closing comment on issues & prs, but i don't see those now?". Investigation confirmed two distinct paths — agent-closed issues retain the rich+signed format, but the auto-close path via `github-actions` strips both summary and signature. Issue #21892 vs #21888 is the canonical contrast.

title: t3205: scan-stale: auto-release defaults OFF in AI agent sessions (TTY-only detection misses OpenCode/Claude Code interactive)
body:
## What

`scan-stale` (no flag) defaults `auto-release` OFF in AI agent sessions (OpenCode TUI, Claude Code CLI) because the agent's bash subprocess is piped from the runtime — `[[ -t 0 && -t 1 ]]` returns false. The TTY check in `_isc_cmd_scan_stale` collapses two distinct concepts:

- **Truly headless** (pulse, CI workers, GitHub Actions) — should default OFF.
- **AI agent interactive** (user sitting at TUI/CLI driving an agent) — should default ON.

Result: agents that run `scan-stale` at session start (per the t2056 protocol in AGENTS.md) see "stale claims found" but auto-release silently no-ops, leaving the user surprised when the same stamps reappear next session. Each session has to re-discover the `--auto-release` workaround.

## Why

The qualification rule (dead PID **AND** missing worktree) is itself the safety net — those stamps are categorically un-recoverable. The TTY check on top is belt-and-suspenders to the point of being a foot-gun. Real-world impact: 2 of 6 stale stamps in a fresh session this morning required a second invocation with `--auto-release` after the default no-op'd. Multiply across dozens of agent sessions per day.

Canonical incident: t3087 cleanup (marcusquinn/aidevops#21861) — agent surfaced 6 stale stamps; default `scan-stale` released zero; explicit `--auto-release` released 2 (the rest had been released by other paths). Agent had to discover the flag in `--help` mid-session.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh`

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh:437-439` — replace the bare TTY check with a three-way detection that distinguishes truly-headless from AI-agent-interactive.

  Current code:

  ```bash
  if [[ -z "$auto_release_flag" ]]; then
      [[ -t 0 && -t 1 ]] && auto_release_flag=1 || auto_release_flag=0
  fi
  ```

  Replacement (model on `is_main_allowlisted_path()` headless detection in `pre-edit-check.sh`, which uses the same env-var family):

  ```bash
  if [[ -z "$auto_release_flag" ]]; then
      if [[ -t 0 && -t 1 ]]; then
          auto_release_flag=1                                           # human TTY
      elif [[ -n "${FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS:-}${AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS:-}${OPENCODE_HEADLESS:-}${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ]]; then
          auto_release_flag=0                                           # explicitly headless
      elif [[ -n "${OPENCODE_SESSION_ID:-}${OPENCODE_TUI:-}${CLAUDECODE:-}${CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT:-}" ]]; then
          auto_release_flag=1                                           # AI-agent interactive
      else
          auto_release_flag=0                                           # conservative default
      fi
  fi
  ```

  Verify the exact OpenCode/Claude Code env-var names by inspecting `env` output from a live agent session — adjust the third branch to match what's actually exported by the runtime.

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh` — add two new test cases:
  - Test 8: `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID=test` (no TTY) → auto-release ON
  - Test 9: `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1` + `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID=test` → auto-release OFF (headless wins)

  Model on Test 6/Test 7 patterns at lines 219-245.

### Reference pattern

Headless detection in `pre-edit-check.sh::is_main_allowlisted_path` — same env-var family (`FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`, `OPENCODE_HEADLESS`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`). The new branch in `_isc_cmd_scan_stale` should mirror that detection logic, plus AI-agent runtime markers.

### Verification

```bash
# Existing tests still pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh

# Shellcheck clean
shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh

# Manual smoke (in OpenCode session — no TTY but AI-agent runtime):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale 2>&1 | grep "auto-released"
# Expected: shows "auto-released N stamp(s)" for any qualifying dead stamps
```

### Complexity Impact

`_isc_cmd_scan_stale` is currently ~36 lines (422-457). Adding the three-way detection adds ~5 lines → ~41 lines, well under the 80-line warning threshold. No refactor needed.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `scan-stale` (no flag) auto-releases dead+missing stamps in OpenCode/Claude Code agent sessions
- [ ] `scan-stale` (no flag) preserves stamps in headless contexts (`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1`, GitHub Actions)
- [ ] Existing tests 1-7 still pass
- [ ] Two new tests (Test 8 and Test 9) cover the new branches
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on the modified file

## Tier

`tier:standard` — narrow scope (one helper function + tests), clear pattern to follow, no architecture decisions.

title: t3206: pulse-unbound-var-check: accumulated-diff false-positive on intra-branch fixes
body:
## Task

Pulse Unbound-Var Check uses accumulated-diff extraction that produces false positives when a violation is introduced and then fixed within the same branch.

## Why

CI gate scans `git log -p --first-parent MERGE_BASE..HEAD -- <file>` and pipes `grep '^+'` into the validator. Bad lines from an early commit AND their corrected replacements from a later commit BOTH appear in the `+` stream — the scanner flags the bad lines even though they're not in the final tree.

Forces contributor to squash + force-push to get a clean CI run, which is forbidden by the agent's destructive-ops rule without explicit user approval.

## How

EDIT: `.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml` step "Get changed pulse-*.sh files and extract diff additions" (the loop that builds /tmp/puv-diff-lines/). Replace the `git log -p --first-parent | grep '^+'` extraction with:

- **Preferred**: `git diff "$MERGE_BASE..$HEAD_SHA" -- "$file" | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' | sed 's/^+//'` — gives the NET delta of the branch, so intra-branch reversals don't leak bad lines.

Scanner itself (.agents/scripts/pulse-unbound-var-check.sh) is correct; only the CI extraction step is broken.

## Verification

1. Repro: in a branch, add `local foo bar` to a pulse-*.sh file (commit 1), then split to `local foo=""\nlocal bar=""` (commit 2). Push and confirm the gate fails today.
2. Apply the fix. Push the same two-commit branch. Confirm the gate passes.
3. Confirm a brand-new violation introduced by a single commit still fails.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Two-commit branch with intro+fix passes the gate
- [ ] Single-commit branch with violation still fails the gate
- [ ] Local + CI agree on result

## Files Scope

- .github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml

## Related

- Surfaced during PR #21912 (t3194) — required force-push squash to merge a clean fix; force-push forbidden by framework destructive-ops rule without explicit user request.

title: t3207: test-scan-stale: Test 2 fails on origin/main due to t2421 worker-pattern PID liveness check
body:
## Task

Test 2 in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh` ("live PID + missing worktree → stamp preserved") fails on `origin/main` independent of any in-flight work. This was uncovered while shipping t3205 (PR #21920, GH#21913); the failure was verified to predate that work via `git stash && git checkout origin/main -- .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`.

## Why

The test's invariant — "live PID = preserve stamp regardless of `--auto-release`" — is correct in spirit but encodes the pre-t2421 contract. After t2421 ("command-aware liveness — bare kill -0 lies on macOS PID reuse"), `_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase` calls `_is_process_alive_and_matches "$pid" "${WORKER_PROCESS_PATTERN:-}" "$stored_hash"` instead of bare `kill -0`. The test uses `LIVE_PID=$$` (the bash test-runner's PID) which is alive but does NOT match `WORKER_PROCESS_PATTERN` (opencode/claude/aidevops), so the helper classifies it as dead and the stamp is auto-released.

Either the test needs to seed a process pattern that matches `WORKER_PROCESS_PATTERN`, or the function needs a documented contract change. Without resolution, the test is permanently red on `main`, which trains future sessions to ignore that file's exit code and erodes its value as a regression guard.

## How

### Files to modify

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh` — likely the right fix (test must reflect the post-t2421 liveness contract, not the pre-t2421 one).

OR

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh::_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase` — only if the t2421 contract for non-worker PIDs needs to change. Read t2421's commit message and `shared-constants.sh::_is_process_alive_and_matches` BEFORE touching this — t2421 was deliberate and the test bug is the more likely culprit.

### Reference pattern

Read `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh::_is_process_alive_and_matches` and `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh::WORKER_PROCESS_PATTERN` to understand what counts as "alive enough". Look for an existing test that sets up a worker-pattern-matching child process (search `tests/` for `WORKER_PROCESS_PATTERN` or `exec -a opencode`).

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh
# expected: 9 / 9 tests pass on main, no failures
```

Run shellcheck clean on whichever file is touched.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`

## Acceptance

- All 9 tests in `test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh` pass on origin/main.
- No regression in `_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase` behaviour for real worker PIDs (the t2421 contract for OpenCode/Claude Code/aidevops process patterns must remain intact).
- Shellcheck clean on the modified file.
- PR body cites the t2421 contract and explains which side of the fix was chosen and why.

## Session Origin

Discovered while shipping t3205 (PR #21920, GH#21913 — scan-stale auto-release ON in AI agent interactive sessions). Failure verified on origin/main via stash-and-checkout before t3205 changes were applied — independent of t3205.

title: t3208: Circuit-breaker trip should auto-file sibling root-cause investigation task
body:
## What

Circuit breaker trip notifications (e.g. marcusquinn/aidevops#21919) are notification-only. They report the trip, list manual resolution steps, then auto-reset after 1800s — without driving any automated root-cause investigation. As a result, the same underlying failure (e.g. canary timeouts, OAuth drift, rate limits) keeps tripping the breaker on subsequent cycles until a human notices, or the underlying transient resolves on its own.

Evidence (recurring pattern, all closed without root-cause fix):

- marcusquinn/aidevops#21919 — 2026-04-30 (current, OPEN, last_failure=`no_worker_process` on #21891)
- marcusquinn/aidevops#21556 — 2026-04-28
- marcusquinn/aidevops#4360 — 2026-03-13
- marcusquinn/aidevops#4318 — 2026-03-13
- marcusquinn/aidevops#2293 — 2026-02-25
- marcusquinn/aidevops#2292 — 2026-02-25

Six identical issues in two months. The breaker is doing its job (preventing token waste from doomed dispatches); the gap is that the trip event doesn't *teach* the system anything — it just pauses, auto-resets, and hopes.

## Why

`_cb_create_new_issue` (`.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh:608-641`) creates the trip notification with only two labels: `circuit-breaker` and `source:circuit-breaker`. No `auto-dispatch`. No sibling investigation task. The body says "1. Investigate the recent failures (check worker logs)" but nothing in the framework actually does step 1 — it's a TODO addressed to the human.

This is a `capture-don't-advise` violation by the framework itself: every trip is a labelled, structured failure event with rich diagnostic context (last failed task, failure reason, log paths) that we throw away.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-circuit-breaker-helper.sh` (extend)

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh:608-641` — extend `_cb_create_new_issue` to also file a sibling auto-dispatch investigation task after the trip notification is created. Pattern: model on `pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh` for the LLM-driven brief composition, but the investigation worker itself does the analysis (we just hand it the file paths and the failure event).

  Sibling task structure:

  - **Title:** `Investigate circuit-breaker trip #<trip-issue-num>: <failure_reason> after <count> consecutive failures`
  - **Labels:** `auto-dispatch`, `tier:thinking` (root-cause analysis on flaky infrastructure deserves opus), `bug`, `framework`, `source:circuit-breaker-investigation`
  - **Body:** must include
    - Link to trip notification (`Ref #<trip-issue-num>`)
    - Last failure task ID
    - Last failure reason (e.g. `no_worker_process`, `cli_usage_output`)
    - Log paths to inspect: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log`, `/tmp/pulse-<runner>-<repo>-<task>.log`, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/headless-runtime/canary-last-fail*`
    - Concrete acceptance: either file ≥1 fix task with `Ref #<trip-issue>` linking back, OR close trip notification with `transient` rationale + evidence (canary now passing, prior recurrences absent in last 7 days, etc.)
    - Tautology guard: if the worker investigation itself fails to spawn (i.e. the canary issue is the live blocker), the failure cascades and the existing `dispatch-cooldown-until` marker (t3197) prevents tight-loop retries — no special handling needed.

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-circuit-breaker-helper.sh` — add a test case that asserts trip-issue creation also files a sibling investigation task with the required label set.

### Reference pattern

- `pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh:140-190` (LLM-driven labelling pattern; here we don't need the LLM — we just create a structured task with deterministic content)
- `gh_create_issue` wrapper (already imported via `shared-constants.sh`) for the actual issue creation
- `task-brief-helper.sh` for body composition if the body grows beyond inline composition

### Verification

```bash
# Trip the breaker in test mode and confirm both issues are filed
CB_TEST_MODE=1 .agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh trip "test-task" "no_worker_process"
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label circuit-breaker --state open --limit 5
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label source:circuit-breaker-investigation --state open --limit 5
# Both should appear with correct labels and cross-references.

# Tests
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-circuit-breaker-helper.sh

# Shellcheck
shellcheck .agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh
```

### Complexity Impact

`_cb_create_new_issue` is currently ~33 lines (608-641). Adding the sibling-task creation as an inline block adds ~25 lines → ~58 lines total, under the 80-line warning threshold. Or extract into a new `_cb_file_investigation_task` helper (cleaner) — same total complexity.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every circuit-breaker trip creates BOTH a notification issue (current behaviour) AND a sibling `auto-dispatch tier:thinking` investigation task referencing it
- [ ] Investigation task body lists the canonical log paths and failure-reason-specific hypotheses
- [ ] Investigation task acceptance is either "file ≥1 concrete fix task" OR "close trip notification as transient with evidence"
- [ ] Existing tests still pass; one new test asserts the sibling task is filed
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean

## Tier

`tier:standard` — helper modification with well-defined scope and clear reference pattern. The investigation task itself (when dispatched) gets `tier:thinking`; this task is just plumbing to file it.

#auto-dispatch #framework #bug

title: Review followup: PR #21911 — GH#21903: status: threshold-based PILE-UP detection
body:
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions

PR #21911 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment
below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline
review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was
flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's
GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether
the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue
with a wontfix rationale.

**Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/21911

---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `prompts/build.txt`
section 6a). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.
4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate,
   merge, postflight).

title: t3209: pulse-unbound-var-check.yml diff-scoping double-counts replaced lines
body:
## Task

Fix `.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml` lines 100-102 so the diff-scoped scan reports the **net diff** between merge-base and HEAD, not the **aggregated added lines** across all commits in the PR.

## Why

The current logic uses:

```bash
git log -p --first-parent "${MERGE_BASE}..${HEAD_SHA}" -- "$file" \
  | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' | sed 's/^+//' \
  > "$diff_file"
```

This concatenates every `+` line across every commit in the PR. If a commit adds a buggy line and a later commit replaces it with a correct line, **both versions** end up in the synthetic diff file. The scanner then flags the buggy version even though it no longer exists in HEAD.

This false-positive forced t3198 (PR #21908) to squash + force-push the branch to clear the lint, despite HEAD's actual content being correct.

## How

EDIT: `.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml:100-102`

Replace the `git log -p --first-parent` pipeline with:

```bash
git diff "${MERGE_BASE}..${HEAD_SHA}" -- "$file" \
  | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' | sed 's/^+//' \
  > "$diff_file"
```

`git diff merge-base..HEAD` produces the **net** patch between two commits — only lines that exist in HEAD but not in merge-base. Lines added then replaced disappear from this view.

## Verification

Add a regression test that:
1. Creates a synthetic two-commit branch where commit 1 adds a buggy `local foo bar` and commit 2 replaces it with `local foo="" bar=""`.
2. Runs the workflow's diff-scoping logic.
3. Asserts the synthetic diff file contains ONLY the corrected line, not the buggy version.

Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-runner-health-helper.sh` for sandbox-isolated workflow logic tests.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml` uses `git diff merge-base..HEAD` (net diff), not `git log -p` (per-commit aggregate).
- [ ] Regression test asserts replaced-then-fixed lines are excluded from the synthetic diff.
- [ ] Existing test-suite for the unbound-var checker still passes.
- [ ] Comment in the workflow file documents WHY `git diff` is used (so future authors don't 'fix' it back).

## Context

- Discovered during t3198 (PR #21908). Required squash + force-push to clear false-positive.
- Reference fix: t2841 (commit `e05bcae1f`).
- Same pattern likely exists in other diff-scoped workflows — audit `.github/workflows/*` for similar `git log -p ... | grep '^+'` patterns.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/**`
